jobs.title: Summer 2027 - Mechanical Engineering Intern
jobs.location: Seattle, Washington
jobs.body: Shield AI is a venture-backed defense-tech company with the mission of protecting service members and civilians with intelligent systems. Its products include Hivemind autonomy software, V-BAT and X-BAT aircraft, and Aechelon simulation and synthetic reality technologies. With offices and facilities across the U.S., Europe, the Middle East, and Asia-Pacific, Shield AI’s technology actively supports operations worldwide. For more information, visit www.shield.ai https://shield.ai/. Follow Shield AI on LinkedIn https://www.linkedin.com/company/shield-ai, X https://x.com/shieldaitech, Instagram https://www.instagram.com/shield_ai, and YouTube https://www.youtube.com/@Shield_AI. Our Summer Internship program is a wonderful opportunity for Fall and Spring graduates to immerse themselves in an innovative and mission driven culture. Our paid internship program will provide you with hands on mentorship, an opportunity to add real contribution to our company via your internship project, and a possible job offer at the end. You will have the chance to make lifelong friendships, expand your network, and learn all about what it's like to work in a high-growth, fast scaling tech unicorn. You'll take part in company sponsored events and enjoy exploring a new city. Read on below to learn more about this unique internship! Job Description: The mechanical engineering team is responsible for mechanical design and development projects for Shield AI's autonomous UAV products. We follow a rigorous design process, as we innovate, prototype, test, and release creative design solutions. We work with cross-functional teams to ensure the successful development and launch of new products. Intern Project Scope & Description: - - Own requirements gathering, design, and validation of multiple test stands used to test components and subsystems on X-BAT or V-BAT - Design tooling to hold devices-under-test (DUTs) during environmental testing. - Design test stands and test fixtures that interface with engines, electric motors, circuit boards, and various other aeronautical components. - Specify facilities requirements (electrical, plumbing, etc…) for environmental test chambers. - Contribute to and attend cross-functional design reviews. Advocate for design changes that result in simpler testing processes. - Other duties as assigned. Required qualifications: - - You are an undergraduate, graduate or PhD student pursuing a degree in Mechanical Engineering or related STEM field. - Strong understanding of fundamental engineering concepts, including EE, Mech E, Programming, Physics, and Mathematics. - Experience working on multidisciplinary hardware development projects, which can be from an internship, job, club, team, personal project, etc. - Great written and verbal communication. - Demonstrated history of showing ownership of project outcomes and delivering exceptional results. - Record of working hard, being a trustworthy teammate, holding yourself and others to high standards, and being kind to others. Preferred qualifications: - - Experience with CAD tools such as SolidWorks, NX, CATIA, etc… (NX preferred). - Ability to rapidly manufacture your designs in a machine shop. - Experience working with internal combustion engines. This could be in design, tuning, and/or assembly. - Familiarity with designing mechanical tooling or test fixtures. - Demonstrated adaptability, agility, and the ability to innovate under pressure to meet dynamic project demands and drive successful #intern Shield AI is proud to offer competitive pay and a housing stipend for qualified hires. While our People Experience team provides resources and assistance, interns are responsible to find their own housing and travel to and from their office location. ### Shield AI is proud to be an equal opportunity workplace and is an affirmative action employer. We are committed to equal employment opportunity regardless of race, color, ancestry, religion, sex, national origin, sexual orientation, age, marital status, disability, gender identity or Veteran status. If you have a disability or special need that requires accommodation, please let us know.

jobs.title: Mechanical Engineer Intern
jobs.location: Milpitas, CA, United States of America
jobs.body: To make electronics, you need chips, wafers, transistors, reticles, and... To make these, you must see, test and manufacture them at scale—faster and better than ever before. That's where KLA comes in. Whether you're early in your career or an experienced professional, you'll solve complex challenges, work alongside brilliant minds and help shape the future of technology. Group/Division The Semiconductor Products and Customers (Semi PC) business unit designs, builds and sells KLA’s product portfolio to help chip manufacturers meet high-quality standards for technologies like AI, data centers, automotive and electronic devices. Our inspection, metrology, and analytics systems detect and monitor defects across logic and memory chips, specialty semiconductors, wafers, reticles, advanced packaging, process equipment and materials. We also develop technologies for specialty processes, IC substrates, and PCB manufacturing, including etch and deposition, component inspection, and imaging and analytics. The e-Beam division plays a critical role in KLA’s inspection ecosystem, with tools that deliver high-resolution, timely insights into defects and critical locations on the wafer. Used alongside KLA’s patterned and bare wafer inspectors, e-Beam systems help our customers quickly identify and understand yield-impacting issues—enabling faster, more effective actions to correct the manufacturing process. What You'll Do In this role, you will play a key part in advancing business priorities by delivering high-impact work across your area of expertise. Mechanical engineering is fundamental to the semiconductor industry. Every wafer inspection and metrology system depends on precise and reliable mechanical design. As a Mechanical Engineering Intern at KLA, you'll learn how advanced semiconductor tools work from the inside out. You'll also own a real design project that ships to the team. What you'll do Design, model and document a functional subsystem for an e-beam tool, or tooling and fixtures that support tool build, alignment, test or service. Create 3D CAD models and production-ready 2D drawings using GD&T. Run engineering analysis (tolerance stack-ups, structural, thermal or vibration) to validate your design. Work with suppliers and the machine shop on prototypes, then assemble, test and iterate. Present your design and results to the engineering team at the end of the internship. What we're looking for Pursuing a BS or MS in Mechanical Engineering or a related field. Strong foundation in mechanical design, materials and manufacturing processes. Experience with 3D CAD (e.g., SolidWorks, Creo or NX). Hands-on build experience, such as a lab, a design team or personal projects. Clear communication and a curiosity to learn how complex systems work. Minimum Qualifications Requires less than 1 year of related experience About KLA We provide advanced inspection tools, metrology systems, process solutions, and computational analytics that make electronics possible, tackling complex challenges. From electron and photon optics to machine learning and data analytics, we seek perfection at the most fundamental level of matter in the universe. If you want to make electronics that push industries forward and make the world a better place, join us. Total Rewards Base Pay Range: $0.00 - $0.00 Primary Location: USA-CA-Milpitas-KLA KLA’s total rewards package for employees may also include participation in performance incentive programs and eligibility for additional benefits including but not limited to: medical, dental, vision, life, and other voluntary benefits, 401(K) including company matching, employee stock purchase program (ESPP), student debt assistance, tuition reimbursement program, development and career growth opportunities and programs, financial planning benefits, wellness benefits including an employee assistance program (EAP), paid time off and paid company holidays, and family care and bonding leave. Interns are eligible for some of the benefits listed. Our pay ranges are determined by role, level, and location. The range displayed reflects the pay for this position in the primary location identified in this posting. Actual pay depends on several factors, including state minimum pay wage rates, location, job-related skills, experience, and relevant education level or training. We are committed to complying with all applicable federal and state minimum wage requirements where applicable. If applicable, your recruiter can share more about the specific pay range for your preferred location during the hiring process. Use of AI Statement At KLA, our interviews seek to understand your individual skills, problem-solving approach and authentic thinking. To ensure a fair and consistent evaluation, the use of AI, recording tools or other technologies to generate, suggest or provide responses during interviews—whether virtual or in person—is not permitted unless explicitly approved in advance as part of a reasonable accommodation or invited by the interviewer. Use of these tools may interfere with our ability to evaluate your individual qualifications and affect your candidacy. KLA is committed to advancing innovation through responsible AI, and we value candidates who share this mindset. Equal Opportunity Statement KLA is proud to be an Equal Opportunity Employer. We will ensure that qualified individuals with disabilities are provided reasonable accommodation to participate in the job application or interview process, to perform essential job functions, and to receive other benefits and privileges of employment. Please contact us at talent.acquisition@kla.com or at +1-408-352-2808 to request accommodation. For additional information, view the US Know Your Rights poster on the U.S. Equal Employment Opportunity Commission website.

jobs.title: Product Design Engineering Intern (Summer 2027)

jobs.body: Who We Are HP IQ is HP’s new AI innovation lab. Combining startup agility with HP’s global scale, we’re building intelligent technologies that redefine how the world works, creates, and collaborates. We’re assembling a diverse, world-class team—engineers, designers, researchers, and product minds—focused on creating an intelligent ecosystem across HP’s portfolio. Together, we’re developing intuitive, adaptive solutions that spark creativity, boost productivity, and make collaboration seamless. By embedding AI advancements into every HP product and service, we’re expanding what’s possible for individuals, organisations, and the future of work. Join us as we reinvent work, so people everywhere can do their best work. The position offers the opportunity to own the mechanical and systems integration challenges that transform concepts into shipping products. thrives in startup-like, fast-moving environments Preferred Skills Minimum 1-2 years of hardware product design or related experience; prior internship at a consumer electronics company is preferred Experience communicating with contract manufacturers or FATP (final assembly) partners Exposure to design of experiments (DOE) or design validation methodologies Portfolio demonstrating complete hardware projects from design through prototype or production Experience with assembly process design, datuming, and fixturing Familiarity with cross-functional product development from concept through production ramp Hourly Pay Range: $40.00–$50.00 per hour. Final salary offered is based upon multiple factors including individual job-related qualifications, education, experience, knowledge and skills. At HP IQ, we offer a competitive and comprehensive benefits package, including: Health insurance Dental insurance Vision insurance Long term/short term disability insurance Employee assistance program Flexible spending account Life insurance Generous time off policies, including; 4-12 weeks fully paid parental leave based on tenure 11 paid holidays Additional flexible paid vacation and sick leave ( US benefits overview ) Why HP IQ? HP IQ is HP’s new AI innovation lab, building the intelligence to empower humanity—reimagining how we work, create, and connect to shape the future of work. jobs.title: Electromechanical Design Engineering Intern (Summer 2027)
jobs.location: Palo Alto, California
jobs.body: ABOUT US Rivian and Volkswagen Group Technologies is a joint venture between two industry leaders with a clear vision for automotive’s next chapter. From operating systems to zonal controllers to cloud and connectivity solutions, we’re addressing the challenges of electric vehicles through technology that will set the standards for software-defined vehicles around the world. The road to the future is uncharted. By combining our expertise across connectivity, AI, security and more, we’ll map a new way forward. Working together, we’ll create a future that’s more connected, more intelligent, more sustainable for everyone. This is a general application used to fill multiple internship openings across our Electrical Hardware teams. If selected, you will be matched to a specific team based on your background and interests during the interview process. - Electrical Design Engineering Intern - Electrical Engineering Design Intern - Electrical Functional Safety Engineering Intern - Embedded Software Engineering Intern - Mechanical Design Engineering Intern - Product Launch Engineering Intern - Reliability Engineering Intern - Software Engineering Intern, Vehicle Lab - Supplier Excellence Engineering Intern - Test Automation Systems Engineering Intern ROLE SUMMARY Every Electronic Control Unit goes through a full lifecycle of design, validation, manufacturing readiness, and release. As an Electromechanical Design Engineering intern, you will be involved in one part of that lifecycle, which may include circuit design, mechanical packaging, hardware validation and test, reliability and functional safety analysis, or supplier and manufacturing readiness work. Specific project areas vary by team and may include: - Designing and developing analog, digital, or mixed signal circuits, including schematic capture and component selection - Supporting mechanical packaging design or structural and thermal simulation for ECU enclosures - Building or running hardware validation tests and test automation systems - Contributing to hardware functional safety analyses such as FMEA or FMEDA - Supporting supplier quality, product launch, or manufacturing readiness activities for ECU programs RESPONSIBILITIES - Support proof of concept, design, or validation work for an assigned hardware project - Debug and troubleshoot hardware issues at the board or system level - Document component release information and maintain accurate design records - Collaborate with cross functional engineering and design teams to understand requirements - Communicate progress and findings to your team throughout the internship QUALIFICATIONS Minimum: - Currently enrolled in a Bachelor's or Master's program at an accredited US university - Proficient in electrical engineering fundamentals Preferred: - Actively pursuing a degree in Electrical Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Hardware Engineering, or a closely related field, with intent to return to school after the internship - Understanding of electronics, packaging, and hardware design - Familiarity with communication protocols such as CAN, Ethernet, USB, I2C, or SPI - Coursework or project experience with PCB design tools, CAD tools, or simulation software - Familiarity with product lifecycle management and component release processes TOTAL REWARDS We build the exceptional — and we believe the people doing that work should be rewarded accordingly. jobs.title: Summer 2027 Mechanical Engineer Intern- Bachelor's/Master's (Santa Clara, CA)
jobs.location: Santa Clara,CA, United States of America
jobs.body: Who We Are Applied Materials is the global leader in materials science and engineering solutions that are at the foundation of virtually every new semiconductor chip and advanced display in the world. The equipment that we create and service is essential to advancing AI and accelerating the commercialization of next-generation semiconductor chips. Join us and push the boundaries of materials science and engineering in a company at the foundation of the electronics industry. The work we do together advances the world’s technology. What We Offer Location: Santa Clara,CA You’ll benefit from a supportive work culture that encourages you to learn, develop, and grow your career as you take on challenges and drive innovative solutions for our customers. We empower our team to push the boundaries of what is possible—while learning every day in a supportive leading global company. Visit our Careers website to learn more. At Applied Materials, we care about the health and wellbeing of our employees. We’re committed to providing programs and support that encourage personal and professional growth and care for you at work, at home, or wherever you may go. Learn more about our benefits . Position Overview We are seeking a highly motivated Mechanical Engineering Intern to join our Hardware Engineering team. This role provides an opportunity to work alongside experienced engineers on the development, analysis, testing, and improvement of semiconductor equipment and subsystems. The intern will gain hands-on experience in mechanical design, product development, experimental validation, and failure analysis while contributing to real-world engineering projects that impact customer performance and product reliability. Key Responsibilities Work as a Mechanical Design Engineer of Critical Chamber Hardware of Capital Equipment Product Lines, with following additional responsibilities: ​ Support mechanical design and development activities for semiconductor manufacturing equipment and related hardware. Assist in creating and modifying 3D CAD models, drawings, and engineering documentation. Design and execute engineering experiments, collect and analyze data, and present findings to project teams. Participate in prototype development, testing, and validation activities. Conduct root cause investigations and support failure analysis efforts. Collaborate with cross-functional teams including manufacturing, quality, sourcing, and suppliers. Contribute to design reviews and recommend improvements for performance, reliability, manufacturability, and cost. Prepare technical reports and presentations to communicate project results and recommendations. Preferred Technical Skills Fundamentals of mechanics, materials, heat transfer, fluid mechanics, and machine design. Experience with CAD software such as Siemens NX, SolidWorks, Creo, or similar platforms. Basic knowledge of Geometric Dimensioning & Tolerancing (GD&T). Familiarity with Finite Element Analysis (FEA) and engineering simulation tools. Knowledge of Design of Experiments (DOE), statistical analysis, or data analytics is a plus. Strong problem-solving, analytical, and communication skills. Ability to work effectively in a team environment and manage multiple priorities. Minimum Qualifications Currently pursuing a Bachelor's or Master's degree in Mechanical Engineering or a related engineering discipline. Good academic standing with a preferred GPA of 3.0 or higher preferred Available for a full-time internship during the summer or designated internship period. Strong interest in product design, mechanical systems, and semiconductor manufacturing technologies. Applications will be reviewed on a rolling basis. Please apply by December 31, 2026. Note: This position may close early based on application volume or candidate selection. Additional Information Time Type: Full time Employee Type: Intern / Student Travel: No Relocation Eligible: Yes The salary offered to a selected candidate will be based on multiple factors including location, hire grade, job-related knowledge, skills, experience, and with consideration of internal equity of our current team members. In addition to a comprehensive benefits package, candidates may be eligible for other forms of compensation such as participation in a bonus and a stock award program, as applicable. For all sales roles, the posted salary range is the Target Total Cash (TTC) range for the role, which is the sum of base salary and target bonus amount at 100% goal achievement. Applied Materials is an Equal Opportunity Employer. Qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, national origin, citizenship, ancestry, religion, creed, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, age, disability, veteran or military status, or any other basis prohibited by law. In addition, Applied endeavors to make our careers site accessible to all users. If you would like to contact us regarding accessibility of our website or need assistance completing the application process, please contact us via e-mail at Accommodations_Program@amat.com, or by calling our HR Direct Help Line at 877-612-7547, option 1, and following the prompts to speak to an HR Advisor. jobs.title: Test Engineering Intern
jobs.location: East Bay Area
jobs.body: ABOUT US: Astro Mechanica is a vertically integrated aerospace company developing a scalable technology platform to power critical infrastructure, mission operations, and the future of flight. We apply aerospace engineering and quality standards across our products, delivering high performance, reliability, and efficiency for the most demanding operating environments. Astro Mechanica is backed by leading venture and strategic investors, including Andreessen Horowitz (a16z), Giant Step Capital, United Airlines Ventures, and Voyager Ventures. WHO WE ARE: We’re a team of passionate engineers dedicated to advancing aerospace. We’re generalists with specialist depth, united by a flat structure and a shared obsession with building things that work well. We move fast, stay pragmatic, and let engineering excellence speak louder than hierarchy. WHO YOU ARE: Astro Mechanica is seeking an intern to join our Test Team for the summer of 2027 (program begins on June 7, 2027 for semester schools and June 27, 2027 for quarter schools). The ideal candidate is excited to help design, fabricate, operate, and improve the test infrastructure supporting our jet engine and subsystems. As an intern, you’ll be embedded with the test team in Antioch or Alameda, working on real test stands and hardware alongside full-time engineers. Your work will help keep test operations running smoothly while expanding and improving our test capabilities. In this role, your mission will be to help create and operate test infrastructure for hardware research and development, with mentorship from senior engineers along the way. You’ll see firsthand how new designs are rigorously tested to meet quality and performance targets before they’re integrated into the aircraft. You embody the test-like-you-fly philosophy. WHAT YOU’LL DO: - Help design test stands, fixtures, and supporting hardware to enable new test capabilities - Support development of test plans, instrumentation schemes, and data collection methods that capture high-quality, decision-driving data - Create and update documentation, including P&IDs, electrical schematics, and test procedures, while working with stakeholders to make sure stand requirements are met - Assist with fabrication, assembly, and activation of test stands and fixtures - Support test operations, including setup, instrumentation, execution, and teardown - Analyze test data and compare results with analytical models or simulations - Help troubleshoot test facility problems and find ways to improve test throughput and reliability - Own a scoped project through the summer and present your results to the team at the end of the internship WHAT WE’RE LOOKING FOR: - Currently pursuing a Bachelor’s, Master’s, or PhD in Mechanical Engineering, Aerospace Engineering, Electrical Engineering, or a related discipline - Club, project, research, or internship hands-on experience with fluidic, mechanical, or electrical systems - Exposure to instrumentation and test hardware (pressure transducers, thermocouples, load cells, relays, solenoids, pneumatics) - Familiarity with CAD and the ability to design simple test hardware, fixtures, or modifications - Experience with Python, MATLAB, or similar tools for data analysis - Exposure to data acquisition systems (e.g., LabVIEW, NI hardware) is a plus - Hands-on fabrication skills (machining, wiring, soldering, plumbing) are a plus - Respect for safety when working around pressurized systems, flammables, and high voltage - Attentive to detail and committed to a high level of quality in all work - Flexibility to work in a fast-paced environment - Available for a full-time, in-person internship in San Francisco during Summer 2027 (approximately 10–12 weeks) PERKS & BENEFITS: - Competitive hourly pay - Hands-on mentorship from experienced engineers - Company-funded perks, including team lunches, game nights, and other activities ADDITIONAL INFORMATION: At Astro Mechanica, we highly value in-office work to foster collaboration and strengthen our company culture. We consider working in the office five days a week an essential part of the employee's role. Astro Mechanica is an equal opportunity employer. We proudly recruit and hire a diverse workforce and are committed to creating an inclusive environment for all employees. Pay range: $40 – $55 per hour.

jobs.title: Intern, Haptic Metrology & Stylus Tablet Development - Summer 2027
jobs.body: > Requisition Number: 79110 The company built on breakthroughs. ​ Join us.​ Corning is one of the world’s leading innovators in glass, ceramic, and materials science. From the depths of the ocean to the farthest reaches of space, our technologies push the boundaries of what’s possible. ​ How do we do this? With our people. They break through limitations and expectations – not once in a career, but every day. They help move our company, and the world, forward. ​ ​ At Corning, there are endless possibilities for making an impact. You can help connect the unconnected, drive the future of automobiles, transform at-home entertainment, and ensure the delivery of lifesaving medicines. And so much more.​ ​ Come break through with us. Role Purpose We are seeking a motivated Summer Intern to support the development of haptic metrology methods and tools for stylus-enabled tablet applications. This rotational internship provides hands-on exposure to the interdisciplinary work involved in evaluating, measuring, and improving stylus haptic experiences. The intern will collaborate with engineering, product, research, and quality teams to help characterize haptic performance, develop repeatable measurement approaches, analyze test data, and translate findings into recommendations for product development. This role is well suited to a student interested in hardware, sensing, human-computer interaction, mechanical or electrical engineering, embedded systems, or experimental measurement. Program Perks: Competitive salaries Assistance with housing and travel Meaningful project and final project presentation Intern Activities: Social and networking opportunities Weekly tech talks Community involvement Key Responsibilities Support development and validation of metrology methods for measuring haptic performance in stylus and tablet systems. Assist with test setup design, fixture development, calibration, and documentation of measurement procedures. Conduct repeatable experiments to evaluate variables such as vibration, force, latency, frequency response, contact behavior, pressure sensitivity, and user-perceived haptic quality. Collect, clean, analyze, and visualize experimental data; identify trends, variation, and potential sources of error. Help define performance metrics, test protocols, acceptance criteria, and reporting formats for haptic features. Collaborate with hardware, firmware, software, mechanical, UX research, and quality teams to understand product requirements and test results. Investigate measurement equipment, sensors, data-acquisition tools, and industry practices relevant to haptic characterization. Support root-cause investigations for performance issues and help propose improvements to test methods, designs, or processes. Maintain organized lab records, test reports, experiment logs, and technical presentations. Participate in professional-development programming and present a final project summary to technical stakeholders. Experiences/Education - Required Currently pursuing a bachelor’s or master’s degree in Mechanical Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, Physics, Robotics, Human-Computer Interaction, Materials Science, or a related technical discipline. Interest in haptics, sensing, precision measurement, stylus input, consumer electronics, or human-device interaction. Familiarity with experimental methods, data collection, and basic statistical analysis. Experience with one or more of the following is preferred: Python, MATLAB, LabVIEW, Excel, data visualization, signal processing, microcontrollers, sensors, or data-acquisition systems. Ability to interpret technical drawings, test plans, specifications, and engineering documentation is a plus. Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, with attention to detail and a commitment to measurement repeatability. Clear written and verbal communication skills and the ability to work effectively on a cross-functional team. Ability to work safely and responsibly in a laboratory or prototyping environment. Experiences/Education - Desired Coursework or projects involving vibrations, controls, mechatronics, instrumentation, signal processing, embedded systems, or human factors. jobs.title: 2027 Summer Intern - Research & Development - Energy and Propulsion Controls
jobs.location: Warren, Michigan, United States of America
jobs.body: Job Description The Role: As a 2027 Summer Intern on the Energy and Propulsion Controls team, you will support researchers and engineers working on advanced vehicle energy-management, propulsion-control, and thermal-management technologies. A primary focus of this role will be the EVE Research Program, where thermal management is a core technical deliverable. You will help translate ongoing research into vehicle-level control concepts, models, simulations, and implementation activities that support efficient, safe, and high-performing electrified propulsion systems. You will gain experience connecting control strategies with batteries, power electronics, electric machines, propulsion systems, thermal loops, sensors, actuators, and vehicle-level energy requirements. GM’s thermal-control work includes coordinating battery, power-electronics, drive-unit, charging, HVAC-related, and front-end airflow requirements while balancing efficiency, performance, comfort, and component protection. The Team: The Research and Development organization explores technologies that can improve vehicle efficiency, propulsion performance, charging, thermal behavior, durability, and customer experience. The EVE Research Program includes work across advanced controls, thermal management, propulsion-energy conversion, fast charging, and vehicle health management. You will work in a multidisciplinary environment with controls researchers, thermal engineers, propulsion specialists, modeling and simulation experts, and vehicle-development teams. The team applies systems engineering, controls theory, experimentation, simulation, and data analysis to evaluate new concepts and transition promising research into vehicle applications. What You’ll Do: Support ongoing research assignments related to energy management, propulsion controls, thermal management, and vehicle-level control coordination. Help develop, evaluate, and document control strategies for battery, power electronics, electric machines, drive units, charging systems, and related thermal systems. Support the vehicle implementation of thermal-management research, including control logic for coolant pumps, valves, compressors, heaters, fans, shutters, and other thermal actuators. Develop or modify models used to study battery, propulsion, and thermal-system behavior under representative vehicle operating conditions. Run simulations and analyze system behavior across drive cycles, ambient conditions, charging conditions, operating modes, and component limits. Evaluate tradeoffs among energy consumption, range, component temperature, charging performance, propulsion capability, drive quality, efficiency, and occupant comfort. Support the development of interfaces between propulsion controls, energy-management functions, battery systems, thermal systems, HVAC-related systems, and vehicle-level controllers. Analyze sensor and actuator data to identify trends, control issues, performance limitations, and opportunities for improvement. Compare simulation results with laboratory, bench, hardware-in-the-loop, or vehicle-test data when available. Assist with control-strategy verification and validation through test-case development, test execution, data review, and issue investigation. Support the documentation of requirements, control logic, system assumptions, interfaces, calibration parameters, test procedures, and technical results. Create plots, dashboards, presentations, technical summaries, and other materials that communicate findings to engineering and research stakeholders. Collaborate with researchers and engineers to define technical questions, establish analysis plans, review results, and recommend next steps. Present progress and technical findings in team reviews and incorporate feedback into follow-on work. Required Qualifications: Pursuit of an advanced degree (MS or PhD) in electrical engineering, mechanical engineering, controls engineering, computer engineering, chemical engineering, systems engineering, aerospace engineering, or a related engineering discipline. Able to work fulltime, 40 hours per week during the summer months. Must be willing to work in a laboratory, engineering test, or vehicle-development environment, as applicable to the assignment. Preferred Qualifications: Coursework, research, or project experience in control systems, thermal systems, energy management, vehicle dynamics, battery systems, power electronics, electric propulsion, or mechatronics. Experience with MATLAB/Simulink, Python, Modelica, GT-SUITE, or comparable modeling and simulation tools. Familiarity with feedback control, system identification, optimization, state estimation, calibration, or control-oriented modeling. Experience analyzing time-series data from simulations, laboratory testing, hardware-in-the-loop testing, or vehicle testing. Experience with sensors, actuators, data acquisition, embedded controls, or software development. Understanding of battery state of charge, battery power limits, thermal limits, energy consumption, regenerative braking, or propulsion-system operating modes. Familiarity with CAN, LIN, signal databases, vehicle data logging, or other automotive communication and measurement technologies. Ability to organize technical work, document assumptions, investigate unexpected results, and communicate conclusions clearly. Strong analytical, written, and verbal communication skills, along with curiosity and a willingness to learn. GM does not provide immigration-related sponsorship for this role. This includes direct company sponsorship, entry of GM as the immigration employer of record on a government form, and any work authorization requiring a written submission or other immigration support from the company (e.g., H1-B, OPT, STEM OPT, CPT, TN, J-1, etc.). jobs.body: SUMMER 2027 INTERNSHIP/CO-OP: MECHANICAL ENGINEERING Kirkland, WA · Full-time · Onsite ABOUT SKYBAND GPS jamming and spoofing affect thousands of flights every day (GPSThreatMap.com http://GPSThreatMap.com). Skyband Systems has built the M100, a certified avionics system to overcome this threat to safety and operational reliability. The M100 fuses satellite signals from Low Earth Orbit (LEO) with inertial sensing to give pilots a trusted position source that doesn't depend on GPS. We're a VC-backed, fast-paced team based in Kirkland, WA, made up of engineers who built and scaled Starlink Aviation at SpaceX. We design, build, test, and fly our own hardware in our own aircraft. Everyone on the team has significant ownership over product areas or problem spaces. THE ROLE You'll join our mechanical team and assist in design and operational engineering scope for the M100 and subsequent products. You will work to improve M100 performance, reliability, and cost throughout its life cycle - from concept to physical aircraft installation, flight test, and fleet operation. You will also help conceptualize and design the next generation of Skyband products. Your products will integrate into a wide variety of airframes, enabling wireless connections to satellites, data bus connections to aircraft, and IP networking to store and analyze data. You will design the future of pilot-focused navigation equipment, and stand up the production line to build it. WHAT YOU'LL DO - Help design the future of aviation PNT with new Skyband products - Build, test, and refine production M100 avionics assemblies - Design and build test fixtures and automated test setups for development and production - Support environmental and EMI/EMC qualification testing to DO-160: planning, execution, and data review - Build and expand production equipment and tooling - Support aircraft integration and flight test, including installation and mounting, harnessing, instrumentation, and airframe modifications BASIC QUALIFICATIONS - Bachelor's degree or equivalent in mechanical engineering, aerospace engineering, manufacturing engineering, or a related field - 3+ months of hands-on engineering experience from internships, research labs, or student project teams - Comfortable with basic shop processes: torque and measurement tools, manual machining, adhesives, surface cleaning and finishing - Authorized to work in the United States PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE - You've designed, built, and tested something yourself (such as project teams, research, or personal projects) - CAD experience (Solidworks, Fusion, or similar) - CAM experience is a plus (MasterCAM, HSMWorks, Fusion CAM, etc) - Python or similar scripting experience for automation and analysis - Finite Element Analysis experience and understanding of core principles - Familiarity with structural and mechanical strength margins, mechanism designs - Exposure to environmental, material, or destructive testing - Interest in aviation, navigation, or GNSS; a pilot's license or flight test experience is a plus - Clear written communication and the discipline to document what you did and what you found ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS - Full-time, onsite in Kirkland, WA for a minimum of 12 consecutive weeks beginning June-July 2027 - Able to lift up to 25 lbs. and work in lab and hangar environments - Occasional travel for aircraft integration and flight test will be required COMPENSATION AND BENEFITS - $50.00/hour - $2500 relocation bonus - Paid holidays based on company holiday schedule - Direct mentorship from engineers who have shipped flight hardware at scale EEO STATEMENT Skyband Systems is an Equal Opportunity Employer employment with Skyband is governed on the basis of merit, competence and qualifications and will not be influenced in any manner by race, color, religion, gender, national origin/ethnicity, veteran status, disability status, age, sexual orientation, gender identity, marital status, mental or physical disability or any other legally protected status.

jobs.body: Internship – Mechanical Design Engineer Introduction to the job ASML US, including its affiliates and subsidiaries, bring together the most creative minds in science and technology to develop lithography machines that are key to producing faster, cheaper, more energy-efficient microchips. We design, develop, integrate, market and service these advanced machines, which enable our customers - the world’s leading chipmakers - to reduce the size and increase the functionality of their microchips, which in turn leads to smaller, more powerful consumer electronics. Our headquarters are in Veldhoven, Netherlands and we have 18 office locations around the United States including main offices in Chandler, Arizona, San Jose and San Diego, California, Wilton, Connecticut, and Hillsboro, Oregon. Roles and Responsibilities As a Summer Intern in Mechanical Design Engineering, you will participate in developing hardware solutions for the lithography system and/or associated tooling. You will work on the Level Sensor Lens sub-system involving precision mechanics and/or opto-mechanics. Precision machine design at ASML starts with understanding the functional requirements and deriving specifications. You will collaborate with design engineers and sub-system architects in a multidiscipline project team to develop concepts, perform engineering analysis, build and test prototypes, generate detailed CAD designs, create engineering drawings, partner with suppliers, and support system integration and testing. This position is located on-site in Wilton, CT. It requires onsite presence to attend in-person work-related events, trainings and meetings and to further ensure teamwork, collaboration and innovation. Must be available for 12 weeks for one of these sessions starting with the following dates: 6/2/2027 or 6/14/2027 Education and Experience Seeking an individual with a strong background in mechanical design and engineering. A background in mechanical design of mechatronics, precision design, or complex optical systems is desirable, as well as good complex mechanical system intuition. · Must be pursuing a degree in Mechanical Engineering, Physics, Optical Engineering, Optics, or related Engineering discipline and completed 2 years. Mechanical design exposure to kinematics, dynamics, material properties and behavior, and structural analysis. Experience with 3D solid modelling for design conceptualization and realization. Familiar with thermal and structural engineering fundamentals Basic experience with mechanical analytical techniques, including “first principle” engineering equations and Finite Element Analysis such as stress, strain, deformation, modal response, etc. Demonstrated ability to derive conclusions from analysis and make practical recommendations. Strong technical writing, communication and presentations skills. jobs.body: Anduril Industries is a defense technology company with a mission to transform U.S. and allied military capabilities with advanced technology. jobs.title: 2027 Internship Hardware Engineer, Machine Integration & Test
jobs.location: San Francisco, CA
jobs.body: JOIN THE TEAM BRINGING AUTONOMY TO THE BUILT WORLD At Bedrock, we're moving AI out of the lab and onto real job sites. Our team includes veterans who helped launch Waymo, scaled Segment to a $3.2B acquisition, and grew Uber Freight to $5B in revenue. We retrofit the heavy equipment contractors already own, starting with excavators, so experienced crews can safely take on more projects and deliver more of the critical infrastructure our society needs. In August 2026, Bedrock-equipped excavators began doing fully autonomous, paid work on live commercial job sites. We've more than doubled our customer base since 2025, and our machines now work with contractors across the South, Midwest, and Mid-Atlantic In October 2026, we raised a $600M Series C co-led by CapitalG and Emergence Capital, bringing our total funding to nearly $1B. We're using it to put more autonomous machines to work, build the field and operations teams behind every deployment, and expand into new machine types and job-site tasks. This is where algorithms meet steel-toed boots. You'll work alongside construction veterans and world-class engineers to solve physical-world problems that simulations can't touch. If you're ready to do meaningful work on hard problems, we'd love to have you join us. ABOUT THE ROLE & TEAM Getting an autonomy stack onto a 40-ton excavator is a hardware problem long before it's a software one — brackets, harnesses, enclosures, and interfaces that survive vibration, dust, and weather. As our Machine Integration intern, you'll design and build the physical interfaces between our system and the machine, plus the test stands we use to prove them out before they ever hit a jobsite. WHAT YOU'LL DO - Integrate sensors, compute, and wiring onto machines alongside the hardware team - Design brackets, enclosures, and interface hardware in CAD, then help fabricate and install them - Build test stands for validating subsystems on the bench instead of in the field - Run lab tests, capture data, and iterate on designs based on what breaks - Document build and install procedures so the next machine goes faster than the last - Close the loop with the field team on what's working and what isn't WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR REQUIRED - Currently pursuing a BS or MS in mechanical engineering, electrical engineering, robotics, or a related field — or bringing equivalent hands-on experience - CAD proficiency (SolidWorks, Onshape, or similar) - Genuine hands-on shop skills — you've built physical things, not just modeled them - Basic electrical competence: harnessing, connectors, multimeter, reading a schematic - Willingness to work on and around heavy equipment in PPE PREFERRED - Wiring harness design or manufacturing experience - Exposure to off-highway, automotive, or industrial equipment - Machining, welding, or 3D printing experience About This Internship This is a fixed-term, project-based internship designed strictly for students (undergraduate or graduate) seeking resume-building experience, hands-on skill development, or industry exposure rather than a direct career launchpad. Candidates will own discrete, short-term projects that can be fully completed within the internship timeframe. Please note that while exceptional interns may occasionally be considered if business needs align, opportunities for full-time conversion are highly limited." jobs.title: Mechanical Engineer, Atlas Hardware Co-Op
jobs.location: Waltham Office (POST), United States of America
jobs.body: We’re looking for an ambitious, self-starting, hands-on mechanical engineering co-op to join the team building Atlas, our humanoid robot. Our co-ops design, build, and test prototypes; they investigate weird problems; and they run experiments of all kinds. Boston Dynamics is a world leader in mobile robots, tackling some of the toughest robotics challenges. For years, our awe-inspiring viral videos on YouTube have shown the world what remarkably capable robots can do. Now we are quickly becoming a recognized leader in automation solutions for industrial applications , warehouse logistics and general purpose labor . What our co-ops do Work with mechanical, electrical, and software engineers to help design and support complex robotic systems Plan and perform verification and validation testing on prototype and production systems Design and develop new features for existing products Troubleshoot issues, perform root cause failure analysis and design/implement corrective actions to sustain existing products Design and release parts and assemblies using Catia CAD software Develop and maintain product support documentation including bills of material (BOMs) and detailed part/assembly drawings Support system design analyses, including reliability, DFM / DFA, cost-reduction What we want to see in our co-ops: A demonstrated passion for robotics and mechanical design Design experience w/ 3D CAD tools (CATIA, Solidworks, Onshape, &c.) That you’re hands-on. Our best co-ops can and want to build, assemble, and troubleshoot stuff That you can write well. A poorly written test plan, report, or spec robs the team of the knowledge we need to make our robots even better. That you’re working toward a BS or MS in Mechanical Engineering, Robotics, or similar Nice to Have: You know Python, LabView, MATLAB, or similar You know some FEA/CFD tools You have designed stuff for manufacturing (eg injection molding, castings, extrusions, sheet metal, weldments, &c.) You’re acquainted with ASME drafting standards including GD&T, (Y14.5-2018) You’ve worked systems comprising sensors, actuators and mechanisms Additional Info: Public transportation is accessible from Boston/Alewife. Boston Dynamics will never ask you to divulge your personal financial or account information as part of its recruiting process . We are interested in every qualified candidate who is eligible to work in the United States. However, we are not able to sponsor visas for this position. Boston Dynamics will never ask you to divulge your personal financial or account information as part of its recruiting process. The hourly pay range for this position is between $30-$35/ hour. jobs.location: Waltham Office (POST), United States of America
jobs.body: Boston Dynamics is a world leader in mobile robots, tackling some of the toughest robotics challenges. For years, our awe-inspiring viral videos on YouTube have shown the world what remarkably capable robots can do. We embody cutting-edge Artificial Intelligence in advanced robotics, quickly moving from the research lab into increasingly impactful roles across industrial spaces. The Systems Engineering, Integration, and Test (SEIT) Department of Boston Dynamics (BD) seeks a Systems Test Engineer Co-op to help verify and validate the most capable humanoid robot system in the world. This role provides hands-on technical support to a peer group of test engineers and technicians. The team will include mechanical, electrical, and software expertise. The Systems Test Engineer Co-op reports to the Verification, Validation, & Test Associate Director on the Atlas team and helps BD continue the development of the most capable full-body-manipulating mobile robots in the world. How you will make an impact: Work across electrical, mechanical, firmware, and technician teams to validate and integrate robot systems into test stands for reliability, verification, and software testing. Oversee and execute the integration of testing fixtures, including instrumentation, wiring, and configurations. Test and validate assemblies and firmware for critical components of our robot, such as actuators, grippers, power distribution boards, battery management systems, sensing boards, motor controllers, or compute boards. Contribute to the definition of our test system design and test process. Support system integration and test activities by contributing to test execution and debugging. Work alongside test engineers to develop and execute accelerated life reliability test specifications for actuators, batteries, structures, bushings, wirings, sensors, and the full system. Support failure analysis efforts for failures resulting from reliability testing. Required Skills & Experience: In progress Bachelor's or Master's degree in Mechanical Engineering, Electrical Engineering or a related field. Desirable Skills & Experience: Solid mechatronics fundamentals with hands-on experience designing, building, and testing PCBAs or subsystem test stands used for hardware and software validation. Experience using 3D Modeling SW or Altium (or similar EDA tools). Experience in the test and debugging of complex electromechanical systems. General experience in firmware, automation, and controls. Data analysis and visualization. Software tools including: Python, C++, Jama, Jira, Google Suite, Matlab, Arena, Altium, Solidworks, Catia v6, Raspberry Pi, Arduino.

Key Responsibilities Assist in designing fluid and process systems, including piping, valves, pumps, compressors, and heat exchangers Support definition of process equipment specifications, performance criteria, and operating conditions Contribute to prototype setup and testing activities for iterative system design and validation Help prepare technical documentation to support system layout, fabrication, installation, and operation Collaborate with engineers on analyses to evaluate performance and inform design refinements Document results and methods in a clear and professional manner for use across design and regulatory teams Required Qualifications Working toward a bachelor’s or master’s degree in Mechanical Engineering, Chemical Engineering, Nuclear Engineering, or a related discipline Background in thermodynamics, fluid mechanics, and heat transfer through coursework or projects Familiarity with process or system modeling tools (e.g., MATLAB, Python, Aspen, or similar) Strong problem-solving skills with attention to detail Ability to clearly communicate technical findings through reports or presentations Bonus Qualifications Experience with lab work, prototyping, or experimental systems Exposure to piping and instrumentation diagrams (P&IDs) or process design coursework Familiarity with pumps, heat exchangers, or thermal-fluid systems from research or internships Prototyping/Manufacturing Intern The prototyping engineering intern will be a part of the prototyping and visualization team. This role is ideal for someone looking to grow their operational skill set in core business operational functions and is passionate about contributing to initiatives that drive efficiency while supporting key compliance functions across the organization. Key Responsibilities Assist with day-to-day business operations, including process documentation, workflow optimization, and project coordination. Collect, organize, and analyze operational and financial data to generate insights and support decision-making. Prepare reports, presentations, and dashboards for internal stakeholders. Collaborate with cross-functional teams (finance, HR, marketing, product, etc.) to support operational initiatives. Conduct research on industry trends, competitors, and best practices to support strategic planning. Identify and recommend opportunities for process improvements and increased efficiency. Strong analytical, organizational, and problem-solving skills. Proficiency in Microsoft Office Suite (Excel, PowerPoint, Word) or Google Workspace. Excellent written and verbal communication skills. Ability to work independently and collaboratively in a fast-paced environment. Attention to detail and eagerness to learn. Competencies We are looking for interns that are: Passionate about making advanced fission a reality Willing and able to learn quickly Eager to work on a dynamic team, receive constructive feedback, and grow with us Willing to think differently and do things in new ways Comfortable in a fast-paced, highly iterative startup environment Excited to think creatively, critically, and reflectively about the problems they are solving, while not leaning only on what has been done before Willing to propose novel and creative solutions to technical problems An excellent writer who can write in modern active voice, so make your cover letter compelling and write it well! Able to communicate technical content and results verbally Who you are: A startup person : You aren't driven by titles or hierarchy, and prefer efficiency to excess process. You don't need or expect to have a lot of guidance but you enjoy working in a fast-paced team. If you prefer the culture and feel of a large organization, that is great, but you likely won’t enjoy working with us! There is plenty of important work and plenty of good opportunities with organizations like that. Motivated : You are self-motivated. You bring an enthusiasm to the team, and imbue a sense of passion that goes beyond clocking in and clocking out. This isn’t about a fake or arbitrary “pieces of flair” mentality or lack of work-life balance! It is about being a part of the vision and feeling a part of reaching team goals. A team-player : Oklo genuinely is a team. We aren’t about taking credit for ourselves, and we aren’t about pushing blame to others. We do incredible things because we work as a team. An excellent communicator : We need a person who is not only technically competent but also a clear and upbeat communicator. Creative : Being creative means that when things fall outside clear scopes or processes or problems arise without clear solutions, you are able to identify it as well as invent ways to solve a problem or fill a need without micromanagement. The successful person in this job will not only be creative, but also enjoy being creative and solving open-ended problems which may change day-by-day. Detail-oriented : This focus is a big part of excellence, consistency, and quality. Excellent grammar and spelling matter for both good communication as well as the image of the company that we put forward. About Oklo's Intern compensation: Oklo offers housing assistance, $35 - $44 per hour (compensation is determined based on education, skills, and experience), 1-on-1 mentorship, hands-on training, and the opportunity to engage in fun team-building activities as well as interactive workshops, enhancing both professional and personal growth. Due to the nature of Oklo's work, only U.S. citizens can be considered for these positions. About Oklo Inc.: Oklo Inc. is developing fast fission power plants to deliver clean, reliable, and affordable energy at scale; establishing a domestic supply chain for critical radioisotopes; and advancing nuclear fuel recycling to convert nuclear waste into clean energy. Oklo was the first to receive a site use permit from the U.S. Department of Energy for a commercial advanced fission plant, was awarded fuel material from Idaho National Laboratory, and submitted the first custom combined license application for an advanced reactor to the U.S. Nuclear Regulatory Commission. Oklo is also developing advanced fuel recycling technologies in collaboration with the U.S. Department of Energy and U.S. National Laboratories. #CHOP: Oklo’s Values Collaboration : We go further, together. We bring diverse perspectives, listen actively, and build trust through transparency and respect. We work across disciplines, sharing ownership to turn complex challenges into shared successes. Humility : We are team players who act for the good of the company and for the world. We are focused on our mission, not personal recognition. Ownership : We take pride in what we do and how we do it. We are proactive in finding solutions and see tasks through to completion. We are committed to delivering on our promises to provide clean, reliable, and affordable energy. Pathfinding : We chart new ground where no path exists by approaching challenges with curiosity, courage, and creativity while navigating ambiguity. Candidates should be aware that employment may be contingent upon successful completion of a drug screening, and employees may be subject to drug testing at any time in accordance with company policy and applicable laws. Recruitment Fraud Disclaimer Oklo is aware of recent recruitment fraud attempts targeting job seekers. Please be cautious of anyone claiming to represent Oklo who does not contact you from an official Oklo email address. All legitimate communications from our recruiting team— including application updates, interview requests, and job offers — will come exclusively from an @oklo.com email. Oklo will never ask for sensitive personal information, payments, or account credentials during the hiring process. If you receive suspicious outreach or have concerns about the authenticity of any communication claiming to be from Oklo, please contact us through the official channels listed on our website.

jobs.body: Skydio is the leading US drone company and the world leader in autonomous flight, the key technology for the future of drones and aerial mobility. The Skydio team combines deep expertise in artificial intelligence, best-in-class hardware and software product development, operational excellence, and customer obsession to empower a broader, more diverse audience of drone users, from utility inspectors https://www.skydio.com/solutions/energy-and-utilities to first responders https://www.skydio.com/solutions/public-safety, soldiers in battlefield scenarios https://www.skydio.com/solutions/national-security/tactical-isr, and beyond https://www.skydio.com/solutions. About the role: We are seeking Summer 2027 interns or Co-ops for our Hardware Test & Reliability Team! Autonomous systems are a new breed of product that bring together electronics hardware and real-time AI software. The complexity of the systems combined with the fact they can move freely in the real world, makes the development and reliability testing strategy a key element of delivering a great product. We are seeking a driven and cross-functional engineering intern to help the development and execution of test plans and testing infrastructure to enable rapid design iteration and robust product validation for state-of-the-art autonomous flying machines servicing a broad range of consumer and commercial use cases. How you’ll make an impact: - Own the design and implementation of hardware and software systems to execute comprehensive performance and reliability validation for products performing in a wide array of use cases - Analyze data, calculate statistics, and carefully document results to explain trends and inform impactful design improvements - Perform failure analysis to identify root cause and help develop process/design mitigations to resolve system issues, collaborating with mechanical, electrical, software, manufacturing, and quality engineering teams - Participate in design reviews and provide key design for reliability inputs to mitigate risks at every stage of the product development lifecycle What makes you a good fit: - A sense of how to test, how not to test, and how to find vulnerabilities in processes and design - A systematic approach to problem solving, and a knack for rapidly identifying issues within electro-mechanical systems; strong desire to drive failure analyses to true root cause - Enthusiastic tendencies toward diving in and applying first principles to engineer creative solutions to complex problems - Experience with Python or other programming languages for test automation, data analysis and visualization - Strong desire to learn and contribute across multiple domains within a dynamic and growing organization - Excellent project management, written & verbal communication and cross-functional teamwork skills - Familiarity with testing equipment and basic knowledge of stress, environmental, and accelerated life testing methods to assess product durability and reliability. Compensation Range: The hourly rate for this position is $47/hr for Undergrad, $53/hr for Graduate students, and $58 for PhD students*. Compensation will vary based on factors, including skill level, proficiencies, transferable knowledge, and experience. *For some positions the pay may be dependent upon the individual's regional location. #LI-ZD1 At Skydio we believe that diversity drives innovation. We have created a multidisciplinary environment that embraces the power of diverse perspectives to create elegant solutions for complex problems. We are committed to growing our network of people, programs, and resources to nurture an inclusive culture. Qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, disability, protected veteran status, or other characteristics protected by federal, state or local anti-discrimination laws. To learn more about E-Verify, including your rights and responsibilities, please visit https://www.e-verify.gov/

jobs.title: Hardware Reliability Intern (Summer 2027)
jobs.location: Somerville, MA
jobs.body: Do you want to change how the world creates? At Formlabs, we’re building the tools that make it possible for anyone to bring their ideas to life, from cutting-edge products to life-saving medical devices. Our 3D printing technology powers innovation at more than 50,000 industry leaders worldwide, including Apple, Google, Tesla, New Balance, and NASA. Together, we’re helping everyone design, prototype, and manufacture faster than ever before. We’re a team of hands-on builders, engineers, and innovators reinventing how the world makes physical things. If you’re ready to shape the future of fabrication, come build it with us. We’re looking for a R&D Test Engineer who will play a key role in running tests and partner closely with the engineers to perform systemized tests on 3d printers and report your findings. The output of this work will determine future features and settings for our 3d printers. The Hardware Reliability Engineering team ensures that Formlabs products in development are reliable and ready to ship, as well as triaging reliability issues of current products already in the field. We work closely with design teams of all disciplines to find product flaws as fast as possible and then work on redesigns to make more robust systems. Are you a cross-functional engineer that is passionate about creating robust products? We want you as a Hardware Test Engineering Intern . Internship Term: Summer (May/June - August) Commitment: Full-time Location: Onsite in Somerville, MA Application Materials : A portfolio of your previous engineering work/projects is recommended. View our Portfolio FAQ ! The Job Develop, execute, and manage system, subsystem, and component level validation test plans to ensure products meet design and reliability requirements. Work with other teams to ensure a thorough system is completed. Perform hands-on and data-driven root cause analysis to triage field failures and electromechanical systems, utilizing common problem-solving methodologies and a "physics of failure" approach. Design, build, and implement automated testing equipment for subsystem characterization and reliability/environmental testing Collaborate with the design team throughout product development to perform risk assessments, manage continuous testing, and contribute to design reviews You Are well versed with complex electromechanical systems and are passionate about understanding what it takes to make them work reliably Have experience developing full system test plans and know how to execute them in fast-paced product development timelines Have experience with testing a wide range of sensors, actuators, and mechanical components Can prototype and run your own tests, from experimental setup to hardware and software implementation Bonus skills: Familiarity with Linux systems and scripting in various languages (Python preferred) Familiarity with HALT and HASS testing Intern Benefits & Perks: Flexible Out of Office Plan – take time when you need it Ample on-site parking & pre-tax commuter benefits Catered on-site lunches (3x per week), snacks, beverages, & treats Cohort-based social and professional development experience for interns Many opt-in culture events across our diverse community And of course… unlimited 3D prints We are an equal opportunity employer and value diversity at our company. We do not discriminate on the basis of race, religion, color, national origin, gender, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, or disability status. Even if you don't check every box, but see yourself contributing, please apply. Help us build an inclusive community that will change the face of 3D printing. Compensation: Interns at Formlabs are paid on a bi-weekly pay schedule. The pay range for this role will depend on your skills, qualifications, experience, location and expected impact on the organization. This is a salaried role, so you will always be paid based on the assumed 40 hours per week as a full-time intern. This position does not offer housing or relocation assistance. The weekly pay range for this role is: $1,575 — $1,950 USD

Our programs provide real-world experience, technical skills, and professional development opportunities, empowering you to make a meaningful impact and achieve your career goals. Join us for our U.S. 2027 summer intern class ! Maximize Your Opportunities: Our internship hiring model routes candidates from this application into multiple project specific roles. Steps: Log Into Your Eightfold Candidate Home Account Hover Over The "Profile" Dropdown Open Settings Edit "Profile Visibility" Role Overview As a Qualcomm Mechanical Engineering Intern , you’ll have the opportunity to push the boundaries of what exists and help establish the new standards for tomorrow. You will work as an equal contributor on a team of leading engineers to design, simulate, and test mechanical and thermal systems that support Qualcomm’s advanced semiconductor technologies. Projects may span IC packaging, chip/package co-design, thermal modeling, signal and power integrity, and next-generation cooling solutions. This internship supports the Mechanical Engineering track.
