jobs.title: Fluid Component Intern Summer 2027
jobs.location: Long Beach, CA
jobs.body: ABOUT ROCKET LAB Rocket Lab is the end-to-end space company building rockets, spacecraft, and critical subsystems that keep the world connected, protected, expand humanity’s reach to the Moon, Mars, and beyond. We move fast, build real hardware for meaningful missions, and make the impossible routine. Come shape the future with us. As a Fluid Component Intern based at Rocket Lab’s site in Long Beach, California, you will have the opportunity to support the Components team in working to design second generation devices to achieve the next level of maturity and reliability for future missions. The Fluid Components team designs and manufactures valves and actuators which manage fluid handling on our oxidizer-rich staged combustion engine and medium-lift launch vehicle. WHAT YOU’LL GET TO DO As an intern, you will work closely with your mentor and other employees within the department to apply your knowledge and grow your skills both technically and professionally Work with a fast-paced group of professionals to apply engineering and industry concepts to solve real challenges Attend frequent 1:1’s with mentors and supervisors to facilitate success and learning while providing progress updates Enjoy tech talks and network with other interns and employees through social and professional events YOU’LL BRING THESE QUALIFICATIONS Ideal candidates will thrive in ambiguity and are excited to work in small, high-performing teams that are focused on continued learning and growth. Success in this position will be measured by the knowledge and experience you bring to the role, your ability to lead development projects without supervision, and your ability to successfully collaborate across teams to deliver results. Must be enrolled in a bachelor’s, master's or doctorate degree program in Aerospace, Aeronautical, Astronautical or Mechanical Engineering discipline and have at least one semester of school remaining post internship GPA of 3.0 or above 3+ months of applied engineering experience (internship, laboratory, and personal/team project experience is applicable) THESE QUALIFICATIONS WOULD BE NICE TO HAVE GPA of 3.5 or above 6+ months of applied engineering experience (internship, laboratory, and personal/team project experience is applicable) Computer-aided design and manufacturing (CAD/ CAM) CNC Experience 3D printing experience Python experience Geometric Dimensioning & Tolerancing (GD&T) experience Finite Element Analysis (FEA) experience Lathe experience Knowledge of fluid dynamics, thermodynamics, materials science or physics ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS Able to work full-time, on-site for a minimum of 12 consecutive weeks beginning May or June 2027 COMPENSATION AND OTHER BENEFITS Pay Range CA: $28.00 USD Hourly You may be eligible for a stipend to subsidize relocation costs Level and base salary will be determined on a case-by-case basis and may vary based on the following considerations: job-related knowledge and skills, education, and experience. Base salary is just one component of our total rewards package at Rocket Lab. Our comprehensive benefits package includes our industry-leading Employee Stock Purchase Program (with a 15% discount on company stock), top-tier medical plans (HMO, PPO, and a zero cost HDHP option with a significant HSA company contribution), dental and vision coverage, paid vacation and sick time, 11 paid holidays, flexible spending and dependent care accounts, paid parental leave, disability and life insurance, and a 401(k) retirement plan with company match. Additional perks include subsidized EV charging, onsite fitness centers (where available), discounted gym memberships, complimentary snacks and beverages, 50% employee discount on our popular merch store, and a variety of other employee discounts. Eligibility for benefits may vary based on employment status, please check with your recruiter for a comprehensive list of the benefits available for this role. Benefit programs are subject to change at the company’s discretion. Hourly Pay Range (CA Only) $28 — $28 USD WHAT TO EXPECT We’re on a mission to unlock the potential of space to improve life on Earth, but that’s not an easy task. It takes hard work, determination, relentless innovation, teamwork, grit, and an unwavering commitment to achieving what others often deem impossible. Our people out-think, out-work, and out-pace. We pride ourselves on having each other’s backs, checking our egos at the door, and rolling up our sleeves on all tasks big and small. We thrive under pressure, work to tight deadlines, and our focus is always on how we can deliver, rather than dwelling on the challenges that stand in the way. jobs.body: Work Flexibility: Onsite What You Get Out of the Internship ​​ At Stryker, we believe that developing the next generation of talent is just as important as developing life-changing medical technologies. As an intern, you won’t just observe — you’ll contribute to meaningful projects, gain exposure to leaders who will mentor you, and experience a culture of innovation and teamwork that is shaping the future of healthcare. As an intern, you will: ​ ​ Apply classroom knowledge and gain experience in a fast-paced and growing industry setting​ Implement new ideas, be constantly challenged, and develop your skills​ Network with key/high-level stakeholders and leaders of the business​ Be a part of an innovative team and culture​ Experience documenting complex processes and presenting them in a clear format Who we want ​​ Challengers. People who seek out the hard projects and work to find just the right solutions.​ Teammates. Partners who listen to ideas, share thoughts and work together to move the business forward.​ Charismatic networkers. Relationship-savvy people who intentionally make connections with both internal partners and external contacts.​ Strategic thinkers. Interns who propose innovative ideas and consistently exceed their performance objectives.​ Customer-oriented achievers. Individuals with an unparalleled work ethic and customer-focused attitude who bring value to their partnerships.​ Game changers. Persistent interns who will stop at nothing to live out Stryker’s mission to make healthcare better. Opportunities Available ​ ​As a Mechanical Engineering intern at Stryker, you will be placed in one of the following teams: Research & Development New Product Development R&D interns in New Product Development work with cross-functional teams to identify the needs and the goals of future products. They research new technologies, customer expectations, business requirements and regulations. They may work with a variety of tools, including CAD, FEA, and our Test Labs to develop new product concepts. These interns utilize their technical education to design new products and drive them from concept to production. Product Engineering R&D interns in Product Engineering work with cross-functional teams to identify the greatest needs for improvements on current products. They research new technologies, customer feedback, and product performance data to make our products better for Stryker and for our customers. Product Engineering interns work with a variety of tools, including CAD, FEA, Test Labs, and root cause analysis methods. These interns utilize their technical education to improve the safety and efficacy of our existing products. Test Lab Test interns partner closely with Test Engineers and R&D to experiment with early prototypes and vet out product designs throughout the design process. What this really means is that we get to be the Mythbusters of our division. You think your design can last the entire expected service life? We put it to the test. Just like the show, we quickly design and build fixtures to simulate real life situations. In addition to these experiments, we are ultimately responsible for design verification – the quantitative testing of the technical specifications of the product. A team’s experience ranges from 2 to over 15 years with technical specialties ranging from sterilization, mechanical, electrical, software, and optics. If you’re the type of person that has the magic ability to break things – we want you! Majors Targeted: Biomedical Engineering, or related majors What You Need ​​ Currently pursuing a Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in a related field; must remain enrolled in a degree-seeking program after the internship.​ Cumulative 3.0 GPA or above (verified at time of hire) Must be legally authorized to work in the U.S. and not require employment-based sponsorship now or in the future.​ Strong written and verbal communication skills, with proven ability to collaborate and build relationships Demonstrated leadership, problem-solving, and organizational skills with the ability to manage multiple priorities Proficiency in Microsoft Office (Excel, Word, PowerPoint) and eagerness to learn in a dynamic environment. $20 min hourly wage – $35 max hourly wage, sign-on bonus, 11 paid holidays annually, and either paid corporate housing or a living stipend, dependent upon hiring location Travel Percentage: None Stryker Corporation is an equal opportunity employer. Qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, ethnicity, color, religion, sex, gender identity, sexual orientation, national origin, disability, or protected veteran status. Stryker is an EO employer – M/F/Veteran/Disability. However, employees who have access to the compensation information of other employees or applicants as a part of their essential job functions cannot disclose the pay of other employees or applicants to individuals who do not otherwise have access to compensation information, unless the disclosure is (a) in response to a formal complaint or charge, (b) in furtherance of an investigation, proceeding, hearing, or action, including an investigation conducted by the employer, or (c) consistent with the contractor’s legal duty to furnish information.

jobs.body: Anduril Industries is a defense technology company with a mission to transform U.S. and allied military capabilities with advanced technology. By bringing the expertise, technology, and business model of the 21st century’s most innovative companies to the defense industry, Anduril is changing how military systems are designed, built and sold. Anduril’s family of systems is powered by Lattice OS, an AI-powered operating system that turns thousands of data streams into a realtime, 3D command and control center. As the world enters an era of strategic competition, Anduril is committed to bringing cutting-edge autonomy, AI, computer vision, sensor fusion, and networking technology to the military in months, not years. WHAT YOU’LL DO Own a portion of the production quality support process for a certain product or set of products. Protecting Yourself from Recruitment Scams Anduril is committed to maintaining the integrity of our Talent acquisition process and the security of our candidates. To ensure your safety and help you navigate your job search with confidence, please keep the following critical points in mind: No Financial Requests: Anduril will never solicit payment or demand personal financial details (such as banking information, credit card numbers, or social security numbers) at any stage of our hiring process. Always confirm the sender's email domain is @anduril.com before providing any personal information or clicking on links. What to Do If You Suspect Fraud: Should you encounter any questionable or fraudulent outreach claiming to be from Anduril, please report it immediately to contact@anduril.com . Students gain hands-on exposure , work on real projects , and make meaningful contributions . Throughout the program, co-ops build technical skills , strengthen problem-solving abilities , and gain real-world experience that enhances both their academic learning and future career opportunities.- About the Role As a Manufacturing Test Development Engineer Co-op , you will gain hands-on experience designing, developing, and supporting test equipment used in a fast-paced manufacturing environment. You will work closely with cross-functional teams to help ensure products meet quality, performance, and reliability standards. This role provides exposure to real-world engineering challenges, including the design, development, and validation of electrical and mechanical test solutions, fixture design, and hardware-level debugging of test systems. Through this experience, you will develop practical engineering skills, learn how testing integrates into large-scale manufacturing, and contribute directly to improving efficiency and product quality. Familiarity with modeling software such as SolidWorks/Creo or AutoCAD Familiarity with schematic and PCB design tools such as Altium, KiCad, QElectroTech Familiarity with fabrication tools such as calipers, hand tools, 3d printing, etc. Familiarity with measurement tools and equipment such as DMM’s, Oscilloscopes, Data acquisition systems (DAQ), etc. Experience with project management tools such as Gantt charts, Microsoft Project/Planner, etc. Why Choose Axcelis for Your Co-op? jobs.title: Undergraduate Engineering Intern - Mechanical Design
jobs.location: Rochester, MN, United States
jobs.body: This undergraduate internship is a full-time position Summer-Fall 2027 (May or June through December) on site in Rochester, Minnesota. The Mechanical Engineering Design intern will join the Mechanical Development Unit within the Division of Engineering (DOE). This unit is one of several specialized groups within DOE, similar to the Software and Electronics development units. The Mechanical Development Unit leverages mechanical engineering expertise as part of DOE's multidisciplinary approach to developing unique devices and systems for Mayo Clinic providers and researchers. The candidate will be assigned to projects alongside other Mechanical Engineers as well as other engineering disciplines. Some projects only require Mechanical Engineers, while other projects require multiple engineering disciplines. Project work for this candidate will include computer-aided design (CAD) work using SolidWorks, prototype development with both traditional and additive manufacturing technologies, verification testing, and engineering documentation. The candidate will be assigned one or more members to provide work direction and guidance on projects. The ideal candidate will have a strong understanding of mechanical engineering principles, a working knowledge of SolidWorks, experience with design for manufacturing, and excellent written and verbal communication skills. The primary purpose of the Undergraduate Engineer Internship is to provide the student with relevant engineering experiences. One or more mentors will be assigned to the intern to provide instruction, guidance and to assess performance. The intern is responsible for learning the procedures and processes of the Division of Engineering and the assigned work unit. In addition, the intern will be given selected engineering work assignments to reinforce the learning experience and to provide benefit to the work unit. The engineering assignments may include designing components, developing a project strategy, gathering user needs, requirements and specifications, evaluating commercial components, assembling prototype systems, performing design verification and design validation, troubleshooting, and participating in design reviews. All assignments are within the context of the Division of Engineering Quality Management System (including safety risk management) and are performed in a multi-disciplinary development environment. The intern will be responsible for completing all internship-related assignments and reports for both Mayo and the participating educational facility (if applicable). The incumbent must be enrolled in an engineering, management information systems, or other technology-related degree program from an accredited college or university and have completed a minimum of four semesters – or the equivalent – of instruction toward their degree. ***To be considered for this position please attach the following to your application: 3.3 GPA or higher Current Transcript Resume or CV Applicants are strongly encouraged to include a Cover Letter Applicants are strongly encouraged to include current portfolio of sample work/writing

jobs.title: Hardware Test Intern (Summer 2027)
jobs.location: South San Francisco, California, USA
jobs.body: About Zipline Zipline is the world’s largest and most experienced drone delivery service. We are on a mission to serve all humans equally by ensuring access to food, medicine and essential goods anytime, anywhere. We design, build, and operate the world’s largest autonomous logistics system, delivering critical supplies quickly and reliably. Today, Zipline operates on four continents, makes a delivery somewhere in the world every 30 seconds, and has completed millions of deliveries to date, including blood, vaccines, medical supplies, food, and retail products. Our customers include the world’s largest and most prominent healthcare systems, governments, retailers, restaurants and global businesses who rely on us to save lives, reduce emissions, increase economic opportunity, and provide delivery from point A to point B as fast as possible. The drone is only 15% of what we’ve built to enable seamless, reliable, global operations. Our system strengthens supply chains, reduces congestion, and gives people time back. With more than 140 million commercial autonomous miles safely flown, Zipline is redefining access to healthcare, consumer products, and food across the globe. We operate at a global scale and are looking for practical problem solvers who thrive on real-world challenges and rapid growth. Our team is motivated by building systems that have a direct, meaningful impact on people’s lives and by scaling the future of logistics. We are seeking people who sculpt from first principles, enjoy facing adversity, and can do the impossible at record breaking speeds. About the Hardware Test Team The Hardware Test Team plays a critical role in ensuring the performance, reliability, and safety of the systems that power Zipline’s life-saving delivery drones. As a cross-functional group supporting multiple hardware engineering domains, we design and execute rigorous testing strategies across avionics, power systems, mechanical assemblies, sensors, and other mission-critical components. Operating at the intersection of hardware and software, we validate integrated systems under real-world and simulated conditions to ensure our products perform flawlessly in some of the most demanding environments on Earth. Our work directly advances Zipline’s mission to provide fast, dependable access to essential medical and commercial supplies around the globe. The Role In developing a test asset, you will gain a deep understanding of the system you are working on—whether that includes embedded electronics, avionics, sensing systems, power distribution, mechanical actuation, or full subsystem integrations. Building these test assets often involves designing and constructing mechatronic systems as well as developing complex automation scripts that coordinate sensors, actuators, and instrumentation with operator safety in mind. You will own your test asset end-to-end: from early concept and system definition, to implementation, data collection, analysis, and ultimately the recommendations that inform engineering decisions. If you are excited by hands-on engineering, solving ambiguous technical problems, and building tools that raise the bar for hardware quality, this role is for you. What You'll Do Collaborate with cross-functional engineering teams to define clear component and tester requirements Validate the design and assembly of components ranging from circuit boards to large mechanical or electromechanical assemblies Streamline testing, data collection, analysis, and reporting Gain deep expertise in the components or systems under test to understand their expected behavior under a variety of operating conditions Own a test asset through its entire lifecycle—from planning and implementation to system validation, troubleshooting, and analysis of results What You'll Bring Ability to interpret datasheets and write basic drivers for new components Understanding of fundamental electrical and/or mechanical engineering principles Experience working with common electrical test equipment (multimeters, oscilloscopes, power supplies, etc.) Nice to have: Experience programming in Python, with foundational knowledge of embedded C; Experience developing software that interfaces directly with hardware and instrumentation What Else You Should Know Our internships are full-time positions, in-person at our South San Francisco or Dallas office. We will host our Summer 2027 interns from May/June to August/September. The hourly rate for this internship is $40 per hour. Additional benefits may include relocation support, a housing stipend, overtime pay, paid sick time, and other benefits, where applicable and subject to local requirements. Candidates are limited to three (3) applications within a 30-day period. Zipline is an equal opportunity employer and prohibits discrimination and harassment of any type without regard to race, color, religion, age, sex, national origin, disability status, genetics, protected veteran status, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, or any other characteristic protected by federal, state or local laws or our own sensibilities. Zipline is also committed to providing reasonable accommodations to individuals with disabilities. Please let your point of contact at Zipline know if you require any accommodations throughout your interview process. Voluntary Self-Identification For government reporting purposes, we ask candidates to respond to the below self-identification survey. Completion of the form is entirely voluntary. Whatever your decision, it will not be considered in the hiring process or thereafter. Any information that you do provide will be recorded and maintained in a confidential file. As set forth in Zipline ’s Equal Employment Opportunity policy, we do not discriminate on the basis of any protected group status under any applicable law.

jobs.title: Robotics Engineering Intern
jobs.location: Sunnyvale, CA, us
jobs.body: It started with a simple idea: what if surgery could be less invasive and recovery less painful? Nearly 30 years later, that question still fuels everything we do at Intuitive . As a global leader in robotic-assisted surgery and minimally invasive care , our technologies—like the da Vinci surgical system and Ion —have transformed how care is delivered for millions of patients worldwide. We’re a team of engineers, clinicians, and innovators united by one purpose: to make surgery smarter, safer, and more human. Every day, our work helps care teams perform with greater precision and patients recover faster, improving outcomes around the world. The problems we solve demand creativity, rigor, and collaboration. The work is challenging, but deeply meaningful—because every improvement we make has the potential to change a life. If you’re ready to contribute to something bigger than yourself and help transform the future of healthcare , you’ll find your purpose here. Primary Function of Position The Robotics Engineering Intern will report to future forward research lad and contribute to creating a sim-to-real-to-sim platform for the Intuitive surgical robot system. The intern will enable rapid prototyping and de-risking of new controller architectures, particularly semi-supervised and supervised autonomous systems that are data-hungry and require extensive validation. Key functions include developing tools that systematically transfer and test controllers from simulation to robot hardware, building virtual models of the surgical field for simulation interaction, and closing the loop between simulation and reality to accelerate development and evaluation of autonomous controllers. Essential Job Duties Implement novel control architectures in high-level (e.g., MATLAB) and low-level (e.g., embedded C++) targets. Systematically test controller performance in simulation and on robot hardware. Create simulation environments that integrate constrained rigid-body dynamics (e.g., MuJoCo) and realistic texture and lighting (e.g., Isaac Sim). Synthesize simulated environments from video data, including geometry, texture, and inferred stiffness. Execute closed-loop round-trip tests: train a controller in simulation, test it experimentally, and use experimental data to construct new simulation environments. Required Skills and Experience University Hiring Program Eligibility Requirements: University Enrollment: Must be currently enrolled in and returning to an accredited degree-seeking academic program after the internship. Internship Work Period: Must be available to work full-time (approximately 40 hours per week) during a 10-12 week period starting May or June. Specific start dates are shared during the recruiting process. Required Education and Training Current enrollment in a Robotics, Electrical Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Computer Science, or related degree-seeking program at the Master's or Doctorate level. Working Conditions None. Preferred Skills and Experience Experience with MATLAB and/or Python for control system design and analysis. Experience with MuJoCo or similar constrained rigid-body dynamics simulators. Experience with sim-to-real transfer methods for robotic systems. Familiarity with NVIDIA Isaac Sim or similar platforms for realistic rendering and simulation. Familiarity with embedded C++ for low-level controller implementation. Awareness of video-based 3D reconstruction and environment synthesis techniques. Awareness of autonomous or semi-autonomous control architectures. This goal will be accomplished through the commercialization of the fluoride-salt-cooled, high-temperature reactor (FHR) that can be deployed with robust safety, affordable costs, and flexible operation to accommodate the expansion of variable renewables. Please note: This is a pipeline posting for anticipated Summer 2027 internship opportunities. jobs.title: Co-op - Test and Measurement Facility Engineer (Internship)
jobs.location: Wilton, CT, USA, United States of America
jobs.body: Introduction to the job ASML US brings together the most creative minds in science and technology to develop lithography machines that are key to producing faster, cheaper, more energy-efficient microchips. We design, develop, integrate, market and service these advanced machines, which enable our customers - the world’s leading chipmakers - to reduce the size and increase the functionality of their microchips, which in turn leads to smaller, more powerful consumer electronics. Our headquarters are in Veldhoven, the Netherlands, and we have 18 office locations around the United States including main offices in Chandler, Arizona, San Jose and San Diego, California, Wilton, Connecticut, and Hillsboro, Oregon. Role and responsibilities Through exposure to advanced test and measurement techniques, you will design and develop test systems and/or applications to support feasibility, robustness, reliability or lifetime testing of advanced semiconductor lithography mechatronic parts and modules. As a Co-op in the Test and Measurement Facility (TMF) within the Service and Enablers Department, you will participate in the following: Develop portions of the lithography system and/or associated tooling and test equipment. You will work on sub-systems involving robotics, mechatronics, precision mechanics and/or opto-mechanics You will need to consider engineering specifications and performance, lifetime, failure modes, root cause analysis, statistical analysis, reliability predictions, 6 sigma techniques, measurement system capability, etc. You will collaborate with system architects and engineers in a multidiscipline project team to develop concepts, perform engineering analysis, build and test prototypes, partner with suppliers, analyze data and support system integration and test This position is located on-site in Wilton, CT. It requires onsite presence to attend in-person work-related events, trainings and meetings and to further ensure teamwork, collaboration and innovation. Must be available for 6 to 9 months Education and experience Pursuing a Bachelor's, Master’s or PhD Degree in Mechatronics, Mechanical Engineering, Electrical Engineering or Machine Controls with a minimum 2 years completed (Must be a current student and pursuing a degree) Prior use of LabVIEW preferred Prior use of CAD software (Siemens NX) preferred Prior use of measurement equipment, such as but not limited to the following: Accelerometers Data Acquisition systems National Instruments equipment Oscilloscopes Multimeters Hand tools Skills Working at the cutting edge of tech, you will always have new challenges and new problems to solve – and working together is the only way do that. You will not work in a silo. Instead, you will be part of a creative, dynamic work environment where you will collaborate with supportive colleagues. There is always space for creative and unique points of view. You will have the flexibility and trust to choose how best to tackle tasks and solve problems. To thrive in this job, you will need the following skills: Hands-on attitude Capability to interface with multidisciplinary groups including senior leadership High energy self-motivated team player with strong desire to learn Customer oriented and willing to work with high level problem solvers on a daily basis Possess strong leadership and ownership characteristics with commitment to achieve results on time Other information Co-Ops typically work at ASML for a semester and a summer, 8 months total This position is located on-site in Wilton, Connecticut. It requires onsite presence to attend in-person work-related events, trainings and meetings and to further ensure teamwork, collaboration and innovation While performing the duties of this job, the employee routinely is required to sit; walk; talk; hear; use hands to keyboard, finger, handle, and feel; stoop, kneel, crouch, twist, reach, and stretch The employee is occasionally required to move around the campus The employee may occasionally lift and/or move up to 20 pounds May require travel dependent on company needs Specific vision abilities required by this job include close vision, color vision, peripheral vision, depth perception and ability to adjust focus Can work under deadlines The environment generally is moderate in temperature and noise level Must be able to read and interpret data, information, and documents Can observe and respond to people and situations and interact with others encountered in the course of work Can learn and apply new information or skills The current base hourly range for this role is currently: $18.00 to $48.00 per hour Pay scales are determined by role, level, location and alignment with market data. jobs.body: Worker Type Supplemental Job Description Summer Internship Program Our paid Summer Internship Program is designed to provide students with an immersive, hands-on experience within the aerospace and defense industry. This is a 12-week, onsite program intended for highly motivated and passionate students who are currently enrolled in college or are recent graduates. Our program has been recognized by Yello and WayUp as one of the Top 100 Internship Programs in the United States for multiple years. Under the guidance of experienced manufacturing engineers, you will assist in analyzing production processes and data, help optimize manufacturing workflows, and contribute to continuous improvement initiatives using Lean Manufacturing and Six Sigma principles. jobs.title: Propulsion Engineering Intern
jobs.location: San Francisco
jobs.body: ABOUT US: Astro Mechanica is a vertically integrated aerospace company developing a scalable technology platform to power critical infrastructure, mission operations, and the future of flight. We apply aerospace engineering and quality standards across our products, delivering high performance, reliability, and efficiency for the most demanding operating environments. Astro Mechanica is backed by leading venture and strategic investors, including Andreessen Horowitz (a16z), Giant Step Capital, United Airlines Ventures, and Voyager Ventures. WHO WE ARE: We’re a team of passionate engineers dedicated to advancing aerospace. We’re generalists with specialist depth, united by a flat structure and a shared obsession with building things that work well. We move fast, stay pragmatic, and let engineering excellence speak louder than hierarchy. WHO YOU ARE: Astro Mechanica is seeking an intern to join our Propulsion Engineering Team for the summer of 2027 (program begins on June 7, 2027 for semester schools and June 27, 2027 for quarter schools). The ideal candidate is someone who wants to take ownership of real hardware, from concept through test, and is eager to understand how their work affects surrounding systems. You approach technical challenges from first principles. As an intern, you’ll be embedded with the propulsion team in San Francisco, working on real projects alongside full-time engineers, and your work will have a direct impact on the configuration and performance of the Duality™ engine. In this role, your mission will be to help design, analyze, and validate propulsion hardware, with mentorship from senior engineers along the way. You’ll get hands-on experience across the full development cycle, from design trades to assembly to test, and you’ll learn to embody the test-like-you-fly philosophy. WHAT YOU’LL DO: - Support design trade studies while learning to consider system-level impacts - Complete detailed design of propulsion components and support structural, thermal, and fluid analyses - Present your work in design reviews and gather feedback from stakeholders - Assemble prototypes firsthand, design supporting tooling, and help write work instructions - Support hardware testing and analyze data to verify requirements and performance metrics - Help diagnose hardware problems and determine corrective actions - Own a scoped project through the summer and present your results to the team at the end of the internship WHAT WE’RE LOOKING FOR: - Currently pursuing a Bachelor’s, Master’s, or PhD in Aerospace Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, or a related discipline - Club, project, or research-level hands-on experience with fluidic, mechanical, or propulsion systems - Experience with solid, surface, and sheet metal CAD modeling (Siemens NX preferred) - Exposure to manufacturing processes, precision measurement, and GD&T - Coursework or experience in heat transfer, thermodynamics, and turbomachinery - Exposure to data acquisition, instrumentation, and power electronics - Desire for continuous improvement - Flexibility to work in a fast-paced environment - Attentive to detail and committed to a high level of quality in all work - Available for a full-time, in-person internship in San Francisco during Summer 2027 (approximately 10–12 weeks) PERKS & BENEFITS: - Competitive hourly pay - Hands-on mentorship from experienced engineers - Company-funded perks, including team lunches, game nights, and other activities ADDITIONAL INFORMATION: At Astro Mechanica, we highly value in-office work to foster collaboration and strengthen our company culture. We consider working in the office five days a week an essential part of the employee's role. Astro Mechanica is an equal opportunity employer. We proudly recruit and hire a diverse workforce and are committed to creating an inclusive environment for all employees. Pay range: $40 – $55 per hour.

jobs.title: Intern - SSD Hardware Engineering
jobs.location: Longmont-MAX- Office, CO, United States of America
jobs.body: Our vision is to transform how the world uses information to enrich life for all . Micron Technology is a world leader in innovating memory and storage solutions that accelerate the transformation of information into intelligence, inspiring the world to learn, communicate and advance faster than ever. The SSD Hardware Engineering team develops next-generation storage solutions that power data centers, AI infrastructure, client computing, and intelligent edge applications. Working across hardware, firmware, validation, manufacturing, and system engineering fields, the team delivers high-performance, reliable SSD products while using advanced design methodologies, automation, and AI-enabled engineering tools. As an SSD Hardware Engineering Intern, you will support the design, validation, characterization, and debug of next-generation SSD products. You will gain hands-on experience with high-speed hardware design, PCB development, signal integrity, power integrity, board bring-up, and hardware validation while collaborating with multi-functional engineering teams to solve complex technical challenges and deliver industry-leading storage solutions. Responsibilities Support the design, validation, characterization, and debug of SSD hardware platforms and subsystems. Assist with schematic reviews, PCB design activities, board bring-up, electrical measurements, and laboratory-based hardware testing. Perform data collection, analysis, and documentation of validation results to support product quality and performance objectives. Support signal integrity (SI), power integrity (PI), and system-level analysis through simulation, measurement, and correlation activities. Develop automation tools, scripts, dashboards, and AI-assisted workflows that improve engineering productivity, validation efficiency, and technical decision-making. Minimum Qualifications 0-2 years of relevant experience through internships, research, academic projects, laboratory work, or engineering experience in hardware design, electronics, embedded systems, storage systems, or related technical fields. Currently pursuing a Bachelor's or Master's degree in Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, or a related technical field. Knowledge of circuit analysis, digital electronics, PCB design fundamentals, and electronic components. Familiarity with high-speed interfaces such as PCIe, DDR, USB, Ethernet, or similar technologies. Understanding of signal integrity, power integrity, transmission lines, or high-speed digital design concepts. Experience with building electronic circuits or PCB design tools through coursework, academic projects, research, or internships. Experience using laboratory equipment such as oscilloscopes, logic analyzers, multimeters, spectrum analyzers, or similar test equipment. Strong analytical, solving, problem-solving, written, and verbal communication skills. Demonstrated ability to use AI-enabled tools and technologies to improve productivity, technical analysis, documentation, and engineering workflows. Preferred Qualifications Pursuing a Master's degree in Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, or a related technical field. Coursework, research, or project experience involving high-speed digital design, hardware validation, or board-level development. Knowledge of SSD architecture, NAND flash memory, storage systems, embedded systems, or data center technologies. Experience with board-level debugging, failure analysis, and root-cause investigation. Familiarity with SI/PI simulation and analysis tools such as HyperLynx, ADS, Sigrity, HFSS, or equivalent technologies. Experience using Python, MATLAB, Tcl, or similar languages for automation, testing, and data analysis. Experience applying AI-assisted engineering tools, workflow automation, or data-driven analysis techniques. Previous internship, research, or project experience related to hardware development, validation, or electronic system design. Do you want to learn from and collaborate with some of the greatest minds in the industry? At RTX , our internships, co-ops and full-time careers provide an exceptional foundation to work on complex problems, advance your skills and create a safer, more connected world. Discover opportunities to make a difference at RTX. At Raytheon , the Electro-Optics (EO) Department is responsible for requirements decomposition, detailed design and production support of the EO Sensors/Seekers, including the detectors, cryogenic systems, and structures making up the sensor/seeker subsystems. The multi-disciplined department includes engineers that may be responsible for the following: Designing, modeling/analyzing, and verifying optical components within a sensor/seeker designing the structures that hold the optics, including any mechanisms needed to move optics, as well as the cryogenic systems used to cool and maintain the temperature of EO detectors. Relaying critical detector interface and performance requirements to detector suppliers and verifying requirements are met. Utilize many different engineering discipline skills to assemble, test and verify optical, electrical, and mechanical components as they are built up into the sensor/seeker subsystem What You Will Do: The Intern will be responsible for spending their time learning and assisting on development programs and will be asked to be flexible while learning subsystem architecture, subsystem integration, or hardware design as well as innovation related roles that could include design, design review, production support, process and metric development. Participate as mentee and Individual Contributor supporting program activities. Optical alignment/testing of telescope assembly processes. EO modeling, simulation, and analysis applications. Requirements development, requirement validation, and subsystem trade studies. Design of optical and opto-mechanical seeker systems and/or test fixtures for missiles. Working with engineering and production personnel to troubleshoot and provide root cause and corrective action to design and process issues. Support production related activities in the assembly and documentation of electro-optical subsystems. This position is an onsite role. Qualifications You Must Have: Must be pursuing Bachelor’s or Advanced degree in Optical Engineering, Systems Engineering or related Science, Technology, Engineering or Mathematics (STEM) major and actively enrolled through the completion of the internship/co-op session. Optical design or systems integration and test experience or coursework in one or more of the following areas: optical testing and alignment, optical laboratory experience. Qualifications We Prefer: ABET is the preferred, although not required accreditation standard. 3.0 cumulative GPA desired. Class projects, professional internships, or academic research demonstrating the ability to apply technical coursework or computer skills. Using Computer Analysis Tools (MatLab, CodeV, FRED, or Microsoft Excel for EO modeling, simulation, and analysis applications. Prior RTX internship, co-op, or work experience. jobs.location: Ho Chi Minh City, vn
jobs.body: Bosch first started in Vietnam with a representative office in 1994. Bosch has its main office in Ho Chi Minh City, with branch offices in Hanoi and Da Nang, and a Powertrain Solutions plant in the Dong Nai province to manufacture pushbelt for continuously variable transmissions (CVT) in automobiles. In addition, Bosch operates a software and engineering R&D center (Robert Bosch Engineering and Business Solutions Vietnam Co., Ltd). In July 2014, Bosch set up a new Automotive R&D Center, located in Ho Chi Minh City. The continuous growth of this Centre is in line with Bosch’s strategy in Vietnam, which aims at becoming a manufacturing and R&D hub in the Southeast Asian region. Currently four products are available: connectors, pushbelt, fuel supply, and diagnosis module (tank leakage). For further information, please visit our website: www.bosch.com.vn Testing & Validation Activities Support Testing Engineers in the preparation and execution of validation activities for automotive components and materials. Prepare test samples, specimens, test setups, and measurement equipment before testing. Perform different validation tests under the supervision of Testing Engineers, such as: Samples preparation , wires harness preparation Mechanical force and strength testing Electrical testing and measurement Sealing and leakage testing Environmental and component-level validation testing Monitor test execution, identify abnormalities, and communicate issues to the responsible engineer. Record, organize, and analyze test data according to defined test procedures. Assist Senior Testing Engineers in component development and validation project. Laboratory Equipment & Technical Support Learn to understand and operate various laboratory and analytical equipment. Support equipment setup, basic maintenance, laboratory organization, 5S, Inventory management. Design or support the development of test jigs, fixtures, adapters, and simple mechanical setups for different validation activities. Undergraduate students majoring in technical field (e.g., mechanical, mechatronic or any relevant fields). International experience is a plus. Ability to read and understand basic technical drawings. Interest or experience in designing and building simple fixtures or mechanical test setups. Proficiency in Microsoft Office, particularly Excel, PowerPoint, and Word. Hands-on experience with laboratory, workshop, or fabrication tools is an advantage. Hands-on and practical approach to engineering and problem-solving. Analytical mindset with strong attention to detail. Proactive, open-minded, and willing to take responsibility. Quality-oriented with a strong willingness to learn. Good command of English in speaking, listening, reading, and writing. A learning-driven, professional, inclusive multinational work environment fosters personal growth and expands professional networks. An attractive monthly allowance. Hands-on experience in an advanced engineering simulation and product development field. Opportunity to apply technical knowledge skills in a real work. Collaboration with experienced engineers and professionals.

jobs.title: Mechanical Engineering Intern (Summer 2027)
jobs.location: Lincoln, NE, United States
jobs.body: Job Summary The Mechanical Engineering Intern supports new product development and product sustaining tasks for the company’s Global Rack Power Distribution products for the Integrated Rack Solutions line of business. The Mechanical Engineering Intern uses mechanical CAD software to transform product specifications into a manufacturable product, then releases that design into the engineering Product Lifecycle Management (PLM) system. The candidate must be a self-starter with a positive “make it happen” approach to meet multiple project goals and deliverables including product schedules, product design and manufacturability cost targets. The candidate must also manage complex development programs comprised of multiple and sometimes concurrent deliverables in a matrixed team environment interfacing with global internal and external (supplier/partner) team members. Responsibilities: · Create drawings and bills of material for sheet metal and purchased parts. · Create 3D mechanical models using sheet metal and part modeling functionality of 3D mechanical CAD software. · Generate assembly drawings and product submittal drawings. · Collaborate across the disciplines of mechanical, electrical, and process engineering, as well as production and product offering teams. · Work with manufacturing engineers and production associates to build prototypes and provide direction when needed. · Write, submit, and release engineering changes in the PLM system. Requirements: · Junior or Senior student studying for a Bachelor of Science in Mechanical Engineering or other engineering degree with mechanical design experience. · Some experience in engineering design and product development preferred. · Working knowledge of mechanical 3D CAD modeling. CREO and/or SolidWorks preferred. · Electrical and electromechanical knowledge preferred. · Ability to multitask and work effectively within cross functional engineering teams. · Excellent planning, organizing, documentation, and communication skills. #LI-RB1

jobs.body: Introduction to the job ASML US, including its affiliates and subsidiaries, bring together the most creative minds in science and technology to develop lithography machines that are key to producing faster, cheaper, more energy-efficient microchips. We design, develop, integrate, market and service these advanced machines, which enable our customers - the world’s leading chipmakers - to reduce the size and increase the functionality of their microchips, which in turn leads to smaller, more powerful consumer electronics. Our headquarters are in Veldhoven, Netherlands, and we have 18 office locations around the United States including main offices in Chandler, Arizona, San Jose and San Diego, California, Wilton, Connecticut, and Hillsboro, Oregon. Founded in 1984, ASML is the world’s leading provider of lithography systems for the semiconductor industry, manufacturing complex machines that are critical to the production of integrated circuits or microchips. Role and Responsibilities As an Electromechanical Intern, you will be working with teams developing portions of the lithography system and/or associated tooling related to the electronics. Additionally, you will collaborate with a multidiscipline project team working on the design and documentation of all mechanical aspects of the electrical infrastructure.; including engineering analysis and generation of electromechanical designs. The position requires highly motivated, extremely organized and self-driven individuals with strong communication skills. This position is located on-site in Wilton, CT. It requires onsite presence to attend in-person work-related events, trainings and meetings and to further ensure teamwork, collaboration and innovation. Must be available for 12 weeks for one of these sessions starting with the following dates: 6/2/2027 or 6/14/2027 Education and Experience Pursuing Bachelor’s Degree in Engineering discipline with a major in Mechanical Engineering or Industrial Engineering or equivalent experience 2 years of completed college courses Rising Junior or Rising Senior Your profile Working at the cutting edge of tech, you will always have new challenges and new problems to solve – and working together is the only way to do that. You will not work in a silo. Instead, you will be part of a creative, dynamic work environment where you will collaborate with supportive colleagues. There is always space for creative and unique points of view. You will have the flexibility and trust to choose how best to tackle tasks and solve problems. To thrive in this job, you will need the following skills: Can observe and respond to people and situations and interact with others encountered in the course of work Can learn and apply new information or skills Must be able to read and interpret data, information and documents Strong customer focus and commitment to customer satisfaction through prioritization, quality, efficiency and professionalism Ability to complete assignments with attention to detail and high degree of accuracy Proven ability to perform effectively in a demanding environment with changing workloads Result driven-demonstrate ownership and accountability Identifies bottlenecks and drives improvements Work independently or as part of a team and follow through on assignments with minimal supervision Demonstrate open, clear, concise and professional communication Ability to establish and maintain cooperative working relationships with co-workers and customer Work according to a strict set of procedures within the provided timelines The current base hourly range for this role is currently: $18.00 to $48.00 per hour Pay scales are determined by role, level, location and alignment with market data. jobs.body: Eaton’s ES AMER ARS division is currently seeking a Mechanical Engineer Internship / Co-op. This position can either be a rotational co-op assignment, or a Summer 2027 internship. The hourly rate for this position is $22.15 - $27.69 per hour. Please note the salary information shown above is a general guideline only. Salaries are based upon candidate skills, experience, and qualifications, as well as market and business considerations. What you’ll do: Position Overview: The Product Development Mechanical Engineer is responsible for the creative design and development of residential miniature circuit breaker. This position will contribute to the overall mechanical design of the product with involvement from project initiation thru manufacturing launch, plus ongoing developments. Functional responsibility includes design, testing and certification of the components plus systems as well as product qualification for performance, reliability, DFMA, and cost optimization of the final product. This position will work closely with the Engineering Manager, Program Manager, other Mechanical Engineers and System Architects, Electrical Engineers, Product Line Marketing Manager, and Operations team members, Sourcing and Manufacturing personnel to develop the products in an organized and expedient fashion per our Pro-Launch process. As a Mechanical Engineer, you will be responsible for developing and designing new products that will penetrate the national and international markets. This role will also require you to project manage some of these projects to completion using a phase gate project management platform, working cross-functionally with other business areas including Marketing, Sales, and Operations. It will require you to have strong communication skills, ambition, drive, strong engineering experience, with enthusiasm in the product design arena. The position responsibilities also entail the identification of product adjacencies and identification and execution of cost savings initiatives through Value Analysis/Value Engineering (VA/VE). What you’ll do: • Perform mechanical engineering, CAD solid modeling, design simulation, product specifications, drawing packages, Bill of Material (BOM) and Engineering Change Order (ECO) creation, systems development, product testing and design validation. • Design parts and assemblies which include component types including: sheet metal, plastics, mechanisms, electrical and wiring, packaging. • Participate in new product development/introduction, innovation, idea creation and implementation, prototype assembly and testing, DFMA assessments, plus other design-to-industrialization activities. • Participate in project management and engaging with multi-disciplined teams to achieve goals using ProLaunch and other project management tools. • Participate in Voice of the Customer (VOC) product and market requirements research. • Maintain and upgrades existing products, plus VA/VE activities. • Provide assistance with 3rd party certifications such as UL, CSA and other regulatory agencies. • Ensure timely completion to project commitment dates. Qualifications: Basic Qualifications: • Actively enrolled in a Bachelor's degree program in Mechanical Engineering from an accredited institution with graduation no later than August 2029. • Minimum of one internship or co-op experience or an equivalent of 3 months work experience completed at the time of this application. • Eaton will not consider applicants for employment immigration sponsorship or support for this position. jobs.body: Golden, CO | Full-Time | 12-15 Weeks | Summer 2027 Today, everything we send to space is constrained by what fits inside a rocket fairing. That's a fundamental bottleneck to building more capable spacecraft. Rendezvous Robotics is solving this problem with electromagnetic self-assembling tiles: modular spacecraft components that rendezvous, dock, and latch to assemble bigger and more powerful spacecraft than anything that can be folded to fit into a rocket. We're a small team based in Golden, Colorado, executing on a clear path from flight demonstration to our first operational systems. Our work spans hardware, software, and systems engineering. We are looking for the best people in the world who want to build the next generation of advanced spacecraft. Every unit in our system has to dock, undock, and re-dock repeatedly without wearing, fit together in a manner that allows reliable connections, and provide the stiffness needed to build extremely large structures in orbit. That puts a lot of pressure on the mechanical design: docking connector design, mechanical latching, thermal management, structural loads through the docking interface, and packaging everything else around it. You'll be a critical member of the team contributing to the development and hands-on assembly of real flight hardware Responsibilities Design and iterate on structural components and docking interface hardware Work on thermal management for onboard electronics and battery packs Support mechanical integration of electronics, power systems, and sensors within a tight envelope Develop and refine harness and connector layouts between internal subsystems Run structural and thermal analysis to validate designs before build Basic Qualifications Currently pursuing a degree in Mechanical Engineering, Aerospace Engineering, or a related field Proficiency in CAD (Onshape, NX, SolidWorks, Fusion 360, or similar) Understanding of basic structural and thermal analysis principles Preferred Qualifications Experience designing for space environments (thermal cycling, vacuum, vibration, radiation shielding) Familiarity with ruggedized connectors and cable harness design Hands-on machining, 3D printing, or prototyping experience Experience with FEA tools (NX Simcenter3D, FEMAP, ANSYS, etc.) ITAR Requirements To conform to U.S. Government export regulations, applicant must be a (i) U.S. citizen or national, (ii) U.S. lawful, permanent resident (aka green card holder), (iii) Refugee under 8 U.S.C. § 1157, or (iv) Asylee under 8 U.S.C. § 1158, or be eligible to obtain the required authorizations from the U.S. Department of State. jobs.title: Hardware Engineering Intern (EE)
jobs.location: Santa Rosa, California
jobs.body: Overview Keysight is a mission-critical design enablement partner for organizations solving the world’s most complex engineering challenges. With deep engineering expertise and leading design, emulation, and test solutions, our ~16,800 employees help customers in over 100 countries accelerate innovation across communications, automotive, energy, quantum, aerospace and defense, semiconductor, and artificial intelligence markets. Learn more about what we do. At Keysight, people come together to explore new ideas, challenge what's possible, and advance the technologies defining the future. Here, you'll find opportunities to do your best work, take your career further, and thrive in an award-winning culture. Learn more about our benefits. This position is based in Santa Rosa, in the heart of California’s beautiful wine country and home to Keysight’s corporate headquarters and many product-development R&D labs. The Digital and Photonics R&D team develops and produces some of the world’s highest-performance oscilloscopes—giving early-career engineers the opportunity to learn from experienced specialists while contributing to real products and challenging measurement problems. You will join a collaborative environment where learning is part of the job. Experienced hardware, signal-integrity, FPGA, software, and measurement specialists will provide technical guidance, design feedback, and hands-on mentorship as you build confidence and depth. You’ll gain experience with advanced hardware, modern design and simulation tools, and state-of-the-art laboratory equipment while contributing to the communications-electronics measurement challenges of today and tomorrow. We are seeking an Electrical Engineer who is excited to grow their hardware-design skills while helping design, integrate, and validate high-performance electronic hardware for advanced instrumentation and measurement systems. This opportunity is especially well suited to a recent BS or MS graduate with strong fundamentals and meaningful hands-on experience from internships, university research, labs, or engineering projects. You do not need to arrive as an expert in every technology listed below. We are looking for curiosity, practical problem solving, a willingness to learn, and enthusiasm for working with experienced technical specialists who can help accelerate your development. Responsibilities What You’ll Do: Contribute to the design and development of high-speed board-level digital and mixed-signal hardware, including multi-GHz designs and applications approaching 10 GHz. Learn and participate across the hardware-development lifecycle, from architecture and component selection through schematic capture, PCB/PCA implementation, board bring-up, characterization, validation, and troubleshooting. Develop experience with circuits ranging from basic RLC networks to high-speed op-amps, filters, low-noise oscillators, microcontrollers, FPGAs, ADCs/DACs, memory, and power-supply conditioning. Design and evaluate clock and timing circuitry, including oscillators, PLLs, clock generators, buffers, synchronization, distribution, and jitter-sensitive circuits. Apply and deepen your understanding of high-speed signal-integrity and noise-control principles. Develop robust power architectures incorporating DC/DC converters, LDOs, sequencing, decoupling, grounding, and low-noise power distribution for sensitive analog, digital, FPGA, and clock circuitry. Partner with PCB and signal-integrity engineers on materials, stack-up, impedance targets, placement, high-speed routing, via structures, connectors, grounding, power planes, and return paths. Learn how PCB materials, packages, connectors, launches, vias, and other interconnects influence electrical behavior at multi-GHz frequencies. Participate in pre-layout and post-layout design reviews and, where applicable, use tools and models such as SPICE, IBIS/IBIS-AMI, S-parameters, and SI/PI simulation to predict and correlate hardware performance. Perform hands-on board bring-up and troubleshooting using advanced lab equipment such as high-bandwidth oscilloscopes, spectrum analyzers, VNAs where applicable, TDR/TDT techniques, logic analyzers, DMMs, and power supplies. Investigate and solve hardware challenges involving signal integrity, timing, jitter, clocks, power integrity, interfaces, FPGA behavior, embedded firmware, and PCB implementation—with support and mentorship from experienced engineers. Collaborate with software and FPGA engineers on device initialization, register configuration, diagnostics, communication interfaces, and hardware/software integration. Participate in multi-functional peer design reviews and use measurement results to improve subsequent hardware revisions. Support hardware verification, design documentation, design-for-manufacturability, EMI/EMC activities, and transition to production. How You’ll Grow: Learn directly from experienced engineers through collaborative design reviews, lab work, troubleshooting, and technical discussions. Build breadth across digital, analog, mixed-signal, signal-integrity, power-integrity, FPGA, and embedded-system domains while developing deeper expertise in the areas that interest you most. Take on increasing ownership as your skills grow—from contributing to individual circuits and measurements to driving larger pieces of a hardware design. Strengthen your engineering judgment by connecting simulation, design decisions, and real laboratory measurements on production-relevant hardware. Develop communication and collaboration skills by working across disciplines and participating in peer reviews with specialists throughout the development process. Qualifications BS or MS in Electrical Engineering, Electronics Engineering, Computer Engineering, or a related discipline. Hands-on hardware experience gained through internships, university research, laboratory work, student teams, personal projects, or professional engineering experience. Strong digital-electronics fundamentals and a practical foundation in analog and mixed-signal circuitry. Some experience with schematic design, PCB/PCA development, board bring-up, measurement, troubleshooting, or root-cause analysis through academic, project, internship, or professional work. Foundational understanding of transmission lines, controlled impedance, termination, reflections, crosstalk, return paths, and PCB parasitics. Interest in developing deeper expertise in signal integrity and power integrity for high-performance hardware. Familiarity with high-speed digital interfaces through coursework, projects, research, internships, or professional experience. Familiarity with clock/timing concepts such as oscillators, PLLs, clock generation/distribution, synchronization, and jitter. Enthusiasm for hands-on laboratory work and systematic troubleshooting. Ability and willingness to work across hardware, software, and FPGA boundaries when diagnosing complex system behavior. Preferred Qualifications: We encourage you to apply even if you do not check every box below. These are areas you may already know or have the opportunity to develop on the job. jobs.body: About JLG, an Oshkosh company JLG began in 1969, when our founder, John L. Grove set out to resolve growing safety concerns in the construction industry. Since then we have been committed to understanding the challenges and delivering innovative solutions to the access market. We partner with customers to provide quality equipment, training opportunities and trusted support within the access industry. We are a global company, and our products—including mobile elevating work platforms, telehandlers, utility vehicles and accessories—can be found all over the world. As an R&D Engineering Intern with JLG, you will work alongside engineers and technicians in a hands-on research, development, and test environment supporting new and existing JLG products. This role provides exposure to the design, fabrication, assembly, testing, and modification of heavy equipment, vehicle systems, components, tooling, and test fixtures. You will spend significant time in the R&D shop working directly with technicians to support prototype builds, test setups, fabrication, machining, welding, and troubleshooting. The ideal candidate enjoys working in a heavy manufacturing environment and is interested in combining engineering design and analysis with hands-on problem solving. YOUR IMPACT Support the design, fabrication, assembly, testing, and modification of vehicles, subsystems, components, tooling, fixtures, and test stands. Work directly with R&D technicians and engineers to support prototype builds, test setups, equipment configuration changes, repairs, and troubleshooting. Create and revise engineering drawings, component layouts, tooling, and fixtures using CAD software such as Creo Parametric. Read and interpret engineering drawings, blueprints, specifications, and technical documentation to support shop activities. jobs.title: Test Engineering Intern (Summer)
jobs.location: North Kingstown, Rhode Island, USA
jobs.body: At REGENT, we’re on a mission to revolutionize regional transportation between coastal cities. We're not just building vehicles, we're creating a new category of transportation: the Seaglider. These groundbreaking wing-in-ground-effect craft travel just above the water’s surface, combining the speed of an airplane with the low operating costs of a boat. Capable of 180 miles at 180 mph on today's battery tech (and up to 400 miles with next-gen batteries), Seagliders will unlock fast, affordable, and sustainable coastal transit for passengers and cargo - connecting cities, islands, and communities like never before. Backed by leading investors and powered by a team of passionate, forward-thinking engineers, builders, and operators, we’re now scaling from a breakthrough prototype to full production - and building the team to make it happen. ROLE OVERVIEW The rhythm of this role changes constantly: prepping a test plan one day, monitoring a live run the next, and diving into post-event analysis the day after, because Paladin and Squire are both advancing toward manufacturing in parallel, and testing has to keep pace with both. You'll need a real engineering foundation to do this well, since understanding what a subsystem is supposed to do is what lets you write a test plan and recognize an anomaly instead of just a number. You don't need prior test experience. The team teaches how a test event runs, how to build a test card, and how to work a Data Room station, and you'll be on live tests early in the term. The Test Operations team cares deeply about getting that rigor right, because safe and effective testing is what lets REGENT build Seagliders and reinvent how coastal communities move. If you want a front-row seat to how a vehicle actually gets tested and moves toward certification, and you're energized by precision, fast shifts in focus, and learning from senior technical experts, this internship was built for you. WHAT YOU'LL DO - Help Build the Test Plans: You'll help write the test cards and test plans that tell the team exactly what to check and how, for both Paladin and Squire. Clear, well-structured plans are what keep a test event efficient and its data usable. - Learn the Live Watch: During test events, you'll sit in the Data Room alongside a test engineer tracking real-time telemetry as the vehicle operates, learning to catch something odd in the moment rather than after the fact. - Drive Issues to Resolution: After a test, you'll dig into the data alongside subject matter experts to understand what happened and why. You'll help carry open questions through to a real answer, not just a note in a file. - Move Between Modes Fast: Your week will shift between prepping the next test, running one live, and analyzing the last, often all within the same few days. Priorities on both vehicles move in parallel, and you'll move with them. - Work Indoors and On the Water: You'll operate in the Data Room for some tests and out on the water for others, adjusting to very different environments and requirements. Comfort in both settings is part of the job. - Partner Across Engineering: You'll work closely with engineers across electrical, mechanical, and aero/hydro disciplines to understand what a subsystem is supposed to be doing. That shared understanding is what makes a test plan, and an anomaly call, meaningful. WHAT YOU'LL BRING - Engineering Coursework: You're currently pursuing a degree in engineering, with coursework in electrical, mechanical, or aero/hydro principles that gives you a working sense of what a system should be doing under normal conditions. That foundation is what lets you start recognizing when something isn't. - Curiosity About Live Data: You've worked with data or instrumentation in a lab, a project, or a class, and you want to learn to watch it stream in during a live test rather than only reviewing it afterward. - Clear Technical Writing: You write documentation someone else can follow, like lab reports or project write-ups, and you care about getting the details right. The team teaches the test card format; the writing habits are yours to bring. - Composure at Speed: You stay sharp and organized when things move fast, because live testing of air and water vehicles doesn't pause for you to catch up. High tempo doesn't rattle you. - Genuine Adaptability: You're comfortable moving between prep work, live execution, and analysis, and between indoor and on-water environments, sometimes within the same week. You don't need a fixed routine to do good work. - A Bonus in Aviation or Maritime: Coursework, projects, or club work in aerodynamics, aviation, or on the water gives you a head start, since Paladin and Squire blend both worlds. Familiarity with wind, water, or flight dynamics helps you get oriented faster. - A Bonus in Scripting or Data Tools: Some exposure to Python, MATLAB, or similar tools is a plus, since post-event analysis moves faster when you can pull patterns out of a dataset instead of scrolling through it by hand. WHO WE'RE LOOKING FOR - Collaborative Team Player: You believe that great things happen when teams work together. You communicate effectively and collaborate with engineers, stakeholders, and other cross-functional teams to align on goals and move projects forward. You bring people together, ensuring that everyone is on the same page and moving towards a shared vision. - Creative Problem Solver: You thrive on tackling complex challenges and finding innovative solutions. Whether you're resolving installation challenges, debugging elusive electrical issues, or adapting on the fly during integration and test, you bring a practical, inventive mindset to every problem. You don't just patch issues - you improve processes, anticipate downstream impacts, and help turn one-off fixes into scalable solutions that raise the bar for future builds. - Adaptable & Agile: In a fast-paced, ever-evolving startup environment, you quickly adapt to changing priorities and requirements. You approach challenges with a calm, resilient mindset, and know how to pivot and adjust your approach as needed, ensuring that progress continues without missing a beat. - Innovative Mindset: You're driven by curiosity and a passion for technology. You're passionate about driving continuous improvement, embracing new technologies and methodologies to enhance efficiency, quality, and team performance. WHAT WE OFFER - Competitive compensation - Housing Stipend available for those temporarily moving to join our team - Daily, free catered lunches - Learning & professional development opportunities - Meaningful projects that make an impact - Mentorship & guidance from experienced team members If you’re ready to take on an exciting challenge, grow with us, and make a lasting impact, we want to hear from you. Even if you don’t meet every requirement, but you see yourself contributing to our mission, we encourage you to apply! We value diverse skillsets and experiences and believe in the potential of passionate individuals to make a big impact. Equal Opportunity Employer REGENT is an Equal Opportunity Employer. We are committed to creating a diverse and inclusive work environment. Employment decisions are made without regard to race, color, religion, national origin, gender, sexual orientation, gender identity, age, disability, or any other characteristic protected by law.

jobs.body: Work Flexibility: Onsite What You Get Out of the Internship ​​ At Stryker, we believe that developing the next generation of talent is just as important as developing life-changing medical technologies. jobs.body: Introduction ASML US brings together the most creative minds in science and technology to develop lithography machines and metrology that are key to producing faster, cheaper, more energy-efficient microchips. Our headquarters are in Veldhoven, the Netherlands, and we have 18 office locations around the United States including main offices in Chandler, Arizona, San Jose and San Diego, California, Wilton, Connecticut, and Hillsboro, Oregon.
