jobs.title: Test & Reliability Engineering Intern
jobs.location: Pittsburgh
jobs.body: WHAT WE DO Gecko Robotics is helping the world’s most important organizations ensure the availability, reliability, and sustainability of critical infrastructure. Gecko's complete and connected solutions combine wall-climbing robots, industry-leading sensors, and an AI-powered data platform to provide customers with a unique window into the current and future health of their physical assets. This enables real-time decision making to increase the efficiency and safety of operations, promote mission readiness, and protect the environment and civilization from the effects of infrastructure failure. ROLE AT A GLANCE Gecko Robotics is seeking a Test & Reliability Engineer Intern to join Field Infra’s Test & Reliability (T&R) team in Pittsburgh for Summer 2027. This is a full-time, onsite internship, Monday through Friday. You will contribute to a defined engineering project focused on making our robotic systems more dependable by building software tools, automating tests, and analyzing system data and logs. Working alongside experienced engineers, you will develop practical tools, execute tests, and generate evidence that improves how Gecko validates and learns from its robotic systems. What you will do - Own a scoped engineering project that improves a test, regression, reliability-analysis, or test-data workflow. - Help plan, execute, and document software and integrated robotic-system tests under the guidance of experienced engineers. - Analyze test results, clearly document findings and open questions, and recommend improvements to test coverage and repeatability. - Develop or improve tooling, automation, scripts, or documentation that makes testing more efficient and reliable. - Collaborate with Test & Reliability engineers and partner teams to understand how field observations and engineering requirements inform validation. - Present your project, results, and recommended next steps at the end of the internship. Technologies We Use Depending on the assigned project, you may work with Python, Linux, Git, hardware and software test equipment, data-analysis tools, and robotic-system logs. The specific tools and technologies will depend on the assigned project. About You You are a curious, hands-on engineering student who enjoys understanding how complex systems behave in the real world. You are comfortable learning across software and hardware boundaries, approaching problems methodically, and communicating what you observed and what you do not yet know. Required Skills - Currently pursuing a bachelor’s or master’s degree in engineering, computer science, robotics, or a related technical discipline, with an expected graduation date between December 2027 and May 2028. - Ability to work onsite in Pittsburgh, Monday through Friday, for the full Summer 2027 internship. - Foundational programming experience in Python or another general-purpose programming language. - Experience writing, testing, or debugging software through coursework, projects, research, competition teams, or a prior internship. - Interest in software testing, reliability, robotics, embedded systems, or complex physical systems. - Strong written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to structure technical problems, document work clearly, communicate findings, and learn from feedback. Preferred Skills - Previous hands-on experience with robotics, embedded systems, electronics, mechanical systems, or other complex physical systems through an internship, research position, engineering lab, competition team, or substantial project. - Experience using Python to automate test workflows or analyze system data, logs, or failures. - Familiarity with Linux, Git, and structured testing or debugging practices. - Experience designing experiments, debugging system behavior, or building tools for others. - Coursework or projects in software testing, controls, mechatronics, reliability engineering, systems engineering, or a related field. WHO WE ARE At Gecko, our people are our greatest investment. In addition to competitive compensation packages, we offer company equity, 401(k) matching, gender-neutral parental leave, full medical, dental, and vision insurance, mental health, ongoing professional development, family planning assistance, and flexible paid time off. Gecko values collaboration, innovation, and partnership, and we believe we do our best work when we're together in person. We’re an office-first culture but understand that sometimes you may need to work from home. Many people are in the office five days a week, others need a bit more flexibility. Ultimately, we care about the outcomes we achieve - and creating a culture of autonomy and trust that enables that impact. Gecko is committed to creating a culture of inclusion and belonging, and we are proud to be an equal opportunity employer. We believe it is our collective responsibility to uphold these values and encourage candidates from all backgrounds to join us in our mission to protect today’s infrastructure and give form to tomorrow’s. All qualified applicants will be treated with respect and receive equal consideration for employment without regard to race, color, creed, religion, sex, gender identity, sexual orientation, national origin, disability, uniform service, veteran status, age, or any other protected characteristic per federal, state, or local law. If you are passionate about what you do and want to use your talents to support our critical mission, we’d love to hear from you.

jobs.title: Environmental Test Engineering Intern (Summer 2027)
jobs.location: San Jose, CA
jobs.body: About the role Summer internships will range between the months of May and September depending on university schedules. Internship is full-time and on-site in San Jose, California. The Assembly, Integration and Test (AIT) team at Muon is responsible for validating spacecraft hardware through unit acceptance testing as well as spacecraft-level integration and environmental testing. As an Environmental Test Engineering Intern, you will support the planning, setup, execution, and analysis of environmental tests used to validate spacecraft hardware against the extreme conditions of launch and space. You will work alongside experienced environmental test engineers, test engineers, and technicians to prepare hardware and test equipment, develop and execute test procedures, collect and analyze test data, and troubleshoot test issues. This is a hands-on opportunity to gain experience with spacecraft environmental testing and see your work directly contribute to the successful integration and launch of Muon spacecraft. Muon is a small and fast growing startup which offers interns the experience to get direct mentorship and have real impact on our programs. As an intern, you'll collaborate with a dynamic team in a startup environment and have the chance to learn from some of the most accomplished and experienced aerospace professionals in the industry. We're committed to offering an experience where your decisions and contributions play a pivotal role in driving Muon's success. Responsibilities Assist environmental test engineers with the planning, preparation, and execution of spacecraft and subsystem environmental testing, including thermal vacuum, vibration, acoustic, and other qualification or acceptance testing. Support test setup and instrumentation, including thermocouples, accelerometers, pressure sensors, and other test measurement equipment. Assist with preparing spacecraft hardware, fixtures, ground support equipment, and test configurations for environmental test campaigns. Execute functional checkouts and test procedures under engineer supervision before, during, and after environmental testing. Monitor test operations and hardware performance, identify anomalies, and support troubleshooting and root-cause investigations. Collect, process, and perform preliminary analysis of environmental test data to verify hardware performance and test requirements. Support development and improvement of test procedures, test processes, checklists, and laboratory workflows. Assist with configuration and operation of environmental test equipment and data acquisition systems. Support automation and scripting efforts to improve environmental test setup, monitoring, data collection, and analysis. Generate test documentation, data summaries, and reports under the guidance of environmental test engineers. Support integration and handling of spacecraft hardware and ground support equipment in cleanroom, laboratory, and environmental test facilities. Help maintain a safe, organized, and flight-hardware-ready test environment. Qualifications Currently pursuing a Bachelor's or Master's degree in Aerospace, Mechanical, Electrical, Systems Engineering, or a related technical field. Strong understanding of engineering fundamentals, particularly in areas such as mechanics, thermal systems, dynamics, instrumentation, or electrical systems. Demonstrated interest in spacecraft environmental testing, laboratory testing, or hardware development. Experience with a programming or scripting language for data analysis or test automation, such as Python, MATLAB/Simulink, Julia, or C++. Strong problem-solving skills with the ability to approach complex technical challenges from a first-principles perspective. Strong communication and interpersonal skills, with an ability to work effectively in a fast-paced, collaborative team environment. Ability and willingness to work hands-on with engineering hardware and test equipment. Nice-to-have Skills Previous internship, co-op, research, or laboratory experience involving hardware testing. Experience with thermal vacuum, vibration, acoustic, shock, or other environmental testing. Experience with data acquisition systems, instrumentation, sensors, or test equipment. Experience developing test procedures, test plans, or test reports. Experience with accelerometers, thermocouples, pressure transducers, strain gauges, or similar instrumentation. Experience with Python, MATLAB, LabVIEW, or other tools used for test automation and data analysis. Previous experience on technical project teams such as a CubeSat, rocketry, Formula SAE, Solar Car, or other hardware-focused engineering project. Familiarity with spacecraft systems or subsystems and environmental test requirements. Experience with hardware integration, troubleshooting, or hardware-in-the-loop testing. Pay range Bachelor's students $40/hour Master's $45/hour PhD $50/hour About Muon Space Founded in 2021, Muon Space is an end-to-end Space Systems Provider that designs, builds, and operates LEO satellite constellations delivering mission-critical data. Our revolutionary, integrated technology stack enables customers to optimize every dimension of their missions for faster time-to-orbit and superior constellation remote sensing performance. Our state-of-the-art facility in the heart of Silicon Valley is optimized for manufacturing spacecraft and rapid, flexible payload integration at scale. From climate monitoring to national security, Muon Space is dedicated to delivering Earth Intelligence for a safer and more resilient world. Taking Care of Our Team At Muon salary is only part of our total compensation package. In addition to salary, full-time employees receive equity compensation as well as benefits including medical, dental, and vision insurance, a 401k retirement plan, short & long term disability and life insurance. We also offer three weeks paid vacation for new employees, along with 12 paid holidays, unlimited sick time and paid parental leave. Our mission embraces the entire planet and we believe our team should too. Muon is dedicated to creating a diverse and dynamic company and workforce. We believe in equal employment opportunity regardless of race, color, ancestry, religion, sex, age, national origin, citizenship, sexual orientation, marital status, disability, or gender identity. We value diversity in the workplace, and that starts with our applicants. We encourage you to apply, even if you don't check all the boxes, and we look forward to reviewing your application! In addition, if you need a reasonable accommodation as part of your application for employment or interviews with us, please let us know. Muon is currently registered and able to hire in the following states: AL, AZ, CA, CO, CT, DC, FL, GA, IL, IA, ID, MD, MA, MI, MN, MO, NJ, NY, NC, OH, OR, PA, TN, TX, VT, VA, WA ITAR/EAR Requirements This position requires access to export controlled information. jobs.body: Work Flexibility: Onsite What You Get Out of the Internship ​​ At Stryker, we believe that developing the next generation of talent is just as important as developing life-changing medical technologies. As an intern, you won’t just observe — you’ll contribute to meaningful projects, gain exposure to leaders who will mentor you, and experience a culture of innovation and teamwork that is shaping the future of healthcare. As an intern, you will: ​ ​ Apply classroom knowledge and gain experience in a fast-paced and growing industry setting​ Implement new ideas, be constantly challenged, and develop your skills​ Network with key/high-level stakeholders and leaders of the business​ Be a part of an innovative team and culture​ Experience documenting complex processes and presenting them in a clear format Who we want ​​ Challengers. People who seek out the hard projects and work to find just the right solutions.​ Teammates. Partners who listen to ideas, share thoughts and work together to move the business forward.​ Charismatic networkers. Relationship-savvy people who intentionally make connections with both internal partners and external contacts.​ Strategic thinkers. Interns who propose innovative ideas and consistently exceed their performance objectives.​ Customer-oriented achievers. Individuals with an unparalleled work ethic and customer-focused attitude who bring value to their partnerships.​ Game changers. Persistent interns who will stop at nothing to live out Stryker’s mission to make healthcare better. Opportunities Available ​ ​As a Mechanical Engineering intern at Stryker, you will be placed in one of the following teams: Research & Development New Product Development R&D interns in New Product Development work with cross-functional teams to identify the needs and the goals of future products. They research new technologies, customer expectations, business requirements and regulations. They may work with a variety of tools, including CAD, FEA, and our Test Labs to develop new product concepts. These interns utilize their technical education to design new products and drive them from concept to production. Product Engineering R&D interns in Product Engineering work with cross-functional teams to identify the greatest needs for improvements on current products. They research new technologies, customer feedback, and product performance data to make our products better for Stryker and for our customers. Product Engineering interns work with a variety of tools, including CAD, FEA, Test Labs, and root cause analysis methods. These interns utilize their technical education to improve the safety and efficacy of our existing products. Test Lab Test interns partner closely with Test Engineers and R&D to experiment with early prototypes and vet out product designs throughout the design process. What this really means is that we get to be the Mythbusters of our division. You think your design can last the entire expected service life? We put it to the test. Just like the show, we quickly design and build fixtures to simulate real life situations. In addition to these experiments, we are ultimately responsible for design verification – the quantitative testing of the technical specifications of the product. A team’s experience ranges from 2 to over 15 years with technical specialties ranging from sterilization, mechanical, electrical, software, and optics. If you’re the type of person that has the magic ability to break things – we want you! Majors Targeted: Mechanical Engineering, or related majors $20 min hourly wage – $35 max hourly wage, sign-on bonus, 11 paid holidays annually, and either paid corporate housing or a living stipend, dependent upon hiring location What You Need ​​ Currently pursuing a Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in a related field; must remain enrolled in a degree-seeking program after the internship.​ Cumulative 3.0 GPA or above (verified at time of hire) Must be legally authorized to work in the U.S. and not require employment-based sponsorship now or in the future.​ Strong written and verbal communication skills, with proven ability to collaborate and build relationships Demonstrated leadership, problem-solving, and organizational skills with the ability to manage multiple priorities Proficiency in Microsoft Office (Excel, Word, PowerPoint) and eagerness to learn in a dynamic environment. jobs.body: Anduril Industries is a defense technology company with a mission to transform U.S. and allied military capabilities with advanced technology. As the world enters an era of strategic competition, Anduril is committed to bringing cutting-edge autonomy, AI, computer vision, sensor fusion, and networking technology to the military in months, not years. ABOUT THE JOB We are looking for Product Sourcing Engineer interns to join our rapidly growing teams. In this role, you will be responsible for driving the strategic supply network development and cost management of Anduril’s product hardware, across their lifecycles, by collaborating with suppliers and cross-functionally, including stakeholders in engineering, quality, and manufacturing. WHAT YOU’LL DO Conduct supplier selection for a specific product, leveraging approved supplier list. modeling Joint design development, via clear statements of work Simulation of mechanical & electronics designs Develop and execute on sourcing strategy via full market knowledge, supplier plan per part analysis Follow through completion of component qualifications by relevant stakeholders, ahead of production need dates Reduce complexity of supply chain through commonality optimization & component/supplier rationalization Lead all cost engineering activities to converge the bottoms-up cost curve to product cost, maximizing the total cost of ownership (TCO) across the product requirements and are built for scale Manage project schedules, identify critical path activities, and proactively identify and mitigate risks to keep initiatives on track Hold project teams and stakeholders accountable for deliverables and deadlines, navigating organizational complexity to clear roadblocks and drive decisions Establish program structure, milestones, and operating rhythms to ensure accountability and drive results across the business Drive alignment across stakeholders and influence without formal authority in ambiguous, high-stakes situations REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS Must PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS Background within: Design & development of mechanical and/or electronics devices Advanced sourcing activities, including positions working as a commodity/sourcing manager Supplier development (technology, process, supply chain, etc.) Early supplier engagement, ahead of product/engineering requirement realization Exposure to value/procurement engineering or TCO-related work at the component & product level Familiarity with developing high-tech products in a high-mix, low-volume environment US Hourly Range $32 — $45 USD The salary range for this role is an estimate based on a wide range of compensation factors, inclusive of base salary only. Actual salary offer may vary based on (but not limited to) work experience, education and/or training, critical skills, and/or business considerations. Highly competitive equity grants are included in the majority of full time offers; and are considered part of Anduril's total compensation package. Additionally, Anduril offers top-tier benefits for full-time employees, including: Benefits At Anduril, we invest in our people. Our comprehensive, competitive benefits package (available at little to no cost to employees) ensures you’re supported in health, recovery, and whatever comes next. For more information, Explore Our Benefits . Protecting Yourself from Recruitment Scams Anduril is committed to maintaining the integrity of our Talent acquisition process and the security of our candidates. We've observed a rise in sophisticated phishing and fraudulent schemes where individuals impersonate Anduril representatives, luring job seekers with false interviews or job offers. These scammers often attempt to extract payment or sensitive personal information. To ensure your safety and help you navigate your job search with confidence, please keep the following critical points in mind: No Financial Requests: Anduril will never solicit payment or demand personal financial details (such as banking information, credit card numbers, or social security numbers) at any stage of our hiring process. Our legitimate recruitment is entirely free for candidates. Please always verify communications: Direct from Anduril: If you receive an email from one of our recruiters, it will only come from an @anduril.com address. Via Agency Partner: If contacted by a recruiting agency for an Anduril role, their email will clearly identify their agency. If you suspect any suspicious activity, please verify the agency's authenticity by reaching out to contact@anduril.com . Exercise Caution with Unsolicited Outreach: If you receive any communication that appears suspicious, contains grammatical errors, or makes unusual requests, do not engage. Always confirm the sender's email domain is @anduril.com before providing any personal information or clicking on links. What to Do If You Suspect Fraud: Should you encounter any questionable or fraudulent outreach claiming to be from Anduril, please report it immediately to contact@anduril.com . Your proactive caution is invaluable in protecting your personal information and upholding the security and trustworthiness of our recruitment efforts. Data Privacy To view Anduril's candidate data privacy policy, please visit https://anduril.com/applicant-privacy-notice/ . By submitting your application, you consent to Anduril Industries using a third-party service provider to conduct pre-employment risk, integrity, and due diligence screening and assessing potential risks as part of your application process. This third-party service provider does not act as a consumer reporting agency. Use of this provider helps to ensure compliance with applicable laws and protect technology, intellectual property, and organizational security.

jobs.title: 2027 Summer Intern - Research and Development - Energy and Propulsion Systems Architecture
jobs.location: Warren, Michigan, United States of America
jobs.body: Job Description The Role: As a 2027 Summer Intern on the Energy and Propulsion Systems Architecture team, you will work with researchers and engineers to evaluate how energy storage and propulsion systems work together at the vehicle level. You will contribute to architecture studies, simulation and analysis activities, and laboratory testing that help inform the design and development of future electrified propulsion systems. This role offers hands-on exposure to the connection between battery cells, modules and packs, electric propulsion components, power electronics, controls, thermal systems, and vehicle performance. You will apply engineering fundamentals, data analysis, and systems thinking to turn test and simulation results into clear technical insights. The Team: The Research and Development organization explores and evaluates technologies that can improve vehicle energy efficiency, propulsion performance, durability, range, and customer experience. The Energy and Propulsion Systems Architecture team connects research, modeling, simulation, and laboratory experimentation to understand system-level behavior and guide architecture decisions. You will work in a collaborative, multidisciplinary environment with researchers and engineers across battery, propulsion, controls, thermal management, modeling, and vehicle development. The team values sound engineering judgment, careful experimentation, clear documentation, and the ability to communicate technical findings to both specialists and broader project teams. What You’ll Do: Support energy and propulsion systems architecture studies, including the evaluation of battery, electric machine, drive unit, power electronics, controls, and thermal-system interactions. Develop, run, and interpret vehicle-level propulsion and energy simulations across representative operating conditions and drive cycles. Analyze energy consumption, performance, power capability, operating limits, state-of-charge behavior, and other system-level measures to identify trends and architecture tradeoffs. Assist with cell, module, and battery-pack testing by helping prepare test activities, configure equipment or data acquisition, collect data, and maintain organized test records. Support laboratory work related to battery characterization, pack performance, durability, modeling, and analysis while following applicable laboratory safety and handling practices. Compare experimental results with model predictions, investigate differences, and help improve model assumptions, inputs, or analysis methods. Clean, process, visualize, and interpret test and simulation data; summarize results using clear plots, tables, and written technical explanations. Create or update system block diagrams, interface descriptions, requirements documentation, analysis scripts, test summaries, and technical presentations. Collaborate with researchers and engineers to define questions, document assumptions, review results, and recommend next steps. Present technical findings in team discussions and incorporate feedback into follow-on analyses. Required Qualifications: Pursuit of an advanced degree (MS or Phd) in mechanical engineering, electrical engineering, chemical engineering, materials science and engineering, automotive engineering, aerospace engineering, systems engineering, or a related engineering discipline. Able to work fulltime, 40 hours per week during the summer months. Must be willing to work in a laboratory and engineering test environment. Preferred Qualifications: Coursework, research, or project experience in battery systems, electrochemistry, energy storage, electric propulsion, power electronics, controls, thermal systems, vehicle dynamics, or systems engineering. Experience with engineering modeling, simulation, or data analysis using MATLAB/Simulink, Python, Excel, or comparable tools. Experience processing time-series data and communicating technical results through plots, reports, or presentations. Laboratory, test, or instrumentation experience, including an understanding of experimental design, measurement quality, and safe work practices. Ability to organize technical work, manage multiple priorities, and work effectively with cross-functional teams. Strong written and verbal communication skills, curiosity, and a willingness to learn from both successful and unsuccessful experiments. jobs.title: Engineering Intern to the Chief Engineer (Summer)
jobs.location: North Kingstown, Rhode Island, USA
jobs.body: At REGENT, we’re on a mission to revolutionize regional transportation between coastal cities. We're not just building vehicles, we're creating a new category of transportation: the Seaglider. These groundbreaking wing-in-ground-effect craft travel just above the water’s surface, combining the speed of an airplane with the low operating costs of a boat. Capable of 180 miles at 180 mph on today's battery tech (and up to 400 miles with next-gen batteries), Seagliders will unlock fast, affordable, and sustainable coastal transit for passengers and cargo - connecting cities, islands, and communities like never before. Backed by leading investors and powered by a team of passionate, forward-thinking engineers, builders, and operators, we’re now scaling from a breakthrough prototype to full production - and building the team to make it happen. ROLE OVERVIEW REGENT is looking for an Engineering Intern to work with the Chief Engineer - Viceroy, spending a summer at the center of Viceroy, our first manned certification program, working directly alongside the person responsible for how it all comes together. This isn't an internship built around one discipline or one team. You'll move across systems, mechanical, electrical, controls, and software work as the program demands it, picking up analysis, drawings, and integration tasks wherever the need is greatest during an intense and fast-moving stretch of the program. It's a rare chance to see how a complex vehicle program actually fits together end to end, rather than experiencing just one slice of it. You'll sit within our Engineering & Technology team and report directly to the Chief Engineer, who will actively coach and mentor you through the breadth of the role rather than narrowing it down to something more conventional. Because this is a newly created position, you'll have real input into shaping what it becomes, including helping define what a technically grounded systems engineering path looks like at REGENT going forward. If you're the kind of person who gets energized by variety, wants to understand how mechanical, electrical, controls, and software decisions interact to shape a vehicle's performance, cost, and schedule, and is excited by the idea of helping bring Seagliders into reality from the inside, this is a role where you'll thrive. WHAT YOU'LL DO - Float Across the Program: You'll move across systems, mechanical, electrical, controls, and software work on Viceroy, going wherever the program needs help most on a given week. - Dig Into Analysis and Drawings: You'll contribute to the analysis and drawing work driving Viceroy forward during a particularly active stretch of the program. - Lead a Cross-Discipline Trade Study: By the midpoint of the term, you'll complete a trade study that touches multiple disciplines from start to finish, building a real understanding of how system-level decisions affect performance, cost, and schedule. - Build Toward Integration: You'll work toward getting an integrated subsystem running in our hardware-in-the-loop environment by the end of the term, whether that's a VCC controlling an actuator or a sensor-fused solution providing feedback. - Learn Directly From the Chief Engineer: You'll get hands-on coaching and mentorship as you navigate the breadth of the role, with someone invested in helping you connect the dots across disciplines. WHAT YOU'LL BRING - Multidisciplinary Technical Grounding: You have real experience or coursework in systems, mechanical, electrical, controls, or software engineering, and ideally more than one of these. - Mechatronics Curiosity: Exposure to mechanisms or electromechanical systems is a plus and will help you move comfortably between disciplines. - Genuine Enthusiasm for Seagliders: You're drawn to the idea of reinventing coastal transportation and want to understand how a real vehicle program comes together. - Comfort With Ambiguity: You're energized rather than overwhelmed by a role without a fixed lane, and you're ready to shape your own path alongside your manager. - Clear, Confident Communication: You can communicate well across teams and disciplines, translating what you're learning into useful updates and questions. - A Strong Appetite to Learn: You're ready to be taught almost everything, and you bring the curiosity and follow-through to make the most of that. WHO WE'RE LOOKING FOR - Collaborative Team Player: You believe that great things happen when teams work together. You communicate effectively and collaborate with engineers, stakeholders, and other cross-functional teams to align on goals and move projects forward. You bring people together, ensuring that everyone is on the same page and moving towards a shared vision. - Creative Problem Solver: You thrive on tackling complex challenges and finding innovative solutions. Whether you're resolving installation challenges, debugging elusive electrical issues, or adapting on the fly during integration and test, you bring a practical, inventive mindset to every problem. You don't just patch issues - you improve processes, anticipate downstream impacts, and help turn one-off fixes into scalable solutions that raise the bar for future builds. - Adaptable & Agile: In a fast-paced, ever-evolving startup environment, you quickly adapt to changing priorities and requirements. You approach challenges with a calm, resilient mindset, and know how to pivot and adjust your approach as needed, ensuring that progress continues without missing a beat. - Innovative Mindset: You’re driven by curiosity and a passion for technology. You’re passionate about driving continuous improvement, embracing new technologies and methodologies to enhance efficiency, quality, and team performance. WHAT WE OFFER - Competitive compensation - Housing Stipend available for those temporarily moving to join our team - Daily, free catered lunches - Learning & professional development opportunities - Meaningful projects that make an impact - Mentorship & guidance from experienced team members If you’re ready to take on an exciting challenge, grow with us, and make a lasting impact, we want to hear from you. Even if you don’t meet every requirement, but you see yourself contributing to our mission, we encourage you to apply! We value diverse skillsets and experiences and believe in the potential of passionate individuals to make a big impact. Equal Opportunity Employer REGENT is an Equal Opportunity Employer. We are committed to creating a diverse and inclusive work environment. Employment decisions are made without regard to race, color, religion, national origin, gender, sexual orientation, gender identity, age, disability, or any other characteristic protected by law.

jobs.title: System Test Automation Intern (Summer 2027)
jobs.location: South San Francisco, California, USA
jobs.body: About Zipline Zipline is the world’s largest and most experienced drone delivery service. We are on a mission to serve all humans equally by ensuring access to food, medicine and essential goods anytime, anywhere. We design, build, and operate the world’s largest autonomous logistics system, delivering critical supplies quickly and reliably. Today, Zipline operates on four continents, makes a delivery somewhere in the world every 30 seconds, and has completed millions of deliveries to date, including blood, vaccines, medical supplies, food, and retail products. Our customers include the world’s largest and most prominent healthcare systems, governments, retailers, restaurants and global businesses who rely on us to save lives, reduce emissions, increase economic opportunity, and provide delivery from point A to point B as fast as possible. The drone is only 15% of what we’ve built to enable seamless, reliable, global operations. Our system strengthens supply chains, reduces congestion, and gives people time back. With more than 140 million commercial autonomous miles safely flown, Zipline is redefining access to healthcare, consumer products, and food across the globe. We operate at a global scale and are looking for practical problem solvers who thrive on real-world challenges and rapid growth. Our team is motivated by building systems that have a direct, meaningful impact on people’s lives and by scaling the future of logistics. We are seeking people who sculpt from first principles, enjoy facing adversity, and can do the impossible at record breaking speeds. About the System Validation Team The System Validation Team ensures the performance, reliability, and safety of Zipline’s integrated system of systems, including the Zip, Droid, and Dock. We specialize in Hardware-in-the-Loop (HIL) testing, enabling us to validate complex interactions across hardware and software before real-world deployment. Our team builds and maintains automated pipelines that rigorously test software in a simulated environment, ensuring it meets high standards before being tested in flight. By catching potential issues early and refining system behavior, we play a critical role in delivering reliable, safe, and efficient solutions that power Zipline’s mission to transform global logistics. Our team owns automation of flight testing as well to capture issues before it happens in commercial flights. The Role As a System Validation Intern, you will contribute to testing and validating Zipline’s complete system of systems—spanning the Zip, Droid, and Dock. You’ll help build and refine automated testing pipelines, ensuring that software meets rigorous quality standards before being tested in flight. Working closely with a supportive and experienced team, you’ll develop hands-on experience with cutting-edge tools and technologies while solving meaningful challenges. Your work will play an essential role in ensuring the reliability of systems that deliver life-saving goods worldwide. This role offers a unique opportunity to learn, grow, and make an impact in a fast-paced, mission-driven environment. What You'll Do Assist in executing Hardware-in-the-Loop (HIL) tests and flight tests to validate the interaction between Zipline’s Zip, Droid, and Dock systems. Collaborate with a wide range of engineers from different teams to build and refine automated pipelines that test software before it is deployed in flight. Design and improve tools that stress-test the system in off-nominal cases. Analyze and troubleshoot hardware and software issues uncovered during testing, contributing to system improvements. Work alongside a multidisciplinary team to design and execute system-level validation plans. Develop and enhance scripts and tools to support automated testing workflows. Learn how to ensure reliability and quality in complex, safety-critical systems, gaining valuable insights into real-world engineering challenges. What You'll Bring You must have completed the second year of your undergraduate studies. Master's and PhD students are also eligible. Strong understanding of engineering design fundamentals and the ability to triage and identify root causes of technical issues. Experience writing Rust or Python scripts to automate tasks or tests, either through coursework or personal projects. Hands-on experience writing Python tests using tools like Pytest or Unittest. Familiarity with creating and executing test plans or validation plans for software or hardware systems. A hands-on approach to problem-solving, including debugging and triaging technical issues. General understanding of electrical systems such as motors, sensors, cameras, and onboard computers. Experience working in a Linux environment, including using command-line tools effectively. Familiarity with tools like Git for version control, bazel for build and test management and Jira for task tracking. Basic understanding of networking concepts such as RPC or sockets. Experience working with CI tools like GitHub Actions, Buildkite, or similar. Strong attention to detail and organizational skills to document test results and track issues effectively. jobs.title: Intern, Image Analysis - Summer 2027
jobs.body: > Requisition Number: 79593 The company built on breakthroughs. ​ Join us.​ Corning is one of the world’s leading innovators in glass, ceramic, and materials science. From the depths of the ocean to the farthest reaches of space, our technologies push the boundaries of what’s possible. ​ How do we do this? With our people. They break through limitations and expectations – not once in a career, but every day. They help move our company, and the world, forward. ​ ​ At Corning, there are endless possibilities for making an impact. You can help connect the unconnected, drive the future of automobiles, transform at-home entertainment, and ensure the delivery of lifesaving medicines. And so much more.​ ​ Come break through with us. Scope of Position Deep UV (DUV) photolithography depends on glass and crystalline optics that stay highly transparent under 193 nm laser irradiation. As semiconductor features shrink, the laser power passing through these optics continues to rise. This increases the need for materials with prolonged lifetime under UV irradiation. Under these conditions, microscopic material defects can lead to surface or bulk damage. Damage shortens the lifetime of optics in semiconductor process tools, which are highly sensitive to optical performance. A successful candidate will develop an image analysis algorithm that quantifies surface damage on crystalline DUV optics after laser irradiation. The results will improve the fundamental understanding of the underlying laser induced damage mechanisms. After the benchmarking of an image analysis algorithm the candidate will then apply this to historical laser damage features to correlate to the measured laser damage threshold of critical crystalline components. Program Benefits Competitive salaries Housing assistance Travel reimbursement Intern Activities Social and networking events Volunteer opportunities Community Involvement Key Responsibilities Develop an image analysis algorithm to quantify laser-induced damage on crystalline optic surfaces. Validate the algorithm's reliability and repeatability across image sets. Apply the algorithm to historical laser damage images to generate quantitative data. Correlate extracted damage features with laser damage lifetime and laser fluence. Summarize methodology and results in a report or poster presentation. Requirements Currently pursuing a degree in Physics, Materials Science, Computer Science, or an Engineering discipline. Exposure to coding languages and familiarity with basic computation and data analysis. Must be available for 10 weeks during Summer 2027 (May-August 2027) with a graduation date of December 2027 or later Be interested in working for Corning, Inc after graduation, if presented with a full-time job opportunity. Be willing to work at the posted job location Desired Skills Basic experience in any of the following: Java, Matlab, C, C+, C#, Python, or other high level programming languages. Data analysis using Excel, JMP, Origin, or similar tools. Introductory knowledge of optics and materials science of semiconductor materials. Laboratory or Research experience. Success Measures / End-of-Term Outcomes A reliable algorithm that quantifies laser damage on optic surfaces. Quantitative data generated from the historical image set. Documented correlations between damage features and lifetime and fluence. Skills / Competencies Translates raw optical images into quantitative, repeatable measurements. Documents methods and results so others can reproduce the analysis. Interprets data trends and explains findings clearly to technical teammates. Works with engineers and scientists to refine the approach based on feedback. This position does not support immigration sponsorship. ​The range for this position is $1,635.00 - $3,185.00 biweekly. Starting pay for the successful applicant is prescribed based on geographic location, nature of position, and year in school. A job that shapes a life. Skills: • Understanding of phase gate project management tools and techniques • Experience working in a global business environment and with remote teams • Knowledge of ERP systems • Voice of the Customer (VOC) experience • Solid modeling experience and the ability to develop detailed 2D drawings with tolerance controls plus management of engineering documents via Change Order process • Experience performing various engineering tests and analyzing results • Contribute to team-driven product development projects with high level of personal accountability, and excellent communication skills • Adherence to Zero Incident Safety culture and processes

jobs.title: Packaging Engineering Intern - Winter
jobs.location: Austin
jobs.body: About fab2 The fab2 team can build anything. We design all the hardware and software needed to make chips and we make the fabs, tools, and components ourselves. We're looking for exceptional, hands-on people who can iterate to the limits of what's possible. fab2 was founded by Sam Zeloof https://www.youtube.com/@SamZeloof and Jim Keller https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jim_Keller_(engineer). Sam is best known for making chips in his garage, and Jim has been a leader in the semiconductor industry for the past 40 years. About the Role We’re hiring Semiconductor Packaging Engineering Interns for the winter term. The internship begins in January, with a preferred commitment of 4 to 8 months. We are a small team engaged in end-to-end process development and integration work for semiconductor packaging processes, providing exposure to interesting work that is hard to find at larger companies. This is a hands-on engineering role—meaning you will be actively involved in the research and development of new packaging technologies, including mechanical prototyping, experiment design, and data analysis. We train our interns on most of our tools and allow them to use these tools independently, including 3d printing, metal plating, lasering, and metrology. Our philosophy is to get things built and tested in days or weeks, not months. Because of this, a portfolio is required to apply: show us the things you’ve actually built! If you’ve shipped a medium-to-high complexity system through a personal project or previous internship, you’d be a good fit here. Responsibilities - Design and iterate on machines and subsystems for semiconductor packaging fabrication, such as laser ablation machines, reflow ovens, and automated metal plating facilities - Integrate mechanical, electrical, and optical components in system assembly, including wiring, optics alignment, and electronics - Collaborate with cross-functional teams to continuously improve fabrication processes and equipment - Hands-on package/wafer processing (3d printing, metal plating, lithography, metrology) Required Experience - Pursuing a Bachelor’s Degree or higher in engineering - At least 1-2 hands-on wet lab or lab-adjacent experiences, ideally in metal plating work or fabricating devices - Strong foundation in mechanical engineering (Solidworks/Onshape, materials selection, etc.) - Hands-on prototyping experience and the ability to move through design cycles quickly Nice-to-have - Proven experience in mechatronics or electromechanical system design - Familiarity with lasering and 3D printing (stereolithography) - Reliability testing, soldering, and reflow testing - Hands-on experience with nano-fabrication tools (etching, deposition, patterning) and metrology tools (SEM, thin film measurement, X-ray, etc.) Working at fab2 We’re an early-stage hardware startup with solid funding, world-class advisors, and labs/offices in Austin, TX, Lockhart, TX, and San Francisco, CA. fab2 is committed to fair and equitable compensation. Packaging Interns are paid hourly, at a rate equivalent to an annualized range of $108,000–$126,000 depending on experience and education. Actual earnings vary with hours worked. Internship Benefits: - Housing Stipend to help with first month expenses - Lunches daily, Dinners 3x per week, Stocked Office Kitchen with Snacks and Spindrifts - Weekly Learning & Development opportunities - Commuter Benefits including Parking and Late Night Uber rides from the office - Paid Time Off inclusive of Holidays and Sick Time - Visa Sponsorship - Medical, Dental, and Vision insurance - 401(k) retirement plan - Life and Disability Insurance We are an equal-opportunity employer and do not discriminate on the basis of race, religion, national origin, gender, sexual orientation, age, veteran status, disability or other legally protected statuses. Export Control Analysis: This position involves access to technology that is subject to U.S. export controls. Any job offer made will be contingent upon the applicant’s capacity to serve in compliance with U.S. export controls. fab2, formerly known as Atomic Semi Pay range: $108K – $126K • +Housing Stipend.

jobs.body: Skydio is the leading US drone company and the world leader in autonomous flight, the key technology for the future of drones and aerial mobility. ABOUT THE ROLE: We are seeking a motivated and hands-on Process Engineering Intern to support the development, implementation, and continuous improvement of manufacturing processes for our current and next generation of autonomous products. In this role, you will work alongside experienced engineers to improve production efficiency, optimize manufacturing processes, and support new product introductions. Your contributions will help drive quality, productivity, and operational scalability across our manufacturing operations. HOW YOU'LL MAKE AN IMPACT: - Support the development and continuous improvement of manufacturing processes to improve production efficiency, quality, and operator ergonomics. - Conduct time studies and analyze manufacturing cycle times to identify bottlenecks, reduce waste, and improve labor efficiency. - Assist in developing and maintaining standard work instructions, process documentation, and visual manufacturing aids. - Support production capacity studies, line balancing, and labor modeling to identify opportunities for throughput improvements. - Collaborate with Manufacturing Engineering, Quality, Production, and Supply Chain teams to support new product introductions (NPI) and production ramp activities. - Analyze production performance data, including cycle times, downtime, and Overall Equipment Effectiveness (OEE), to identify improvement opportunities. - Assist with production line layouts, workstation design, and material flow improvements to optimize space utilization and manufacturing efficiency. - Participate in Lean Manufacturing and continuous improvement initiatives, including root cause analysis, waste reduction, and process standardization. - Support engineering projects from planning through implementation, including data collection, process trials, and validation of improvements. - Work directly with production operators and technicians to troubleshoot manufacturing challenges and implement practical solutions. WHAT MAKES YOU A GOOD FIT: - Currently pursuing a bachelor's or master's degree in Industrial Engineering, Manufacturing Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, or a related technical field. - Basic understanding of manufacturing processes, industrial engineering principles, and continuous improvement methodologies. - Familiarity with time study techniques, predetermined motion time systems such as MOST or MODAPTS, or work measurement principles is a plus. - Strong analytical and problem-solving skills with the ability to collect, organize, and interpret data. - Proficiency with Microsoft Excel or similar data analysis tools; experience with Python, SQL, or Power BI is a plus. - Familiarity with Lean Manufacturing concepts, standard work, line balancing, or capacity analysis is a plus. - Experience with CAD software such as AutoCAD, Fusion 360, or SolidWorks is a plus. - Strong organizational skills and the ability to manage multiple tasks and projects in a fast-paced environment. - Excellent communication and teamwork skills with an eagerness to learn from engineers, technicians, and production operators. - Enthusiasm for hands-on engineering, manufacturing operations, and developing creative solutions to real-world challenges. - Obtaining FAA Part 107 certification within the first 60 days of employment is strongly encouraged for all Skydio employees and required for certain positions Compensation: The hourly base salary range for this position is $47/hr for Undergrad, $53/hr for Graduate students, and $70/hr for PhD students*. jobs.title: Intern- YE Physical Failure Analysis Engineer
jobs.location: Boise, ID - ID1, United States of America
jobs.body: Our vision is to transform how the world uses information to enrich life for all . Micron Technology is a world leader in innovating memory and storage solutions that accelerate the transformation of information into intelligence, inspiring the world to learn, communicate and advance faster than ever. Job Description As a PFA Engineer Intern on the Yield Enhancement (YE) team, you will support physical failure analysis investigations of defect issues found by YE and Fab customers. You will learn to isolate, expose, and image physical defects in advanced memory devices, analyze the results to help find the root cause, and present clear findings to engineering partners. Alongside your daily work in the lab, you will complete a focused improvement project during the 3-month internship and present the results at the end. You will set your priorities following the YE PFA queue, with guidance from a mentor engineer. Responsibilities and Tasks Physical Failure Analysis and Investigation Performs PFA sample preparation and analysis (e.g., deprocessing/delayering, cross-sectioning, FIB, SEM/TEM imaging) according to area skill guidelines. Reviews EFA results, fault isolation data, and probe/yield data to decide where to target the physical analysis. Identifies and categorizes physical defect signatures using defect references, and helps characterize new or unknown defect types. Performs data analysis to back up PFA results in pursuit of root cause. Summarizes findings in clear, concise reports (images, defect location, likely root cause) and communicates them to part owners and YE/Fab engineers. Lab Equipment Operation Learns to operate PFA lab equipment safely and efficiently, following defined safety and contamination-control guidelines. Builds an understanding of how the equipment works and supports basic troubleshooting with equipment owners. Internship Project and Continuous Improvement Owns a focused, short-term project that fits a 3-month timeline and presents the outcome to the team and leadership at the end of the internship. Completes all required safety and equipment training certifications defined by area guidelines. Builds technical knowledge of device structure, process flow, and failure mechanisms for current and future parts. Suggests improvements for the department and participates in team projects that support department and company objectives. AI-Enabled Analysis and Productivity Uses approved AI and digital productivity tools (e.g., Microsoft Copilot) to work more efficiently on data analysis, image/report generation, knowledge retrieval, and problem-solving. Uses AI tools to speed up documentation, communication, and investigation workflows while keeping data accurate and applying engineering judgment. Uses AI technologies responsibly, following company policies, data protection requirements, and intellectual property safeguards. Schedule 3-month full-time internship, day shift (Monday–Friday). Education Currently pursuing a Bachelor's or Master's degree in Electrical Engineering, Materials Science & Engineering, Physics, Chemical Engineering, or a related field. Qualifications Basic understanding of semiconductor devices and fabrication processes. Hands-on lab experience is a plus (e.g., microscopy, SEM/FIB, sample preparation, cleanroom). Strong attention to detail and good analytical and problem-solving skills. Clear written and verbal communication; able to summarize technical results simply. Familiarity with data tools (Excel, JMP, Python, etc.) is preferred. Experience No prior industry experience required. Previous internships or research projects in semiconductor or failure analysis are preferred. jobs.title: Actuation Engineering Intern (Summer)
jobs.location: North Kingstown, Rhode Island, USA
jobs.body: At REGENT, we’re on a mission to revolutionize regional transportation between coastal cities. We're not just building vehicles, we're creating a new category of transportation: the Seaglider. These groundbreaking wing-in-ground-effect craft travel just above the water’s surface, combining the speed of an airplane with the low operating costs of a boat. Capable of 180 miles at 180 mph on today's battery tech (and up to 400 miles with next-gen batteries), Seagliders will unlock fast, affordable, and sustainable coastal transit for passengers and cargo - connecting cities, islands, and communities like never before. Backed by leading investors and powered by a team of passionate, forward-thinking engineers, builders, and operators, we’re now scaling from a breakthrough prototype to full production - and building the team to make it happen. ROLE OVERVIEW REGENT's Viceroy and Squire Seagliders rely on actuators and drive systems that have to perform flawlessly in a demanding, real-world environment, and getting them there starts in the lab. As an Actuation Engineering Intern, you'll work alongside our actuation engineering team to build test setups, run evaluations, and dig into vendor documentation to assess how different actuators and drives stack up against each other. You'll spend real time with real hardware, installing actuators on test stands, building jigs, and generating the data that directly informs which components earn a place on our Seaglider product line. This role sits within our Electrical Systems team, part of Engineering & Technology, where hands-on rigor and clear-eyed evaluation matter as much as clever design. You'll be given increasing independence as the term goes on, moving from guided lab work to running your own experiments and assembling findings into a presentation that will genuinely shape the actuation approach for Viceroy and Squire. If you've got your engineering fundamentals down and are looking for a chance to apply them to real test hardware on a team that's reinventing coastal transportation, you'll feel right at home here. WHAT YOU'LL DO - Build Real Test Setups: You'll construct test stands and jigs in the actuation lab, installing actuators and drives and getting hands-on with the hardware that powers our Seagliders. - Evaluate Actuators and Drives: You'll run performance evaluations on actuators and drive systems, comparing them against similar models to understand tradeoffs and capabilities. - Dig Into Vendor Documentation: You'll interpret datasheets and manuals and work directly with vendors to understand product specifications and communication requirements. - Talk to the Hardware: You'll use programming tools like Python to communicate with actuators and drives, pulling data and verifying behavior firsthand. - Support Qualification Work: You'll help qualify actuators and drives for service on Viceroy and Squire, contributing evidence-based assessments that inform real engineering decisions. - Work With Assemblies and CAD: You'll navigate CAD models and help arrange actuation equipment within assemblies as part of your evaluation work. - Present Your Findings: You'll compile the results of your assessments into a presentation for the mechanical and electrical teams, directly shaping the actuation approach used across our product line. WHAT YOU'LL BRING - Engineering Fundamentals in Place: You're a rising senior or grad student in mechanical, electrical, aerospace, mechatronics engineering, or a related field, with the core fundamentals already solid. - Comfort With Hand Tools: You're mechanically inclined and comfortable working with hand tools, building jigs, and handling hardware constantly. - Basic Programming Ability: You have working knowledge of a language like Python, enough to communicate with actuators and drives and make sense of the data they produce. - Clear Communicator: You write and speak clearly, including when working with outside vendors to interpret datasheets and learn about new products. - Bonus: Actuator or Sensor Experience: Prior hands-on exposure to actuators, communication protocols, or sensors such as temperature, force, strain, or position would give you a real head start in this niche domain. - Bonus: CAD and Circuits Know-How: Experience with 3D CAD and drawings, and comfort working with low-voltage DC power circuits, means less time spent learning the basics and more time in the lab. - Bonus: MATLAB/Simulink Exposure: Familiarity with MATLAB or Simulink is a plus, since it's key software for post-processing actuator data and modeling actuation systems. WHO WE'RE LOOKING FOR - Collaborative Team Player: You believe that great things happen when teams work together. You communicate effectively and collaborate with engineers, stakeholders, and other cross-functional teams to align on goals and move projects forward. You bring people together, ensuring that everyone is on the same page and moving towards a shared vision. - Creative Problem Solver: You thrive on tackling complex challenges and finding innovative solutions. Whether you're resolving installation challenges, debugging elusive electrical issues, or adapting on the fly during integration and test, you bring a practical, inventive mindset to every problem. You don't just patch issues - you improve processes, anticipate downstream impacts, and help turn one-off fixes into scalable solutions that raise the bar for future builds. - Adaptable & Agile: In a fast-paced, ever-evolving startup environment, you quickly adapt to changing priorities and requirements. You approach challenges with a calm, resilient mindset, and know how to pivot and adjust your approach as needed, ensuring that progress continues without missing a beat. - Innovative Mindset: You’re driven by curiosity and a passion for technology. You’re passionate about driving continuous improvement, embracing new technologies and methodologies to enhance efficiency, quality, and team performance. WHAT WE OFFER - Competitive compensation - Housing Stipend available for those temporarily moving to join our team - Daily, free catered lunches - Learning & professional development opportunities - Meaningful projects that make an impact - Mentorship & guidance from experienced team members If you’re ready to take on an exciting challenge, grow with us, and make a lasting impact, we want to hear from you. Even if you don’t meet every requirement, but you see yourself contributing to our mission, we encourage you to apply! We value diverse skillsets and experiences and believe in the potential of passionate individuals to make a big impact. Equal Opportunity Employer REGENT is an Equal Opportunity Employer. We are committed to creating a diverse and inclusive work environment. Employment decisions are made without regard to race, color, religion, national origin, gender, sexual orientation, gender identity, age, disability, or any other characteristic protected by law.

jobs.body: What you'll do: Fall 2027 Start Date: Sophomore - $22.15, Junior - $24.92, Senior - $27.69 PRIMARY RESPONSIBILITY: The Product Development Engineering Co-op will work under the guidance of the engineering team and is responsible for design and development of innovative solutions for the Busway product line. Functional responsibility includes design, testing and certification of busway and busplug assemblies with respect to performance, reliability, DFMA, and cost optimization of the final product. Maintain a clean, orderly, and safe workplace. Work from written or verbal information, sketches, and drawings to perform design tests necessary to prove engineering designs, modifications, and improvements. What you’ll do: Assist technical personnel in recommending changes pertaining to dimensions, fits, tolerances, finishes, configuration, material and processes of parts and assemblies to enhance the possibility for design to pass design tests. Using basic mathematical principles make necessary mathematical computations and mechanical setups involved in the process of running electrical design tests. Understand and demonstrate knowledge of test equipment at on-site lab - impulse generator, current generator, Hi-pot box, environmental chamber along with oscilloscopes, oscillograms, camera, and digital camera Assist in preparing equipment for design tests – support the equipment, making electrical connections to the test equipment, attaching thermal couples, applying insulation techniques, etc. Complete test reports and all data entry using a computer, printer, photographs. Assist witness tests for ETL, UL, CSA, and other certifying organizations. Conduct required tests and calibration using design test equipment described above under the direction of technical personnel. Analyze design test results, such as temperature rise data, and make structure change recommendations to improve test results, if necessary. Work with engineering sketches and oral instructions and/or engineering to set-up and perform design tests. Provide prompt responses to design test requests to support production and customer ship dates. Identify special or unusual conditions of design test failure modes, recommend design fixes to engineering, and assist engineering in developmental work. Become familiar with all industry standards (IEEE, ANSI, NEMA, IEC, UL, & CSA) as necessary, to perform required equipment design tests. Required travel to high power labs, like Belmont Labs, Belmont, NC or KEMA Labs, Chalfont, PA to assist engineering perform design tests, such as short circuit current and are resistant tests. Obtains all necessary information to perform job assignment from Engineers and manager. Works with little supervision to act as the primary contact for coordination of improvements. Researches, analyzes, and helps specify purchases and equipment required for Design Lab projects with assistance from the Manufacturing and Maintenance of Line Engineers. Under direction from Engineers, modify or create technical drawings, material specs, work instructions, and relevant safety documentation. Relocation assistance will be provided for candidates that reside outside a 50-mile radius of Hodges, SC Skills: Understanding of phase gate project management tools and techniques Experience working in a global business environment and with remote teams Knowledge using ERP systems Voice of the Customer (VOC) experience CAD/SolidWorks/Inventor solid modeling experience and the ability to develop detailed 2D drawings with tolerance controls plus management of engineering documents via Engineering Change Order process Experience performing various engineering tests and analyzing results Contribute to team-driven product development projects with high level of personal accountability, and excellent communication skills Adherence to Zero Incident Safety culture and processes

jobs.body: Peak Energy Role Title : Test Engineer Intern Location: Burlingame, CA Department: Engineering Reports To: Senior Manager, Test Engineering Position Type: Internship (Summer 2027) About Peak Energy Peak Energy is the first American venture to advance globally proven Sodium-Ion battery systems as the storage standard for the new era of renewable energy on a resilient grid. Sodium-Ion is cheap, readily available and safe, making it the leading contender in a rapidly evolving market. Our leadership team is powered by decades of expertise in scaling gigawatt-level innovation at world-class companies such as Tesla, Northvolt, Apple, Powin, Enovix, Zipline, Solid Power, and Fluence. We are backed by strategic investment and product partners such as TDK Ventures and Eclipse Ventures. We are a team of engineers, operators, entrepreneurs, and partners driven by a shared ambition to set the new performance standard for renewable energy and grid resilience. About the Role – Test Engineer Intern We are looking for a Test Engineer Intern to support our testing and functional verification efforts for our energy storage systems, from battery to power electronics. This role will work closely with design and simulation teams to understand needs, develop procedures, set up and run tests, and report on findings that directly inform the design direction of our products. You will interface with design, simulation, and manufacturing engineering partners and gain hands-on experience across a fast-moving, early-stage energy company. Candidates should be available to begin employment in Summer 2027. The ideal candidate is a self-starter who is hungry for knowledge, holds themselves and others to high standards, and brings a get-it-done attitude to every challenge — big or small. What You'll Do Conduct comprehensive testing of functional, high voltage, thermal, and mechanical systems across our energy storage products Develop test strategies, plans, and procedures to evaluate key risks Spearhead the design and acquisition of testing infrastructure Collaborate with engineering teams to ensure design integrity and drive improvements Analyze complex test data, report findings, and drive system enhancements Identify, diagnose, and resolve intricate technical issues during testing Perform root cause analysis on system failures and develop corrective and preventive actions Drive innovation in testing methodologies and practices Interface tightly with design, simulation, and manufacturing engineering partners to inform design decisions Maintain detailed records of tests, analyses, and corrective actions; prepare reports and presentations for internal and external stakeholders Drive and participate in a culture of rapid prototyping and automation What You'll Bring Working towards a Bachelor's degree in Mechanical Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Aerospace Engineering, or a related field Experience in test engineering, preferably within battery storage or renewable energy sectors Strong understanding of electromechanical engineering first principles Proficiency in data processing and analysis tools Excellent problem-solving skills with the ability to think critically and act decisively Strong communication skills with the ability to present complex technical information clearly to both technical and non-technical stakeholders Ability to work collaboratively in a fast-paced, dynamic environment Proactive ownership mindset with a strong sense of accountability Preferred Qualifications Experience with battery systems, energy storage, or power electronics testing Familiarity with automated test systems or rapid prototyping workflows Background in reliability, abuse, or environmental stress testing Peak Energy is committed to building a diverse and inclusive workforce. We strongly encourage women, people of color, and individuals from underrepresented groups to apply. We value skills, potential, and perspective over specific credentials. If you're excited about this role but your experience doesn't look perfect on paper, we still want to hear from you. Our Core Values Speed Through Focus – Move fast but understand why. Focus on the goal, don't sacrifice quality. Mission Over Self – It's about the greater good; confident humility. Take ownership and accountability. jobs.body: Anduril Industries is a defense technology company with a mission to transform U.S. and allied military capabilities with advanced technology. By bringing the expertise, technology, and business model of the 21st century’s most innovative companies to the defense industry, Anduril is changing how military systems are designed, built and sold. Anduril’s family of systems is powered by Lattice OS, an AI-powered operating system that turns thousands of data streams into a realtime, 3D command and control center. As the world enters an era of strategic competition, Anduril is committed to bringing cutting-edge autonomy, AI, computer vision, sensor fusion, and networking technology to the military in months, not years. As a Manufacturing Engineer Co-op, you will work on projects supporting teams designing and building aerospace structures using carbon fiber composite material systems. As an intern you will have direct exposure to engineers designing and analyzing composite structures in aerospace programs, and to technicians manufacturing those structures. WHAT YOU’LL DO Receive problem statements guidelines, requirements, and reporting milestones Independently perform trade studies, designs, and generate solutions for approval Execute the procurement of hardware as necessary to implement solutions Test, verify, and demonstrate the effectiveness of your solutions REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS Must be pursuing a bachelor’s or master’s degree in Mechanical Engineering, Aerospace Engineering, or a related field. Hands-on experience with R/C and/or autonomous flight vehicles, flight controllers, or other related control systems A genuine interest in manufacturing and desire to learn. Coursework, internships, or school-related experience in a relevant field, preferably manufacturing related. Exposure to PCBA fabrication, including coursework or project work with SMT processes. Hands-on experience physically manufacturing hardware via any means (machining, fabrication, soldering, assembly, etc.), including work on personal or extracurricular projects. Software scripting experience in any language. Familiarity with CAD software, Manufacturing Execution Systems, or ERP/MRP systems. US Hourly Range $28 — $45 USD The salary range for this role is an estimate based on a wide range of compensation factors, inclusive of base salary only. Actual salary offer may vary based on (but not limited to) work experience, education and/or training, critical skills, and/or business considerations. Highly competitive equity grants are included in the majority of full time offers; and are considered part of Anduril's total compensation package. Additionally, Anduril offers top-tier benefits for full-time employees, including: Benefits At Anduril, we invest in our people. Our comprehensive, competitive benefits package (available at little to no cost to employees) ensures you’re supported in health, recovery, and whatever comes next. For more information, Explore Our Benefits . Protecting Yourself from Recruitment Scams Anduril is committed to maintaining the integrity of our Talent acquisition process and the security of our candidates. We've observed a rise in sophisticated phishing and fraudulent schemes where individuals impersonate Anduril representatives, luring job seekers with false interviews or job offers. These scammers often attempt to extract payment or sensitive personal information. To ensure your safety and help you navigate your job search with confidence, please keep the following critical points in mind: No Financial Requests: Anduril will never solicit payment or demand personal financial details (such as banking information, credit card numbers, or social security numbers) at any stage of our hiring process. Our legitimate recruitment is entirely free for candidates. Please always verify communications: Direct from Anduril: If you receive an email from one of our recruiters, it will only come from an @anduril.com address. Via Agency Partner: If contacted by a recruiting agency for an Anduril role, their email will clearly identify their agency. If you suspect any suspicious activity, please verify the agency's authenticity by reaching out to contact@anduril.com . Exercise Caution with Unsolicited Outreach: If you receive any communication that appears suspicious, contains grammatical errors, or makes unusual requests, do not engage. Always confirm the sender's email domain is @anduril.com before providing any personal information or clicking on links. What to Do If You Suspect Fraud: Should you encounter any questionable or fraudulent outreach claiming to be from Anduril, please report it immediately to contact@anduril.com . Your proactive caution is invaluable in protecting your personal information and upholding the security and trustworthiness of our recruitment efforts. Data Privacy To view Anduril's candidate data privacy policy, please visit https://anduril.com/applicant-privacy-notice/ .
