jobs.title: Construction Project Management INTERN
jobs.location: Santiago de Querétaro, Qro., MX
jobs.body: Overview Come build community, explore your passions and do your best work at Microsoft. This opportunity will allow you to bring your aspirations, talent, potential and excitement for the journey ahead. The AMERS EPC construction team delivers the critical infrastructure that powers our cloud services, including new data center campuses, expansions, and upgrades across the Americas. As a Construction Project Management Intern in Querétaro, you will support the project team through planning and field execution of new data center construction, helping coordinate stakeholders and track schedule, cost, safety, and quality to contribute to the successful delivery of safe, reliable data center capacity. You will contribute to all construction priorities, including safety (e.g., leading and driving a safety culture), compliance (e.g., MS Policy/SOX, OLC/Anti-Bribery Anti-Corruption), quality, schedule and cost (e.g., financial accountability), and help create detailed scope of work documentation and troubleshoot issues to avoid delays or escalations. Working alongside the project team in a role similar to an entry-level project engineer, you may review drawings and submittals, track requests for information (RFIs) and action items, document field progress, and coordinate with contractors, designers, and internal stakeholders. You may also help maintain schedules, cost and change logs, safety and quality documentation, meeting minutes, and project status reports, gaining exposure to preconstruction, active construction, commissioning, and the transition to operation. At Microsoft, Interns work on real-world projects in collaboration with teams across the world, while having fun along the way. You’ll be empowered to build community, explore your passions and achieve your goals. This is your chance to bring your solutions and ideas to life while working on cutting-edge technology. This role is located in Querétaro, Mexico and is fully on-site at the data center construction site. It is expected to start in May 2027 Responsibilities Project Management: Contributes to datacenter construction/integration activities on local/campus projects (e.g., new or retrofit data center facilities) and provides findings and learns to provide recommendations on all datacenter fit-out related activities and ensures sound and data-driven decisions, as well as prioritization of security in documentation, design, and/or execution, with guidance from a manager and/or experienced peers. Technical Acumen: Provides feedback to engineering documentation/designs, site, and building plans by examining and analyzing technical information. Analyzes and reviews potential risks/gaps and provides recommendations to teammates, with guidance from a manager and/or experienced peers to ensure solutions adhere to security core priorities and guidelines. Coordination: Coordinates meetings and activities of vendors and cost managers, and attends project meetings, advocating for a safe and secure, security-first mindset during project planning, as needed and with guidance from a manager and/or project team. Project Tracking: Assists with the organization of specific project data supporting cost and key performance indicator (KPI) metrics, invoices, processes, and policies in order to communicate the status to the project team. Assists with the reporting on project progress regarding scope, schedule, standards, and budget with guidance from a manager and/or project team. Drives Results: Follows guidance from others to complete local projects (e.g., new construction, infrastructure improvements) by organizing information to help others make timely data-based decisions in partnership with the local project team and stakeholders, supporting milestone delivery and core priorities (Safety, Security, Quality, Schedule, Cost). Safety and Regulation: Follows guidelines to ensure adherence to Microsoft safety standards and regulatory requirements to ensure compliance. Conducts routine safety program, security, project, and contractor audits with direction from a manager or senior colleagues. Qualifications Required Qualifications Currently enrolled in a Bachelor’s degree program in Construction Project Management, Architecture, Engineering, or a related field (e.g., Civil, Production, Mechanical, or Electrical Engineering; Architecture and Urbanism). Must remain enrolled for the entire internship period, with an expected graduation date after the internship end date. Preferred Qualifications Familiarity with tools such as, AutoCAD, Autodesk BIM, Autodesk Construction Cloud (ACC), Revit, and Microsoft 365. Ability to communicate effectively in English (verbally and in writing) at an intermediate or Higher level. This position will be open for a minimum of 5 days, with applications accepted on an ongoing basis until the position is filled. Microsoft is an equal opportunity employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to age, ancestry, citizenship, color, family or medical care leave, gender identity or expression, genetic information, immigration status, marital status, medical condition, national origin, physical or mental disability, political affiliation, protected veteran or military status, race, ethnicity, religion, sex (including pregnancy), sexual orientation, or any other characteristic protected by applicable local laws, regulations and ordinances. jobs.body: ABOUT ROCKET LAB Rocket Lab is the end-to-end space company building rockets, spacecraft, and critical subsystems that keep the world connected, protected, expand humanity’s reach to the Moon, Mars, and beyond. We move fast, build real hardware for meaningful missions, and make the impossible routine. Come shape the future with us. As a Mechanical Engineering Intern based at Rocket Lab’s site in Long Beach, California, you will have the opportunity to support the team as they develop new concepts and hardware, build and test our designs to ensure they will stand up to the extreme space environments, and ultimately deliver our fully tested hardware to the spacecraft integration team. You’ll contribute to improving our capabilities by supporting the development of the next generation of high performing spacecraft. WHAT YOU’LL GET TO DO As an intern, you will work closely with your mentor and other employees within the department to apply your knowledge and grow your skills both technically and professionally Work with a fast-paced group of professionals to apply engineering and industry concepts to solve real challenges Attend frequent 1:1’s with mentors and supervisors to facilitate success and learning while providing progress updates Enjoy tech talks and network with other interns and employees through social and professional events YOU’LL BRING THESE QUALIFICATIONS Ideal candidates will thrive in ambiguity and are excited to work in small, high-performing teams that are focused on continued learning and growth. Success in this position will be measured by the knowledge and experience you bring to the role, your ability to lead development projects without supervision, and your ability to successfully collaborate across teams to deliver results. Must be enrolled in a bachelor’s, master's or doctorate degree program in an Aerospace, Aeronautical, Astronautical, or Mechanical engineering discipline and have at least one semester of school remaining post internship GPA of 3.0 or above 3+ months of applied engineering experience (internship, laboratory, and personal/team project experience is applicable) THESE QUALIFICATIONS WOULD BE NICE TO HAVE GPA of 3.5 or above 6+ months of applied engineering experience (internship, laboratory, and personal/team project experience is applicable) Proficient in Computer-aided design and manufacturing (CAD/ CAM) software (NX & Teamcenter) for designing and modeling mechanical components Finite Element Analysis experience (ANSYS, Simcenter 3D, FEMAP/NASTRAN) 3D printing experience Geometric Dimensioning & Tolerancing machining experience Lathe machining experience Familiarity with spacecraft design principles ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS Able to work full-time, on-site for a minimum of 12 consecutive weeks beginning May or June 2027 COMPENSATION AND OTHER BENEFITS Pay Range CA: $28.00 USD Hourly You may be eligible for a stipend to subsidize relocation costs Level and base salary will be determined on a case-by-case basis and may vary based on the following considerations: job-related knowledge and skills, education, and experience. Base salary is just one component of our total rewards package at Rocket Lab. Our comprehensive benefits package includes our industry-leading Employee Stock Purchase Program (with a 15% discount on company stock), top-tier medical plans (HMO, PPO, and a zero cost HDHP option with a significant HSA company contribution), dental and vision coverage, paid vacation and sick time, 11 paid holidays, flexible spending and dependent care accounts, paid parental leave, disability and life insurance, and a 401(k) retirement plan with company match. Additional perks include subsidized EV charging, onsite fitness centers (where available), discounted gym memberships, complimentary snacks and beverages, 50% employee discount on our popular merch store, and a variety of other employee discounts. Eligibility for benefits may vary based on employment status, please check with your recruiter for a comprehensive list of the benefits available for this role. Benefit programs are subject to change at the company’s discretion. Hourly Pay Range (CA Only) $28 — $28 USD WHAT TO EXPECT We’re on a mission to unlock the potential of space to improve life on Earth, but that’s not an easy task. It takes hard work, determination, relentless innovation, teamwork, grit, and an unwavering commitment to achieving what others often deem impossible. Our people out-think, out-work, and out-pace. We pride ourselves on having each other’s backs, checking our egos at the door, and rolling up our sleeves on all tasks big and small. We thrive under pressure, work to tight deadlines, and our focus is always on how we can deliver, rather than dwelling on the challenges that stand in the way. jobs.body: Rockwell Automation is a global technology leader focused on helping the world’s manufacturers be more productive, sustainable, and agile. With more than 28,000 employees who make the world better every day, we know we have something special. Behind our customers - amazing companies that help feed the world, provide life-saving medicine on a global scale, and focus on clean water and green mobility - our people are energized problem solvers that take pride in how the work we do changes the world for the better. We welcome all makers, forward thinkers, and problem solvers who are looking for a place to do their best work. And if that’s you we would love to have you join us! Job Description As a Hardware Engineering Intern/Co-op for Rockwell Automation, you will join a dynamic team developing the next-generation of automation control systems. You'll contribute to all stages of hardware product development—from sub-circuit design and integration to functional analysis and regulatory compliance—while building key technical skills in a supportive environment. If you value knowledge sharing, teamwork, innovation, and continuous improvement, Rockwell Automation is the place for you. This position is full time, paid, internship from May 2027 through August 2027. It is located in Mayfield Heights, Ohio and does not provide relocation assistance. Your Responsibilities: Collaborate on an agile team to design electrical circuits, develop test requirements and execute hardware verification testing on new industrial automation products. Perform programming, functional analysis, and hands-on troubleshooting of electronic hardware prototypes. Contribute to associated product design documentation and test reports. Participate in technical projects such as researching new technologies, implementing new circuit design tools, and troubleshooting failures. Take ownership of assignments by understanding expected output, requesting help, and helping teammates. Build relationships with technical leads and peers to grow your knowledge of the product development lifecycle. The Essentials - You Will Have: You must be currently pursuing a bachelor's or advanced degree from an accredited college or university. Legal authorization to work in the US is required. We will not sponsor individuals for employment visas for this internship. The Preferred - You Might Also Have: Previous co-op/intern experience in Hardware Development Experience using design capture tools, able to understand schematics. Graduating in December 2027 or later Basic knowledge of circuit theory and operation, including microprocessors, digital logic devices, analog and/or DC-power conversion, programmable devices (CPLDs, FPGAs). Hands-on experience with hardware test equipment, including debuggers, oscilloscopes, and logic analyzers. The Program is rotational between various departments, including Product Engineering, Product Development, Manufacturing , Labs and Compliance, and Digital Media Development . It is designed to engage students in the entire engineering process from development, through testing and applications, and to production. Students are assigned rotations and projects based on their academic levels and engineering capabilities and are given opportunities to champion these projects to completion and make significant contributions to existing processes. You will work with experienced engineers to evaluate advanced deep ultraviolet (DUV) and extreme ultraviolet (EUV) imaging concepts, perform feasibility studies, and contribute to software solutions that help customers tackle increasingly complex semiconductor manufacturing challenges. Perform prototype testing and generate technical data to evaluate imaging concepts and software features. Develop and enhance software functionality that meets customer requirements and product specifications. Create and maintain technical documentation, including user guides and engineering reports. Analyze simulation results and communicate findings to engineering teams. Collaborate with software engineers, imaging specialists, and product teams to support ongoing development efforts. jobs.body: Astranis builds advanced satellites for high orbits, expanding humanity’s reach into the solar system. With five satellites on orbit and many more set to launch soon, the company is servicing a backlog of more than $1 billion of commercial contracts. jobs.body: Graco manufactures and markets premium equipment to move, measure, control, dispense and spray a wide variety of fluid and powder materials. What does that mean? Well, we pump peanut butter into your jar, and the oil in your car. We glue the soles of your shoes, the glass in your windows and the screen on your phone. We spray the finish on your vehicle, coatings on your pills, the paint on your house and texture on your walls. Graco is part of your daily life. The Graco Intern Program offers more than just work experience—it’s a chance to make an impact. As an intern, you’ll take on projects that matter to the business, contribute to initiatives that drive progress, and develop skills that prepare you for what’s ahead. Throughout the program, you’ll expand your industry knowledge, collaborate with professionals who are passionate about doing things the right way, and experience a culture that thrives on new ideas and continual growth. You’ll also take part in events designed to support both your learning and personal development. The program concludes with a final presentation where you’ll showcase your achievements and the difference you’ve made. Join our dynamic team at Graco as a Mechanical Engineering Intern, where you will work alongside our Mechanical Engineers to design, support, analyze and develop solutions to challenging problems with fluid handling equipment. You will build skills in machine design, failure analysis, strength of materials, fluid mechanics, and problem solving. What You Will Do at Graco Assist in new product development activities, such as: Mechanical design ideation & collaboration Hands-on support of project team prototyping & testing Design test plans and perform tests Analysis of design to applicable standards (SAE, UL, etc.) Analysis of design using engineering analysis tools and techniques (CREO, Finite Element Analysis, etc.) Review of instruction manuals and product literature Work effectively in a team environment Assist in standard product support activities, such as: Solve real problems Troubleshooting product problems in manufacturing, lab or field Conduct tests and analysis results Develop and implement design solutions that solve problem Develop knowledge of: What it is to be part of a new product development team Graco product line equipment & applications Product development considerations such as product cost, project schedules, customer considerations in product design Operational systems Graco and industry design standards Graco Quality Management System Graco customer applications and requirements Other duties as assigned What You Will Bring to Graco Pursuing BS degree in Mechanical Engineering Minimum GPA of 3.0 on a 4.0 scale Strong written, verbal, and interpersonal communication skills Ability to work independently and as an effective team member Mechanical aptitude and desire for hands on work Accelerators CAD software experience such as Solid Works, Creo, etc. Applicants must be legally authorized to work in the United States on a permanent and unrestricted basis. This position is not eligible for immigration sponsorship now or in the future (e.g., H-1B, TN, E-3, O-1, L-1, or employment-based permanent residence sponsorship). Candidates working under temporary employment authorization, including F-1 OPT, STEM OPT, CPT, or similar programs, are not eligible for this position. At Graco, you truly make a difference. Your unique talents contribute to our organizational growth and future. Not only do you make a difference, but Graco’s culture empowers employees to create their own career path. Whether you choose to advance within your current department or explore new opportunities in different divisions, you have the ability to build your future. jobs.body: Summary GrayMatter Robotics is a well-capitalized Physical AI company headquartered in Los Angeles, building Factory SuperIntelligence (FSI) through systems that learn, adapt, and develop genuine process intelligence across every part they touch. We deliver our system through a Robots-as-a-Service (RaaS) model that converts capital expenditure into an operating subscription, making Physical AI accessible to the manufacturers who need it most. jobs.body: HADRIAN - MANUFACTURING THE FUTURE Hadrian is building autonomous factories to reindustrialize America. By combining AI, advanced software, robotics, and full-stack manufacturing, we help aerospace and defense companies build rockets, satellites, aircraft, ships, and other mission-critical systems up to 10x faster and at significantly lower cost. Following our $1.37B Series D at a $7.87B valuation, Hadrian is rapidly expanding our manufacturing footprint, launching new capabilities across welding, casting, forging, electronics, additive manufacturing, and more, while scaling our Factory-as-a-Service platform to transform how critical products are built. Backed by leading investors including JPMorgan Chase, Valor Equity Partners, Andreessen Horowitz, Founders Fund, 137 Ventures, Lux Capital, T. Rowe Price, and Morgan Stanley, we’re building the future of American manufacturing—and looking for exceptional people to help make it happen. If you’re ready to take on the most challenging and rewarding work of your career while helping create American manufacturing jobs for generations to come, you’re exactly who we’re looking for. The Role Hadrian's Robotics team builds hardware and software that powers next-generation manufacturing. We're looking for a Robotics Software Engineer Intern to help design, develop, and deploy the software behind our intelligent automation systems. You'll work alongside experienced engineers on real production systems that operators, technicians, and factories depend on every day. We move quickly, ship continuously, and turn real factory needs into production-ready products. jobs.body: Our vision is to transform how the world uses information to enrich life for all . Micron Technology is a world leader in innovating memory and storage solutions that accelerate the transformation of information into intelligence, inspiring the world to learn, communicate and advance faster than ever. Micron Technology is a world leader in innovating memory and storage solutions that accelerate the transformation of information into intelligence, inspiring the world to learn, communicate, and advance faster than ever. Within the HBM organization, our highly collaborative engineering teams advance next-generation High Bandwidth Memory (HBM) solutions through device characterization, data analysis, modeling, and root-cause investigation. The team partners across Design Technology Co-Optimization (DTPCO), Product Engineering, Packaging, Test, Reliability, and Technology Development to drive product innovation and quality. jobs.body: The Aerospace Corporation is the trusted partner to the nation’s space programs, solving the hardest problems and providing unmatched technical expertise. When you join our team, you’ll be part of a special collection of problem solvers, thought leaders, and innovators. Join us and take your place in space. The Aerospace Corporation is the trusted partner to the nation’s space programs, solving the hardest problems and providing unmatched technical expertise. As the operator of a federally funded research and development center (FFRDC), we are broadly engaged across all aspects of space— delivering innovative solutions that span satellite, launch, ground, and cyber systems for defense, civil and commercial customers. When you join our team, you’ll be part of a special collection of problem solvers, thought leaders, and innovators. Join us and take your place in space. Physical Sciences Laboratories (PSL) supports the effective and timely development and operation of national security systems through scientific research and the application of advanced technologies. PSL has more than 150 specialized laboratories used to test, analyze, and troubleshoot virtually every aspect of rocket and satellite system design, development, construction, deployment, and operation. The expertise of the laboratories’ technical staff allows PSL to stay abreast of new technological developments and program support issues associated with rapidly evolving space systems. The Propulsion Science Department (PSD) is seeking a Propulsion Science Undergraduate Intern with a foundation propulsion and combustion, thermodynamics, fluid mechanics, plasma physics, or electric engineering, as well as an interest in developing hands-on experience safely conducting experiments with gaseous, liquid, solid, or hybrid rocket propulsion systems, or performing plasma science or electric propulsion (EP) experiments in vacuum facilities. Our section addresses a broad range of launch and in-space propulsion challenges and plasma phenomena across all phases of development—from technology proof-of-concept through anomaly resolution of propulsion systems currently in service. Highlights of our lab's capabilities can be seen here: Virtual Tour The selected candidate will be required to work full time, on-site at our facility in El Segundo, CA. What You’ll Be Doing · Test and application of chemical and electric propulsion technologies in support of national security and civil space programs · Assist in the execution of advanced propulsion research and development · Responsible for safely participating in experiments within our existing propulsion research facilities and laboratories · Research areas of interest may include: booster-class liquid-propellant rocket engines, in-space chemical propulsion systems, solid rocket motors, detonation-based propulsion, ordnance (explosives), propellant chemistry, propellant material compatibility, combustion diagnostics, high-power EP testing, air-breathing EP, electrostatic discharge testing, EMI/EMC of EP devices, multipactor, plasma-material interaction · Duties, responsibilities and activities may change, or new ones may be assigned as needed; training and mentorship will be provided What Corporate Skills You’ll Bring · Strong written and oral communication skills · Must work well in a team environment · Possess organizational, time management and project management skills · Demonstrate flexibility and ability to adapt to changing organizational needs · Interpersonal skills to coordinate efforts and work with other internal and external organizations What You Need to be Successful Minimum Requirements: · Currently enrolled full-time in an accredited college/university program pursuing a Bachelor’s degree in Aerospace Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Chemical Engineering Applied Physics, or a related discipline · Availability to work full-time for a minimum of 10 weeks outside of university term and ability to return to a Bachelor’s degree program full-time after completion of the internship · Minimum GPA of 3.0 · Coursework in classical physics, electricity and magnetism, thermodynamics, and chemistry · Familiarity with report writing and scientific analysis or engineering software · This position requires ability to obtain and maintain a security clearance, which is issued by the US government. U.S citizenship is required to obtain a security clearance. · Transcripts required How You Can Stand Out It would be impressive if you have one or more of these: · GPA 3.5 or higher · Active security clearance · Experience with compressed gases, cryogenic systems, and RF electronics · Experience with high-purity flow system components · Experience with installation and operation of load cells, thermocouples, pressure transducers, or flowmeters · Experience with MATLAB, SolidWorks, Python, and/or LabVIEW · Experience with NI LabVIEW, DAQ system development, and PLC programming · Experience with electrostatic or optical plasma diagnostics · Coursework in propulsion, combustion, plasma physics, gas dynamics, electronics, or fluid mechanics · Experience supporting laboratory operations in high vacuum test facilities We offer a competitive compensation package where you’ll be rewarded based on your performance and recognized for the value you bring to our business. Analyze process data, control performance, and manufacturing trends to identify opportunities for improved stability, quality, throughput, or efficiency. Assist with controls-oriented modeling, system identification, simulation, and evaluation of traditional PID and model-based control strategies. Contribute to model predictive control, internal model control, or other advanced-control concepts under the guidance of experienced engineers. Build prototype optimization or analytics models using tools such as MATLAB, Simulink, Python, or related packages. Apply data analytics, statistical methods, or machine learning techniques to process monitoring, fault detection, defect classification, predictive maintenance, or continuous improvement problems. Work with process subject matter experts to understand manufacturing requirements, translate project needs into technical tasks, and communicate findings clearly. Prepare technical summaries, presentations, code, models, and documentation to share results with engineering and manufacturing stakeholders. Complete an internship project with defined deliverables and present outcomes, recommendations, and next steps at the end of the assignment. Experiences/Education - Required Currently pursuing a B.S., M.S., or Ph.D. in Electrical Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Chemical Engineering, Systems Engineering, Operations Research, Computer Science, Data Science, Applied Mathematics, or a related technical field. Coursework or project experience in process controls, optimization, data analytics, machine learning, or dynamic systems is preferred. Prior industry experience is not required. Relevant academic research, coursework, capstone projects, internships, co-ops, or hands-on technical projects are strongly valued. Required Skills Foundational understanding of process controls, dynamic systems, statistics, optimization, or machine learning. Programming experience in Python, MATLAB/Simulink, or a comparable technical computing environment. Ability to analyze data, build models, test hypotheses, and communicate technical findings clearly. Strong problem-solving skills, technical curiosity, and willingness to learn new manufacturing processes and engineering tools. Ability to work effectively on team-based projects as well as independently assigned tasks. Comfort working in an engineering and manufacturing environment, including following safety expectations and site procedures. Desired Skills Coursework or project experience with model predictive control, PID control, system identification, or simulation. Experience with numerical optimization, including LP, NLP, MILP, convex optimization, or solver-based modeling tools. Experience with machine learning, statistical modeling, multivariate analysis, PCA, PLS regression, or time-series analysis. Experience with Git, version control, data visualization, or software development practices. Interest in manufacturing, applied research, advanced controls, operations research, or industrial data science. Strong communication skills and interest in collaborating with cross-functional engineering teams. jobs.body: At Formlabs, we’re building the tools that make it possible for anyone to bring their ideas to life. Internships at Formlabs give students the opportunity to create, build, solve, and discover in every area of our business. Come build your career and build the future of 3D printing. Internship perks include social events, networking opportunities, access to our fully-stocked kitchens and onsite lunches, and unlimited 3D printing! The Print Optimization Team takes on the challenge of optimizing the intersection of hardware, software, and materials to deliver industry leading print performance. We strive to make our products print parts as quickly, reliably, easily, accurately, and beautifully as possible. We are a collaborative team, with a diverse background, passionate about pushing the boundaries of print performance across our product lines. As an SLS Print Process Intern, you will be continuously using your problem solving skills to drive improved performance. You will support the development, optimization, and standardization of manufacturing processes for circuit breakers and instrument transformers. Develop and update Standard Work, work instructions, process documentation, and manufacturing process maps. Participate in Lean and continuous improvement activities, including Kaizen, 5S, waste elimination, and process optimization initiatives. Assist with PFMEA, root cause analysis, and structured problem-solving activities to identify and reduce manufacturing risks. Demonstrated academic or project experience applying engineering, analytical, or problem-solving principles. Must have the ability to work in the US for an unlimited amount of time without sponsorship What will make you stand out (Desired Qualifications) You have a passion for manufacturing, continuous improvement, Lean, or operational excellence. You are someone who brings curiosity, initiative, and a hands-on approach to solving problems. You have experience with Lean Manufacturing, Six Sigma, Kaizen, 5S, Value Stream Mapping, or other continuous improvement methodologies. You have experience using Microsoft Excel, Power BI, Minitab, or other data analysis tools. You have experience with CAD software such as SolidWorks or AutoCAD. You have demonstrated the ability to analyze data, communicate findings, and present recommendations. You have participated in academic projects, internships, co-ops, student organizations, or other activities involving teamwork and technical problem solving. jobs.body: Job Description The Role We are seeking highly motivated, technically exceptional interns to join our team in the rapidly growing field of Vehicle Health Management (VHM). This is an exciting opportunity to work at the intersection of connected vehicles, data science, physics-based modeling, and advanced AI to develop technologies that make vehicle ownership more convenient and seamless for millions of customers. You will also help advance vehicle and propulsion systems in support of enterprise cost reduction through improved warranty performance and greater engineering development efficiency. In this role, you will transform vehicle engineering data into actionable insights that can predict system issues and identify root causes before they affect vehicle performance or disrupt customers’ daily lives. Our VHM research combines fundamental physics-based understanding with modern machine learning approaches, including but not limited to large language models, causal AI, and reinforcement learning, to deliver scalable solutions for diagnostics, prognostics, and system performance management. GM is a leader in this field. One example is the industry-first OnStar Proactive Alert for Starting System, which warns customers of potential component failures before they become emergencies, turning unplanned repairs into scheduled maintenance. Now available on more than 15 million GM vehicles, this service demonstrates the real-world impact of our work at scale. By joining this team, you will help advance technologies that improve the ownership experience for millions of customers. What You’ll Do: Generate innovative ideas in VHM related areas, utilizing physics-based, data-driven, as well as latest AI-based modeling methodologies Develop next-generation technologies for vehicle system diagnosis, prognosis, and fault-tolerant controls as well as integration Develop and execute specific research plans, including concept generation, prototype development, system implementation, and performance evaluation Document and present results Required Qualifications: Pursuit of an advanced degree (Master or PhD) in one of the following areas: Electrical Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Aerospace Engineering, Computer Science, Artificial Intelligence, or related field of study Must be a current student Able to work fulltime, 40 hours per week during the summer months Background in fault detection and isolation, diagnostics and prognostics, root cause analysis Understanding of AI/ML development workflows, including data preparation, model training and deployment, performance evaluation and monitoring Experience in Python (including familiarity with ML frameworks such as PyTorch or Tensorflow), PySpark, MATLAB/Simulink Effective verbal and written communication skills Ability to work both independently and in teams Preferred Qualifications: Prior internship experience in automotive, technology, or manufacturing Strong critical thinking and analytical skills, especially the ability to synthesize large amounts of data involving multiple variables into comprehensive, impactful insights Strong theoretical and experimental skills, especially in controls, optimization, signal processing Background in latest AI technologies such as deep learning, LLMs, causal AI, reinforcement learning, foundation models, physics-informed machine learning GM does not provide immigration-related sponsorship for this role. jobs.body: Job Description The Role: The Manufacturing Excellence IE Intern will support the development and deployment of digital tools that improve workforce planning, data usability, and standardized work across GM manufacturing operations. The intern will help assess current files, preserve data integrity and functionality, standardize templates, and document practical ways for teams to use Google Sheets, Docs, Slides, and Drive effectively. The intern will also assist with the development and deployment of a new, digitized version of the Global Workbook Manpower Tracking tool. This work may include gathering user needs, helping define requirements, supporting solution development, testing functionality and data, preparing user guidance, and assisting with rollout and adoption. The team partners with plant operations, manufacturing engineering, industrial engineering, information technology, and other cross-functional stakeholders to simplify work, improve visibility to critical information, and enable data-driven decisions. Convert and standardize selected files in Google Sheets, Docs, Slides, and Drive while maintaining data integrity, usability, and appropriate access controls. Identify opportunities to simplify spreadsheets, reduce manual work, improve consistency, and establish repeatable standards for converted files. jobs.body: Overview Research Internships at Microsoft provide a dynamic environment for research careers with a network of world-class research labs led by globally-recognized scientists and engineers, who pursue innovation in a range of scientific and technical disciplines to help solve complex challenges in diverse fields, including computing, healthcare, economics, and the environment. The Interactive Multimodal Futures (IMF) group at Microsoft Research seeks a PhD-level Research Intern to work on a project at the intersection of situated interaction , social computing , ubiquitous computing, and human-centered Artificial Intelligence (AI) systems . The project will include elements of multimodal sensing (physiology, speech, gaze, gestures, olfaction/gas, etc.), signal processing, and real-time interaction. Our group’s research spans several sub-areas: Human-centered AI for affective and social computing, and adaptive experiences. Situated interaction between humans and AI systems such as robots deployed in the physical world. Conversational AI Agents that are socially and context aware. Ubiquitous sensing and ambient intelligence with unobtrusive sensing in the real world. You will collaborate with IMF researchers to prototype systems, run user studies, develop machine learning models, and explore technical capabilities of generative AI for human-AI interaction. Responsibilities Research Interns put inquiry and theory into practice. Alongside fellow doctoral candidates and some of the world’s best researchers, Research Interns learn, collaborate, and network for life. Research Interns not only advance their own careers, but they also contribute to exciting research and development strides. During the 12-week internship, Research Interns are paired with mentors and expected to collaborate with other Research Interns and researchers, present findings, and contribute to the vibrant life of the community. Research internships are available in all areas of research, and are offered year-round, though they typically begin in the summer. Additional Responsibilities Design and implement research prototypes for real-time situated and adaptive interaction. Explore the use of the latest generative AI techniques related to interpreting multimodal interaction, conversation, and behavioral signals. Conduct user studies and analyze multimodal data. Contribute to publications and share findings with the research community. Qualifications Required Qualifications Currently enrolled in a Doctorate degree program in Human-Computer Interaction (HCI), Human-Robot Interaction (HRI), Computer Science, Cognitive Science, Robotics, Electrical Engineering, Psychology, or related STEM field. Other Requirements Research Interns are expected to be physically located in their manager’s Microsoft worksite location for the duration of their internship. Please include a cover letter indicating which of the above research topics you are most interested in and aligned with. Be sure to indicate which of the specific preferred qualifications (listed below) you possess. Candidates can upload other documents under the “Resume Manager” tab in the top right of their careers profile Preferred Qualifications We are looking for some combination of the following qualifications (please address these in your cover letter): 2+ years of research experience using human-centered approaches in HCI, HRI, Machine Learning (ML), Computer Vision (CV), Ubiquitous Computing, or Affective Computing. Experience writing peer-reviewed publications. Experience with generative AI techniques, ML frameworks (e.g., PyTorch), and real-time interactive systems. Proficient collaboration and communication skills. Conducting human-subjects research. Experience implementing research prototypes (frontend, backend, or both). Using human-centered design & research methods. Familiarity with reinforcement learning or time-series signal processing. Working with large datasets (e.g., text, vision, physiology, behavioral). Affective and Social Computing sub-area : Background in affective computing, behavioral, or physiological sensing. Experience collecting data with wearable devices. Hardware prototyping or wearable device experience. Healthcare/wellbeing experience - e.g., pain assessment and modeling (nociceptive signals, stress/anxiety detection), or collaboration with clinical partners. Olfaction & gas sensing - e.g., experience with electronic noses, breath analysis, or volatile organic compound sensing. Situated Interaction sub-area : Demonstrated experience in programming multimodal systems that interact with real human users, e.g., robots or virtual agents, particularly by integrating multiple machine-learned components such as computer vision, speech recognition, dialogue handling, natural language generation, etc. Demonstrated experience in conducting research outside of a controlled lab environment, e.g., field research, ethnography, in-the-wild studies, etc. Conversational AI Agents sub-area: Experience prototyping real-time conversational AI agents using tools such as the OpenAI Realtime API, including function calling, and supporting interactions via text, voice, and other interfaces. Designed, implemented, and evaluated different personality styles for AI agents, varying factors such as communication style, voice characteristics, and emotional tone to study their impact on user experience, engagement, and trust. Incorporated multimodal sensory inputs (e.g., text, audio, contextual signals) to enhance interaction quality and make agent responses more adaptive and context aware. Ubiquitous Computing and Ambient Intelligence sub-area : Leveraging the latest in AI techniques to perform sensing in the real world Working with multimodal AI models The base pay range for this internship is USD $6,810 - $13,480 per month. There is a different range applicable to specific work locations, within the San Francisco Bay area and New York City metropolitan area, and the base pay range for this role in those locations is USD $8,920 - $14,610 per month. Certain roles may be eligible for benefits and other compensation. Find additional benefits and pay information here: https://careers.microsoft.com/us/en/us-intern-pay Microsoft accepts applications and processes offers for these roles on an ongoing basis throughout the academic calendar (September - April). This position will be open for a minimum of 5 days, with applications accepted on an ongoing basis until the position is filled. Microsoft is an equal opportunity employer. jobs.title: Systems Engineering Intern (Commercial) (Summer)
jobs.location: North Kingstown, Rhode Island, USA
jobs.body: At REGENT, we’re on a mission to revolutionize regional transportation between coastal cities. We're not just building vehicles, we're creating a new category of transportation: the Seaglider. These groundbreaking wing-in-ground-effect craft travel just above the water’s surface, combining the speed of an airplane with the low operating costs of a boat. Capable of 180 miles at 180 mph on today's battery tech (and up to 400 miles with next-gen batteries), Seagliders will unlock fast, affordable, and sustainable coastal transit for passengers and cargo - connecting cities, islands, and communities like never before. Backed by leading investors and powered by a team of passionate, forward-thinking engineers, builders, and operators, we’re now scaling from a breakthrough prototype to full production - and building the team to make it happen. ROLE OVERVIEW REGENT's Seagliders are a new category of vehicle, and getting them from concept to certified product depends on a strong Systems | Certification team. As REGENT's engineering efforts move through their design milestones, this team makes sure the right requirements are written, the right safety assessments are done, and the right evidence is ready when it's needed. As a member of the Systems | Certification team, you'll work hands-on with these processes and the systems engineering evidence that forms the regulatory backbone of REGENT's Seagliders. You'll learn Jama Connect and REGENT's Engineering Lifecycle Management (RELM) processes from the inside, working with real vehicle requirements, helping draft safety assessment analyses, and contributing to verification artifacts. You'll also own a project that strengthens how the team operates: developing a formal, repeatable milestone review process and, where it makes sense, dashboard tools that give the team clear visibility into what's ready at each review. This is a process- and systems-focused role, not a craft design role. You won't be running mechanical or electrical calculations or drafting in CAD, but you will be digging into how REGENT structures requirements, safety assessments, and certification evidence, and helping make that structure clear and trustworthy. You'll have real latitude to bring in modern tools, including AI-assisted approaches, and you'll leave with hands-on experience in how a certification program actually runs. If you're energized by bringing rigor and clarity to something ambitious, and you'd rather help build the system that keeps a certification program honest than just follow one, this is a great place to spend your internship. WHAT YOU'LL DO - Join The Systems/Cert Team: As a member of the Systems | Certification team, you'll be working with real vehicle requirements, helping draft safety assessment analyses, and contributing to verification artifacts. - Learn the Systems Toolchain: You'll dive into Jama Connect, REGENT's requirements management platform, and learn how requirements, safety assessments, and certification artifacts are structured and tracked across design efforts. - Map The Milestones: You'll study REGENT's Engineering Lifecycle Management (RELM) processes to understand how major design milestones — CoDR, PDR, CDR, and TRR — are structured, then build a clear list of exactly which Jama items need review and sign-off at each one. - Building a Review Process: You'll design a documented, repeatable process the team can count on for every future design review. This may include drafting review checklists, creating dashboard tools, or developing AI-assisted workflows. - Ship Something The Team Will Use: By the end of your internship, you'll hand off either a formal process document folded into RELM or a working dashboard tool, built and ready for the team to adopt on day one. WHAT YOU'LL BRING - A Self-Starter Mentality: You're comfortable reaching out to engineers across teams, asking questions, and driving your own project forward without needing constant direction. - Curiosity About Systems Thinking: Familiarity with the Systems Engineering V-Model is a plus, since it underlies how REGENT structures design milestones and reviews. - An Eye for Good Requirements: Exposure to requirements-writing practices like the INCOSE guidelines will help you quickly make sense of the artifacts you'll be working with in Jama. - Experience With Requirements Tools: Prior experience with Jama Connect or similar platforms like IBM DOORS or Siemens Polarion is a bonus, though not required to succeed here. - Interest in Safety Engineering: Basic familiarity with system safety concepts such as MIL-STD-882, ARP4761, FHAs, FMEAs, or FTAs will help you engage directly with the artifacts you'll be reviewing. - Comfort Building With AI Tools: Experience using AI tools to build workflows or dashboards is a strong plus as you design and prototype your deliverable. WHO WE'RE LOOKING FOR - Collaborative Team Player: You believe that great things happen when teams work together. You communicate effectively and collaborate with engineers, stakeholders, and other cross-functional teams to align on goals and move projects forward. You bring people together, ensuring that everyone is on the same page and moving towards a shared vision. - Creative Problem Solver: You thrive on tackling complex challenges and finding innovative solutions. Whether you're resolving installation challenges, debugging elusive electrical issues, or adapting on the fly during integration and test, you bring a practical, inventive mindset to every problem. You don't just patch issues - you improve processes, anticipate downstream impacts, and help turn one-off fixes into scalable solutions that raise the bar for future builds. - Adaptable & Agile: In a fast-paced, ever-evolving startup environment, you quickly adapt to changing priorities and requirements. You approach challenges with a calm, resilient mindset, and know how to pivot and adjust your approach as needed, ensuring that progress continues without missing a beat. - Innovative Mindset: You’re driven by curiosity and a passion for technology. You’re passionate about driving continuous improvement, embracing new technologies and methodologies to enhance efficiency, quality, and team performance. WHAT WE OFFER - Competitive compensation - Housing Stipend available for those temporarily moving to join our team - Daily, free catered lunches - Learning & professional development opportunities - Meaningful projects that make an impact - Mentorship & guidance from experienced team members If you’re ready to take on an exciting challenge, grow with us, and make a lasting impact, we want to hear from you. Even if you don’t meet every requirement, but you see yourself contributing to our mission, we encourage you to apply! We value diverse skillsets and experiences and believe in the potential of passionate individuals to make a big impact. Equal Opportunity Employer REGENT is an Equal Opportunity Employer. We are committed to creating a diverse and inclusive work environment. Employment decisions are made without regard to race, color, religion, national origin, gender, sexual orientation, gender identity, age, disability, or any other characteristic protected by law.

jobs.title: Mechanical Engineering Co-Op (Spring Co-Op)
jobs.location: North Kingstown, Rhode Island, USA
jobs.body: At REGENT, we’re on a mission to revolutionize regional transportation between coastal cities. We're not just building vehicles, we're creating a new category of transportation: the Seaglider. These groundbreaking wing-in-ground-effect craft travel just above the water’s surface, combining the speed of an airplane with the low operating costs of a boat. Capable of 180 miles at 180 mph on today's battery tech (and up to 400 miles with next-gen batteries), Seagliders will unlock fast, affordable, and sustainable coastal transit for passengers and cargo - connecting cities, islands, and communities like never before. Backed by leading investors and powered by a team of passionate, forward-thinking engineers, builders, and operators, we’re now scaling from a breakthrough prototype to full production - and building the team to make it happen. ROLE OVERVIEW REGENT's mechanical team is in the middle of a defining stretch of work: carrying Squire, our production Seaglider, through a full design and release cycle, while simultaneously shaping Viceroy from early concept into preliminary design. As a Mechanical Engineering Co-Op, you'll be dropped right into both efforts — designing parts in CAD, producing drawings, and supporting release on a vehicle headed toward production, while also contributing iterative design work on a program that's still taking shape. This isn't an adjacent, watch-and-learn co-op experience; you'll be trusted with real parts, real drawings, and real ownership from day one. You'll join Hardware Engineering's Mechanical team, helping take Squire from prototype to production. The fast-moving team values sound judgment in early design and disciplined production execution. If you have a foundation in mechanical design and assembly complexity and want ownership of flight hardware bound for the water, this role could shape your education or launch a career building Seagliders that will reinvent coastal transportation. WHAT YOU'LL DO - Design and Release Squire Hardware: You'll design mechanical parts in CAD and carry them through release, stepping into a production cycle where your drawings become real hardware on REGENT's Seaglider platform. It's the kind of direct contribution that goes well beyond a typical co-op assignment. - Help Shape Viceroy From Concept Forward: You'll jump into Viceroy while it's still being defined, doing the iterative CAD work that shapes a vehicle's geometry before anything is locked in. Bring solid engineering instincts and your early ideas will hold up, not get reworked from scratch. - Draft With Precision: A large part of your time will go toward engineering drawings and tolerancing, turning design intent into documentation our team and manufacturing partners can actually build from. If you already have a good eye for drafting, this is where it gets put to work immediately. - Support Manufacturing and Integration: You'll work alongside technicians during build and integration, helping fit checks go smoothly and feeding what you learn on the floor straight back into your CAD models. It's a fast feedback loop that sharpens your design judgment quickly. - Own Systems End to End: You'll take a reasonably scoped project from concept through integration, with support from senior engineers, and build toward real ownership of at least one system on the vehicle. By the end, you'll have a portfolio of work that stands on its own, whether you're headed back to finish school or straight into a full-time role. WHAT YOU'LL BRING - Comfort Inside Complex Systems: Whether it came from an internship, a competition team, or a school project that got surprisingly real, you've worked inside assemblies where parts depend on each other. You're used to thinking several components deep instead of in isolation. - CAD as Second Nature: You're comfortable living in CAD day to day, not just opening it when a class requires it. Whatever your tool of choice, you pick up new CAD environments quickly. - An Eye for Drawings: You've spent real time with engineering drawings and tolerancing, enough to know that a good drawing is what keeps a part's design intent alive once it leaves your screen and heads to manufacturing. - Instincts That Hold Up: You have a working sense of load paths, material choices, and how manufacturing methods shape part design. That means your early ideas are something the team can build on, not something they have to rebuild. - Steady Under Ambiguity: You're not thrown off by incomplete information or a plan that's still taking shape. You can make a reasonable call, move forward, and adjust as new information comes in. - A Builder's Instinct: If you've spent time in a machine shop or messing around with rapid prototyping, you know the value of walking over, testing a quick fit, and bringing what you learn straight back into the model. That loop matters a lot while Viceroy is still taking shape. - Real Pull Toward Vehicles: You're genuinely into aerospace, marine, or vehicle programs, not just checking a box for your resume. You'll be helping shape hardware on a Seaglider headed toward production, and that should be exactly the kind of thing that gets you excited to show up. WHO WE'RE LOOKING FOR - Collaborative Team Player: You believe that great things happen when teams work together. You communicate effectively and collaborate with engineers, stakeholders, and other cross-functional teams to align on goals and move projects forward. You bring people together, ensuring that everyone is on the same page and moving towards a shared vision. - Creative Problem Solver: You thrive on tackling complex challenges and finding innovative solutions. Whether you're resolving installation challenges, debugging elusive electrical issues, or adapting on the fly during integration and test, you bring a practical, inventive mindset to every problem. You don't just patch issues - you improve processes, anticipate downstream impacts, and help turn one-off fixes into scalable solutions that raise the bar for future builds. - Adaptable & Agile: In a fast-paced, ever-evolving startup environment, you quickly adapt to changing priorities and requirements. You approach challenges with a calm, resilient mindset, and know how to pivot and adjust your approach as needed, ensuring that progress continues without missing a beat. - Innovative Mindset: You're driven by curiosity and a passion for technology. jobs.title: Facilities Mechanical & Process Water Intern
jobs.location: Dallas, TX, United States
jobs.body: About TI Texas Instruments Incorporated (TI) is a global semiconductor design and manufacturing company that develops analog ICs and embedded processors. By employing the world’s brightest minds, TI creates innovations that shape the future of technology. TI is helping about 100,000 customers transform the future, today. We’re committed to building a better future – from the responsible manufacturing of our semiconductors, to caring for our employees, to giving back inside our communities and developing great minds. Put your talent to work with us – change the world, love your job! About the Internship As an Intern at TI, you will be assigned meaningful projects related to your educational background that are challenging, rewarding, and beneficial to the Facilities organization. Your projects will focus on cost and energy reduction, plant and process safety improvements, reliability enhancement, and complex problem-solving. You will be fully integrated into the Facilities team and supported by a network of engineers, technicians, operators, and leadership as you work through real-world industrial challenges. Beyond your technical work, you will have unique opportunities to network with other interns through social events, volunteering, and professional development sessions. Put your talent to work with us as a Manufacturing Facilities Mechanical Engineering Intern – change the world, love your job! About the Job Facilities Mechanical Engineering interns will have the opportunity to work on the critical infrastructure and mechanical systems that support our semiconductor manufacturing operations. You will gain hands-on experience with large-scale mechanical systems, including HVAC (air systems, Fan Filter Units, and exhaust systems), chilled and condenser water systems, cooling towers, and fire protection systems. Working in a cross-disciplinary setting, you will collaborate alongside electrical, chemical, and controls engineers to improve the reliability and efficiency of our facility's mechanical infrastructure. Key Learning & Support Opportunities: 1. Sustaining & Systems Engineering: Mechanical Systems Exposure: Gain practical knowledge of Non-Process Systems such as HVAC, DX systems, and plant/house vacuum systems. Operational Excellence: Support the team in maximizing operational and maintenance efficiency for mechanical systems. Reliability & Risk Analysis: Learn to apply reliability-focused methodologies, including FMEA (Failure Mode and Effects Analysis) and Root Cause Analysis (RCA). Technical Modeling: Assist in learning hydraulic system calculations, flow modeling, and psychrometric heat transfer calculations. Compliance: Understand how mechanical systems integrate with building codes (IFC, IBC, NFPA) and semiconductor high-purity requirements. 2. Project Management Support: Project Lifecycle: Participate in the engineering analysis, design, and installation oversight for mechanical distribution systems. Construction Management: Support the review of construction documentation, such as submittals and Requests for Information (RFIs). Financial Literacy: Learn how to manage project-related financial information, including change notices, purchase orders, and capital forecasting. Commissioning: Assist in the execution of project commissioning to ensure all mechanical equipment and infrastructure perform as designed. Design Documentation: Assist in creating and managing project documentation, including construction drawings, Piping & Instrumentation Diagrams (P&ID), and Process Flow Diagrams (PFD). Put your talent to work with us as a Facilities Process Water & Mechanical Intern! Texas Instruments will not sponsor job applicants for visas or work authorization for this position. Minimum Requirements: Currently pursuing a undergraduate or graduate degree in Mechanical Engineering or a related engineering field. Cumulative 3.0/4.0 GPA or higher Preferred Qualifications: Strong interest in industrial facilities, HVAC, or large-scale mechanical systems. Ability to work in a fast-paced, dynamic manufacturing environment. Strong analytical and problem-solving skills. Excellent communication and teamwork skills. Proficiency in Microsoft Office (Excel, Word, PowerPoint).

jobs.title: AI Solutions Engineer Intern
jobs.location: San Jose, California, United States of America
jobs.body: This is a summer internship starting May/June and is fully on-site at the listed office location. Company Overview At Bloom Energy, our vision for a world powered by clean, reliable, and affordable energy is more than just a dream—we’re making it a reality. For over two decades, we’ve been at the forefront of the global energy transition, pioneering solutions that empower critical industries to thrive in a rapidly digitizing, energy-intensive world. From revolutionizing power for AI-driven data centers to ensuring resilience for hospitals, electric grids, manufacturing facilities, and utilities, our solid oxide fuel cell (SOFC) and solid oxide electrolyzer (SOEC) technologies are redefining what’s possible by delivering energy abundance for all. With more than 30,000 fuel cell modules deployed worldwide, we are the trusted partner for Fortune 100 companies and innovators alike. Our cutting-edge solutions enable unparalleled “time-to-power” capabilities, reliability, and sustainability, ensuring our customers remain ahead in a world where soaring energy demand and intensifying energy scarcity are rapidly becoming the new norm. At Bloom, we thrive on collaboration, bold thinking, and relentless innovation. We believe that, together, we can create a brighter, more sustainable future while tackling the most pressing challenges of the 21st century. Department Overview The Services Business Intelligence team develops analytics, data products, AI solutions, and automation that help Bloom Energy operate and scale its global service organization. The team supports fleet performance, predictive maintenance, product optimization, supply chain and financial forecasting, maintenance planning, and executive reporting. We work across engineering, operations, data engineering, product management, and data science to turn complex operational data into reliable tools and actionable decisions. Intern Project Interns will have a primary project during the summer internship and may work on additional projects. While the project could change by the time of the internship, we anticipate that the main project will involve the following: The intern will help design and develop an enterprise AI solution that enables employees to find information, answer operational questions, and complete workflows using company data and knowledge sources. The project may include agentic AI, retrieval-augmented generation, enterprise search, API integration, prompt and workflow design, and solution evaluation. The intern will collaborate with business and technical teams to develop a secure, source-grounded prototype and measure its accuracy, usability, and business value. Position Responsibilities Develop AI-powered applications using enterprise data and knowledge sources. Build and test agentic AI, retrieval, search, and workflow capabilities. Integrate AI solutions with APIs, databases, and business applications. Evaluate solution accuracy, source grounding, performance, and usability. Document the solution and present results to technical and business stakeholders. Minimum Qualifications Currently pursuing a Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Computer Science, Software Engineering, Computer Engineering, Data Science, Information Systems, or a related field. Must be graduating between spring 2027 and summer 2028 Desired Qualifications Proficiency in Python or another modern programming language. Experience developing applications, APIs, or data-driven software. Familiarity with generative AI, large language models, or retrieval-augmented generation. Familiarity with databases, cloud platforms, Git, and REST APIs. Interest in agentic AI, enterprise search, and workflow automation. Strong problem-solving, communication, and collaboration skills. Visa Sponsorship Bloom Energy is unable to provide VISA sponsorship to interns or new grad hires on an F-1, J-1 or other visa for this position, regardless of CPT or OPT status. jobs.title: GE Aerospace Research - Controls & Optimization Internship, 2027
jobs.location: Niskayuna, United States of America
jobs.body: Job Description Summary Are you ready to see your future take flight? At GE Aerospace, we believe the world works better when it flies. We are a world-leading provider of jet engines, components, and integrated systems for commercial and military aircraft. We have a relentless dedication to the future of safe and more sustainable flight and believe in our talented people to make it happen. Job Description Our Controls & Optimization team develops advanced control system technology for jet engines and aircraft systems, helping enable more sustainable air travel and the next generation of military propulsion. As an intern on this team, you will work alongside researchers from a range of technical disciplines to develop modeling, controls, optimization, estimation, and detection technologies that are used to design, test, and operate advanced prototypes and products. You will own a focused research project and deliver results you present to the team at the end of the summer. In this role you will: Develop and implement advanced modeling, control, optimization, estimation, or detection algorithms for complex aerospace systems such as jet engines. Build simulation models of dynamic systems and use them to evaluate, tune, and compare your algorithms. Validate the performance of your solution through simulation. Collaborate with researchers across GE Aerospace Research and GE Aerospace, sharing progress in team meetings and technical reviews. Document your methods and results in a technical report and present your work to research leadership at the end of the internship. At GE Aerospace Research, scientists, engineers, and technicians innovate for the future of flight. An internship with us will provide valuable hands-on experience to help you launch your career and you will have the opportunity to work on really cool things with smart and collaborative people. Qualifications/Requirements: Current enrollment in a full-time Master’s or PhD degree program at an accredited university, in Electrical Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Aerospace Engineering, Chemical Engineering, Applied Mathematics, or a related field with a focus on controls. Must be willing to work from the GE Aerospace Research office in Niskayuna, NY. Must be available for a 12 - 14 week internship, May-August, 2027. Minimum GPA 3.0 / 4.0 scale This role requires use of Controlled Unclassified Information (CUI) or security clearance to access classified information. Therefore, employment is contingent upon your ability to prove that you meet the qualification of being a US Citizen. Desired Qualifications - you will stand out if you have one or more of these attributes: Coursework or research experience in control theory, state estimation, optimization, or fault detection. Proficiency in MATLAB/Simulink and at least one of Python, C, or C++. Experience with dynamic system simulation tools, such as the Numerical Propulsion System Simulation (NPSS) software. Experience implementing algorithms in real time on hardware platforms, such as embedded processors or hardware-in-the-loop test setups. Prior internship or co-op experience in technical research, the aerospace industry or similar. Exceptional academic performance with research orientation. Humble: respectful, inclusive, curious/inquisitive Transparent: clear communicator, collaborator, creative problem solver Focused: sets strategic priorities, uses data to make decisions, critical thinker Eligibility Requirements: Any offer of employment is conditioned upon the successful completion of a background investigation and drug screen. Due to the nature of our projects, US Citizenship is required. The pay range for this position is $1,000-$2,200 USD weekly. The specific weekly rate offered to a candidate may be influenced by a variety of factors including the candidate’s experience, their education, and the work location. jobs.location: Austin, Texas
jobs.body: Overview Keysight is at the forefront of technology innovation, delivering breakthroughs and trusted insights in electronic design, simulation, prototyping, test, manufacturing, and optimization. Our ~16,800 employees create world-class solutions in communications, 5G, automotive, energy, quantum, aerospace, defense, and semiconductor markets for customers in over 100 countries. Learn more about what we do. Our award-winning culture embraces a bold vision of where technology can take us and a passion for tackling challenging problems with industry-first solutions. We believe that when people feel a sense of belonging, they can be more creative, innovative, and thrive at all points in their careers. We are seeking a motivated engineering intern to support the implementation of Smart Visual Inspection within our Austin Order Fulfillment and packaging operations. The intern will work with engineering, operations, quality, and production teams to develop and validate a computer-vision-enabled inspection process for packaging and finished-product verification. The internship will provide hands-on experience with smart manufacturing, computer vision, machine learning, manufacturing process improvement, inspection-system development, and operational deployment. The intern will help convert existing inspection requirements into repeatable digital workflows, develop image datasets, configure inspection recipes, validate model performance, optimize camera and lighting conditions, and document the solution for production use. The Smart Visual Inspection platform enables engineers to create guided inspection procedures, train and deploy AI models, provide immediate pass/fail feedback, and capture inspection results for traceability. The Austin proof of concept will initially focus on pack-out applications such as verifying product accessories, quantities, text, labels, orientation, and packaging contents Responsibilities Assist with the development and implementation of Smart Visual Inspection solutions for Order Fulfillment, packaging, and finished-product inspection. Study current inspection and pack-out processes, identify improvement opportunities, and translate operational requirements into structured inspection workflows. Work with engineers and production personnel to identify representative products and packaging configurations for proof-of-concept testing. Capture, organize, and maintain image datasets under representative operating conditions. Label and annotate images used for computer-vision model training. Safely move, position, and prepare product cartons and packaging materials while capturing images from multiple angles for computer-vision model development and validation. Develop and maintain digital inspection procedures and inspection recipes. Train and test computer-vision models for applications such as: Object presence and absence verification Quantity verification Packaging-content validation Label and text recognition Product-position and orientation checks Region-based classification Evaluate model performance and help adjust confidence thresholds to balance false accepts and false rejects. Conduct controlled tests using representative products, packaging materials, accessories, labels, and configurations. Support the setup and optimization of cameras, fixtures, workstations, backgrounds, and diffuse lighting. Evaluate how camera position, lighting, glare, shadows, object placement, and image quality affect inspection reliability. Record test results, model performance, inspection exceptions, process times, and identified improvement opportunities. Assist with root-cause analysis and troubleshooting when an inspection process produces inconsistent or unexpected results. Develop standard operating procedures, work instructions, training materials, and technical documentation. Support operator training and collect feedback during pilot deployment. Collaborate with cross-functional teams to incorporate operational feedback and improve the inspection process. Help establish a repeatable process for maintaining inspection procedures, trained models, configuration files, and revision history. Present project status, technical findings, validation results, and final recommendations to engineering and operations stakeholders. These responsibilities reflect the project’s documented needs around image capture and annotation, model training, validation thresholds, camera and lighting consistency, inspection-workflow development, traceability, and pack-out verification Qualifications Required: Currently pursuing a bachelor’s or master’s degree in: Industrial Engineering Manufacturing Engineering Mechanical Engineering Robotics, Automation, or a related technical discipline Basic understanding of manufacturing, engineering, quality, automation, computer vision, or data-analysis concepts. Strong analytical and structured problem-solving skills. Ability to collect, organize, analyze, and clearly present technical data. Ability to follow defined test methods and accurately document results. Ability to work effectively in a hands-on manufacturing or operations environment. Strong written and verbal communication skills. Ability to collaborate with engineers, operators, quality personnel, and other cross-functional stakeholders. Proficiency with Microsoft Excel, PowerPoint, and Word. Willingness to learn new software tools, inspection methods, and manufacturing processes. Ability to manage assigned tasks with appropriate guidance and communicate progress, risks, and technical issues. Ability to occasionally lift and move boxes weighing up to 50 pounds, with or without reasonable accommodation, as needed to position products and packaging materials for image capture, model training, and inspection testing. Preferred Qualifications: Coursework or project experience in one or more of the following: Computer vision Machine learning Image processing Industrial automation Robotics Manufacturing systems Quality engineering Operations research Lean manufacturing or Six Sigma Data analytics Experience using Python, MATLAB, OpenCV, or another analytical or image-processing tool. Experience collecting, cleaning, labeling, or analyzing image datasets. Familiarity with object detection, optical character recognition, classification, or anomaly-detection concepts. jobs.title: Intern – AMHS Equipment Engineer ID1
jobs.location: Boise, ID - Main Site, United States of America
jobs.body: Our vision is to transform how the world uses information to enrich life for all . Micron Technology is a world leader in innovating memory and storage solutions that accelerate the transformation of information into intelligence, inspiring the world to learn, communicate and advance faster than ever. As an AMHS Engineering Intern in the ID1 – High Volume Manufacturing Engineering group at Micron Technology, you'll join our Automated Material Handling System (AMHS) team in supporting our 300mm semiconductor processes and equipment used at a state-of-the-art fabrication facility. Typical internships run during the summer months and are based in Boise, ID. You will be assigned a scoped project intended to span the full 3-month internship and occupy the majority of your time. Robust training in safety procedures and in the operations required for your assignment is provided to ensure a safe, productive experience. A portion of the internship will involve work inside the cleanroom fabrication environment. Near the end of your internship, you will deliver a verbal presentation on your project results. Responsibilities include, but are not limited to: Own a defined summer project that advances AMHS capability, reliability, or throughput; plan, execute, and drive it to completion. Support 300mm fab material handling operations and equipment performance within the ID1 HVM environment. Assist in product defect investigations and in maintaining tools and processes used for R&D experiments. Work with fab tool automation systems and software; pursue and resolve routine automation errors when they arise. Apply AI-enabled tools and techniques to support engineering analysis, troubleshooting, data interpretation, documentation, and process improvement activities. Work with fellow AMHS Engineers on ID1 construction goal activities, learning how to manage projects and keep construction scheduling on target. Create and document Quality Deviation Reports (QDRs) and/or Engineering Change Notices (ECNs) as needed. Collaborate cross-functionally with manufacturing, equipment, process, and software teams to implement improvements. jobs.title: Research Intern - Coding Agents & Post-Training Optimization
