jobs.body: ABOUT ROCKET LAB Rocket Lab is the end-to-end space company building rockets, spacecraft, and critical subsystems that keep the world connected, protected, expand humanity’s reach to the Moon, Mars, and beyond. We move fast, build real hardware for meaningful missions, and make the impossible routine. Come shape the future with us. As a Propulsion Analyst Intern based at Rocket Lab’s site in Long Beach, California, you will have the opportunity to support the Propulsion team in creating FEA models or CFD models of new and updated designs as well as gain hands experience analyzing critical rocket engine hardware. You will join a multidisciplinary propulsion team responsible for designing and testing our Archimedes rocket engine. WHAT YOU’LL GET TO DO As an intern, you will work closely with your mentor and other employees within the department to apply your knowledge and grow your skills both technically and professionally Work with a fast-paced group of professionals to apply engineering and industry concepts to solve real challenges Attend frequent 1:1’s with mentors and supervisors to facilitate success and learning while providing progress updates Enjoy tech talks and network with other interns and employees through social and professional events YOU’LL BRING THESE QUALIFICATIONS Ideal candidates will thrive in ambiguity and are excited to work in small, high-performing teams that are focused on continued learning and growth. Must be enrolled in a bachelor’s, master's or doctorate degree program in an engineering, physics or math discipline and have at least one semester of school remaining post internship GPA of 3.0 or above 3+ months of applied engineering experience (internship, laboratory, and personal/team project experience is applicable) THESE QUALIFICATIONS WOULD BE NICE TO HAVE GPA of 3.5 or above 6+ months of applied engineering experience (internship, laboratory, and personal/team project experience is applicable) Experience in Python, ANSYS, Simens NX, MATLAB, and Solidworks Finite Element Analysis (FEA) experience Computation Fluid Dynamics (CFD) experience Proficient in CAD/CAM Knowledge of heat transfer, cryogenics and superficial fluid behavior ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS Able to work full-time, on-site for a minimum of 12 consecutive weeks beginning May or June 2027 COMPENSATION AND OTHER BENEFITS Pay Range CA: $28.00 USD Hourly You may be eligible for a stipend to subsidize relocation costs Level and base salary will be determined on a case-by-case basis and may vary based on the following considerations: job-related knowledge and skills, education, and experience. jobs.title: R&D Operations Intern
jobs.location: Salt Lake City, Utah, United States of America
jobs.body: Work Flexibility: Onsite What You Get Out of the Intern s hip ​​ At Stryker, we believe that developing the next generation of talent is just as important as developing life-changing medical technologies. As an intern, you won’t just observe — you’ll contribute to meaningful projects, gain exposure to leaders who will mentor you, and experience a culture of innovation and teamwork that is shaping the future of healthcare. As an intern, you will : ​ ​ Apply classroom knowledge and gain experience in a fast-paced and growing industry setting ​ Implement new ideas , be constantly challenged, and develop your skills ​ Network with key/high-level stakeholders and leaders of the business ​ Be a part of an innovative team and culture ​ Experience documenting complex processes and presenting them in a clear format Who we want ​​ Challengers. People who seek out the hard projects and work to find just the right solutions. ​ Teammates. Partners who listen to ideas, share thoughts and work together to move the business forward. ​ Charismatic networkers. Relationship-savvy people who intentionally make connections with both internal partners and external contacts. ​ Strategic thinkers. Interns who propose innovative ideas and consistently exceed their performance objectives . ​ Customer-oriented achievers. Individuals with an unparalleled work ethic and customer-focused attitude who bring value to their partnerships. ​ Game changers. Persistent interns who will stop at nothing to live out Stryker’s mission to make healthcare better. Opportunities Available ​ ​ As an Electrical Engineering intern at Stryker, you will be placed in one of the following teams: Advanced Quality AQE interns work on engineering projects related to development of new products. Areas of emphasis may include human factors engineering, risk management, application of statistics, reliability engineering, design verification, and design validation including customer interaction. As Homer Stryker pointed out, “If your tools don’t work, make them work. If you can’t make them work, make some that do work.” In this directive, the AQE team works to make sure that the products we develop at Stryker will work consistently for our customers to meet or exceed their expectations. Process Quality PQE interns collaborate with cross-functional teams to support product sustainment. When non-conforming issues arise in production, it is our responsibility to perform robust root cause analysis and implement effective corrective actions. Do you enjoy deep dive investigations and driving collaboration and communication to achieve issue resolution? If so, you may be a great fit for this team! PQE interns are focused on quality, compliance and continuous improvement. They use their education to work with a variety of tools including CAD for fixture design, root cause analysis methods, LabView, and validation activities to optimize production, inspection, and quality system processes. Supplier Quality SQE interns are responsible for all things supplier-related . Stryker uses a number of critical suppliers to manufacture components and finished products, and to provide critical services. This team’s job is to work closely with the suppliers to ensure components and their manufacturing processes meet our required standards. Do you enjoy using your technical background and communication skills to influence suppliers? If so, you might be a great fit for this diverse and talented team! The role requires working closely with internal customers from multiple functions, meeting with suppliers frequently , and the use of both technical and business skills. Quality Quality interns work with our internal cross-functional teams and external sales team and customers to ensure we develop and sustain a product with the highest quality. The team’s job is to ensure we develop the right products up front – evaluate risk, ensure our customer’s user needs are met, and help drive craftsmanship, safety, durability and reliability into the product. On the post-market side, they also work closely with regulatory to handle any complaints and implement design changes, as needed, to address quality issues. The role requires someone who has great communication , problem-solving, and technical skills. Research & Development New Product Development R&D interns in New Product Development work with cross-functional teams to identify the needs and the goals of future products. They research new technologies , customer expectations, business requirements and regulations. They may work with a variety of tools, including CAD, FEA, and our Test Labs to develop new product concepts. These interns utilize their technical education to design new products and drive them from concept to production. Product Engineering R&D interns in Product Engineering work with cross-functional teams to identify the greatest needs for improvements on current products. They research new technologies , customer feedback, and product performance data to make our products better for Stryker and for our customers. Product Engineering interns work with a variety of tools, including CAD, FEA, Test Labs, and root cause analysis methods. These interns utilize their technical education to improve the safety and efficacy of our existing products. Test Lab Test interns partner closely with Test Engineers and R&D to experiment with early prototypes and vet out product designs throughout the design process. What this really means is that they get to be the MythBusters of the division. You think your design can last the entire expected service life? We put it to the test. Just like the show, we quickly design and build fixtures to simulate real life situations. In addition to these experiments, they are ultimately responsible for design verification – the quantitative testing of the technical specifications of the product. A team’s experience ranges from 2 to over 15 years with technical specialties ranging from sterilization, mechanical, electrical, software, and optics. If you’re the type of person that has the magic ability to break things – we want you! Manufacturing Manufacturing Engineer interns will collaborate with Design and Operations to deliver best-in-class new products to market. Interns will partner with technicians and engineers to improve Stryker’s manufacturing lines through new fixture development, assembly line process enhancement, implementation of lean manufacturing principles, and improving ergonomics and safety. Majors Targeted: Electrical Engineering, or related majors . What You Need ​​ Currently pursuing a Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in a related field; must remain enrolled in a degree-seeking program after the internship . ​ Cumulative 3.0 GPA or above ( verified at time of hire ) Must be legally authorized to work in the U.S. and not require employment-based sponsorship now or in the future . ​ Strong written and verbal communication skills, with proven ability to collaborate and build relationships Demonstrated leadership, problem-solving, and organizational skills with the ability to manage multiple priorities Proficiency in Microsoft Office (Excel, Word, PowerPoint) and eagerness to learn in a dynamic environment . $ 20 min hourly wage – $3 5 max hourly wage, sign-on bonus, 11 paid holidays annually, and either paid corporate housing or a living stipend, dependent upon hiring location Travel Percentage: None Stryker Corporation is an equal opportunity employer. Qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, ethnicity, color, religion, sex, gender identity, sexual orientation, national origin, disability, or protected veteran status. Stryker is an EO employer – M/F/Veteran/Disability. Stryker Corporation will not discharge or in any other manner discriminate against employees or applicants because they have inquired about, discussed, or disclosed their own pay or the pay of another employee or applicant. However, employees who have access to the compensation information of other employees or applicants as a part of their essential job functions cannot disclose the pay of other employees or applicants to individuals who do not otherwise have access to compensation information, unless the disclosure is (a) in response to a formal complaint or charge, (b) in furtherance of an investigation, proceeding, hearing, or action, including an investigation conducted by the employer, or (c) consistent with the contractor’s legal duty to furnish information.

jobs.title: Change Management Intern (Summer 2027)
jobs.location: South San Francisco, California, USA
jobs.body: About Zipline Zipline is the world’s largest and most experienced drone delivery service. We are on a mission to serve all humans equally by ensuring access to food, medicine and essential goods anytime, anywhere. We design, build, and operate the world’s largest autonomous logistics system, delivering critical supplies quickly and reliably. Today, Zipline operates on four continents, makes a delivery somewhere in the world every 30 seconds, and has completed millions of deliveries to date, including blood, vaccines, medical supplies, food, and retail products. Our customers include the world’s largest and most prominent healthcare systems, governments, retailers, restaurants and global businesses who rely on us to save lives, reduce emissions, increase economic opportunity, and provide delivery from point A to point B as fast as possible. The drone is only 15% of what we’ve built to enable seamless, reliable, global operations. Our system strengthens supply chains, reduces congestion, and gives people time back. With more than 140 million commercial autonomous miles safely flown, Zipline is redefining access to healthcare, consumer products, and food across the globe. We operate at a global scale and are looking for practical problem solvers who thrive on real-world challenges and rapid growth. Our team is motivated by building systems that have a direct, meaningful impact on people’s lives and by scaling the future of logistics. We are seeking people who sculpt from first principles, enjoy facing adversity, and can do the impossible at record breaking speeds. About the NPI Team The New Product Introduction (NPI) team moves hardware design changes and brand-new products from concept development through large-scale production and commercial use. We coordinate across design, testing, supply chain, quality, manufacturing, and field operations to ensure products are ready to build, launch, and scale in support of Zipline’s mission. About The Role This role on the Change Management/NPI team will help us level up our ability to process and implement changes at high volume and high change velocity. Zipline’s unique ability to quickly improve our hardware and develop new designs allowed us to launch our hardware so successfully, and this role with unlock our ability to expand across the United States and beyond while maintaining the same design improvement velocity. What You'll Do Build a tool that visualizes hardware changes over time, shows how product configurations evolve, and highlights hardware capabilities at specified timestamps. Build a tool that evaluates configuration compatibility across current and previous hardware revisions and summarizes hardware capabilities for specified configurations. Build a user interface for submitting engineering changes that standardizes required information, reduces errors, and generates complete change summaries for technical and non-technical audiences. What You'll Bring Currently pursuing a bachelor’s degree in mechanical engineering, computer science, information systems, data science, or a related technical field. Demonstrated experience through coursework, personal projects, research, student organizations, or prior internships building software, data, dashboard, or automation tools. Familiarity with at least one technical tool or language used to build solutions, such as Python, JavaScript, SQL, APIs, spreadsheets, databases, or low-code application platforms. Strong analytical and systems-thinking skills, with the ability to understand relationships, dependencies, and business rules within complex, multi-level assemblies or product data. Ability to gather requirements from users, ask clarifying questions, and turn ambiguous problems into clear workflows, visualizations, or user-friendly interfaces. Strong written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to document information, explain technical outputs to non-technical audiences, and incorporate feedback from technical and non-technical stakeholders. Detail-oriented and organized, with the ability to validate data, manage changing priorities, and work independently and collaboratively on complex projects. What Else You Should Know This internship is a full-time position, in-person at our South San Francisco office. We will host our Summer 2027 interns from May/June to August/September. Zipline is unable to sponsor work visas for applicants to this position. The hourly rate for this internship is $40 per hour. Additional benefits may include relocation support, a housing stipend, overtime pay, paid sick time, and other benefits, where applicable and subject to local requirements. Candidates are limited to three (3) applications within a 30-day period. Zipline is an equal opportunity employer and prohibits discrimination and harassment of any type without regard to race, color, religion, age, sex, national origin, disability status, genetics, protected veteran status, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, or any other characteristic protected by federal, state or local laws or our own sensibilities. Zipline is also committed to providing reasonable accommodations to individuals with disabilities. Please let your point of contact at Zipline know if you require any accommodations throughout your interview process. Whatever your decision, it will not be considered in the hiring process or thereafter. Any information that you do provide will be recorded and maintained in a confidential file. As set forth in Zipline ’s Equal Employment Opportunity policy, we do not discriminate on the basis of any protected group status under any applicable law.

jobs.title: 2027 Internship Sensor Systems Engineer
jobs.location: San Francisco, CA
jobs.body: JOIN THE TEAM BRINGING AUTONOMY TO THE BUILT WORLD At Bedrock, we're moving AI out of the lab and onto real job sites. Our team includes veterans who helped launch Waymo, scaled Segment to a $3.2B acquisition, and grew Uber Freight to $5B in revenue. We retrofit the heavy equipment contractors already own, starting with excavators, so experienced crews can safely take on more projects and deliver more of the critical infrastructure our society needs. In August 2026, Bedrock-equipped excavators began doing fully autonomous, paid work on live commercial job sites. We've more than doubled our customer base since 2025, and our machines now work with contractors across the South, Midwest, and Mid-Atlantic In October 2026, we raised a $600M Series C co-led by CapitalG and Emergence Capital, bringing our total funding to nearly $1B. We're using it to put more autonomous machines to work, build the field and operations teams behind every deployment, and expand into new machine types and job-site tasks. This is where algorithms meet steel-toed boots. You'll work alongside construction veterans and world-class engineers to solve physical-world problems that simulations can't touch. If you're ready to do meaningful work on hard problems, we'd love to have you join us. ABOUT THE ROLE & TEAM Every new machine type we bring into the fleet raises the same question from scratch: which sensors, where do they go and what are they used for? The Systems / Sensors team answers it with analysis rather than guesswork, trading off coverage, cost, durability, and what will actually survive on a jobsite. As our Sensor Systems intern, you'll own sensor selection and placement analysis for a new machine platform, from first trade study to validation on real steel. WHAT YOU'LL DO - Work at the intersection between sensor physics, autonomy systems architecture, mechanical integration and design. - Analyze sensor coverage, occlusion, and blind spots for candidate sensor suites on new machine types - Build or extend tooling that models field of view, range, and coverage geometry - Run trade studies weighing performance against cost, durability, and mounting constraints - Prototype mounting concepts and validate coverage assumptions on actual machines - Turn your analysis into sensor requirements and specs the hardware team can build to - Work across perception, hardware, and safety to make sure the suite serves everyone downstream WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR REQUIRED - Currently pursuing a BS, MS, or PhD in an engineering or engineering-adjacent discipline such as mechanical, electrical, physics, mechatronics, robotics, or computer science (or bringing equivalent hands-on experience) - Solid grasp of 3D geometry, coordinate frames, and transforms - Python for analysis and tooling - CAD fluency - enough to reason about where hardware physically goes - Willingness to go to mock construction sites and test sensor configurations PREFERRED - Experience with device physics, ray tracing, rendering or coverage simulation - Familiarity with autonomous vehicle sensor suites - Exposure to heavy equipment or off-road machinery About This Internship This is a fixed-term, project-based internship designed strictly for students (undergraduate or graduate) seeking resume-building experience, hands-on skill development, or industry exposure rather than a direct career launchpad. Candidates will own discrete, short-term projects that can be fully completed within the internship timeframe. Please note that while exceptional interns may occasionally be considered if business needs align, opportunities for full-time conversion are highly limited." jobs.body: Onto Innovation is a leader in process control, combining global scale with an expanded portfolio of leading-edge technologies that include: 3D metrology spanning the chip from nanometer-scale transistors to micron-level die-interconnects; macro defect inspection of wafers and packages; metal interconnect composition; factory analytics; and lithography for advanced semiconductor packaging. Our breadth of offerings across the entire semiconductor value chain helps our customers solve their most difficult yield, device performance, quality, and reliability issues. Onto Innovation strives to optimize customers’ critical path of progress by making them smarter, faster and more efficient. Job Summary & Responsibilities This internship offers a unique opportunity to contribute to a high-visibility program while gaining hands-on experience with mechanical systems, substrate handling components, and system-level troubleshooting used in advanced manufacturing equipment. The Mechanical Systems Engineer Intern will work closely with senior engineers and cross-functional teams to support system design, testing, troubleshooting, and continuous improvement initiatives. Assist in troubleshooting electromechanical systems under the guidance of senior engineers, identifying root causes and supporting corrective actions. Help reduce production labor, cycle time, and material cost through mechanical design improvements and process optimization. Read, understand, and interpret mechanical drawings, schematics, and system-level documentation, recommending and implementing updates as needed. Use diagnostic and measurement tools (e.g., calipers, torque tools, sensors, multimeters, oscilloscopes) to analyze mechanical and mechatronic system performance. Collaborate with manufacturing, electrical, and systems engineering teams to improve equipment reliability, efficiency, and utilization. Review End-of-Life (EOL) components and support redesign efforts using currently available mechanical or electromechanical components. Assist in improving system documentation, design standards, and test procedures. Document test results, troubleshooting steps, design changes, and recommendations to support future improvements and product scalability. Qualifications Currently pursuing a Bachelor’s degree in Mechanical Engineering or a related field. Ideal candidates will be graduating this year or in 2027. Basic understanding of electrical circuits, troubleshooting, and schematic reading Familiarity with electrical diagnostic tools (e.g., multimeters, oscilloscopes). Strong analytical and problem-solving skills with attention to detail. Ability to work collaboratively in a team-oriented environment. Eagerness to learn and apply engineering principles in a real-world setting. Why Join Onto Innovation? At Onto Innovation, we believe your work should matter—and so should your well-being. From health, dental, and vision coverage to life and disability insurance, PTO, and a 401(k) with employer match, we’ve got you covered. You’ll also enjoy access to our Employee Stock Purchase Program (ESPP), wellness initiatives, and cutting-edge tools—all within a collaborative, inclusive culture where your contributions are valued and recognized. jobs.body: Anduril Industries is a defense technology company with a mission to transform U.S. and allied military capabilities with advanced technology. By bringing the expertise, technology, and business model of the 21st century’s most innovative companies to the defense industry, Anduril is changing how military systems are designed, built and sold. Anduril’s family of systems is powered by Lattice OS, an AI-powered operating system that turns thousands of data streams into a realtime, 3D command and control center. As the world enters an era of strategic competition, Anduril is committed to bringing cutting-edge autonomy, AI, computer vision, sensor fusion, and networking technology to the military in months, not years. Anduril is seeking Industrial Engineering Interns to join our summer internship program. The Manufacturing Engineering organization is responsible for rapidly iterating and building cutting-edge defense hardware, including static equipment, moving ground equipment, sensors, undersea, and flight vehicles, and scaling these products in our new 5M sq ft manufacturing facility, Arsenal-1. As an IE intern, you will work alongside a team of Industrial Engineers who will provide guidance and mentorship while you work to optimize Anduril’s manufacturing operations for best-in-class quality, reliability, speed, and asset utilization. The Industrial Engineering Intern will take a data-driven approach to designing production lines and associated manufacturing processes to meet these objectives. In this role, you will work on a summer-long project where you will be required to actively collaborate with and prepare presentations to various Anduril teams including but not limited to Industrial Engineering, Manufacturing Operations, Manufacturing Engineering, Analytics, and Quality. WHAT YOU’LL DO Own and lead projects to optimize and improve systems, processes, and manufacturing operations, leveraging a data driven approach. Proactively identify opportunities for improvement including high variation processes, imbalances and bottlenecks caused by line layout, equipment constraints, staffing shortages. Work with the appropriate owners across Manufacturing, Supply Chain, Engineering, and Quality to prioritize and drive to resolution. Translate and drive action from metrics, KPIs, and reporting associated with production line health and efficiency, such as cycle time, throughput rate, capacity, utilization, and first pass yield. Produce and maintain capacity plans, balanced line layouts, staffing allocations, and time standards for manufacturing work content. Work across domains, from execution-based work to the strategic future state of a product or business line. REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS Must be pursuing a bachelor’s or master’s degree in Industrial Engineering or any related field. Must be returning to school at the end of the internship to continue academic studies for at least one quarter or semester. Must be a U.S. Person due to required access to U.S. export-controlled information or facilities; U.S. clearance eligibility may be required depending on program. Ability to complete an in-person 12-week internship in one of our offices in summer 2027. PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS Prior work designing and/or setting up new production lines or factories - from process mapping through to collaborating with infrastructure design partners and detailed workstation design Prior work or project experience with engineering design software, such as AutoCad or LucidChart, to develop factory layouts & support line balancing exercises Prior work or project experience conducting manufacturing time studies Experience with Lean Manufacturing and/or Continuous Improvement and Six Sigma principles either through previous coursework or in practice Experience interacting with data via data visualization applications or SQL queries Ability to completely own a value chain from start to finish, measuring each step of the process, creating actionable tasks that culminated in a significant and sustainable business improvement Prior experience with ERP, WMS and MES systems Prior experience with production process simulation using Discrete Event Simulation software (PlantSim, Simio, FlexSim, or similar) Prior work experience or project experience applying Industrial Engineering / Lean Methodologies Ability to read technical documentation such as facility drawings, assembly drawings, technical specifications and procedures for manufacturing processes for electronics, mechanical and electromechanical assembly, system tests, and/or structures work Ability to work through ambiguity and be a self-starter Motivated to plan aggressively, accept challenges, take responsibility for assignments, and deliver objectives on time Strong skills - especially in areas of teamwork, drive for results, and business acumen US Hourly Range $28 — $40 USD The salary range for this role is an estimate based on a wide range of compensation factors, inclusive of base salary only. Actual salary offer may vary based on (but not limited to) work experience, education and/or training, critical skills, and/or business considerations. Highly competitive equity grants are included in the majority of full time offers; and are considered part of Anduril's total compensation package. Our comprehensive, competitive benefits package (available at little to no cost to employees) ensures you’re supported in health, recovery, and whatever comes next. For more information, Explore Our Benefits . jobs.title: Mission Integration Engineer Internship (Spring or Summer 2027)
jobs.location: Los Angeles
jobs.body: Spacecraft represent the most pressing unmet need across the entire aerospace industry. As more launch vehicles come online and the cost to orbit decreases, more companies launching payloads to space continue to emerge. For the first time in history, this influx of payload companies combined with reduced launch costs has resulted in a massive increase in need for commercial spacecraft platforms, known as satellite buses. These buses hold the payloads of our customers and are flown on launch vehicles. Apex manufactures these satellite buses at scale using a combination of software, vertical integration, and hardware that is designed for manufacturing. Our spacecraft enable the future of society: ranging from earth observation to communications and more. We’d love for you to join us on our mission of providing humankind access to the galaxy beyond our planet. ABOUT THE ROLE We are seeking talented engineering students to work closely with Apex’s Mission Integration team for an exciting internship opportunity. This role is ideal for someone who is passionate about space systems, eager to understand how spacecraft, launch vehicles, and ground systems come together, and motivated to learn how real missions are designed, integrated, and flown. As a Mission Integration Engineer Intern, you will support system-level mission planning and integration activities across active programs. You’ll gain exposure to end-to-end mission architecture, customer requirements, and cross-functional engineering collaboration. This role offers a unique opportunity to approach complex mission challenges from a systems perspective, with a focus on reliability, performance, and mission success. INTERNSHIP EXPERIENCE AT APEX During the internship program at Apex, you’ll gain hands-on experience and meaningful professional growth. You’ll be assigned a mission-focused summer project that allows you to contribute directly to real spacecraft programs. Throughout the project, you’ll work closely with a dedicated mentor from the Mission Integration team while participating in technical learning sessions designed to deepen your understanding of satellite systems, launch environments, and mission operations. You’ll also connect with fellow interns and Apex engineers through community events and team activities, making this a well-rounded experience designed to launch your career in aerospace systems engineering. MISSION INTEGRATION ENGINEERING: INTERNSHIP FOCUS Mission Integration Engineer Interns will assist with system-level mission integration activities across spacecraft programs. Responsibilities may include: - Supporting mission architecture definition across spacecraft, launch vehicle, and operations elements - Assisting with mission analysis tasks such as orbital mechanics, deployment concepts, and trajectory trade studies - Helping generate and maintain mission-specific technical budgets (mass, power, data, pointing, etc.) - Supporting requirements analysis, verification, and validation activities - Assisting in the development of technical documentation, interface definitions, and integration procedures - Collaborating with mechanical, electrical, software, and operations teams to ensure system compatibility - Participating in internal design reviews, customer meetings, and technical discussions - Learning how technical risks are identified, assessed, and mitigated at the system level This role emphasizes systems thinking, cross-disciplinary collaboration, and clear technical communication. REQUIREMENTS - Graduating in Fall 2027 or Spring 2028 - Pursuing a BS or MS in Aerospace Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Electrical Engineering, or a related field - Strong interest in spacecraft systems, mission design, and space operations - Coursework or project experience related to orbital mechanics, space systems, or systems engineering preferred - Familiarity with tools such as Python, MATLAB, STK, GMAT, or similar analysis tools is a plus - Strong organizational skills and attention to detail - Ability to communicate technical concepts clearly and work effectively in a team environment - U.S. Person status required due to access to export-controlled data COMMITMENT This internship will begin in March 2027 or June 2027 and offers both full-time (40 hours/week) and part-time (minimum 20 hours/week) options. - Full-time interns should be available to pause or adjust academic commitments (such as taking a semester off or enrolling part-time) for the duration of the 10–12 week program - Part-time interns must maintain consistent availability during standard business hours to collaborate with their teams COMPENSATION $45/hour #LI-RC1 WHY JOIN APEX? Apex believes in creating a work environment that you look forward to embracing every day. Our employees love working at Apex, and we want you to love it too. We're a fast-growing startup that has raised more than $500M in funding, and we invest heavily in our people from day one. WHAT WE OFFER FOR FULL-TIME EMPLOYEES: - Shared upside: Receive equity in Apex, letting you benefit from the work you create - Best-in-class healthcare: 100% company-paid medical, dental, and vision for you and your dependents, plus $100k life insurance at no cost - Comprehensive PTO package: Starting at 15 days vacation, growing to 20+ days annually, plus 10 paid holidays - Competitive 401(k) plan: Generous matching - 100% match on first 3%, 50% on next 2% - 8 weeks paid parental leave: Plus childcare reimbursement up to $350/day for work-related travel - Daily catered lunch and unlimited snacks: To keep you fueled throughout the day - Vibrant community: Monthly office socials, pickleball tournaments, run club, and gatherings for you and your family - Your dream desk setup: All the tools you need to be your most productive self - World-class Playa Vista office: With the benefit of in-person collaboration with amazing coworkers and flexibility to integrate work and life - Real impact opportunity: Work alongside experts from aerospace, new space, and other cutting-edge industries to make a lasting difference ADDITIONAL INFORMATION: Compensation ranges are set by role, level, location, and alignment with market data. A candidate's specific level and base pay are determined case by case and may vary with job-related skills, education, experience, technical capabilities, and internal equity. Beyond base salary, full-time hires are also eligible for long-term incentives in the form of stock options, along with medical, dental, and vision coverage and a 401(k) retirement plan. ITAR REQUIREMENTS Apex's work is governed by U.S. export control laws, including the International Traffic in Arms Regulations (ITAR) and the Export Administration Regulations (EAR). To be eligible for this role, applicants must either (1) qualify as a U.S. Person, meaning a U.S. citizen or national, a lawful permanent resident (green card holder), a refugee admitted under 8 U.S.C. § 1157, or an individual granted asylum under 8 U.S.C. § 1158, or (2) be able to obtain the required export authorizations from the U.S. Department of State, the U.S. Department of Commerce, or another applicable U.S. government agency. You can learn more about ITAR here https://www.pmddtc.state.gov/?id=ddtc_kb_article_page&sys_id=24d528fddbfc930044f9ff621f961987. jobs.title: 2027 Internship Product Intern
jobs.location: San Francisco, CA
jobs.body: JOIN THE TEAM BRINGING AUTONOMY TO THE BUILT WORLD At Bedrock, we're moving AI out of the lab and onto real job sites. Our team includes veterans who helped launch Waymo, scaled Segment to a $3.2B acquisition, and grew Uber Freight to $5B in revenue. We retrofit the heavy equipment contractors already own, starting with excavators, so experienced crews can safely take on more projects and deliver more of the critical infrastructure our society needs. In August 2026, Bedrock-equipped excavators began doing fully autonomous, paid work on live commercial job sites. We've more than doubled our customer base since 2025, and our machines now work with contractors across the South, Midwest, and Mid-Atlantic In October 2026, we raised a $600M Series C co-led by CapitalG and Emergence Capital, bringing our total funding to nearly $1B. We're using it to put more autonomous machines to work, build the field and operations teams behind every deployment, and expand into new machine types and job-site tasks. This is where algorithms meet steel-toed boots. You'll work alongside construction veterans and world-class engineers to solve physical-world problems that simulations can't touch. If you're ready to do meaningful work on hard problems, we'd love to have you join us. ABOUT THE ROLE & TEAM Bedrock's Product team decides what our autonomous machines should learn to do next. We also make sure the people who work alongside them get real value from them: operators, site managers and the construction companies we partner with. Our problems rarely arrive as specs. Which task or machine type is worth taking on next? How do you turn "digs like an expert" into a number you can measure? What does a partner need to see before trusting a 40-ton machine on their site? As our Product intern, you'll get a problem like that, not a task list, and own it for the summer. You'll frame it, work out the answer, build what's needed, and bring the team a recommendation they can act on. You'll work the way our team does: with AI tools in hand, going from question to working prototype in days, not weeks. WHAT YOU'LL DO - Own an open product problem end to end: frame it, find the data and the people who know, decide what to build, and ship it before the summer ends - Turn fleet data from real jobsites into decisions: how well our machines perform, where they struggle, and what that means for what we build next - Prototype with AI coding tools and agents: internal tools, data pipelines, automated workflows, and working demos that make an idea concrete instead of slides about it - Spend time at our field sites with operators and site teams, and turn what you see into requirements engineers can build against - Work across autonomy, evaluation, operations and commercial teams to pressure-test ideas and unblock yourself - Write up your findings and present a clear recommendation to leadership: what you found, what you built, and what we should do next WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR REQUIRED - Currently pursuing a BS or MS in computer science, engineering, math, economics or another technical or quantitative field, or bringing equivalent experience building things - A track record of agency: you've taken on a problem nobody assigned you (a project, a tool, a company, a research question) and carried it to a real result - AI-native: you use tools like Claude Code, Cursor or Codex every day to build, analyze and write, and you know how to check their output and when not to trust it - Hands-on with data: Python or SQL, plus comfort reading code and following a technical discussion with engineers - Clear, concise writing: you can turn a messy problem into a one-page recommendation someone can act on - Willingness to spend time at our field sites, in PPE, around heavy equipment PREFERRED - Something you built that real people use: an app, an internal tool, an open-source project, a startup - Prior product, engineering or founding-team experience at a startup - Experience with robotics, autonomy, ML or data-heavy products - Interest in construction or other physical-world industries; no prior experience needed About This Internship This is a fixed-term, project-based internship designed strictly for students (undergraduate or graduate) seeking resume-building experience, hands-on skill development, or industry exposure rather than a direct career launchpad. Candidates will own discrete, short-term projects that can be fully completed within the internship timeframe. jobs.body: MANUFACTURING ENGINEERING INTERN, CNC MACHINING (SUMMER 2027) Freeform builds AI-native manufacturing systems that unify software, hardware, and physics to produce industrial-scale parts at the speed of human ideation. By treating manufacturing as a single integrated system, we unlock a new era of innovation where complex hardware is designed, built, and scaled without limits. As a Manufacturing Engineering Intern (CNC Machining), you will play a critical role in achieving Freeform’s goal of becoming the world leader in the manufacturing of high-value metal 3D printed parts. You will be responsible for developing, implementing, and optimizing CNC programs for precision machining operations as well as working closely with our engineers and machinist to establish machining standards for Freeform’s high-volume, vertically integrated machining workflow. You’ll use top of the line multi-axis machines - including DMG Mori and Haas - to develop complex geometries and refine machining processes for maximum efficiency, quality, and repeatability. If you want to be at the forefront of the next era of manufacturing technology, we’d love to hear from you! 3D printing experience is not required to be successful here—we look for smart, motivated, and collaborative individuals who love tackling complex challenges and building world-class technology! control processes, industry standards, and safety regulations Own an intern project from scoping through implementation, and present results to the team at the end of the term Basic Qualifications: or Hypermill Experience with 5-axis machines Experience with DMG Mori and Siemens controls Experience machining hard metals such as titanium or Inconel Exposure to automation programming for probe alignment, in-situ quality checks, and adaptive process compensation based on measurement feedback Familiarity with metal 3D printed parts and their post-processing requirements Familiarity with machining castings or forgings Strong problem-solving skills and a hands-on approach to debugging machining processes Experience with quality control tools, including CMM, micrometers, and thread gauges Ability to work with power tools, hand tools, and other shop equipment (training provided for cranes, forklifts, and other heavy equipment) Comfortable lifting/moving up to 50 lbs and standing roof. We help companies connect, protect, analyze, and act on their data and applications wherever they live, from edge to cloud, so they can turn insights into outcomes at the speed required to thrive in today’s complex world. Our culture thrives on finding new and better ways to accelerate what’s next. We know varied backgrounds are valued and succeed here. We have the flexibility to manage our work and personal needs. Job Description: The Systems Architecture Lab is currently seeking highly qualified, self-motivated interns to accelerate research towards new applications, core methodologies and technologies in computing systems architecture with a focus on technologies for sustainability at HPE Labs. HPE Labs is an international research organization with its headquarters and largest facility located in Milpitas, California. As the central research organization for Hewlett Packard Enterprise (HPE), HPE Labs' purpose is to deliver breakthrough technologies and technology advancements that provide a competitive advantage for the company, by investing in fundamental science and technology in areas of interest to HPE and getting the resulting technologies ready for adoption into new and existing markets. The Systems Architecture research team is diverse, with a broad range of skillsets and expertise that enables the exploration and development of new ideas not possible in more traditional monolithic research organizations. We are seeking highly qualified candidates to join one of our research teams as an intern, with the possibility of longer-term co-innovation and collaboration. We expect all our researchers (including interns and post-docs) to provide thought leadership and technical influence both internally and externally to HPE, as well as take innovative ideas and make them real – contributing along the full range from initial novel ideas to design, development, implementation, evaluation, and technology transfer. Deep understanding of the relevant environment, ecosystem, trends, and literature. Excellent research and development skills. Ability to innovate, make research contributions, and bring ideas to reality in compelling ways. Excellent written and verbal communication skills; mastery in English. Strong systems programming and software engineering skills Demonstrated ability to generate, frame, and carry out leadership research as shown, for example, by papers published in top-tier conferences or journals. Working knowledge of Compiler Technologies and Machine Learning Basic knowledge of computer architecture and server hardware Depending on project the following skills may be preferred: Familiarity with designing, implementing, and managing cloud architecture. Knowledge of hybrid and multi-cloud strategies, including integration with on-premises infrastructure. Knowledge of implementing green data center practices, including energy-efficient technologies and cooling optimization. Understanding of sustainability regulations, standards, and best practices as they apply to data center design and operation. Familiarity with workload scheduling, resource allocation, and optimization in distributed computing environments. Experience programming in C, C++, Python, Go, etc. Knowledge of programming frameworks and libraries such as HPC Mercury, ZeroMQ, CUDA, OpenCL, Libfabric, Pytorch, Simplivity and Kubernetes and GPU programming is a plus. Experience with at least one cloud orchestration and management tools like Docker, Kubernetes, Slurm, Apache Mesos, etc. Experience with serverless platforms like Knative, OpenFaas, etc. Preferred knowledge of Data Analytics and Applied Mathematics are a plus. jobs.title: Undergraduate Engineering Intern - Additive Manufacturing
jobs.location: Rochester, MN, United States
jobs.body: This undergraduate internship is a full-time position Summer-Fall 2027 (May or June through December) on site in Rochester, Minnesota. The primary purpose of the Undergraduate Engineer Internship is to provide an engineering student with relevant engineering experience. One or more mentors will be assigned to the intern to provide instruction, guidance and to assess performance, as well as be a technical resource for questions. The intern is responsible for learning the procedures and processes of the Division of Engineering and the assigned work unit. In addition, the intern will be given selected engineering work assignments to reinforce the learning experience and to provide benefit to the work unit. The engineering assignments may include designing components, developing a project strategy, gathering user needs, requirements and specifications, evaluating commercial components, prototyping, performing design verification and design validation, troubleshooting, and participating in design reviews. All assignments are within the context of the Division of Engineering Quality Management System (including safety risk management) and are performed in a multi-disciplinary development environment. The intern will be responsible for completing all internship-related assignments and reports for both Mayo and the participating educational facility (if applicable). The Additive Manufacturing (AM) intern will be assigned to the Additive Manufacturing Facility (AMF) in the Mechanical Fabrication Unit within the Division of Engineering (DOE). The Mechanical Fabrication Unit leverages mechanical designer, technician, machinist, and engineer expertise as part of DOE’s multidisciplinary approach to developing unique devices and systems for Mayo Clinic providers and researchers. The AMF, a dedicated Mayo Clinic 3D printing space, houses a titanium printer, a variety of polymer printers, and a suite of post-processing equipment. The parts fabricated here support the development of one-of-a-kind medical devices, laboratory instruments, and other products in service to Mayo Clinic patients. DOE designers, technicians, machinists, and engineers iteratively print concept models, functional prototypes, and end-use parts for projects undertaken at the request of Mayo Clinic staff members. The application of AM accelerates the development cycle from initial request through final product by providing parts for faster form, fit, and function evaluation. The candidate will collaborate with designers, technicians, and engineers, and project managers on a variety of project needs. Their project responsibilities will encompass computer-aided design (CAD) using SolidWorks, prototype development with AM, verification testing, and engineering documentation. They will receive guidance and work direction from one or more mentors assigned to them. The candidate will perform hands-on work with both metal and polymer additive manufacturing technologies and will take on tasks from their mentors, including the Additive Manufacturing Facility Coordinator, Metal Lead, and Polymer Lead.​​ The ideal candidate will have experience with 3D printing technologies using one or more feedstock types. Basic understanding of AM processes and material science is preferred. The incumbent must be enrolled in an engineering, management information systems, or other technology-related degree program from an accredited college or university and have completed a minimum of four semesters – or the equivalent – of instruction toward their degree. To be considered for this position please attach the following to your application: 3.3 GPA requirement or higher undergraduate transcript resume Applicants are strongly encouraged to include a cover letter Applicants are strongly encouraged to include a sample of academic work (e.g. screenshots of models or drawings, a lab report)

jobs.title: Research Intern - Extended Perception Interaction Cognition (EPIC)
jobs.location: Redmond, WA, US
jobs.body: Overview Research Internships at Microsoft provide a dynamic environment for research careers with a network of world-class research labs led by globally-recognized scientists and engineers, who pursue innovation in a range of scientific and technical disciplines to help solve complex challenges in diverse fields, including computing, healthcare, economics, and the environment. This position is for a research internship with the EPIC (Extended Perception, Interaction & Cognition) research group in Microsoft Research’s Redmond Lab. We have multiple positions available. Research Internships will be focused on creating new interactive experiences that “blend artificial and human intelligence”. Topics range from coupling the power of generative Artificial Intelligence (AI) techniques with interaction design to reinvent how we work with content, to building the next generation of multi-modal interfaces adapting in real time to user tasks and contexts. Key skills sought for this internship include: Generative AI: Large Language Models (LLMs), Vision Language Models (VLMs), Stable Diffusion, video/world/action models, real-time models, multi-agent development, and related technologies Human-Computer Interaction (HCI) system building and agentic development: Experience building interactive prototypes with TypeScript, Node.js, and React, using coding agents and agentic workflows to accelerate development. Demonstrated programming and software architecture fundamentals are essential to guide agents, review generated code, and validate system behavior. Additional relevant skills (depending on projects): Interaction design: experience with devising multimodal interactions (touch, pen, speech), context sensing, responsive & adaptive User Interfaces (UIs) Experience design: storyboarding, envisioning video techniques User Experience (UX) research: conducting qualitative and quantitative user studies We value your ideas and unique viewpoints on these topics, as well, and hope that our partnership and collaboration will shape initial directions into exciting, ambitious, and impactful research contributions that only you could have crafted. The EPIC group conducts fundamental research that innovates at the nexus of hardware, software, and human potential. We are an interdisciplinary group of researchers, engineers, scientists, and designers at Microsoft Research who study Human-Computer Interaction (HCI) through prototyping, system-building, design sketching, and observational study of human behavior. You can learn more about the EPIC’s research agenda, publications, videos, and team members at EPIC - Microsoft Research , as well as the broader HCI-AI research area Future Experiences . Responsibilities Research Interns put inquiry and theory into practice. Alongside fellow doctoral candidates and some of the world’s best researchers, Research Interns learn, collaborate, and network for life. Research Interns not only advance their own careers, but they also contribute to exciting research and development strides. During the 12-week internship, Research Interns are paired with mentors and expected to collaborate with other Research Interns and researchers, present findings, and contribute to the vibrant life of the community. Research internships are available in all areas of research, and are offered year-round, though they typically begin in the summer. Qualifications Required Qualifications Currently enrolled in a Doctorate Degree program in Computer Science or related STEM field. Other Requirements Research Interns are expected to be physically located in their manager’s Microsoft worksite location for the duration of their internship. In addition to the qualifications below, you’ll need to submit contact information of references so we may contact these references if needed Preferred Qualifications 1+ year(s) experience conducting original research in (or closely related to) Human-Computer Interaction, and further be able to document their research contributions with publicly available resources (e.g. by linking to papers, pre-prints, videos, demonstrations, repositories, articles, press coverage, or research proposals in your submitted CV). The base pay range for this internship is USD $6,810 - $13,480 per month. There is a different range applicable to specific work locations, within the San Francisco Bay area and New York City metropolitan area, and the base pay range for this role in those locations is USD $8,920 - $14,610 per month. Certain roles may be eligible for benefits and other compensation. Find additional benefits and pay information here: https://careers.microsoft.com/us/en/us-intern-pay Microsoft accepts applications and processes offers for these roles on an ongoing basis throughout the academic calendar (September - April). This position will be open for a minimum of 5 days, with applications accepted on an ongoing basis until the position is filled. Microsoft is an equal opportunity employer. jobs.body: Rockwell Automation is a global technology leader focused on helping the world’s manufacturers be more productive, sustainable, and agile. With more than 28,000 employees who make the world better every day, we know we have something special. Behind our customers - amazing companies that help feed the world, provide life-saving medicine on a global scale, and focus on clean water and green mobility - our people are energized problem solvers that take pride in how the work we do changes the world for the better. We welcome all makers, forward thinkers, and problem solvers who are looking for a place to do their best work. And if that’s you we would love to have you join us! Job Description We are looking for a student to join us as a Machinist Intern in our Fabrication Department onsite in Milwaukee, WI. This is a 10–12-week position. You will report directly to the Fabrication Services Mechanical Design Team Lead. Schedule We can arrange a working schedule, accommodating your school schedule. Working hours will be 2-3 days per week. Job Summary You will be a primary member of new product introduction (NPI) programs and support assembly fixtures, test equipment, prototype parts and production tooling. You will build components to support multiple department's and Operation's strategic goals. You will work on intercompany projects of low / medium complexity and scope. You may perform multiple and parallel activities across multiple projects. You will work with others on project issues to develop multiple resolution options. You will also work with technical resources on inter-functional projects to achieve important factors of project success, which include project schedule, project cost, process / product quality, and transferability to manufacturing. You will determine technical goals of assignments while establishing and implementing corrective action plans. Your Responsibilities: Study blueprints, sketches, models, or specifications to plan sequences of operations for fabricating tools, dies, or assemblies. Operate conventional or computer numerically controlled machine tools such as lathes, milling machines, and grinders to cut, bore, grind, or otherwise shape parts to prescribe dimensions and finishes. Use processing and design expertise to work with internal engineers and external suppliers to resolve part design and manufacturability issues. Verify dimensions, alignments, and clearances of finished parts for conformance to specifications, using measuring instruments such as calipers, gauge blocks, micrometers, and dial indicators. Resolve complex process issues, reduce variation and deploy best practices globally. The Essentials - You Will Have: Actively pursuing an education in Machining, Tool and Die or equivalent knowledge in areas of tooling, processing, part and tool design. Legal authorization to work in the U.S. We will not sponsor individuals for employment visas, now or in the future, for this job opening. The Preferred - You Might Also Have: Knowledge of SolidWorks, Creo, CAMWorks, and Cimatix is valuable. Additionally, experience with Stratasys and Bambu 3D Printeres · Familiarity with Mitutoyo Coordinate Measuring Machines is also desirable Have knowledge in new product development processes, manufacturing assembly environments, and associated business systems. At Rockwell Automation we are dedicated to building a diverse, inclusive and authentic workplace, so if you're excited about this role but your experience doesn't align perfectly with every qualification in the job description, we encourage you to apply anyway. You may be just the right person for this or other roles. This position is part of a job family. jobs.body: Stanley Black & Decker Intern – Industrial Design Intern Come build your career. It takes great people to achieve greatness. People with a sense of purpose and integrity. People with a relentless pursuit of excellence. People who care about making things better For Those Who Make The World™. Sound like you? Join our top-notch team of more than 50,000 diverse and high-performing professionals globally who are making their mark on some of the world’s most beloved brands, including DEWALT®, BLACK+DECKER®, CRAFTSMAN®, STANLEY®, CUB CADET®, and HUSTLER®. About Our Internship Program: Throughout your internship, you will have regular events, weekly lunch and learn sessions, and receive customized training from our business units. This is a unique opportunity to gain valuable insights into supporting the needs of Stanley Black & Decker both in the US and abroad. The interns will gain first-hand exposure to Stanley Black & Decker and have the opportunity to build a cross-functional professional network. Interns are expected to adapt to change and demonstrate strong interpersonal and communication skills, creativity, and confidence. Interns must be team-oriented and collaborative. The Job: During your internship, you will have the opportunity to support Industrial Design with key activities including: Assist in delivering new concept direction, brand-specific aesthetics, and optimized ergonomic solutions for all new product development across a wide range of global brands. Support other industrial designers by creating photorealistic renderings and animations of new product designs using 3D Cad and Keyshot Rendering software. Work with and support our UX/UI team. Projects will consist of on-product user interface, embedded displays, and digital applications. Help drive breakthrough industrial design advancement through to our customers on various projects, utilizing the best technology available for the process. Work with the Industrial Designers and other disciplines to create original designs that capture the desired intent of the team. You will have exposure to several areas of the Industrial Design at Stanley Black & Decker. You will work on a wide variety of tasks and projects with a cross-functional team of professionals. A flexible schedule featuring a max of 40 hours. Opportunity for career advancement upon graduation. Competitive compensation and career development opportunities. Your ideas and solutions have the potential to reach millions of customers as we work together to write the next chapter in our history. Come build with us and take your career to new heights. jobs.title: Summer 2027 Internship - Quality Assurance Engineer - Washington -
jobs.location: Redmond, Washington, United States of America
jobs.body: Work Flexibility: Onsite What You Get Out of the Internship ​​ At Stryker, we believe that developing the next generation of talent is just as important as developing life-changing medical technologies. As an intern, you won’t just observe — you’ll contribute to meaningful projects, gain exposure to leaders who will mentor you, and experience a culture of innovation and teamwork that is shaping the future of healthcare. As an intern, you will : ​ ​ Apply classroom knowledge and gain experience in a fast-paced and growing industry setting ​ Implement new ideas , be constantly challenged, and develop your skills ​ Network with key/high-level stakeholders and leaders of the business ​ Be a part of an innovative team and culture ​ Experience documenting complex processes and presenting them in a clear format Who we want ​​ Challengers. People who seek out the hard projects and work to find just the right solutions. ​ Teammates. Partners who listen to ideas, share thoughts and work together to move the business forward. ​ Charismatic networkers. Relationship-savvy people who intentionally make connections with both internal partners and external contacts. ​ Strategic thinkers. Interns who propose innovative ideas and consistently exceed their performance objectives . ​ Customer-oriented achievers. Individuals with an unparalleled work ethic and customer-focused attitude who bring value to their partnerships. ​ Game changers. Persistent interns who will stop at nothing to live out Stryker’s mission to make healthcare better. Opportunities Available ​ ​ As a Quality Engineering intern at Stryker, you will be placed in one of the following teams: Advanced Quality ​ AQE interns work on engineering projects related to development of new products. Areas of emphasis may include human factors engineering, risk management, application of statistics, reliability engineering, design verification, and design validation including customer interaction. As Homer Stryker pointed out, “If your tools don’t work, make them work. If you can’t make them work, make some that do work.” In this directive, the AQE team works to make sure that the products we develop at Stryker will work consistently for our customers to meet or exceed their expectations. ​ ​​ Process Quality ​ PQE interns collaborate with cross-functional teams to support product sustainment. When non-conforming issues arise in production, it is our responsibility to perform robust root cause analysis and implement effective corrective actions. Do you enjoy deep dive investigations and driving collaboration and communication to achieve issue resolution? If so, you may be a great fit for this team! PQE interns are focused on quality, compliance and continuous improvement. They use their education to work with a variety of tools including CAD for fixture design, root cause analysis methods, LabView, and validation activities to optimize production, inspection, and quality system processes. ​ ​ Supplier Quality ​ SQE interns are responsible for all things supplier-related . Stryker uses a number of critical suppliers to manufacture components and finished products, and to provide critical services. This team’s job is to work closely with the suppliers to ensure components and their manufacturing processes meet our required standards. Do you enjoy using your technical background and communication skills to influence suppliers? If so, you might be a great fit for this diverse and talented team! The role requires working closely with internal customers from multiple functions, meeting with suppliers frequently , and the use of both technical and business skills. ​ ​ Quality ​ Quality interns work with our internal cross-functional teams and external sales team and customers to ensure we develop and sustain a product with the highest quality. The team’s job is to ensure we develop the right products up front – evaluate risk, ensure our customer’s user needs are met, and help drive craftsmanship, safety, durability and reliability into the product. On the post-market side, they also work closely with regulatory to handle any complaints and implement design changes, as needed, to address quality issues. The role requires someone who has great communication, problem-solving, and technical skills. Majors Targeted: Quality Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Biomedical Engineering , Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, or related majors . What You Need ​​ Currently pursuing a Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in a related field; must remain enrolled in a degree-seeking program after the internship . ​ Cumulative 3.0 GPA or above ( verified at time of hire ) Must be legally authorized to work in the U.S. and not require employment-based sponsorship now or in the future . ​ Strong written and verbal communication skills, with proven ability to collaborate and build relationships Demonstrated leadership, problem-solving, and organizational skills with the ability to manage multiple priorities Proficiency in Microsoft Office (Excel, Word, PowerPoint) and eagerness to learn in a dynamic environment . $20 min hourly wage – $35 max hourly wage, sign-on bonus, 11 paid holidays annually, and either paid corporate housing or a living stipend, dependent upon hiring location Travel Percentage: None Stryker Corporation is an equal opportunity employer. Qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, ethnicity, color, religion, sex, gender identity, sexual orientation, national origin, disability, or protected veteran status. Stryker is an EO employer – M/F/Veteran/Disability. Stryker Corporation will not discharge or in any other manner discriminate against employees or applicants because they have inquired about, discussed, or disclosed their own pay or the pay of another employee or applicant. However, employees who have access to the compensation information of other employees or applicants as a part of their essential job functions cannot disclose the pay of other employees or applicants to individuals who do not otherwise have access to compensation information, unless the disclosure is (a) in response to a formal complaint or charge, (b) in furtherance of an investigation, proceeding, hearing, or action, including an investigation conducted by the employer, or (c) consistent with the contractor’s legal duty to furnish information.

jobs.body: Anduril Industries is a defense technology company with a mission to transform U.S. and allied military capabilities with advanced technology. By bringing the expertise, technology, and business model of the 21st century’s most innovative companies to the defense industry, Anduril is changing how military systems are designed, built and sold. Anduril’s family of systems is powered by Lattice OS, an AI-powered operating system that turns thousands of data streams into a realtime, 3D command and control center. As the world enters an era of strategic competition, Anduril is committed to bringing cutting-edge autonomy, AI, computer vision, sensor fusion, and networking technology to the military in months, not years. ABOUT THE TEAM Anduril's Maritime Division is transforming American sea power to meet the defining national security challenges of our era and secure our future of maritime dominance. We are scaling at an historic pace, anchored by Arsenal-2, our new software-defined shipyard being built in Baltimore County, Maryland. It's part of a new $6.6 billion investment in America's submarine industrial base. Arsenal-2 is purpose-built to break long-standing industrial bottlenecks and scale production of critical components for the Navy's Virginia-class attack submarines to support fleet requirements. At the same time, it will build the industrial muscle to field our next-generation AUVs at scale. We aren't waiting for the new shipyard to be completed. The work on this transformation starts right now, with development inside our new 160,000 square foot Proto-Factory in Orange County, California, where the team is already laying the foundation. As the prototyping hub for Arsenal-2, this facility gives us a multi-year head start, proving out the advanced manufacturing methods, digital workflows, and quality systems that will scale across our broader shipyard network. In Anduril's Maritime Division, we are actively building America's next decisive advantage at sea, and this is the moment to join us. ABOUT THE JOB Maritime Digital Production builds the digital systems behind Anduril's maritime build chain: data pipelines, contextualization layers, workflow and execution tools, applied intelligence, and the interfaces between OT and IT. Everything we build has to survive production constraints, which means real crews, real equipment, and real disruption. Raw data off the factory floor doesn't mean much on its own. A tag reading PLC4_TT_1142 tells you nothing until someone establishes that it's a temperature sensor, on a specific machine, in a specific cell, measuring a specific process step. Doing that for thousands of signals is a cataloging problem before it's an engineering one. That's the job. You'll build the vocabularies, hierarchies, and metadata standards that give factory data meaning, working alongside data engineers and manufacturing engineers who need the structure and don't have the training to build it. If you like building a taxonomy and want to see one used somewhere other than a library, this is that. WHAT YOU'LL DO Develop and maintain controlled vocabularies for equipment, materials, processes, and locations across the build chain. Build asset hierarchies and naming conventions that structure plant-floor data into a consistent model. Write and apply metadata schemas for industrial data sources, documenting what each field means and how it should be used. Catalog data sources and maintain entries in the team's data catalog, including provenance and ownership. Audit existing tags and data models for inconsistency and gaps and propose corrections. Document standards and authoring guidelines so naming decisions stay consistent after you leave. Work with data and manufacturing engineers to check that the models match how work actually happens on the floor. Present your work to the team at the end of the session. REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS Must be pursuing a bachelor’s or master’s degree in Library Science, Information Science, Knowledge Management, Archival Studies, Linguistics, or a related field. Must be returning to school at the end of the internship to continue academic studies for at least one quarter or semester. Must be a U.S. Person due to required access to U.S. export-controlled information or facilities; U.S. clearance eligibility may be required depending on program. Ability to complete a 12 week in-person internship in one of our offices in summer 2027. PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS Coursework or project experience in metadata, cataloging, taxonomy, controlled vocabularies, or classification systems. Attention to detail, and patience for working through ambiguity toward a consistent structure. Clear writing, particularly for documentation meant to outlast its author. Familiarity with metadata standards and modeling approaches (Dublin Core, SKOS, RDF, OWL, or similar). Exposure to data catalog tooling, knowledge graphs, or ontology editors such as Protégé. Basic scripting in Python or SQL for inspecting and transforming data. Interest in manufacturing and the physical systems behind the data. Coursework in digital curation, data governance, or information architecture. jobs.location: Folsom, CA, United States of America
jobs.body: Our vision is to transform how the world uses information to enrich life for all . Micron Technology is a world leader in innovating memory and storage solutions that accelerate the transformation of information into intelligence, inspiring the world to learn, communicate and advance faster than ever. The Memory Systems Architecture team defines the next generation of High Bandwidth Memory (HBM) solutions that power artificial intelligence, high-performance computing, and data center applications. The team drives architectural innovation across memory systems, controllers, interfaces, and reliability features to deliver industry-leading performance, scalability, and efficiency for future computing platforms. As a Memory Systems Architecture Intern, you will contribute to the architecture and microarchitecture development of future HBM products. You will work alongside experienced architects to evaluate new memory features, analyze architectural trade-offs, develop performance models, and explore solutions that improve memory performance, reliability, and efficiency for AI and high-performance computing workloads. Responsibilities Research and evaluate next-generation HBM architecture and microarchitecture features, including memory scheduling, refresh management, reliability features, thermal behavior, and memory controller interactions. Develop and enhance performance models, simulators, and analytical tools using Python, C++, or similar technologies to assess architectural trade-offs and system performance. Analyze workload behavior, simulation results, and architectural data to provide recommendations for future HBM product development. Utilize AI-assisted engineering tools and workflows to accelerate software development, specification analysis, data exploration, and technical documentation while validating outputs using sound engineering judgment. Collaborate with architecture, design, memory controller, and cross-functional engineering teams to support feature definition, design reviews, specifications, and roadmap development. Minimum Qualifications 0-2 years of relevant experience through internships, research, academic projects, publications, or coursework in computer architecture, memory systems, VLSI, semiconductor design, or related technical fields. Currently pursuing a Bachelor's, Master's, or PhD degree in Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, Computer Science, or a related field. Coursework or project experience in computer architecture, memory hierarchies, DRAM technologies, interconnects, or hardware system design. Programming experience with Python and at least one of the following: C++, SystemVerilog, or similar engineering languages. Ability to read and interpret technical specifications, standards documentation, datasheets, or hardware interface definitions. Strong analytical, problem-solving, written, and verbal communication skills. Experience utilizing AI coding assistants and large language models (LLMs) such as GitHub Copilot, Claude, ChatGPT, or similar technologies as part of engineering workflows. Preferred Qualifications Experience with memory or system simulation environments such as Ramulator, DRAMSim, gem5, or related architectural modeling tools. Knowledge of HBM, DDR, LPDDR, GDDR, memory controller architectures, or memory subsystem design. Familiarity with memory reliability and availability concepts, including ECC, repair mechanisms, refresh algorithms, or RAS features. Experience with SystemVerilog, digital design, RTL development, or verification methodologies. Experience applying AI tools to software development, data analysis, technical research, document analysis, workflow automation, or agentic engineering workflows. Understanding of AI training, inference, accelerator architectures, and the role of HBM in large-scale AI systems. Previous internship, research, publication, or project experience related to memory systems, computer architecture, semiconductor design, or SoC development.
