jobs.title: Coop - Mechatronics Engineer (Internship)
jobs.location: Wilton, CT, USA, United States of America
jobs.body: Introduction to the job The DUV Reticle Stage IBS MDU team is responsible for engineering activities supporting the reticle stage, a precision mechatronic subsystem within ASML’s DUV lithography systems. Our mechatronics engineers use MATLAB-based analysis tools to evaluate system dynamics and performance using large sets of measurement data. As our analysis needs evolve, these engineering tools need to evolve with them. Many have been developed and extended over time by different engineers, which means that understanding the existing methods often requires combining code investigation, technical documentation, and knowledge from experienced engineers. We are looking for a co-op student who is excited to work at the intersection of mechatronics, data analysis, signal processing, and software development . Role and responsibilities Your primary assignment will be to develop and improve MATLAB-based analysis tools for DUV Reticle Stage dynamic performance , with a particular focus on power spectral density (PSD) analysis and visualization . You will work closely with experienced ASML mechatronics engineers to understand existing analysis methods, identify requirements, implement improvements, and validate the results against existing engineering analyses. Your responsibilities will include: Develop and update MATLAB tools for analysis and visualization of Reticle Stage dynamic performance data, particularly PSD and frequency-domain analysis. Learn how existing analysis tools and methods work by reviewing MATLAB code, available documentation, and example datasets. Interview and collaborate with mechatronics engineers to gather requirements and uncover engineering knowledge that may not yet be fully documented. Translate engineering requirements into maintainable MATLAB functions, analysis workflows, and visualizations. Validate new or modified analysis methods against known datasets and existing engineering results. Investigate discrepancies and work with subject-matter experts to determine whether they originate from data processing, algorithms, assumptions, or implementation. Improve usability and documentation so future engineers can understand and confidently use the analysis tools. Participate in code reviews and incorporate feedback from the mechatronics engineering team. This assignment offers the opportunity to work on a real precision-mechatronics system while gaining hands-on experience with engineering data analysis, signal processing, MATLAB development, and collaborative problem solving. This position is located on-site in Wilton, CT. It requires onsite presence to attend in-person work-related events, trainings and meetings and to further ensure teamwork, collaboration and innovation. Must be available for 6 to 9 months Education and experience We are looking for a college junior or senior pursuing a bachelor's degree in Mechanical Engineering, Mechatronics, Electrical Engineering, Controls Engineering, Robotics, or a related engineering field , who is available for a 6-month co-op assignment . To be successful in this role, you should have: Technical skills Experience programming in MATLAB through coursework, projects, research, or previous internships/co-ops. Understanding of fundamental mechanical dynamics and vibrations . Familiarity with signal processing and frequency-domain analysis , such as Fourier transforms, frequency response, or power spectral density. Ability to work with experimental or measurement datasets and create clear engineering plots and visualizations. A structured approach to testing and validating computational results. Familiarity with Git, SVN, or another version-control system is beneficial but not required. Personal skills Strong curiosity and willingness to dig into an unfamiliar technical problem. Comfortable approaching engineers, asking questions, and gathering information from multiple subject-matter experts. Able to take loosely documented requirements and turn them into a structured engineering solution. Strong problem-solving skills and attention to detail, particularly when validating numerical results. Able to work independently while actively seeking feedback and collaborating with an engineering team. Clear written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to document technical work for future users. The current base hourly range for this role is currently: $18.00 to $48.00 per hour Pay scales are determined by role, level, location and alignment with market data. Individual pay is determined through interviews and an assessment of several factors that that are unique to each candidate, including but not limited to job-related skills, relevant education and experience, certifications, abilities of the candidate and pay relative to other team members This position may require access to controlled technology, as defined in the Export Administration Regulations (15 C.F.R. § 730, et seq.). Qualified candidates must be legally authorized to access such controlled technology prior to beginning work. Business demands may require the Company to proceed with candidates who are immediately eligible to access controlled technology. Inclusion and diversity ASML is an Equal Opportunity Employer that values and respects the importance of a diverse and inclusive workforce. It is the policy of the company to recruit, hire, train and promote persons in all job titles without regard to race, color, religion, sex, age, national origin, veteran status, disability, sexual orientation, or gender identity. We recognize that inclusion and diversity is a driving force in the success of our company. Need to know more about applying for a job at ASML? Read our frequently asked questions .

jobs.body: Design and Verification Engineer Intern The Opportunity: As an electrical engineer, you understand the workings behind complex systems. That knowledge is key when it comes to designing, simulating, and verifying digital circuits for advanced microelectronic systems. We’re looking for an electrical engineer who can use their skills to help government clients develop reliable, mission-ready semiconductor technologies. At Booz Allen, you’ll use your engineering skills to transform the defense and national security microelectronics industry. Our team develops and evaluates secure, reliable digital hardware solutions for mission-critical applications. That’s why we need you, an electrical engineer with foundational knowledge of digital design and hardware verification, to help us design and develop digital logic, verification environments, testbenches, and reusable verification components for microelectronic systems. On our team, you’ll learn how to translate system requirements into hardware specifications, develop RTL using a hardware description language, create simulation-based testbenches, execute verification plans, analyze coverage, and troubleshoot any bugs. You’ll impact national security and defense missions by helping deliver trusted and assured microelectronics that operate as intended. This is a chance to grow your digital design and verification skills while gaining experience in RTL development, functional verification, semiconductor design workflows, and electronic design automation tools. Take on exciting challenges in national security microelectronics with us as we improve the reliability and availability of trusted microelectronics technologies for critical government missions. Join us. The world can’t wait. You Have: Knowledge of digital logic design concepts, including Boolean logic, finite-state machines, combinational logic, and sequential logic Knowledge of at least one hardware description or hardware verification language, such as Verilog or SystemVerilog Ability to develop, simulate, debug, or verify digital hardware through academic coursework, laboratory assignments, internships, or technical projects Ability to use scripting or programming languages, such as Python, C, C++, Tcl, or Bash, for engineering or test automation Ability to communicate technical information and collaborate with multidisciplinary engineering teams Ability to obtain a Secret clearance Scheduled to obtain a Bachelor's degree in Electrical Engineering or Computer Engineering by Spring 2030 Nice If You Have: Experience developing RTL, testbenches, assertions, verification plans, or functional coverage Knowledge of verification methodologies, including Universal Verification Methodology Ability to use electronic design automation or simulation tools from vendors such as Cadence, Siemens, or Synopsys Clearance: Applicants selected will be subject to a security investigation and may need to meet eligibility requirements for access to classified information. jobs.body: > Requisition Number: 78521 The company built on breakthroughs. ​ Join us.​ Corning is one of the world’s leading innovators in glass, ceramic, and materials science. From the depths of the ocean to the farthest reaches of space, our technologies push the boundaries of what’s possible. ​ How do we do this? With our people. They break through limitations and expectations – not once in a career, but every day. They help move our company, and the world, forward. ​ ​At Corning, there are endless possibilities for making an impact. You can help connect the unconnected, drive the future of automobiles, transform at-home entertainment, and ensure the delivery of lifesaving medicines. And so much more.​ Come break through with us. Corning’s businesses are ever-evolving to best serve our customers, industries, and consumers. Today, we accelerate and transform life sciences, mobile consumer electronics, optical communications, display, automotive, and solar markets. We are changing the world with: Trusted products that accelerate drug discovery, development, and delivery to save lives Damage-resistant cover glass to enhance the devices that keep us connected Optical fiber, wireless technologies, and connectivity solutions to carry information and ideas at the speed of light Precision glass for advanced displays to deliver richer experiences Auto glass and ceramics to drive cleaner, safer, and smarter transportation Solar polysilicon, wafers, and innovative photovoltaic modules, enabling low-cost solar energy solutions Scope of Position The responsibility of the Pkg Eng Intern is to learn and apply packaging best practices and processes to the set given projects for the COC Packaging program. Receive on-the-job training on overall packaging strategies and processes through work assignments. The purpose of this position is to collaborate, design, validate and provide support on packaging solutions that encompass 3 key areas around cost savings, sustainability, and adding value to innovation solutions for Corning’s customers. All these areas are integral parts of the COC Packaging Program within Corning and include the standardization and optimization of existing packaging solutions to deliver improvements in cost, capability, and quality, and providing manufacturing and commercial support for packaging related issues. The Packaging Intern will collaborate with global packaging engineers, along with internal and external partners to identify appropriate packaging materials and validate packaging designs that meet specifications and customer requirements. Day to Day Responsibilities Apply packaging engineering fundamentals to support assigned projects across the Corning Optical Communications packaging program during a six-month internship assignment. Assist packaging engineers with the design, evaluation, and optimization of primary, secondary, and tertiary packaging solutions for new and existing products. Support packaging cost, quality, sustainability, and capability improvement initiatives by helping assess material usage, manufacturing impact, transportation efficiency, and total cost of packaging. Participate in packaging testing and validation activities, including fit, form, function, handling, distribution, and product protection assessments to help ensure package reliability. Collect, organize, and analyze packaging data to support engineering recommendations, design changes, cost savings assessments, Sphera packaging emissions calculations and continuous improvement opportunities. Prepare and maintain technical documentation, including packaging specifications, test reports, project summaries, drawings, bill-of-material inputs, Packaging weight and emissions reduction tracking and process change support materials. jobs.title: Summer 2027 Internship - Field Engineer
jobs.location: Paducah, Kentucky, United States
jobs.body: About the Company General Matter is enriching uranium in America. Our goal is to design, build, and operate the world’s lowest-cost enrichment services in the United States. Our mission is to restore America’s ability to produce nuclear fuel—fuel that will power AI, advanced manufacturing, critical industries, and the next generation of nuclear reactors. Ultimately, our work will help power national ambitions and enable a high-energy society. We were incubated by Founders Fund, like Anduril and Palantir before us, and are backed by top-tier investors. Our lean, world-class team of engineers and operators is applying a first-principles approach to solving the problem of nuclear fuel production. We are a mission-driven company with a culture of urgency, accountability, and transparency. Help us build a high-energy society by making the cleanest, safest form of baseload energy the most affordable. About This Role As a Summer Field Engineer Intern at General Matter, you'll be on the ground in Paducah during active construction of our flagship uranium enrichment facility. It's a first-of-a-kind plant being built on the site of the former Paducah Gaseous Diffusion Plant, which helped fuel America for sixty years. You'll be the link between design and the field, helping turn drawings and specifications into installed work, catch problems before they cost the schedule, and build the record that shows the plant was built right. Most construction interns are one of dozens on a job at a large contractor, with little ownership of real work. Here you'll sit on the owner's team for one project of national importance. You'll take on meaningful scopes of work and work directly alongside the superintendents, engineers, and quality team delivering it. You'll see how a nuclear facility comes together, and you'll help build it. If you seek high impact and are excited by fast-paced, intense, Skunkworks-style projects, we encourage you to apply to join our team. before they reach the field Assist in drafting and tracking RFIs and submittals for assigned work packages from the first question through the engineering response and closure Perform quantity quality requirements Maintain daily reports, progress photos, and field records that become part of the facility's permanent quality and turnover record Support punch-list walks, as-built markups, and turnover package preparation for completed systems Safety & Field Coordination Help prepare Job Hazard Analyses and take part in daily safety meetings, toolbox talks, and field safety walks Serve as a day-to-day field contact for subcontractor foremen on assigned tasks, raising issues early and closing them out quickly Own a defined intern project over the summer, such as tracking a site utility system or a building's foundation work, and present your results to the project team Basic Qualifications Currently pursuing a bachelor's or master's degree in Civil, Construction, Mechanical, or Electrical Engineering, or Construction Management, with an expected graduation date after summer 2027 Evidence of exceptional ability (construction internships or co-ops, engineering competition teams, hands-on projects, completed builds, etc.) Ability to read and interpret construction drawings and specifications Ability to work outdoors on an active construction site in all weather conditions, including walking uneven terrain, climbing ladders and stairs, and wearing required PPE Valid driver's license Ability to obtain and maintain required security clearance and access authorization Available for the full 12-week summer 2027 internship in Paducah, Kentucky Preferred Skills and Experience Prior construction internship or co-op experience, especially on industrial, power generation, data center, semiconductor, or other mission-critical projects EIT certification or a passing score on the FE exam OSHA 10 or OSHA 30 certification Familiarity with Procore, resource-constrained environment Interest in building a long-term career on a single flagship project rather than moving from job to job Additional Requirements Ability to work extended hours and weekends as necessary. jobs.title: CMOS FEOL Reliability Engineering Intern (Summer 2027)
jobs.location: USA - New York - Malta, United States of America
jobs.body: About GlobalFoundries GlobalFoundries (GF) is a leading manufacturer of essential semiconductors, enabling AI at scale from the cloud to the physical world. Through deep partnerships with customers, GF delivers differentiated, power-efficient and high-performance solutions for high-growth markets. GF is a trusted and holistic technology partner for customers around the world. GF’s talented, global team remains focused every day on security, longevity and sustainability. For more information, visit www.gf.com. Internship Program Overview: Our Interns & Co-ops are our entry-level talent pipeline for GF across the globe. Our goal is to provide students with a meaningful work experience that will equip them with the skills to embark on a career in the fast-paced and growing semiconductor industry after graduation. As an intern at GF, you’ll experience one-on-one mentorship, work assignments that prioritize your growth and potential, professional development opportunities, and the chance to network with executives. Summary of Role: The CMOS FEOL Reliability Engineering Intern will support the Fab 8 Reliability Engineering organization in assessing semiconductor device reliability performance across advanced technology platforms. Working with reliability engineers, device engineers, Process Integration, Product Engineering, Yield Engineering, Reliability Laboratory, and data-analysis teams, the intern will evaluate reliability test data, investigate degradation mechanisms, and improve qualification and monitoring methodologies. Essential Responsibilities include: Learn semiconductor device reliability fundamentals, including Hot Carrier Injection (HCI), Bias Temperature Instability (BTI), Time-Dependent Dielectric Breakdown (TDDB), Gate Oxide Integrity (GOI), and Process Reliability Monitoring (PRM). Support reliability qualification and monitoring activities for advanced CMOS technologies manufactured at Fab 8. Analyze wafer-level reliability (WLR) and fast wafer-level reliability (FWLR) test data using statistical and engineering methods. Develop automated data-analysis, reporting, dashboard, and visualization solutions that reduce manual reporting effort and improve visibility of reliability trends across multiple technology platforms. Perform data mining, trend analysis, comparative studies, and historical PRM correlation analysis to identify process and device factors that influence long-term reliability performance. Develop advanced statistical monitoring methods to improve excursion detection and reliability risk assessment. Collaborate with Device Engineering, Process Integration, Product Engineering, Yield Engineering, and Reliability Laboratory teams to support technology qualification and root-cause investigations. Prepare reliability assessment documentation, engineering reports, and technical presentations, and present project findings and recommendations at the conclusion of the internship. Other Responsibilities: Perform all activities in a safe and responsible manner and support all Environmental, Health, Safety & Security requirements and programs. Required Qualifications: Education – At least a sophomore at time of application and actively pursuing a Bachelor’s, Master’s, or PhD in Electrical Engineering, Materials Science, Physics, Computer Engineering, Data Science, Semiconductor Engineering, or related field through an accredited degree program during the time of internship. Must have at least an overall 3.0 GPA and be in good academic standing. Language Fluency - English (Written & Verbal) Ability to work at least 40 hours per week during the internship. Strong analytical and problem-solving skills. Ability to work independently and in a collaborative engineering environment. Preferred Qualifications: Prior related internship or co-op experience Demonstrated prior leadership experience in the workplace, school projects, competitions, etc. Strong interest in leveraging AI tools and emerging technologies to enhance productivity, streamline workflows, and support effective decision-making. Project management skills, i.e., the ability to innovate and execute on solutions that matter; the ability to navigate ambiguity. Strong written and verbal communication skills Strong planning & organizational skills Knowledge of semiconductor devices and manufacturing processes. Familiarity with statistical data-analysis techniques. Experience with Python, JMP, Minitab, Excel, Power BI, or similar analysis and visualization tools. Exposure to semiconductor reliability concepts, wafer-level reliability, or laboratory testing. #InternshipProgramUS Expected Salary Range $20.00 - $40.00 Expected Salary Range $0.00 - $0.00 The exact Salary will be determined based on qualifications, experience and location. jobs.title: Research Intern - MSR AI Interaction and Learning

jobs.body: Overview Research Internships at Microsoft provide a dynamic environment for research careers with a network of world-class research labs led by globally-recognized scientists and engineers, who pursue innovation in a range of scientific and technical disciplines to help solve complex challenges in diverse fields, including computing, healthcare, economics, and the environment. The AI Interaction and Learning team in Microsoft Research studies and builds next-generation Artificial Intelligence (AI) systems that help people accomplish more valuable work. Our research spans understanding how people use AI in real-world settings, evaluating agents in realistic workflows, and developing methods that make AI systems more capable, adaptive, and effective collaborators. Current research directions include agent evaluation and environments, reinforcement learning and post-training, user modeling and simulation, agent and group memory, personalization and continual learning, analysis of large-scale interaction logs, and human-AI collaboration. We are particularly interested in candidates with research experience in one or more of the following areas: Foundation Models, Reinforcement Learning and Post-Training, Agents, Natural Language Processing, Machine Learning, Interactive or Continual Learning, User Modeling and Simulation, Evaluation, Computational Social Science, Human-AI Interaction and Collaboration, or related areas of Artificial Intelligence. Candidates are encouraged to browse some of our recent publications for examples of active research in the group. Responsibilities Research Interns put inquiry and theory into practice. Alongside fellow doctoral candidates and some of the world’s best researchers, Research Interns learn, collaborate, and network for life. Research Interns not only advance their own careers, but they also contribute to exciting research and development strides. During the 12-week internship, Research Interns are paired with mentors and expected to collaborate with other Research Interns and researchers, present findings, and contribute to the vibrant life of the community. Research internships are available in all areas of research, and are offered year-round, though they typically begin in the summer. Qualifications Required Qualifications Currently enrolled in a Doctorate Degree program in Computer Science, Electrical Engineering or a related STEM field. Other Requirements Research Interns are expected to be physically located in their manager’s Microsoft worksite location for the duration of their internship. In addition to the qualifications below, you’ll need to submit a minimum of two reference letters for this position as well as a cover letter and any relevant work or research samples. After you submit your application, a request for letters may be sent to your list of references on your behalf. Note that reference letters cannot be requested until after you have submitted your application, and furthermore, that they might not be automatically requested for all candidates. You may wish to alert your letter writers in advance, so they will be ready to submit your letter. jobs.title: Internship: Forward Deployed Engineer, Test
jobs.location: Los Angeles
jobs.body: ABOUT REVEL At Revel, we are revolutionizing the way the world’s most critical hardware is controlled—across aerospace, automotive, energy, and manufacturing sectors. Our next-generation software stack combines an intuitive command/control interface, a specialized programming language tailored for hardware control, and a high-performance runtime environment. We empower engineers to build, test, and deploy critical systems rapidly, reliably, and safely. THE INTERNSHIP As a Forward Deployed Test Engineering Intern at Revel, you’ll work at the intersection of software, hardware, and testing to help our customers build and operate better test systems. You’ll work alongside our Forward Deployed Engineering and Software teams to integrate Revel with customer test stands, build test infrastructure, troubleshoot hardware and software issues, develop dashboards and workflows, and help engineering teams get more out of their test operations. You’ll get hands-on exposure to the systems behind aerospace, defense, automotive, energy, and advanced manufacturing. You’ll learn how software, hardware, sensors, data acquisition systems, and test infrastructure come together in real-world environments—and how to diagnose problems when things don't work as expected. This is a highly technical, hands-on internship. You’ll work closely with experienced engineers, take ownership of meaningful projects, and have the opportunity to see your work used with real hardware. WHAT YOU'LL DO - Help deploy and integrate Revel with customer test stands, sensors, actuators, and existing infrastructure - Work alongside customer engineering teams to understand their test processes and identify opportunities to improve them - Build and maintain test infrastructure, dashboards, and software workflows - Write RevelCode and other software to automate and streamline testing - Support data acquisition, telemetry, and hardware validation efforts - Troubleshoot issues across software, networking, firmware, hardware, and physical test systems - Help run and support test campaigns in real-world hardware environments - Deliver training and documentation to help new users get up and running with Revel - Collaborate with internal software and product teams to turn field learnings into product improvements - Occasionally travel to customer sites with the team WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR - Currently pursuing a Bachelor's degree in Mechanical Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, Physics, Computer Science, or a related technical field - Rising Junior or Senior graduating in 2027 or 2028 - Hands-on experience with engineering projects involving hardware, software, testing, or instrumentation - Strong problem-solving and debugging skills - Basic programming experience in Python, C, C++, or another programming language - Basic understanding of how software, hardware, sensors, and networks interact - Interest in test engineering, embedded systems, robotics, aerospace, automotive, or other hardware-focused environments - Comfortable getting hands-on with physical hardware and troubleshooting problems in real-world environments - Strong written and verbal communication skills - Curious, self-directed, and excited to learn from experienced engineers - Comfortable working in a fast-paced, ambiguous environment - US citizen, lawful permanent resident, refugee, or asylee (ITAR requirement) BONUS POINTS - Experience with data acquisition systems, test stands, instrumentation, or test automation - Experience with sensors, actuators, oscilloscopes, multimeters, or other test equipment - Experience with PLCs, control systems, NI software suite, TwinCAT, or CodeSys - Experience building or maintaining test infrastructure through academic, personal, or previous internship projects - Experience with embedded systems, robotics, aerospace, automotive, or other hardware-focused projects - Proficiency in C, C++, Python, Rust, or other systems programming languages - Familiarity with networking and debugging communication between hardware and software - Startup experience and passion for aerospace, defense, advanced manufacturing, or robotics WHY REVEL - Work on hardware that matters — our customers are building aerospace systems, advanced manufacturing lines, and critical infrastructure - Build and test real things — work directly with the hardware and systems used in real-world engineering environments - Learn from exceptional engineers — work closely with experienced Forward Deployed, Test, and Software Engineers - Get customer exposure — see firsthand how engineering teams design, test, and operate complex hardware - Own meaningful projects — take responsibility for projects that directly impact our customers and product - Grow quickly — work in a small, ambitious team where your contributions are visible INTERNSHIP DETAILS - Program: Summer 2027 Internship - Duration: June - August 2027 - Type: Summer, paid internship - Location: Los Angeles or San Francisco - Work environment: On-site - Travel: Occasional travel to customer sites may be required Join us to redefine what’s possible in software for hardware. ITAR Requirements To conform to U.S. Government export regulations, applicant must be a (i) U.S. citizen or national, (ii) U.S. lawful, permanent resident (aka green card holder), (iii) Refugee under 8 U.S.C. 1157, or (iv) Asylee under 8 U.S.C. 1158, or be eligible to obtain the required authorizations from the U.S. Department of State. Learn more about the ITAR here https://www.pmddtc.state.gov/ddtc_public?id=ddtc_kb_article_page&sys_id=24d528fddbfc930044f9ff621f961987.

jobs.body: Work Flexibility: Onsite What You Get Out of the Intern s hip ​​ At Stryker, we believe that developing the next generation of talent is just as important as developing life-changing medical technologies. As an intern, you won’t just observe — you’ll contribute to meaningful projects, gain exposure to leaders who will mentor you, and experience a culture of innovation and teamwork that is shaping the future of healthcare. As an intern, you will : ​ ​ Apply classroom knowledge and gain experience in a fast-paced and growing industry setting ​ Implement new ideas , be constantly challenged, and develop your skills ​ Network with key/high-level stakeholders and leaders of the business ​ Be a part of an innovative team and culture ​ Experience documenting complex processes and presenting them in a clear format Who we want ​​ Challengers. People who seek out the hard projects and work to find just the right solutions. ​ Teammates. Partners who listen to ideas, share thoughts and work together to move the business forward. ​ Charismatic networkers. Relationship-savvy people who intentionally make connections with both internal partners and external contacts. ​ Strategic thinkers. Interns who propose innovative ideas and consistently exceed their performance objectives . ​ Customer-oriented achievers. Individuals with an unparalleled work ethic and customer-focused attitude who bring value to their partnerships. ​ Game changers. Persistent interns who will stop at nothing to live out Stryker’s mission to make healthcare better. Opportunities Available ​ ​As an Electrical Engineering intern at Stryker, you will be placed in one of the following teams: Work on specific purchase product which will involve working on ongoing project deliverables, Robotic projects, Advanced Quality AQE interns work on engineering projects related to development of new products. Areas of emphasis may include human factors engineering, risk management, application of statistics, reliability engineering, design verification, and design validation including customer interaction. As Homer Stryker pointed out, “If your tools don’t work, make them work. If you can’t make them work, make some that do work.” In this directive, the AQE team works to make sure that the products we develop at Stryker will work consistently for our customers to meet or exceed their expectations. Process Quality PQE interns collaborate with cross-functional teams to support product sustainment. When non-conforming issues arise in production, it is our responsibility to perform robust root cause analysis and implement effective corrective actions. Do you enjoy deep dive investigations and driving collaboration and communication to achieve issue resolution? If so, you may be a great fit for this team! PQE interns are focused on quality, compliance and continuous improvement. They use their education to work with a variety of tools including CAD for fixture design, root cause analysis methods, LabView, and validation activities to optimize production, inspection, and quality system processes. Supplier Quality SQE interns are responsible for all things supplier-related . Stryker uses a number of critical suppliers to manufacture components and finished products, and to provide critical services. This team’s job is to work closely with the suppliers to ensure components and their manufacturing processes meet our required standards. Do you enjoy using your technical background and communication skills to influence suppliers? If so, you might be a great fit for this diverse and talented team! The role requires working closely with internal customers from multiple functions, meeting with suppliers frequently , and the use of both technical and business skills. Quality Quality interns work with our internal cross-functional teams and external sales team and customers to ensure we develop and sustain a product with the highest quality. The team’s job is to ensure we develop the right products up front – evaluate risk, ensure our customer’s user needs are met, and help drive craftsmanship, safety, durability and reliability into the product. On the post-market side, they also work closely with regulatory to handle any complaints and implement design changes, as needed, to address quality issues. The role requires someone who has great communication , problem-solving, and technical skills. Research & Development New Product Development R&D interns in New Product Development work with cross-functional teams to identify the needs and the goals of future products. They research new technologies , customer expectations, business requirements and regulations. They may work with a variety of tools, including CAD, FEA, and our Test Labs to develop new product concepts. These interns utilize their technical education to design new products and drive them from concept to production. Product Engineering R&D interns in Product Engineering work with cross-functional teams to identify the greatest needs for improvements on current products. They research new technologies , customer feedback, and product performance data to make our products better for Stryker and for our customers. Product Engineering interns work with a variety of tools, including CAD, FEA, Test Labs, and root cause analysis methods. These interns utilize their technical education to improve the safety and efficacy of our existing products. Test Lab Test interns partner closely with Test Engineers and R&D to experiment with early prototypes and vet out product designs throughout the design process. What this really means is that they get to be the MythBusters of the division. You think your design can last the entire expected service life? We put it to the test. Just like the show, we quickly design and build fixtures to simulate real life situations. In addition to these experiments, they are ultimately responsible for design verification – the quantitative testing of the technical specifications of the product. A team’s experience ranges from 2 to over 15 years with technical specialties ranging from sterilization, mechanical, electrical, software, and optics. If you’re the type of person that has the magic ability to break things – we want you! Manufacturing Manufacturing Engineer interns will collaborate with Design and Operations to deliver best-in-class new products to market. Interns will partner with technicians and engineers to improve Stryker’s manufacturing lines through new fixture development, assembly line process enhancement, implementation of lean manufacturing principles, and improving ergonomics and safety. Majors Targeted: Electrical Engineering, or related majors . What You Need ​​ Currently pursuing a Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in a related field; must remain enrolled in a degree-seeking program after the internship . ​ Cumulative 3.0 GPA or above ( verified at time of hire ) Must be legally authorized to work in the U.S. and not require employment-based sponsorship now or in the future . ​ Strong written and verbal communication skills, with proven ability to collaborate and build relationships Demonstrated leadership, problem-solving, and organizational skills with the ability to manage multiple priorities Proficiency in Microsoft Office (Excel, Word, PowerPoint) and eagerness to learn in a dynamic environment . Majors Targeted: Mechanical Engineering, Biomedical Engineering , or related majors What You Need ​​ Currently pursuing a Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in a related field; must remain enrolled in a degree-seeking program after the internship . ​ Cumulative 3.0 GPA or above ( verified at time of hire ) Must be legally authorized to work in the U.S. and not require employment-based sponsorship now or in the future . ​ Strong written and verbal communication skills, with proven ability to collaborate and build relationships Demonstrated leadership, problem-solving, and organizational skills with the ability to manage multiple priorities Proficiency in Microsoft Office (Excel, Word, PowerPoint) and eagerness to learn in a dynamic environment . $ 20 min hourly wage – $3 5 max hourly wage, sign-on bonus, 11 paid holidays annually, and either paid corporate housing or a living stipend, dependent upon hiring location Travel Percentage: None Stryker Corporation is an equal opportunity employer. Qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, ethnicity, color, religion, sex, gender identity, sexual orientation, national origin, disability, or protected veteran status. jobs.body: What we’re building The marine industry supports recreation, global commerce, and national defense. And yet it runs on technology that hasn't meaningfully changed in fifty years. Until now. Arc is on a mission to electrify the marine industry. We're rethinking powertrains, software, and vessel designs from first principles. And we're already executing. We started with consumers to develop and harden our core technology. We’re now scaling production of our flagship model with new models and sectors on the horizon. Now we’re extending our platform to commercial applications, starting with tugs, ferries, and defense, with years worth of signed contracts and a pipeline that spans every vessel type on the water. The technology is proven, the momentum is building, and the opportunity is enormous. The marine industry is going electric and Arc is building the platform that powers it Who we’re looking for We’re looking for someone who’s fired up by our mission and ready to build. Knowledge of high-voltage systems and HV battery pack design/functionality. Familiarity with CAN communication and advanced control systems. Comfortable pushing a fast but sustainable pace Enthusiasm for boating and clean energy At Arc, we encourage diversity and consider all qualified applicants equally for employment, regardless of background, identity, or status. You’re always welcome to reach out even if you don’t meet many of these qualifications. Passion and aptitude make up for a lot. What we offer The base pay for this role is $42 hourly. Additionally, as an Arc Intern, you'll also get: Boat days – Yes, we actually go out on the water. A lot. Retirement savings — Traditional and Roth 401(k) access Safety support — Reimbursement for PPE, ergonomic equipment, and anything that ensures we keep our crew safe Relocation Assistance Mentorship Opportunities Office perks — Daily lunches, snacks, and good coffee while onsite Our values We move with urgency and build with care. We value these five things above all else: Ownership over both your work and the company’s success Empathy for colleagues and for customers Humility in problem solving and collaboration Pragmatism for navigating ambiguity quickly and sensibly Inclusion of different backgrounds, opinions, cultures, and perspectives. jobs.title: IA Research Engineer Intern
jobs.location: San Jose
jobs.body: About Etched Etched is building hardware for frontier intelligence. We co-design chips, racks, software, and manufacturing to deliver best-in-class throughput and latency across both prefill and decode workloads. Our first products are heavily focused on inference. Backed by hundreds of millions from top-tier investors and staffed by leading engineers, Etched is redefining the infrastructure layer for the fastest growing industry in history. Job Summary We are seeking talented Spring ‘27 and Summer ‘27 IA Research Engineer interns to build the agents that accelerate how Etched produces frontier tokens. You will embed with our kernels team and work alongside our founders on agentic harnesses, tools, and evals that let agents do long-running engineering work people actually rely on. This role is for builders who thrive on ambiguity, have real product sense, and want to own problems end to end. Key responsibilities - Embed with our kernels team to find high-leverage bottlenecks and help turn them into tools engineers use every day. - Build and deploy LLM agents wired into our engineering workflows via tool-calling and MCP. - Help build execution environments where agents can verify their own work, with sandboxed access to simulators, compilers, profilers, and real hardware. - Ship internal products end to end, including the interfaces, data pipelines, and infrastructure behind them. - Design evals and track adoption to measure which tools are working and which aren’t. - Support special projects with the founders across the company. You may be a good fit if you have - Progress towards a Bachelor’s, Master’s, or PhD degree in computer science, computer engineering, or a related field - Strong software engineering fundamentals and a record of shipping projects other people use - Built agents for multi-step tasks beyond calling an API: tool design, context management, evals, and failure analysis - Heavy use of coding agents, including reading their transcripts and changing the system when an agent is confidently wrong - High agency in unfamiliar domains, product sense, and extreme attention to detail Strong candidates may have some experience with - Chip development, GPU kernels, hardware, or manufacturing - Infrastructure, data engineering, or DevOps - Fine-tuning, RAG over technical data, or multi-agent orchestration - Hackathons, startups, or side projects with real users We encourage you to apply even if you do not believe you meet every qualification. Program details - 12-week paid internship - Daily lunch and dinner in our office - Based at our office in San Jose, CA - Direct mentorship from industry leaders and world-class engineers - Opportunity to work on one of the most important problems of our time For any questions, contact internships@etched.com. How we’re different Etched believes in the Bitter Lesson. We are the first inference-focused frontier AI system. Our addressable market is the entirety of inference, unlike many of our competitors. We are a fully in-person team in San Jose (Santana Row), and greatly value engineering skills. We do not have boundaries between engineering and research, and we expect all of our technical staff to contribute to both and work across disciplines as needed.

jobs.body: Figure is an AI robotics company developing autonomous general-purpose humanoid robots. The goal of the company is to ship humanoid robots with human level intelligence. Its robots are engineered to perform a variety of tasks in the home and commercial markets. Figure is headquartered in San Jose, CA. We are looking for a Deployment Engineering Intern to join our Commercial Operations team for Winter 2027. This role works directly with deployment engineers and the pilot team to make our humanoid robots easier to operate and troubleshoot in real-world settings. You will help triage and organize issues from the field: reproducing problems, spotting patterns and preparing clear, well-documented reports for the deployment engineering team. You'll also turn what you learn into documentation and training that helps pilots troubleshoot on their own. Responsibilities: Triage incoming field issues alongside deployment engineers. Reproduce problems, gather logs and context, and build a playbook for pilots to reference for common issues. Test software and hardware changes and gather feedback from pilot team to create robust SOP and technical systems. Build and maintain a system that keeps technical documentation and training up to date as software and hardware change. Develop curriculum that strengthens pilots' troubleshooting skills, and help coaches teach it efficiently. Shadow deployment engineers on bug triage, issue tracking, and testing, and turn what you learn into better documentation. Collect feedback from pilots and coaches and communicate gaps clearly to engineering. Requirements: Currently pursuing a Bachelor's in Electrical, Computer, or Robotics Engineering, Computer Science, or a related field. Minimum 10 weeks internship, starting January 2027. Excellent problem solving and debugging skills. Strong technical writing skills and the ability to explain complex concepts simply. Comfortable learning new systems quickly and working hands-on with hardware. Organized and self-directed, with good judgment in a fast-paced environment. jobs.body: MANUFACTURING ENGINEERING INTERN (SUMMER 2027) Freeform builds AI-native manufacturing systems that unify software, hardware, and physics to produce industrial-scale parts at the speed of human ideation. By treating manufacturing as a single integrated system, we unlock a new era of innovation where complex hardware is designed, built, and scaled without limits. As a Manufacturing Engineering Intern at Freeform, you’ll be at the forefront of scaling production for high-performance metal 3D printed parts. jobs.body: About GlobalFoundries GlobalFoundries is a leading full-service semiconductor foundry providing a unique combination of design, development, and fabrication services to some of the world’s most inspired technology companies. With a global manufacturing footprint spanning three continents, GlobalFoundries makes possible the technologies and systems that transform industries and give customers the power to shape their markets. For more information, visit www.gf.com. Internship Program Overview: Our Interns & Co-ops are our entry-level talent pipeline for GF across the globe. Our goal is to provide students with a meaningful work experience that will equip them with the skills to embark on a career in the fast-paced and growing semiconductor industry after graduation. As an intern at GF, you’ll experience one-on-one mentorship, work assignments that prioritize your growth and potential, professional development opportunities, and the chance to network with executives. Summary of Role: Join the New Product Development team for a hands-on engineering internship focused on automated test solutions for complex digital, analog, and mixed-signal integrated circuits used in automotive and industrial applications. You will work alongside Product and Test Engineers on defined assignments spanning test planning, ATE development, silicon bring-up, validation, data analysis, and manufacturing-readiness activities using Advantest and Teradyne platforms. Essential Responsibilities include: Support pre-silicon planning by translating product requirements and datasheets into technical specifications, specification-compliance matrices, design-for-test requirements, and ATE test plans. Assist with the design of cost-effective ATE hardware and resource allocation that improve multisite efficiency and pin multiplexing for silicon bring-up, validation, and production release. Develop, bring up, validate, and debug automated test programs for digital, analog, and mixed-signal integrated circuits on Advantest and Teradyne ATE platforms. Analyze test and characterization data to investigate design margins, wafer-fabrication process variation, parametric performance, yield, and test-time opportunities. Support process-window experiments, silicon and package qualification activities, and product specification compliance across automotive, industrial, or commercial requirements. Collaborate with Design, DFT, Design Validation, Program Management, Quality and Reliability Engineering, Customer Quality Engineering, Bench Characterization, Applications, Fab, Assembly, and factory Test teams. Contribute to ATE test hardware, socket design, board schematics, layout, diagnostic code, and test automation specifications under the guidance of experienced engineers. Document gaps, lessons learned, and best practices, and contribute reusable methods to the Standard Test Methods Library (STML) across ATE platforms. Other Responsibilities: Perform all activities in a safe and responsible manner and support all Environmental, Health, Safety & Security requirements and programs. Required Qualifications: Education – At least a sophomore at time of application and actively pursuing a Bachelor’s or Master’s in Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, or related field through an accredited degree program during the time of internship. Must have at least an overall 3.0 GPA and be in good academic standing. Language Fluency - English (Written & Verbal) Ability to work at least 40 hours per week during the internship. Preferred Qualifications: Prior related internship or co-op experience Demonstrated prior leadership experience in the workplace, school projects, competitions, etc. Strong interest in leveraging AI tools and emerging technologies to enhance productivity, streamline workflows, and support effective decision-making. Project management skills, i.e., the ability to innovate and execute on solutions that matter; the ability to navigate ambiguity. Strong written and verbal communication skills Strong planning & organizational skills Coursework or project experience in semiconductor test, design-for-test, integrated-circuit design, electronics, or semiconductor physics. Programming experience in one or more languages, including C, C++, Python, or Perl. Familiarity with digital, analog, or mixed-signal circuits, test automation, or laboratory measurement equipment. #InternshipProgramUS Expected Salary Range $20.00 - $40.00 Expected Salary Range $0.00 - $0.00 The exact Salary will be determined based on qualifications, experience and location. jobs.body: Job Details: Job Description: What if your next project helped power the future of technology? At Intel, you'll do more than learn, you'll contribute. You'll work side-by-side with industry leaders, gain hands-on experience on meaningful projects, and help solve real-world challenges that affect billions of people worldwide. From advanced semiconductor manufacturing to AI-powered innovations, you'll play a role in technologies that redefine how the world works, learns, and connects. What makes Intel unique is the opportunity to see the entire technology lifecycle in action. Unlike many companies where hardware, software, and manufacturing operate separately, Intel brings them together, giving you exposure to everything from research and design to advanced semiconductor manufacturing and global deployment. Whether you're tackling engineering challenges, improving operations, analyzing data, advancing next-generation technologies, or supporting global customers, you'll build valuable skills while contributing to innovations that enable a more sustainable and connected future. Bring your curiosity, make an impact, and see where your ideas can take you at Intel. What You'll Do You'll gain hands-on experience supporting Intel's advanced semiconductor manufacturing operations while working with experienced engineers and operations teams. Develop and optimize semiconductor manufacturing processes. Analyze data to improve yield, quality, reliability, and factory performance. Work with advanced semiconductor equipment and fabrication technologies. Apply statistics, data analytics, and failure analysis to solve engineering challenges. Support process control, quality assurance, and continuous improvement initiatives. Contribute to safe, sustainable, and high-performing manufacturing operations. Through these experiences, you will strengthen technical expertise in manufacturing, process optimization, data analytics, quality systems, and problem solving. Where Your Career Could Take You By applying to this requisition, you may be considered for future opportunities such as: Industrial Engineer Manufacturing Operations Manager Module Engineer Process Integration Engineer Repair Development Engineer Gain experiences that can open doors to future opportunities in semiconductor manufacturing, process development, factory automation, yield improvement, quality engineering, and operations leadership. Qualifications: Must possess the minimum qualifications below to be initially considered for this position. Experience may be gained through coursework, research, academic projects, internships, laboratory work, student organizations, leadership experiences, or other relevant experiences. Minimum Qualifications Currently pursuing a Bachelor’s degree in Chemical Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Materials Science, Microelectronics Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Chemistry, Physics, Computer Science, Data Science, Mathematics, or related STEM field. 3+ months of experience gained through coursework, projects, research, internships, lab work, student organizations, or industry experience. Preferred Qualifications Strong academic performance with a cumulative GPA of 3.0 or higher preferred. Experience with programming, data analysis, modeling, simulation, automation, or visualization tools such as Python, MATLAB, SQL, JMP, R, or similar. Coursework, research, academic projects, or internship experience related to semiconductor technology, advanced manufacturing, process development, engineering, materials science, or data analytics. jobs.body: At Jabil (NYSE: JBL), we are proud to be a trusted partner for the world's top brands, offering comprehensive engineering, supply chain, and manufacturing solutions. With 60 years of experience across industries and a vast network of over 100 sites worldwide, Jabil combines global reach with local expertise to deliver both scalable and customized solutions. Our commitment extends beyond business success as we strive to build sustainable processes that minimize environmental impact and foster vibrant and diverse communities around the globe. Summary of Program Jabil’s Summer Internship Program was recognized as one of the Top 100 Internship Programs in the country for 2026 by WayUp. This is the result of a holistic and engaging experience that summer interns at Jabil experience. As a result, interns that are a part of this program for summer 2027 will get to engage with members of Jabil’s leadership team and participate in events related to professional development, networking & socializing, and community engagement. In addition, interns will have the opportunity to work with each other in committees, be assigned a mentor, tour some of Jabil’s facilities and much more! What will you do? - System Architects at Jabil collaborate with customers, sales, and product planning to establish the technical direction for Jabil design teams in the Cloud and Compute markets. As a Mechanical System Architect Intern, you will be expected to: Complete a primary project that includes project management and solution development. Contribute to determining the technical direction for customer originated projects and Jabil's own cloud compute product offerings: Documenting product requirements Communicating the plan of record design and tradeoffs System layout and mechanical feasibility Collaborating with system architects in the mechanical, electrical, thermal, firmware, and software domains Train on detailed design requirements of CPUs, GPUs, Storage, Memory, FPGAs, board materials, regulators, power supplies etc. Hands-on assembly and disassembly of cloud computing products How will you get here? jobs.location: Boise, ID - Main Site, United States of America
jobs.body: Our vision is to transform how the world uses information to enrich life for all . Micron Technology is a world leader in innovating memory and storage solutions that accelerate the transformation of information into intelligence, inspiring the world to learn, communicate and advance faster than ever. The high-volume manufacturing engineering team plays a key role in keeping Micron’s wafer fabs running safely, efficiently, and at scale. We work at the center of manufacturing execution, balancing capacity, risk, and performance to support both development and high-volume production goals. If you enjoy solving complex operational challenges in a fast-paced environment, this is the place to make an impact! As an intern in the Area Manufacturing Engineering (AME) team, you will focus on strengthening area industrial engineering performance by reducing operational risk and building stable, predictable capacity. Working closely with Manufacturing, Process Development, Industrial Engineering, and Operations, you will lead improving cycle time, throughput, and redundancy while supporting ambitious program timelines. This focus directly influences fab performance and development success. Responsibilities Identify and resolve systemic area issues affecting throughput, cycle time, capacity, and operational risk, including supporting capacity planning and modeling. Analyze operational data and performance metrics to identify trends, assess risks, recommend improvement opportunities, and inform capital and capacity decisions. Partner with Industrial Engineering, Process Development, Manufacturing, and Operations to evaluate capacity scenarios, develop mitigation plans, and drive cross-functional projects. Lead and support strategic meetings and capacity-management activities, clearly communicating performance, risks, priorities, and recommended actions to stakeholders. Support safety and quality initiatives, including audits, good catches, and human QDR follow-up. Minimum Qualifications Currently a junior pursuing a bachelor’s degree or a first-year master’s student in Industrial Engineering or an equivalent semiconductor engineering field. Experience using SQL and Python for data analysis, modeling, or engineering applications through coursework, projects, internships, or research. Experience using Tableau or comparable visualization tools to analyze data and communicate trends and results. Experience using Generative AI tools to support data analysis, problem-solving, engineering productivity, or technical communication. Demonstrated ability through academic, project, or work experience to manage multiple priorities and collaborate effectively in a dynamic environment. Preferred Qualifications Experience applying industrial engineering methods to capacity planning, cycle-time improvement, throughput optimization, operational risk reduction, or manufacturing systems. Experience analyzing semiconductor manufacturing, high-volume manufacturing, or other complex operational datasets. Experience developing data-driven capacity scenarios, risk assessments, dashboards, or recommendations using SQL, Python, Tableau, or Generative AI . Demonstrated leadership experience through academic projects, internships, research, student organizations, or other team-based activities. Experience presenting technical analyses, recommendations, or project results to cross-functional stakeholders. jobs.location: Tempe, Arizona, United States of America
jobs.body: Work Flexibility: Onsite What You Get Out of the Internship ​​ At Stryker, we believe that developing the next generation of talent is just as important as developing life-changing medical technologies. As an intern, you won’t just observe — you’ll contribute to meaningful projects, gain exposure to leaders who will mentor you, and experience a culture of innovation and teamwork that is shaping the future of healthcare. As an intern, you will : ​ ​ Apply classroom knowledge and gain experience in a fast-paced and growing industry setting ​ Implement new ideas , be constantly challenged, and develop your skills ​ Network with key/high-level stakeholders and leaders of the business ​ Be a part of an innovative team and culture ​ Experience documenting complex processes and presenting them in a clear format Who we want ​​ Challengers. People who seek out the hard projects and work to find just the right solutions. ​ Teammates. Partners who listen to ideas, share thoughts and work together to move the business forward. ​ Charismatic networkers. Relationship-savvy people who intentionally make connections with both internal partners and external contacts. ​ Strategic thinkers. Interns who propose innovative ideas and consistently exceed their performance objectives . ​ Customer-oriented achievers. Individuals with an unparalleled work ethic and customer-focused attitude who bring value to their partnerships. ​ Game changers. Persistent interns who will stop at nothing to live out Stryker’s mission to make healthcare better. Opportunities Available ​ ​ As a Mechanical Engineering intern at Stryker, you will be placed in one of the following teams: Research & Development New Product Development R&D interns in New Product Development work with cross-functional teams to identify the needs and the goals of future products. They research new technologies , customer expectations, business requirements and regulations. They may work with a variety of tools, including CAD, FEA, and our Test Labs to develop new product concepts. These interns utilize their technical education to design new products and drive them from concept to production. Product Engineering R&D interns in Product Engineering work with cross-functional teams to identify the greatest needs for improvements on current products. They research new technologies , customer feedback, and product performance data to make our products better for Stryker and for our customers. Product Engineering interns work with a variety of tools, including CAD, FEA, Test Labs, and root cause analysis methods. These interns utilize their technical education to improve the safety and efficacy of our existing products. Test Lab Test interns partner closely with Test Engineers and R&D to experiment with early prototypes and vet out product designs throughout the design process. What this really means is that we get to be the Mythbusters of our division. You think your design can last the entire expected service life? We put it to the test. Just like the show, we quickly design and build fixtures to simulate real life situations. In addition to these experiments, we are ultimately responsible for design verification – the quantitative testing of the technical specifications of the product. A team’s experience ranges from 2 to over 15 years with technical specialties ranging from sterilization, mechanical, electrical, software, and optics. If you’re the type of person that has the magic ability to break things – we want you! Majors Targeted: Biomedical Engineering , Mechanical engineering or related majors What You Need ​​ Currently pursuing a Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in a related field; must remain enrolled in a degree-seeking program after the internship . ​ Cumulative 3.0 GPA or above ( verified at time of hire ) Must be legally authorized to work in the U.S. and not require employment-based sponsorship now or in the future . ​ Strong written and verbal communication skills, with proven ability to collaborate and build relationships Demonstrated leadership, problem-solving, and organizational skills with the ability to manage multiple priorities Proficiency in Microsoft Office (Excel, Word, PowerPoint) and eagerness to learn in a dynamic environment . $ 20 min hourly wage – $3 5 max hourly wage, sign-on bonus, 11 paid holidays annually, and either paid corporate housing or a living stipend, dependent upon hiring location Travel Percentage: None Stryker Corporation is an equal opportunity employer. Qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, ethnicity, color, religion, sex, gender identity, sexual orientation, national origin, disability, or protected veteran status. Stryker is an EO employer – M/F/Veteran/Disability. Stryker Corporation will not discharge or in any other manner discriminate against employees or applicants because they have inquired about, discussed, or disclosed their own pay or the pay of another employee or applicant. However, employees who have access to the compensation information of other employees or applicants as a part of their essential job functions cannot disclose the pay of other employees or applicants to individuals who do not otherwise have access to compensation information, unless the disclosure is (a) in response to a formal complaint or charge, (b) in furtherance of an investigation, proceeding, hearing, or action, including an investigation conducted by the employer, or (c) consistent with the contractor’s legal duty to furnish information.

jobs.title: Intern - Field Application and Services Eng (Teradyne, Mexico)
jobs.body: > Teradyne Robotics — Redefining Automation Together At Teradyne Robotics, we’re shaping the future of automation. As part of Teradyne Inc., we unite market-leading automation brands Universal Robots and MiR to create next-generation robotics for markets across the world. With over 110,000 industrial collaborative robots and autonomous mobile robots sold globally, we’re transforming industries and empowering businesses of all sizes. We’re proud to say that our customers count on us. Our Purpose At Teradyne Robotics, our mission is simple: Automation for Anyone. Anywhere. Our vision is to create a world where people work with robots, not like robots. With more than 100,000 collaborative robots deployed worldwide, Universal Robots leads the global market in collaborative automation while MiR provides cutting-edge autonomous mobile robots that transform internal logistics. Together, we enable manufacturers of all sizes to automate, improve productivity, and empower people through robotics. Opportunity Overview The Field Applications and Service Engineer Intern is an early-career technical role designed to support the Teradyne Robotics Service Center in Mexico. Working side by side with experienced service and application engineers, the intern helps deliver day-to-day service operations for the Universal Robots collaborative robots and Mobile Industrial Robots autonomous mobile robots portfolio, including unit intake and diagnostics, repairs and testing, case documentation, and warranty support. Beyond the service bench, this role acts as a flexible support resource for the team: extending its capacity, helping standardize processes, building documentation and tools, and supporting field visits, demonstrations, and application validations when needed. This is a hands-on learning opportunity, with mentorship and real responsibility, for students who want to build a career in robotics and industrial automation. Key Responsibilities Play an active role in daily Service Center operations for UR and MiR products, gaining hands-on experience with unit intake, inventory, logistics, equipment readiness, and essential safety and quality practices. Learn alongside experienced engineers as you help diagnose, troubleshoot, repair, test, and validate robotic systems, and participate in field service, installations, inspections, application trials, demonstrations, and hands-on training. Help deliver a great customer experience by providing first-level technical support to customers and partners, maintaining accurate service and warranty records, and supporting administrative and invoicing documentation. Make a meaningful impact on team performance by analyzing service trends, creating reports and technical resources, improving processes and tools, and supporting events, pre-sales activities, and other team priorities. All About You We seek individuals who share our passion and determination. Our commitment to customer success drives us to go the extra mile. If you’re ready to join us in this mission, take a closer look at the minimum criteria for the position. Minimum Job Requirements Currently enrolled in a Bachelor’s degree program in Mechatronics, Electrical, Electronics, Mechanical, Robotics, Industrial, or a related field. At least two (2) years remaining to complete university studies. Availability to work 20 hours per week, with a schedule agreed upon with the manager and compatible with class schedules. Ability to provide proof of active student status and to formalize the internship through the university’s agreement process, in accordance with applicable regulations in Mexico. Working knowledge of English, with the ability to read technical documentation and communicate in writing. Solid fundamentals in electrical and electronic circuits, mechanical systems, and basic programming or industrial automation concepts. Hands-on aptitude and willingness to work in a service center and workshop environment, including handling equipment and tools. Proficiency with Microsoft Office tools, especially Excel and Word, and ability to learn new software and case management systems quickly. Availability for occasional local travel within Mexico to support customer visits, events, or partner activities. Preferred Job Requirements Exposure to collaborative or industrial robotics through coursework, projects, competitions, or internships, with hands-on experience in technical support, laboratory, or workshop settings preferred. Knowledge of PLCs, industrial communication protocols, sensors, vision systems, electrical schematics, mechanical drawings, or CAD tools. Programming experience in Python or C++, familiarity with ROS, PolyScope, or URScript, and exposure to ticketing, CRM, or case management systems. Curious, proactive, and safety-minded team player with strong analytical, organizational, communication, and customer-service skills; able to work independently, collaborate across teams, take ownership, and seek feedback. *This position is not eligible for visa sponsorship or relocation assistance. #LI-PS1 <span

Our vision is to create a world where people work with robots, not like robots. With more than 100,000 collaborative robots deployed worldwide, Universal Robots leads the global market in collaborative automation while MiR provides cutting-edge autonomous mobile robots that transform internal logistics. Together, we enable manufacturers of all sizes to automate, improve productivity, and empower people through robotics. Opportunity Overview The Field Applications and Service Engineer Intern is an early-career technical role designed to support the Teradyne Robotics Service Center in Mexico. Working side by side with experienced service and application engineers, the intern helps deliver day-to-day service operations for the Universal Robots collaborative robots and Mobile Industrial Robots autonomous mobile robots portfolio, including unit intake and diagnostics, repairs and testing, case documentation, and warranty support. Beyond the service bench, this role acts as a flexible support resource for the team: extending its capacity, helping standardize processes, building documentation and tools, and supporting field visits, demonstrations, and application validations when needed. This is a hands-on learning opportunity, with mentorship and real responsibility, for students who want to build a career in robotics and industrial automation. Key Responsibilities Play an active role in daily Service Center operations for UR and MiR products, gaining hands-on experience with unit intake, inventory, logistics, equipment readiness, and essential safety and quality practices. Learn alongside experienced engineers as you help diagnose, troubleshoot, repair, test, and validate robotic systems, and participate in field service, installations, inspections, application trials, demonstrations, and hands-on training. Help deliver a great customer experience by providing first-level technical support to customers and partners, maintaining accurate service and warranty records, and supporting administrative and invoicing documentation. Make a meaningful impact on team performance by analyzing service trends, creating reports and technical resources, improving processes and tools, and supporting events, pre-sales activities, and other team priorities. All About You We seek individuals who share our passion and determination. Our commitment to customer success drives us to go the extra mile. If you’re ready to join us in this mission, take a closer look at the minimum criteria for the position. Minimum Job Requirements Currently enrolled in a Bachelor’s degree program in Mechatronics, Electrical, Electronics, Mechanical, Robotics, Industrial, or a related field. At least two (2) years remaining to complete university studies. Availability to work 20 hours per week, with a schedule agreed upon with the manager and compatible with class schedules. Ability to provide proof of active student status and to formalize the internship through the university’s agreement process, in accordance with applicable regulations in Mexico. Working knowledge of English, with the ability to read technical documentation and communicate in writing. Solid fundamentals in electrical and electronic circuits, mechanical systems, and basic programming or industrial automation concepts. Hands-on aptitude and willingness to work in a service center and workshop environment, including handling equipment and tools. Proficiency with Microsoft Office tools, especially Excel and Word, and ability to learn new software and case management systems quickly. Availability for occasional local travel within Mexico to support customer visits, events, or partner activities. Preferred Job Requirements Exposure to collaborative or industrial robotics through coursework, projects, competitions, or internships, with hands-on experience in technical support, laboratory, or workshop settings preferred. Knowledge of PLCs, industrial communication protocols, sensors, vision systems, electrical schematics, mechanical drawings, or CAD tools. Programming experience in Python or C++, familiarity with ROS, PolyScope, or URScript, and exposure to ticketing, CRM, or case management systems. Curious, proactive, and safety-minded team player with strong analytical, organizational, communication, and customer-service skills; able to work independently, collaborate across teams, take ownership, and seek feedback. *This position is not eligible for visa sponsorship or relocation assistance. #LI-PS1 <span
