jobs.title: Government Affairs Intern
jobs.location: DC
jobs.body: About Us At Antares, our long-term mission is to make clean energy abundant from Earth to the Asteroid Belt. We’re fueled by the belief that advanced nuclear energy can strengthen our military, solve the climate crisis, elevate global living standards, and expand humanity's presence in outer space. To achieve our mission, we’re building mass-producible, inherently safe, deployable microreactors that can be used terrestrially, underwater, and in space. The Antares team hails from SpaceX, the White House, the Pentagon, the Department of Energy, MIT, Rigetti Computing, General Atomics, Relativity Space, Ursa Major, and National Laboratories like Idaho, Oak Ridge, Los Alamos, and Savannah River. Antares has raised over $600M in venture capital from top-tier investors and has hundreds of million-dollars on contract with the military services, NASA, and the Department of Energy. ABOUT THE SUMMER INTERNSHIP PROGRAM Internships at Antares are anything but ordinary. You'll work alongside our team as we design, build, and test fission microreactors built to deliver reliable energy for critical missions on Earth, in space, and underwater. Our interns contribute to real work from day one. Depending on your role, you may touch hardware, write and test software, support manufacturing and operations, or help build the systems that allow Antares to move quickly as we scale. You'll work alongside engineers, operators, and other experts solving challenging problems—and you'll leave your internship with hands-on experience that's difficult to find anywhere else. We work hard, move quickly, and take pride in what we're building. If you're excited to learn by doing and want to contribute to the next generation of nuclear energy, we'd love to have you join us next summer. We will be running two separate cohorts to accommodate students on both semester and quarter schedules: Cohort #1 Monday, May 17 – Friday, August 13 Cohort #2 Monday, June 14 – Friday, September 10 All internship roles are based at one of our offices (Torrance/Idaho Falls/Washington D.C.) and require interns to work onsite five days per week. We will not be considering candidates for remote or hybrid arrangements. Interns will receive a relocation and housing stipend as part of their offer package if eligible. ABOUT THE ROLE Antares Nuclear is seeking a highly motivated and resourceful Government Affairs Intern to support the company's government affairs, communications, international business development, and commercial business development efforts from our Washington, D.C. office. This position offers a unique opportunity to work on emerging national security and energy policy issues while helping advance the commercialization and international deployment of next-generation nuclear technology. The intern will support research, stakeholder engagement, strategic planning, and business development initiatives, working closely with Antares leadership and cross-functional teams. The ideal candidate is an excellent writer and researcher, has a strong interest in national security, energy, public policy, or emerging technologies, and thrives in a fast-paced environment where initiative and attention to detail are essential. ROLES AND RESPONSIBILITIES: - Monitor congressional activity, federal legislation, appropriations, defense authorization, and executive branch initiatives relevant to advanced nuclear energy and microreactor deployment. - Research and analyze policy developments across the Pentagon, Department of Energy, Department of State, Department of Commerce, NASA, and other relevant federal agencies. - Assist in preparing briefing materials, talking points, policy memoranda, presentations, and other materials for meetings with government officials and congressional offices. - Track engagement with congressional offices, federal agencies, military services, and other key stakeholders. - Identify opportunities to advance policies, programs, and funding initiatives that support microreactor deployment for national security and commercial applications. - Support the development of strategic communications materials that articulate Antares’ mission, technology, and value proposition to government, commercial, and international audiences. - Draft and edit executive talking points, briefing materials, presentation content, website copy, and other communications products. - Monitor media coverage, industry developments, and public discourse related to advanced nuclear energy, national security, and microreactor deployment. - Help translate complex technical and policy issues into clear, accessible messages tailored to different audiences, including policymakers, prospective customers, strategic partners, and the general public. - Assist in developing communications strategies for key company milestones, government announcements, industry events, and strategic partnerships. - Identify opportunities to raise awareness of Antares’ work through relevant publications, industry forums, conferences, and other external channels. - Research international markets and identify countries, government agencies, utilities, defense organizations, and other prospective customers for Antares microreactors. - Assess country-level opportunities based on energy demand, national security priorities, regulatory frameworks, financing mechanisms, and government support for nuclear energy. - Support engagement with U.S. embassies, the State Department, the Foreign Commercial Service, international partners, and prospective overseas customers. - Research foreign government procurement processes, export requirements, financing options, and other factors affecting international reactor deployment. - Prepare country profiles, market assessments, customer briefings, and presentations to support Antares' international growth strategy. - Identify prospective commercial customers and strategic partners across sectors such as data centers, critical infrastructure, industrial facilities, remote power systems, and other energy-intensive applications. - Research customer power requirements, market dynamics, competing energy technologies, and potential use cases for microreactors. - Assist with developing customer presentations, market analyses, business cases, and strategic partnership proposals. - Maintain and update business development pipelines, stakeholder databases, and opportunity trackers. - Support preparation for customer meetings, industry conferences, and strategic partner engagements. BASIC QUALIFICATIONS: - Currently pursuing an undergraduate or graduate degree in public policy, international relations, political science, economics, business, engineering, energy policy, or a related field. - Strong research, analytical, and written communication skills. - Demonstrated interest in national security, energy, emerging technologies, international affairs, or commercial strategy. - Ability to synthesize complex information into clear, concise briefings and recommendations. - Strong organizational skills, attention to detail, and the ability to manage multiple projects simultaneously. - Proficiency in Microsoft Office, particularly PowerPoint, Word, and Excel. - A proactive, intellectually curious approach and willingness to take ownership of assignments. PREFERRED SKILLS & EXPERIENCE: - Sound judgment, discretion, and the ability to manage sensitive matters and competing priorities in a fast-moving environment. - Experience with congressional offices, federal agencies, think tanks, political campaigns, consulting, or business development. - Familiarity with U.S. national security policy, federal appropriations, international trade, or the energy sector. - Experience conducting market research, developing presentations, or preparing policy and business memoranda. - Foreign language proficiency or international experience. ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS: - Ability to travel as needed for government, regulator, supplier, customer, and international partner engagements. - Ability to support time-sensitive milestones or incidents outside standard business hours when necessary. LOCATION - We are located in downtown Washington, DC in a space designed for team collaboration and easy access to Capitol Hill, federal government offices, foreign embassies, and DC-based think tanks. Culture At Antares, we like to specifically tie each role to our founding document’s set of values–here are the top five cultural values we think you should believe at your core to be successful: - Think in Systems - Energy and Defense are complex ecosystems with numerous stakeholders with competing priorities, conflicting policies, perverse incentives, and emergent and path-dependent properties. First principles thinking alone is insufficient. Think probabilistically and then take action. “If you want to be certain, then you are apt to be obsolete.” Over-optimizing the components often degrades the system - Obsess over the End User - The customer and end user are often not the same. We will never build globally competitive commercial products if we lose sight of our end users and their entire interaction with the product life cycle - Be Unconstrained by Convention - Our only limits are the laws of physics. Many, even experts, will say what we are working on is impossible. They said the same about SpaceX reusing rockets. Generationally impactful companies, by definition, must accomplish the seemingly impossible. If it were easy, it would have already been done. Never shy away from a solution because it has never been tried before, and never choose to do something because that's “how it's always been done” - Go Where the Work Is - Never miss a chance to meet a customer, user, or stakeholder face to face, even if that means hopping on a plane. If you can’t make it, find a teammate who can channel your intentions and go in your place. Deep work can be done from anywhere, but we believe teams are built in person, and aim to maximize our time together - Operate in the Grey - Embrace nuance in pursuit of truth. Question every fundamental assumption Equal Opportunity Antares is an Equal Opportunity Employer. Employment decisions are based solely on merit, competence, and qualifications, without regard to race, color, religion, gender, national origin/ethnicity, veteran status, disability status, age, sexual orientation, gender identity, marital status, mental or physical disability, or any other legally protected status. ITAR REQUIREMENTS To conform to U.S. Government export regulations, applicant must be a (i) U.S. citizen or national, (ii) U.S. lawful, permanent resident (aka green card holder), (iii) Refugee under 8 U.S.C. § 1157, or (iv) Asylee under 8 U.S.C. § 1158, or be eligible to obtain the required authorizations from the U.S. Department of State. Learn more about the ITAR here https://www.pmddtc.state.gov/?id=ddtc_kb_article_page&sys_id=24d528fddbfc930044f9ff621f961987. Pay range: $34 per hour.

jobs.body: ABOUT ROCKET LAB Rocket Lab is the end-to-end space company building rockets, spacecraft, and critical subsystems that keep the world connected, protected, expand humanity’s reach to the Moon, Mars, and beyond. We move fast, build real hardware for meaningful missions, and make the impossible routine. Come shape the future with us. As a Test Engineering Intern based at Rocket Lab’s site in Stennis, Mississippi, you will have the opportunity to learn about the Archimedes Engine test operations on-site as well as actively participate as an operator by supporting engine rebuilds, test readiness, and hardware swaps. The Test Operations team manages the activation and operation of test facilities for the Archimedes rocket engine, collaborating with propulsion teams to develop test procedures and sequencing and ultimately enabling the path to launch our Neutron vehicle. WHAT YOU’LL GET TO DO As an intern, you will work closely with your mentor and other employees within the department to apply your knowledge and grow your skills both technically and professionally Work with a fast-paced group of professionals to apply engineering and industry concepts to solve real challenges Attend frequent 1:1’s with mentors and supervisors to facilitate success and learning while providing progress updates Enjoy tech talks and network with other interns and employees through social and professional events YOU’LL BRING THESE QUALIFICATIONS Ideal candidates will thrive in ambiguity and are excited to work in small, high-performing teams that are focused on continued learning and growth. Success in this position will be measured by the knowledge and experience you bring to the role, your ability to lead development projects without supervision, and your ability to successfully collaborate across teams to deliver results. Must be enrolled in a bachelor’s, master's or doctorate degree program in an engineering discipline such as Electrical Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Aerospace Engineering, or a related discipline and have at least one semester of school remaining post internship GPA of 3.0 or above 3+ months of applied engineering experience (internship, laboratory, and personal/team project experience is applicable) THESE QUALIFICATIONS WOULD BE NICE TO HAVE GPA of 3.5 or above 6+ months of applied engineering experience (internship, laboratory, and personal/team project experience is applicable) Experience with Soildworks, MATLAB, and SiemensNX Python and Java experience Proficient in Computer-aided design and manufacturing (CAD/ CAM) Geometric Dimensioning & Tolerancing experience Experience working with pressurized systems ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS Able to work full-time, on-site for a minimum of 12 consecutive weeks beginning May or June 2027 COMPENSATION AND OTHER BENEFITS Pay Rate: $25.00 USD Hourly You may be eligible for a stipend to subsidize relocation costs WHAT TO EXPECT We’re on a mission to unlock the potential of space to improve life on Earth, but that’s not an easy task. It takes hard work, determination, relentless innovation, teamwork, grit, and an unwavering commitment to achieving what others often deem impossible. Our people out-think, out-work, and out-pace. We pride ourselves on having each other’s backs, checking our egos at the door, and rolling up our sleeves on all tasks big and small. We thrive under pressure, work to tight deadlines, and our focus is always on how we can deliver, rather than dwelling on the challenges that stand in the way. jobs.body: The 2027 Summer Internship Program will run from May 17, 2027, through August 6, 2027. Candidates must be available to start on May 17 and participate through the duration of the program. Applicants must be legally authorized to work in the United States. We are unable to sponsor or take over sponsorship of a school/employment or any other visa, regardless of expiration date, now or in the future. Who Are We? The Toro Company (TTC) has delivered market-leading, innovative products and outstanding customer care for more than 100 years. With over 11,000 employees worldwide, TTC is headquartered in Bloomington, Minnesota, USA. Our company designs and manufactures turf maintenance equipment; turf irrigation systems; landscape and lighting products; snow and ice management solutions; agricultural irrigation systems; rental, specialty and underground construction equipment; and residential turf and snow equipment. We market and sell TTC products worldwide through a network of distributors, dealers, mass retailers, hardware retailers, equipment rental center and home centers—as well as online direct to end users. Join The Toro Company’s Advanced Manufacturing Engineering (AME) Team, where innovation meets hands-on experience. As an intern, you’ll work alongside industry experts to help bring new products from concept to production. You’ll gain exposure to design for manufacturability (DFMA), process development, cost optimization, and advanced tooling technologies—all while contributing to real-world projects that make an impact. Participate in the New Product Development (NPD) process from prototype to production. Support local plant builds (prototype, pilot, and production). Assist in assembly process development and improvement. Perform DFMA reviews and contribute to cost justification/ROI analyses. Evaluate vertical integration and outsourcing opportunities. Contribute to the creation of data-driven analytics tools. Deliver a final presentation to Toro leaders on your project work and outcomes. What Do You Need? To be considered for this role, an individual should meet the following minimal requirements: Currently enrolled in a 4-year accredited program in Manufacturing, Mechanical, Industrial, Electrical or Agricultural Engineering. Junior standing or higher (graduation no sooner than Dec 2026). Strong problem-solving skills and ability to work independently or in a team. Proficiency with Microsoft Office Suite. Experience with Microsoft Power BI and Power Apps. Experience with CAD/CREO/CreoView (preferred). Interest in manufacturing technologies and continuous improvement. What Can We Give You? At The Toro Company, we are always working to make sure our interns know just how valued they are. In addition to a competitive pay- The Toro Company offers interns a variety of perks, including: Dress for your day – We know you're more productive when you're comfortable, which is why TTC employees are encouraged to take advantage of our casual, corporate environment. jobs.location: El Segundo, California, United States
jobs.body: About Varda Low Earth orbit is open for business. Varda is accelerating the development of commercial space infrastructure, from in-orbit pharmaceutical processing to reliable and economical reentry capsules. Varda’s W-Series vehicles are built, designed, and operated by Varda in-house, including the pharmaceutical processing payloads, the capsules, the C-PICA heat shields, and the satellite buses. From life-saving pharmaceuticals to more powerful fiber optics, there is a world of products used on Earth today that can only be manufactured in space. Varda is accelerating innovation in the orbital economy by creating both the products and infrastructure needed so space can directly benefit life on Earth. Our mission is to expand the economic bounds of humankind. Our team is uniquely suited to accomplishing this goal, with leadership and staff comprised of veterans from SpaceX, Blue Origin, major pharmaceutical companies and Silicon Valley. Varda was founded in January 2021 by Will Bruey and Delian Asparouhov with significant backing from world class investors including Khosla Ventures, Lux Capital, Founders Fund, Caffeinated Capital, General Catalyst, and Also Capital. Varda is headquartered in El Segundo, California, where we have offices and a production facility where our vehicles, equipment, and materials are built, integrated, and tested. Varda also has offices in Washington, DC and Huntsville, AL. Join Varda, and work to create a bustling in-space ecosystem. About This Role Summer internships will range between the months of May and August. All dates dependent upon the university schedule of the selected students. Internships are full-time and on-site in Los Angeles, CA. To be considered for this internship, candidates must be actively enrolled in an accredited undergraduate or graduate degree program. The aerodynamic department is responsible for all aerodynamic and aero-heating analysis for all our flight vehicles in all flight regimes. Varda already has a flight-proven vehicle; however, this summer we will work on extending our vehicle payload capabilities for commercial customers and flight test capabilities for hypersonic testbed customers. The occupant of this role will contribute by running simulations and supporting wind tunnel activities that would help improve the capabilities of Varda vehicles! Internships at Varda are optimal for students looking to grow technically and professionally while working on impactful projects critical to the company’s success. You will be working on a collaborative team in a startup environment while being able to learn from some of most accomplished and experienced aerospace professionals in the world. We’re dedicated to providing an experience that will let your decisions and contributions help drive Varda’s success. Responsibilities Run Computational Fluid Dynamics (CFD) simulations to analyze vehicle performance Support wind tunnel testing campaigns and post-processing of data Collaborate with engineers to assess aerodynamic loads and thermal environments Contribute to vehicle design improvements based on simulation and test data Basic Qualifications Coursework in: Compressible Fluid Mechanics Thermodynamics Numerical Methods Programming in Python and/or MATLAB Experience with: Running CFD tools Using Linux-based systems Programming in Python and/or MATLAB Preferred Skills And Experience Currently pursuing or completed a Master’s degree in Aerodynamics or Numerical Methods Experience running CFD or DSMC Familiar with Tecplot and Pointwise Some graduate school experience in aerodynamics or fluid mechanics Some past experience on an aerodynamics or fluid mechanics project or club Compensation Hourly Rate : $33.00 Housing stipend for interns relocating to the area Commuter benefit to support local transportation Benefits for Interns Health & Wellness Paid observed holidays 100% company-paid Medical, Dental, and Vision insurance plans for employees and dependents with FSA and employer-matched HSA options $120/month wellness reimbursement for gym and fitness expenses Sponsored One Medical memberships for employees and their dependents Financial $20/pay period cell phone reimbursement Up to $4,000 gross up in relocation support, if eligible Up to $850 commute credit through Lyft or car rental reimbursement, if eligible Workplace Experience & Perks Fully stocked kitchen with lunch provided daily and dinner provided twice weekly Company and team-bonding events, happy hours and mission-success celebrations Complimentary EV charging ITAR Requirements Varda, like all employers, must ensure that its employees working in the United States are lawfully authorized to work in the U.S. Additionally, our employees are exposed to and have access to certain export-controlled items. jobs.title: Launch & Scale Intern (Summer 2027)
jobs.location: South San Francisco, California, USA
jobs.body: About Zipline Zipline is the world’s largest and most experienced drone delivery service. We are on a mission to serve all humans equally by ensuring access to food, medicine and essential goods anytime, anywhere. We design, build, and operate the world’s largest autonomous logistics system, delivering critical supplies quickly and reliably. Today, Zipline operates on four continents, makes a delivery somewhere in the world every 30 seconds, and has completed millions of deliveries to date, including blood, vaccines, medical supplies, food, and retail products. Our customers include the world’s largest and most prominent healthcare systems, governments, retailers, restaurants and global businesses who rely on us to save lives, reduce emissions, increase economic opportunity, and provide delivery from point A to point B as fast as possible. The drone is only 15% of what we’ve built to enable seamless, reliable, global operations. Our system strengthens supply chains, reduces congestion, and gives people time back. With more than 140 million commercial autonomous miles safely flown, Zipline is redefining access to healthcare, consumer products, and food across the globe. We operate at a global scale and are looking for practical problem solvers who thrive on real-world challenges and rapid growth. Our team is motivated by building systems that have a direct, meaningful impact on people’s lives and by scaling the future of logistics. We are seeking people who sculpt from first principles, enjoy facing adversity, and can do the impossible at record breaking speeds. About the Launch & Scale Team The Launch & Scale team builds the operating system that brings new sites, metros, and partners online and helps the network scale reliably. We turn complex dependencies into clear launch plans, readiness mechanisms, tools, and operating rhythms. We partner across infrastructure, permitting, flight operations, maintenance, commercial, partner readiness, and field operations. Our work stays close to real launches so that field lessons become repeatable systems rather than one-off fixes. As an intern, you will report to the Director, Launch & Site Operations and work closely with Launch Managers and cross-functional teams that bring the network online. The Role As the Launch & Scale Intern, you will contribute to a high-impact project that improves how Zipline plans, executes, and learns from launches. You will support Launch Managers by bringing structure to dependencies, analyzing readiness and performance, and helping teams turn field lessons into repeatable tools. You may spend time close to active launches, but you will work with experienced teammates rather than serve as the accountable launch owner. You will also own a clearly scoped project—such as a dashboard, process improvement, playbook, or lightweight automation—from problem definition through pilot and handoff. Along the way, you will receive coaching from the Director, Launch & Site Operations and collaborate with operators, engineers, commercial teammates, and field teams. What You'll Do Support integrated launch plans for assigned workstreams by organizing milestones, dependencies, owners, risks, and open decisions. Analyze launch and site-operations data to identify bottlenecks, inconsistencies, and opportunities to improve speed, quality, or repeatability. Prepare materials for readiness reviews and operating forums, including concise status summaries, action logs, and decision briefs. Work with Launch Managers and functional teams to follow up on commitments, reconcile conflicting information, and surface blockers early. Build or improve practical tools such as dashboards, playbooks, templates, checklists, or lightweight automations. Participate in selected onsite launch activities, capture field observations, and translate lessons into process improvements. Own a scoped internship project from problem definition through pilot, measurement, and an accepted handoff to the team. What You'll Bring Currently pursuing a bachelor’s or graduate degree in operations, engineering, business, supply chain, data and analytics, or a related field. Structured problem-solving skills and curiosity about how complex physical or technical systems work. Comfort with quantitative analysis, including spreadsheets and at least one data or automation tool such as SQL, Python, or a business-intelligence platform. Clear written and verbal communication, with the ability to make complex information easy to understand. Evidence of following through on a project involving multiple contributors through coursework, work, research, or extracurricular experience. Comfort operating in ambiguity, asking good questions, incorporating feedback, and staying reliable on details. Ability to work onsite in South San Francisco and willingness to travel occasionally within the United States to support launches. What Else You Should Know This internship is a full-time position, in-person at our South San Francisco office. We will host our Summer 2027 interns from (May/June - August/September). Zipline is unable to sponsor work visas for applicants to this position. The hourly rate for this internship is $34 per hour. Additional benefits may include relocation support, a housing stipend, overtime pay, paid sick time, and other benefits, where applicable and subject to local requirements. Candidates are limited to three (3) applications within a 30-day period. Zipline is an equal opportunity employer and prohibits discrimination and harassment of any type without regard to race, color, religion, age, sex, national origin, disability status, genetics, protected veteran status, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, or any other characteristic protected by federal, state or local laws or our own sensibilities. Zipline is also committed to providing reasonable accommodations to individuals with disabilities. Please let your point of contact at Zipline know if you require any accommodations throughout your interview process. Whatever your decision, it will not be considered in the hiring process or thereafter. Any information that you do provide will be recorded and maintained in a confidential file. As set forth in Zipline ’s Equal Employment Opportunity policy, we do not discriminate on the basis of any protected group status under any applicable law.

The Quality / Industrial / Manufacturing Engineering Intern will support key quality improvement and corrective action initiatives across Zurn Elkay's manufacturing operations. This role provides hands-on experience identifying quality issues, conducting root cause investigations, implementing corrective actions, and driving continuous improvement efforts that enhance product quality, operational performance, and customer satisfaction. Working closely with Quality, Manufacturing, Engineering, Supply Chain, and Operations teams, the intern will help analyze defects, investigate warranty and customer concerns, support corrective action processes, and identify opportunities to improve manufacturing quality systems. This position is ideal for a student interested in quality engineering, manufacturing operations, continuous improvement, and problem-solving in a fast-paced production environment. Participate in root cause analysis activities utilizing tools such as 5 Whys, Fishbone Diagrams, Pareto Analysis, and Failure Mode and Effects Analysis (FMEA). Assist in developing, documenting, and implementing corrective and preventive actions (CAPAs). Monitor corrective action effectiveness and validate sustainable solutions. Partner with Manufacturing, Engineering, Operations, Supply Chain, and Customer Service teams to resolve quality concerns. Participate in continuous improvement and Lean Manufacturing initiatives. Support implementation of process changes designed to improve product quality and operational efficiency. Assist in managing project timelines, action item tracking, and project documentation. Learning & Development Opportunities Completion of one or more quality improvement and corrective action projects. Root cause analysis and corrective action recommendations for a significant quality issue. Analysis of quality performance trends with identified improvement opportunities. Measurable contribution to reducing defects, scrap, rework, warranty claims, or process variation. Final presentation summarizing findings, corrective actions, project impact, and future recommendations. Documented improvements to quality processes, reporting, or operational performance. Qualifications Currently pursuing a bachelor’s degree in industrial engineering, manufacturing engineering, quality engineering, mechanical engineering, or other related field. Strong analytical and problem-solving skills. Excellent communication and organizational abilities. Ability to work effectively in a manufacturing environment. jobs.location: Cambridge, Massachusetts
jobs.body: Overview Keysight is at the forefront of technology innovation, delivering breakthroughs and trusted insights in electronic design, simulation, prototyping, test, manufacturing, and optimization. Our ~16,800 employees create world-class solutions in communications, 5G, automotive, energy, quantum, aerospace, defense, and semiconductor markets for customers in over 100 countries. Learn more about what we do. Our award-winning culture embraces a bold vision of where technology can take us and a passion for tackling challenging problems with industry-first solutions. We believe that when people feel a sense of belonging, they can be more creative, innovative, and thrive at all points in their careers. The Quantum Engineering Solution (QES) team at Keysight designs and develops measurement solutions that enable the future of quantum technologies. QES’s world-class solutions address the challenging and exciting market of quantum technologies, including quantum computing, quantum communications, and quantum sensing. Responsibilities We are seeking a curious, creative individual to develop and evaluate techniques for characterizing the electrical properties of quantum devices used in quantum computing. As the industry drives toward utility-scale quantum computing, it is critical to optimize the processes for manufacturing quantum devices repeatably and reliably. Keysight’s expertise in test and measurement in both labs and foundries uniquely positions us to help customers meet these challenges. In this role, you’ll have access to high-performance instrumentation to develop measurement strategies for testing and characterizing quantum devices. In addition, you’ll develop Python workflows to demonstrate how these measurements can be automated through software programming interfaces. Your work will help shape QES’s approach to delivering world-class quantum test and measurement solutions. The ideal candidate has an interest in quantum engineering, particularly quantum computing, and strong Python programming skills. Prior experience with measurement equipment is not required; you will work alongside a team of experts who will provide guidance and support. Success in this role requires initiative, the ability to work independently, and a willingness to ask questions and seek help when needed. Responsibilities Develop measurement techniques on quantum devices using a parametric analyzer Create Python scripts to automate the measurements and demonstrate repeatability Collaborate with QES physicists to identify measurement challenges and develop practical solutions. Present findings and alternative approaches to the team, incorporate feedback to refine measurement techniques and automation workflows. Qualifications Required Skills Currently pursuing a BS or MS in Electrical Engineering, Physics, or a related field. Experience programming in Python, including writing scripts for data collection, analysis, and automation. Strong written, verbal, and visual communication skills, with ability to explain technical concepts clearly. Ability to work independently and collaboratively in a cross-functional team environment. Willingness to quickly learn new technologies and communicate technical concepts clearly. Desired Skills Familiarity with quantum computing or other quantum technologies. Experience programming test instrumentation using PyVisa or similar API. Portfolio or examples of relevant work or academic projects preferred. The level of the role will be based on applicable experience, education and skills; most offers will be between the minimum and midpoint of the salary range listed below. Massachusetts pay range: MIN $30.34 to MAX $32.68 Note: for other locations, pay ranges vary by region. Relocation is available for this position. jobs.body: About Marvell Marvell’s semiconductor solutions are the essential building blocks of the data infrastructure that connects our world. Across enterprise, cloud and AI, and carrier architectures, our innovative technology is enabling new possibilities. At Marvell, you can affect the arc of individual lives, lift the trajectory of entire industries, and fuel the transformative potential of tomorrow. For those looking to make their mark on purposeful and enduring innovation, above and beyond fleeting trends, Marvell is a place to thrive, learn, and lead. Your Team, Your Impact The Custom Cloud Solutions (CCS) Hardware Validation Group is responsible for ensuring the quality, reliability, and performance of next-generation data center ASIC and SoC products — spanning cloud infrastructure, AI accelerators, network processors, NICs, custom ASICs, SSD controllers, CXL devices, and domain-specific accelerators. Our team owns end-to-end hardware validation, working across the full product lifecycle from early silicon bring-up through system-level qualification. As an intern, you will work alongside experienced engineers in a fully instrumented hardware lab, gaining hands-on exposure to cutting-edge silicon validation across high-speed interfaces and complex platform environments. This is a unique opportunity to contribute to real engineering challenges that directly impact the future of data infrastructure. What You Can Expect Assist in functional hardware validation and debug activities for platforms utilizing high-speed interfaces such as PCIe, CXL, and Ethernet Support system bring-up tasks by running test cases, collecting data, and documenting results under the guidance of senior engineers Write and execute automation scripts (Python or similar) to streamline silicon testing and validation workflows Operate standard lab equipment — including logic analyzers and oscilloscopes — to assist with signal integrity analysis and system debugging Collaborate with cross-functional teams (design, firmware, and validation) to investigate and reproduce hardware or protocol-level issues, and contribute to root-cause analysis What We're Looking For Currently enrolled in a Bachelor's Degree in Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, Computer Science, or a related field with an expected graduation date of Fall 2027 – Summer 2028 Basic understanding of digital logic, computer architecture, or hardware design principles gained through coursework or personal projects Familiarity with at least one scripting or programming language (Python, C, or similar) for writing test scripts or automating tasks Ability to work in a hands-on lab environment and a willingness to learn how to use standard lab equipment (e.g., oscilloscopes, logic analyzers) Strong communication skills and a collaborative mindset, with the ability to document findings clearly and work effectively within a team Preferred Qualifications: Coursework or project experience related to high-speed interfaces (PCIe, Ethernet, USB, or similar protocols) Exposure to hardware bring-up, FPGA/ASIC design, or embedded systems through academic projects or internships Experience with version control tools (e.g., Git) and basic familiarity with Linux/Unix environments Expected Base Pay Range (USD) 28 - 56, $ per hour. The successful candidate’s starting base pay will be determined based on job-related skills, experience, qualifications, work location and market conditions. The expected base pay range for this role may be modified based on market conditions. This role is eligible to participate in Marvell's bonus and equity plans, including a new hire equity grant and annual equity refreshers, ensuring you are rewarded for your contributions and remain invested in the company's long-term success. jobs.location: Folsom, CA, United States of America
jobs.body: Our vision is to transform how the world uses information to enrich life for all . Micron Technology is a world leader in innovating memory and storage solutions that accelerate the transformation of information into intelligence, inspiring the world to learn, communicate and advance faster than ever. The HBM Platform Architecture team defines the electrical, thermal, and power-delivery architectures that enable Micron's next-generation High Bandwidth Memory (HBM) solutions. Working closely with architecture, design, packaging, and technology teams, the organization drives innovation in signaling, power integrity, thermal management, and system optimization to support AI, high-performance computing, and data center applications. As an HBM Platform Architecture Intern, you will contribute to the development of future HBM platforms by evaluating electrical, thermal, and power delivery architectures for advanced memory systems. You will work alongside experienced architects to analyze design trade-offs, develop modeling tools, and investigate solutions that improve performance, power efficiency, reliability, and scalability for next-generation memory products. Responsibilities Perform signaling and timing analysis for on-die and off-die interfaces across multiple system and packaging topologies. Develop and evaluate thermal models to analyze heat transfer, thermal performance, and design trade-offs in advanced memory systems. Analyze power delivery networks (PDNs), including IR-drop, electromigration (EM), power integrity, and power grid optimization for advanced HBM architectures. Develop modeling, simulation, and automation tools to support power delivery, thermal analysis, and architecture evaluation activities. Collaborate with architecture, design, packaging, and technology teams to evaluate system-level trade-offs and support future HBM technology development. Minimum Qualifications 0-2 years of relevant experience through internships, research projects, coursework, or academic projects in electrical engineering, VLSI design, signal integrity, power integrity, thermal analysis, semiconductor design, or related technical fields. Currently pursuing a Bachelor's, Master's, or PhD degree in Electrical Engineering, Electronics Engineering, Computer Engineering, Computer Science, or a related field. Coursework or project experience in analog design, I/O design, signaling, DRAM technologies, high-speed interfaces, packaging, or 2.5D/3D integration technologies. Understanding of electrical systems, signal integrity, power delivery, circuit analysis, or semiconductor design fundamentals. Ability to read and interpret technical specifications, datasheets, interface standards, and hardware documentation. Strong analytical, problem-solving, and technical communication skills. Experience using AI-enabled tools and large language models (LLMs) such as Copilot, Claude, ChatGPT, or similar technologies as part of engineering workflows, with the ability to validate and critically evaluate AI-generated outputs. Preferred Qualifications Familiarity with Cadence EDA tools, MATLAB, thermal analysis tools, signal integrity tools, or related engineering software. Knowledge of semiconductor packaging, assembly processes, heterogeneous integration, or advanced packaging technologies. Experience with analog design, I/O design, timing analysis, signal integrity, or system-level electrical modeling through coursework, research, or project work. Experience with thermal modeling, computational analysis, power delivery analysis, IR-drop, electromigration (EM), or power integrity evaluations. Knowledge of HBM, DRAM, memory interfaces, advanced interconnects, or high-speed signaling technologies. Experience developing engineering automation tools, simulation environments, data analysis workflows, or modeling frameworks using Python or similar programming languages. Demonstrated interest in semiconductor architecture, advanced memory technologies, AI infrastructure, and next-generation computing systems. jobs.title: Combustion Devices Intern Summer 2027
jobs.location: Long Beach, CA
jobs.body: ABOUT ROCKET LAB Rocket Lab is the end-to-end space company building rockets, spacecraft, and critical subsystems that keep the world connected, protected, expand humanity’s reach to the Moon, Mars, and beyond. We move fast, build real hardware for meaningful missions, and make the impossible routine. Come shape the future with us. As a Combustion Devices Intern based at Rocket Lab’s site in Long Beach, California, you will have the opportunity to support the team in designing, analyzing and testing combustion devices, as well as gain experience with GD&T drafting and data processing and testing. From designing and testing structures and components, to firing up new engines, to setting up launch pads and test sites across the United States, joining the Combustion Devices team is your opportunity to help launch a new large rocket for the very first time. WHAT YOU’LL GET TO DO As an intern, you will work closely with your mentor and other employees within the department to apply your knowledge and grow your skills both technically and professionally Work with a fast-paced group of professionals to apply engineering and industry concepts to solve real challenges Attend frequent 1:1’s with mentors and supervisors to facilitate success and learning while providing progress updates Enjoy tech talks and network with other interns and employees through social and professional events YOU’LL BRING THESE QUALIFICATIONS Ideal candidates will thrive in ambiguity and are excited to work in small, high-performing teams that are focused on continued learning and growth. Success in this position will be measured by the knowledge and experience you bring to the role, your ability to lead development projects without supervision, and your ability to successfully collaborate across teams to deliver results. Must be enrolled in a bachelor’s, master's or doctorate degree program in an engineering, physics or math discipline and have at least one semester of school remaining post internship GPA of 3.0 or above 3+ months of applied engineering experience (internship, laboratory, and personal/team project experience is applicable) THESE QUALIFICATIONS WOULD BE NICE TO HAVE GPA of 3.5 or above 6+ months of applied engineering experience (internship, laboratory, and personal/team project experience is applicable) Experience with CAD/CAM Geometric Dimensioning and Tolerancing (GD&T) drafting experience Finite Element Analysis (FEA) experience Experience with 3D printing Experience with programs such as: ANSYS, MATLAB, Siemens NX Propulsion experience ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS Able to work full-time, on-site for a minimum of 12 consecutive weeks beginning May or June 2027 COMPENSATION AND OTHER BENEFITS Pay Range CA: $28.00 USD Hourly You may be eligible for a stipend to subsidize relocation costs Level and base salary will be determined on a case-by-case basis and may vary based on the following considerations: job-related knowledge and skills, education, and experience. Base salary is just one component of our total rewards package at Rocket Lab. Our comprehensive benefits package includes our industry-leading Employee Stock Purchase Program (with a 15% discount on company stock), top-tier medical plans (HMO, PPO, and a zero cost HDHP option with a significant HSA company contribution), dental and vision coverage, paid vacation and sick time, 11 paid holidays, flexible spending and dependent care accounts, paid parental leave, disability and life insurance, and a 401(k) retirement plan with company match. Additional perks include subsidized EV charging, onsite fitness centers (where available), discounted gym memberships, complimentary snacks and beverages, 50% employee discount on our popular merch store, and a variety of other employee discounts. Eligibility for benefits may vary based on employment status, please check with your recruiter for a comprehensive list of the benefits available for this role. Benefit programs are subject to change at the company’s discretion. Hourly Pay Range (CA Only) $28 — $28 USD WHAT TO EXPECT We’re on a mission to unlock the potential of space to improve life on Earth, but that’s not an easy task. It takes hard work, determination, relentless innovation, teamwork, grit, and an unwavering commitment to achieving what others often deem impossible. Our people out-think, out-work, and out-pace. We pride ourselves on having each other’s backs, checking our egos at the door, and rolling up our sleeves on all tasks big and small. We thrive under pressure, work to tight deadlines, and our focus is always on how we can deliver, rather than dwelling on the challenges that stand in the way. Only messages left for this purpose will be considered. A response to your request may take up to two business days. jobs.title: Quality Engineering Intern - Summer 2027
jobs.location: Los Angeles
jobs.body: About Us At Antares, our long-term mission is to make clean energy abundant from Earth to the Asteroid Belt. We’re fueled by the belief that advanced nuclear energy can strengthen our military, solve the climate crisis, elevate global living standards, and expand humanity's presence in outer space. To achieve our mission, we’re building mass-producible, inherently safe, deployable microreactors that can be used terrestrially, underwater, and in space. The Antares team hails from SpaceX, the White House, the Pentagon, the Department of Energy, MIT, Rigetti Computing, General Atomics, Relativity Space, Ursa Major, and National Laboratories like Idaho, Oak Ridge, Los Alamos, and Savannah River. Antares has raised over $600M in venture capital from top-tier investors and has hundreds of million-dollars on contract with the military services, NASA, and the Department of Energy. About the Summer Internship Program Internships at Antares are anything but ordinary. You'll work alongside our team as we design, build, and test fission microreactors built to deliver reliable energy for critical missions on Earth, in space, and underwater. Our interns contribute to real work from day one. Depending on your role, you may touch hardware, write and test software, support manufacturing and operations, or help build the systems that allow Antares to move quickly as we scale. You'll work alongside engineers, operators, and other experts solving challenging problems—and you'll leave your internship with hands-on experience that's difficult to find anywhere else. We work hard, move quickly, and take pride in what we're building. If you're excited to learn by doing and want to contribute to the next generation of nuclear energy, we'd love to have you join us next summer. We will be running two separate cohorts to accommodate students on both semester and quarter schedules: Cohort #1 Monday, May 17 – Friday, August 13 Cohort #2 Monday, June 14 – Friday, September 10 All internship roles are based at our Torrance headquarters and require interns to work onsite five days per week. We will not be considering candidates for remote or hybrid arrangements. Interns will receive a relocation and housing stipend as part of their offer package. About the Team Interns on the Quality Engineering team develop inspection methods and qualify inspection equipment for a variety of mechanical and electrical systems. They work cross-functionally with design, manufacturing, test, supply chain, and materials teams to validate hardware, characterize the uncertainty of inspection techniques, and ensure rigor in the build of nuclear systems, structures, and components. Interns begin with small starter projects and quickly progress to a long-duration project that culminates in a technical deliverable and presentation. You will be integrated and evaluated as a first-year junior engineer, not simply as an intern. The bar for success is high: you are expected to use your mentor and available resources thoughtfully, execute on your project, and proactively identify additional issues and opportunities for improvement. Roles and Responsibilities: - Develop inspection methods for mechanical and electrical systems. - Support the qualification and implementation of inspection equipment and techniques. - Collaborate with design, manufacturing, test, supply chain, and materials teams to validate hardware. - Characterize measurement and inspection uncertainty and document technical conclusions. - Help ensure rigor and traceability in the build of nuclear systems, structures, and components. - Research new tools and technologies that could close gaps in the Quality Engineering team's capabilities. - Develop automation and implement process improvements that increase inspection effectiveness and repeatability. - Own a long-duration project through a final technical deliverable and presentation while communicating progress, risks, and opportunities. Basic Qualifications: - Currently enrolled in at least a bachelor's degree program in an engineering discipline relevant to the work and entering the junior or senior year of study. - Prior internship experience or more than one year of significant project-team, laboratory, or research experience. Preferred Skills & Experience: - GPA of 3.5 or above. - Experience in a university club or organization; leadership experience is preferred. - Strong interpersonal and technical communication skills, such as leading a student project team or presenting research at a conference. - Strong analytical and problem-solving skills with close attention to detail. - Ability to work cross-departmentally with different groups and teams. - Ability to work effectively in a dynamic environment with changing needs and requirements. - Ability to work independently and as part of a team, take initiative, and communicate effectively. Location - We are located in Torrance, CA in a 322,000 square foot, brand new facility featuring large open spaces for team collaboration, R&D, and production, as well as easy access to the 405, 105, and 110 freeways. Our facility is in the heart of Los Angeles' vibrant emerging tech ecosystem alongside many other high growth startups and enterprises. Culture At Antares, we like to specifically tie each role to our founding document’s set of values–here are the top five cultural values we think you should believe at your core to be successful: - Think in Systems - Energy and Defense are complex ecosystems with numerous stakeholders with competing priorities, conflicting policies, perverse incentives, and emergent and path-dependent properties. First principles thinking alone is insufficient. Think probabilistically and then take action. “If you want to be certain, then you are apt to be obsolete.” Over-optimizing the components often degrades the system - Obsess over the End User - The customer and end user are often not the same. We will never build globally competitive commercial products if we lose sight of our end users and their entire interaction with the product life cycle - Be Unconstrained by Convention - Our only limits are the laws of physics. Many, even experts, will say what we are working on is impossible. They said the same about SpaceX reusing rockets. Generationally impactful companies, by definition, must accomplish the seemingly impossible. If it were easy, it would have already been done. Never shy away from a solution because it has never been tried before, and never choose to do something because that's “how it's always been done” - Go Where the Work Is - Never miss a chance to meet a customer, user, or stakeholder face to face, even if that means hopping on a plane. If you can’t make it, find a teammate who can channel your intentions and go in your place. Deep work can be done from anywhere, but we believe teams are built in person, and aim to maximize our time together - Operate in the Grey - Embrace nuance in pursuit of truth. Question every fundamental assumption Equal Opportunity Antares is an Equal Opportunity Employer. Employment decisions are based solely on merit, competence, and qualifications, without regard to race, color, religion, gender, national origin/ethnicity, veteran status, disability status, age, sexual orientation, gender identity, marital status, mental or physical disability, or any other legally protected status. ITAR REQUIREMENTS To conform to U.S. Government export regulations, applicant must be a (i) U.S. citizen or national, (ii) U.S. lawful, permanent resident (aka green card holder), (iii) Refugee under 8 U.S.C. § 1157, or (iv) Asylee under 8 U.S.C. § 1158, or be eligible to obtain the required authorizations from the U.S. Department of State. Learn more about the ITAR here https://www.pmddtc.state.gov/?id=ddtc_kb_article_page&sys_id=24d528fddbfc930044f9ff621f961987. Pay range: $34 per hour.

At Voyager Technologies, we’re building technologies that protect lives, expand frontiers and prepare us for what’s next. And we’re doing that with people who are wired to solve, build, adapt and lead. These roles are not for the faint of heart. You’ll help lay the foundation for humanity's future. Requirements Currently enrolled in an undergraduate or graduate program at an accredited university, preferably pursuing a degree in Systems Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Aerospace Engineering, Physics, or a related technical field. Ability to work independently and collaboratively within a cross-functional team environment. Strong written and verbal communication skills. Strong organizational and time-management skills with attention to detail. Ability to learn and apply new engineering tools, processes, and methodologies. Familiarity with engineering software, modeling tools, requirements management systems, programming languages, or other technical tools is preferred. Ability to travel for in-person orientation and program kickoff, as well as for the final presentation at program completion. Preferred Qualifications Previous internship, coursework, academic project, laboratory experience, or other relevant engineering experience. Experience with requirements development, systems engineering, system integration, testing, or technical documentation. Familiarity with engineering design or analysis software, such as CAD, electrical design, modeling/simulation, or requirements management tools. Experience with programming or data analysis tools such as Python, MATLAB, C/C++, or similar languages. Hands-on experience with laboratory equipment, engineering test equipment, prototyping, or experimental testing. Exposure to multidisciplinary engineering projects or cross-functional development environments. jobs.body: Axiom Space is a human space exploration company, building era-defining space infrastructure and delivering technology-driven solutions that will empower civilization to transcend Earth. Beginning with Axiom Station, successor to the International Space Station, the company is pioneering a next-generation orbital settlement that will foster groundbreaking innovation and research in microgravity and drive the global space economy of tomorrow. Today, guided by the vision of leading humanity's expansion off planet, Axiom Space is the principal provider of commercial human spaceflight services and developer of advanced spacesuits for the Moon and beyond. For more information about Axiom Space, visit www.axiomspace.com . Axiom Space fosters a work environment inclusive of all perspectives. We are the pioneers of commercial space, leading the transformation of low-Earth orbit into a global space marketplace. Our mission-driven team is seeking a bold and dynamic Systems Engineering Intern who is fueled by high accountability, execution horsepower, and driven to understand our world, science/technology, and life itself, for the benefit of all on Earth and beyond. This role supports systems engineering activities — including requirements definition, interface management, system architecture, and verification and validation planning — across Axiom's spaceflight hardware and ground systems programs. The role requires strong organizational, time management, and communication skills, along with a genuine curiosity for how complex systems fit together. jobs.body: Crane Aerospace & Electronics has an exciting opportunity for a CNC Machinist Internship at our Auburn, CA location. Hours are Monday-Friday 7am-4:30pm. jobs.title: Drone Operations, Intern - Labs (Summer 2027)
jobs.location: San Francisco, CA
jobs.body: About the Team DoorDash Labs is an independent team within DoorDash. The Drone Operations team keeps DoorDash's drones airworthy and operates them safely. Our missions range from experimental test flights to commercial delivery. We're hiring Drone Operations interns to work at the intersection of operations and robotics to solve key business problems with elegant technical solutions. If you have a passion for applying robotics solutions to a service loved by millions of people, then we want to talk to you! About the Role As a Drone Operations Intern, you will support daily flight operations for DoorDash’s drone delivery program, from our test flight program to our commercial operation. You will get exposure to all elements of our operation, including Pilots, Maintenance Technicians, Quality/Safety, and Engineering. You will rotate around our facilities and get an end-to-end view of our program. In your first 30 days, you will learn our flight procedures and safety practices. By 90 days, you will own a project that improves flight safety, reliability, or efficiency. Success means the team adopts your work and our operations measurably improve. It is an exciting time to join as we scale from test flights to commercial delivery.You will report into the Head of Drone Operations on our Drone Operations team in our Labs organization. You’re excited about this opportunity because you will… Work with pilots, technicians, and engineers to troubleshoot issues and improve procedures. Review flight logs and mission data to find trends in safety, reliability, and delivery performance. Help run field operations at flight sites, including aircraft setup, loading, and recovery. Own an intern project and present your results to the team at the end of summer. We’re excited about you because… You are pursuing a B.S. or M.S. Degree in Aviation Studies or equivalent, have no more than 2 years of full-time work experience, and are graduating between Fall 2027 to Summer 2028.You are available for a May or June 2027 start date (Internships are only hosted during the Summer) You hold, or are willing to obtain, a Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) Part 107 Remote Pilot Certificate. You have hands-on experience building, flying, or maintaining drones or radio-controlled (RC) aircraft. You can operate in field environments with extended periods of standing, repetitive drone handling, and outdoor exposure to varying weather (heat, dust, cold, wind, etc.). You communicate clearly and follow safety procedures carefully. Applications for this position are accepted on an ongoing basis Compensation The internship is 12 weeks long. The intern’s starting pay will fall within the weekly pay range listed below and is determined based on job-related factors including education, work location, and market conditions. Ranges are market-dependent and may be modified in the future. In addition to base pay, interns are eligible for both a housing stipend and relocation stipend. DoorDash cares about you and your overall well-being. That’s why we offer our interns a wellness reimbursement benefit, access to an employee assistance program, in-office lunch credits and more! Base Pay (Weekly) $1,200 — $1,200 USD About DoorDash At DoorDash, our mission to empower local economies shapes how our team members move quickly, learn, and reiterate in order to make impactful decisions that display empathy for our range of users—from Dashers to merchant partners to consumers. We are a technology and logistics company that started by enabling door-to-door delivery, and we are looking for team members who can help us go from a company that is known as the place you order food to a company that people turn to for any and all goods. DoorDash is growing rapidly and changing constantly, which gives our team members the opportunity to share their unique perspectives, solve new challenges, and own their careers. We're committed to supporting employees’ happiness, healthiness, and overall well-being by providing comprehensive benefits and perks including premium healthcare, wellness expense reimbursement, paid parental leave and more. jobs.location: Sunnyvale, CA, us
jobs.body: It started with a simple idea: what if surgery could be less invasive and recovery less painful? Nearly 30 years later, that question still fuels everything we do at Intuitive . As a global leader in robotic-assisted surgery and minimally invasive care , our technologies—like the da Vinci surgical system and Ion —have transformed how care is delivered for millions of patients worldwide. We’re a team of engineers, clinicians, and innovators united by one purpose: to make surgery smarter, safer, and more human. If you’re ready to contribute to something bigger than yourself and help transform the future of healthcare , you’ll find your purpose here. Primary Function of Position The Reinforcement Learning Intern will report to future forward research lead and contribute to the development and evaluation of reinforcement learning (RL) algorithms in support of supervised autonomy initiatives. The intern will identify, train, and test several RL algorithms using data collected from the Intuitive surgical robot systems. While the bulk of this work will take place on offline -collected data (i.e., not in real-time on the robot), a stretch goal would be to deploy an RL algorithm to control the robot in real-time . Essential Job Duties Collect tele-operated simulation and/or real data from the surgical robot while performing a realistic exercise (e.g., Fundamentals of Laparoscopic Surgery pick-and-place). This is referred to as trajectory data and is critical for RL training. Adapt reinforcement learning algorithms to the surgical domain and exercise of interest and identify techniques for improving performance relative to off-the-shelf RL models. jobs.title: Undergraduate Engineering Intern - Microfabrication
jobs.location: Rochester, MN, United States
jobs.body: This undergraduate internship is a full-time position Summer-Fall 2027 (May or June through December) on site in Rochester, Minnesota. The Division of Engineering develops custom medical devices for physicians and researchers at Mayo Clinic. Our devices span the patient care spectrum from bench top research to patient bedside. This includes novel applications of deep brain stimulation, biosensor development, tissue engineering, organ assist devices, and surgical instruments. The Microfabrication Laboratory seeks an undergraduate student in engineering, materials science, or a related technical field who is interested in gaining hands-on experience in microfabrication and medical-device development. The intern will support the fabrication, testing, and characterization of medical microdevices such as thin-film electrode arrays, microfluidic devices, and other microsystems. Project assignments may vary based on active projects and laboratory needs, providing exposure to a range of fabrication technologies, device applications, and clinical problems. The intern will work as part of a multidisciplinary engineering team under the guidance of experienced engineers and laboratory staff and develop increasing independence as their technical skills grow. The internship is intended to provide practical engineering experience while allowing the student to apply concepts learned through undergraduate coursework. Assignments may include: Supporting fabrication and characterization of microdevices and test structures Performing laboratory experiments using established procedures Collecting, organizing, and analyzing experimental data Assisting with troubleshooting and process improvement activities Creating or modifying CAD drawings and device layouts Helping assemble and test prototypes Documenting experimental procedures, results, and observations Participating in project discussions and engineering design reviews Learning appropriate laboratory, safety, and quality procedures The intern will receive instruction and mentoring appropriate to their level of experience and will progressively take on additional responsibility as their skills develop. The incumbent must be enrolled in an engineering, management information systems, or other technology-related degree program from an accredited college or university and have completed a minimum of four semesters – or the equivalent – of instruction toward their degree. ***To be considered for this position please attach the following to your application: 3.3 GPA requirement or higher Undergraduate Transcript Resume or CV Applicants are strongly encouraged to include a Cover Letter Applicants are strongly encouraged to include a sample of academic work (e.g. screenshots of models or drawings, a lab report) Additional Qualifications: Experience is not required in all the following areas. Coursework, laboratory experience, project experience, or demonstrated interest in one or more is desirable: Microfabrication, MEMS, or semiconductor processing Cleanroom laboratory work CAD or engineering design software such as SolidWorks Microdevice layout/design software MATLAB, Python, or similar engineering-analysis tools Thin-film deposition, photolithography, plasma processing, laser processing, or polymer processing Experimental design, data analysis, or technical documentation

jobs.body: Overview Research Internships at Microsoft provide a dynamic environment for research careers with a network of world-class research labs led by globally-recognized scientists and engineers, who pursue innovation in a range of scientific and technical disciplines to help solve complex challenges in diverse fields, including computing, healthcare, economics, and the environment. jobs.title: Composite Structures Engineering Intern
jobs.location: North Kingstown, Rhode Island, USA
jobs.body: At REGENT, we’re on a mission to revolutionize regional transportation between coastal cities. We're not just building vehicles, we're creating a new category of transportation: the Seaglider. These groundbreaking wing-in-ground-effect craft travel just above the water’s surface, combining the speed of an airplane with the low operating costs of a boat. Capable of 180 miles at 180 mph on today's battery tech (and up to 400 miles with next-gen batteries), Seagliders will unlock fast, affordable, and sustainable coastal transit for passengers and cargo - connecting cities, islands, and communities like never before. Backed by leading investors and powered by a team of passionate, forward-thinking engineers, builders, and operators, we’re now scaling from a breakthrough prototype to full production - and building the team to make it happen. ROLE OVERVIEW We're looking for a Composite Structures Engineering Intern to join our Structures team as REGENT scales up design work across multiple Seaglider programs. In this role, you'll work in NX with Fibersim to model composite parts and develop laminate schedules, with the chance to follow those parts through build, analysis, manufacturing, and final assembly into the vehicle. You'll also pick up cross-functional sustaining work that supports our build and maintenance teams, giving you exposure well beyond a single corner of the design process. This is a chance to get hands-on with the kind of detailed composite design work that keeps a novel vehicle program moving — incorporating structural refinements, closing out important sustaining tasks, and helping unlock faster design iterations for the team. As part of Hardware Engineering, you'll work alongside engineers who care deeply about rigor and craftsmanship, and who are excited to introduce you to the advanced composite design and manufacturing technology REGENT uses to bring Seagliders to life. If you're curious about composite structures, energized by variety across the product lifecycle, and eager to learn by doing, we'd love to have you on the team. WHAT YOU'LL DO - Model Composite Parts: You'll work in NX with Fibersim to model composite parts and develop the laminate schedules behind them. - Follow Parts End to End: You'll have the opportunity to take parts through full design cycles, from build and analysis through manufacturing and final assembly into the vehicle. - Support Multiple Programs: You'll contribute to part modeling and drafting work as REGENT scales up design across several active programs at once. - Incorporate Structural Refinements: You'll help translate updates coming out of structural analysis into accurate, build-ready part models. - Pick Up Sustaining Work: You'll take on cross-functional tasks that support our build and maintenance teams, keeping important work from falling through the cracks. - Collaborate Across Teams: You'll partner with manufacturing, build, and analysis engineers, gaining visibility into how composite parts move from concept to finished vehicle. - Learn Cutting-Edge Tools: You'll be introduced to the advanced composite design and manufacturing technology REGENT uses to build Seagliders. WHAT YOU'LL BRING - CAD Fluency: You're comfortable navigating CAD software and thinking like a designer, with an eye for precision and detail. - Mechanical or Aerospace Foundation: You bring a solid grasp of fundamental mechanical or aerospace concepts that helps you integrate smoothly into cross-functional work. - Composite Materials Know-How: You've studied composites and understand Classical Laminate Theory well enough to apply it to real part design. - Creative Problem-Solving: You enjoy adaptive, critical thinking and aren't afraid to find non-traditional solutions for a genuinely novel vehicle. - Clear Communication: You can translate technical concepts for teammates outside your immediate discipline, which helps when working across build and manufacturing teams. - Hands-On Manufacturing Exposure: Any experience working directly with composite manufacturing is a plus and helps you speak the same language as the build team. WHO WE'RE LOOKING FOR - Collaborative Team Player: You believe that great things happen when teams work together. You communicate effectively and collaborate with engineers, stakeholders, and other cross-functional teams to align on goals and move projects forward. You bring people together, ensuring that everyone is on the same page and moving towards a shared vision. - Creative Problem Solver: You thrive on tackling complex challenges and finding innovative solutions. Whether you're resolving installation challenges, debugging elusive electrical issues, or adapting on the fly during integration and test, you bring a practical, inventive mindset to every problem. You don't just patch issues - you improve processes, anticipate downstream impacts, and help turn one-off fixes into scalable solutions that raise the bar for future builds. - Adaptable & Agile: In a fast-paced, ever-evolving startup environment, you quickly adapt to changing priorities and requirements. You approach challenges with a calm, resilient mindset, and know how to pivot and adjust your approach as needed, ensuring that progress continues without missing a beat. - Innovative Mindset: You're driven by curiosity and a passion for technology. You're passionate about driving continuous improvement, embracing new technologies and methodologies to enhance efficiency, quality, and team performance. WHAT WE OFFER - Competitive compensation - Housing Stipend available for those temporarily moving to join our team - Daily, free catered lunches - Learning & professional development opportunities - Meaningful projects that make an impact - Mentorship & guidance from experienced team members If you’re ready to take on an exciting challenge, grow with us, and make a lasting impact, we want to hear from you. Even if you don’t meet every requirement, but you see yourself contributing to our mission, we encourage you to apply! We value diverse skillsets and experiences and believe in the potential of passionate individuals to make a big impact. Equal Opportunity Employer REGENT is an Equal Opportunity Employer. We are committed to creating a diverse and inclusive work environment. Employment decisions are made without regard to race, color, religion, national origin, gender, sexual orientation, gender identity, age, disability, or any other characteristic protected by law.
