jobs.title: Student- Engineering ADAS Vehicle Integration
jobs.location: Auburn Hills, Michigan, US, United States of America
jobs.body: Job descriptions may display in multiple languages based on your language selection. What we offer: At Magna, you can expect an engaging and dynamic environment where you can help to develop industry-leading automotive technologies. We invest in our employees, providing them with the support and resources they need to succeed. As a member of our global team, you can expect exciting, varied responsibilities as well as a wide range of development prospects. Because we believe that your career path should be as unique as you are. Group Summary: Transforming mobility. Making automotive technology that is smarter, cleaner, safer and lighter. That’s what we’re passionate about at Magna Electronics, and we do it by creating world-class Electronic systems. We are a premier supplier for the global automotive industry with full capabilities in design, development, testing and manufacturing of complex Electronic systems. Our name stands for quality, environmental consciousness, and safety. Innovation is what drives us and we drive innovation. Dream big and create the future of mobility at Magna Electronics. Job Responsibilities: Position Overview Magna’s ADAS technologies are shaping an autonomous future and improving lives. The ADAS Intern/Co-op (onsite) primarily supports ADAS vehicle integration by coordinating prototype vehicle activities (build readiness, installations, scheduling support, and issue tracking) across cross-functional teams. The role also supports deployment and use of ROS-based tools as needed. A strong drive to learn, clear communication, and teamwork are essential. Essential Duties and Responsibilities: Coordinate ADAS prototype vehicle activities across cross‑functional teams (build readiness, scheduling support, parts/tools readiness, stakeholder communication, and issue tracking/closure). Support prototype vehicle-build activities with the Engineering Services team, including RRS PC installation and related vehicle integration tasks. Support End-of-Line (EOL) and USS sensor calibration activities as scheduled, and document calibration outcomes and follow-up actions. Create utilities/tools to support the team (e.g., build/test checklists, data/log organization, basic geometry/FOV calculations, or converting a manual workflow into a repeatable script). Support engineers in vehicle testing activities as a second person (as required), following safety procedures and test plans, and capturing results, issues, and logs. Support deployment and use of ROS‑based tools (training will be provided as needed) to assist with sensor feasibility studies and integration workflows. Qualifications: Valid driver’s license Comfortable working hands-on in a garage/vehicle environment (installations, instrumentation, calibration support) and able to follow all safety procedures and PPE requirements. Education / Experience Enrolled in an engineering degree program (Electrical, Automotive, Mechanical, Robotics/Mechatronics, or Computer Science or equivalent) Special Knowledge / Skills: Mandatory: Basic Python programming skills (scripts for automation, data handling, and repeatable workflows). Experience with C++ is a plus. Coursework, projects, or work experience related to ADAS/autonomous systems, sensor integration, or automotive software development. Basic familiarity with a Linux/Ubuntu development environment and version control (Git) is preferred; willingness to learn is required. Strong communication skills and ability to work effectively in a cross-functional team setting (tracking actions, following up, and clearly documenting status). Demonstrates drive to learn and take ownership. Familiarity with ADAS/autonomous driving concepts and common sensors (LiDAR, camera, radar, ultrasonic). Comfortable learning and using new tools and processes to support vehicle integration and coordination (training and mentoring provided as needed). Troubleshooting and debugging skills (software and basic hardware integration issues). Good documentation and reporting habits (test logs, build notes, calibration records). Problem-solving and critical-thinking mindset Must follow safety procedures for vehicle testing, shop/garage environments, and bench testing environments. Attention to detail Preferred: Experience with vehicle testing and data collection using tools such as Vector CANoe/CANalyzer, dSPACE, ETAS, or similar toolchains. Experience with vehicle instrumentation and prototype sensor/ECU integration (mounting, harnessing, power/network bring-up) and/or supporting sensor calibration activities. Exposure to ROS/ROS2 tools (e.g., running existing nodes, basic package structure, RViz/rosbag) and ability to deploy/use ROS-based workflows. Working knowledge of creating maintainable, reusable scripts/tools (clear inputs/outputs, basic testing, readable documentation) in a team environment. Physical Demands / Work Environment: Combination of office and garage/vehicle environments. Includes sitting/standing; working at a computer; frequent walking around vehicles; bending/kneeling; and occasional lifting/moving of equipment (e.g., test hardware, tools, sensors) consistent with safe work practices. Work may occur outdoors or in varying temperatures during vehicle build, testing, and calibration activities. Awareness, Unity, Empowerment: At Magna, we believe that a diverse workforce is critical to our success. That’s why we are proud to be an equal opportunity employer. We hire on the basis of experience and qualifications, and in consideration of job requirements, regardless of, in particular, color, ancestry, religion, gender, origin, sexual orientation, age, citizenship, marital status, disability or gender identity. Magna takes the privacy of your personal information seriously. We discourage you from sending applications via email or traditional mail to comply with GDPR requirements and your local Data Privacy Law. AI-Assisted Screening Disclosure As part of our commitment to a fair, consistent, and efficient recruitment process, we may use artificial intelligence (AI) tools to assist in the initial screening of applications submitted through our Workday system. These tools help identify qualifications and experience that align with the role requirements. Please note that AI is used solely to support our recruiters. Final decisions are always made by the hiring manager and the hiring team. Importantly, no applicant data is shared externally through these AI tools. All information remains securely within our systems and is handled in accordance with our privacy and data protection policies. Under conditions defined by applicable law, you may have the right to request an explanation of how AI is used to support decision-making. If you have any questions or concerns about this process, feel free to contact our Talent Attraction team. Worker Type: Student / Co-Op Group: Magna Electronics

jobs.title: Intern - Snapdragon Computer Technical Enablement Intern - Mexico
jobs.location: México D.F., CDMX, MX
jobs.body: Company: Qualcomm Intl Inc., Mexico Branch Office Job Area: Interns Group, Interns Group > Interim Intern Qualcomm Overview: Qualcomm is a company of inventors that unlocked 5G ushering in an age of rapid acceleration in connectivity and new possibilities that will transform industries, create jobs, and enrich lives. But this is just the beginning. It takes inventive minds with diverse skills, backgrounds, and cultures to transform 5Gs potential into world-changing technologies and products. This is the Invention Age - and this is where you come in. General Summary: Role Overview We are looking for an intern to become the technical point of contact within the Hispanic Latin America Snapdragon Compute team. Working closely with the regional technical team, the intern will build a strong understanding of Snapdragon-powered PCs and help translate that knowledge into practical guidance for promoters, sales representatives, and channel partners. This is a learning role with increasing responsibility. The intern will support common technical questions and partner activities while working with Qualcomm specialists on issues that require deeper investigation or an official technical response. Key Responsibilities Build technical knowledge: Participate in regular sessions with the regional technical team to learn about Snapdragon PC platforms, Windows on Arm, AI experiences, application compatibility, and new products. Connect technical and commercial teams: Capture recurring questions from promoters, sales representatives, and channels; work with technical specialists to obtain accurate answers; and communicate those answers in a clear, useful format. Support partners: Serve as an accessible first point of contact for common product and demonstration questions, keeping track of open items and escalating complex cases. Develop useful resources: Help create and maintain FAQs, troubleshooting guides, product comparisons, talking points, and short technical content based on the questions partners actually ask. Enable product experiences: Prepare and maintain demo devices, validate key experiences, and support technical demonstrations when needed. Share knowledge: Contribute to webinars and training sessions for promoters, sales teams, and channels, initially alongside experienced team members and taking on presentation sections as expertise develops. What Success Looks Like Partners receive clear and consistent answers to common technical questions. Recurring issues reach the right specialists and are followed through. The team has current, practical resources it can reuse across Hispam, and the intern steadily develops the knowledge and confidence to explain Snapdragon PC technology. Basic Qualifications Currently pursuing a degree in Computer Engineering, Computer Science, Information Systems, Electronics, Mechatronics, or a related field. Strong curiosity about PCs, processors, Windows, AI, and how technology works in real-world use. Ability to investigate a question, learn from specialists, and explain the answer clearly to a nontechnical audience. Strong communication, organization, and follow-up skills. Working proficiency in English and Spanish. No prior professional experience required. Preferred Qualifications Familiarity with PC hardware, Windows configuration, or software troubleshooting. Interest in Windows on Arm and AI Pcs. Experience explaining or demonstrating technology through academic or personal projects. Applicants : Qualcomm is an equal opportunity employer. Do you want to learn from and collaborate with some of the greatest minds in the industry? At RTX, our internships, co-ops and full-time careers provide an exceptional foundation to work on complex problems, advance your skills and create a safer, more connected world. Discover opportunities to make a difference at RTX. What You Will Do Join our team as a Quality Management System Co-Op and gain hands-on experience in maintaining and improving our Quality Management Systems (QMS). This onsite co-op opportunity will provide you with valuable exposure to quality processes, audits, and compliance standards in a dynamic and innovative environment. You will work on meaningful projects that directly impact our organization’s commitment to quality and excellence. Your responsibilities will include: Assisting in the preparation and execution of Quality Management System (QMS) and special process audits, including conducting preparatory audits and following up on open actions. Participating in third-party audits as an observer. Supporting the implementation of AS13100 standards, including auditing and assisting with procedure development. Preparing and maintaining Quality systems documentation, processes, and training materials. Contributing to Root Cause and Corrective Action (RCCA) activities, including database management, corrective action development, and follow-up. Supporting Quality Assurance Team (QAT) activities such as human factor investigations, process walks, and floor sweeps. Assisting in the development of systems to manage document review processes, ballot and gap analysis tracking, and alignment of balloted changes within local procedures. Collaborating with cross-functional teams to support continuous improvement initiatives. Qualifications You Must Have Must be pursuing a Bachelor's or advanced degree in an applicable discipline and actively enrolled through the duration of the co-op. Experience with basic Microsoft Office applications, including Word, Excel, and PowerPoint. Qualifications We Prefer Experience with Quality Management Systems (QMS) and related processes. Exposure to Root Cause and Corrective Action (RCCA) processes and tools such as ETQ or similar systems. What We Offer Our values drive our actions, behaviors, and performance with a vision for a safer, more connected world. At RTX we value: Safety, Trust, Respect, Accountability, Collaboration, and Innovation. Learn More & Apply Now! This position is classified as: Onsite: Employees who are working in Onsite roles will work primarily onsite. This includes all production and maintenance employees, as they are essential to the development of our products. As part of our commitment to maintaining a secure hiring process, candidates may be asked to attend select steps of the interview process in-person at one of our office locations, regardless of whether the role is designated as on-site, hybrid or remote. The salary range for this role is 37,000 USD - 82,000 USD. The salary range provided is a good faith estimate representative of all experience levels. Hired applicants may be eligible for benefits, including but not limited to, medical, dental, vision, life insurance, short-term disability, long-term disability, 401(k) match, flexible spending accounts, flexible work schedules, employee assistance program, Employee Scholar Program, parental leave, paid time off, and holidays. Payments under these annual programs are not guaranteed and are dependent upon a variety of factors including, but not limited to, individual performance, business unit performance, and/or the company’s performance. jobs.location: Redmond, Washington, United States of America
jobs.body: Work Flexibility: Onsite Manufacturing Engineering What You Get Out of the Internship ​​ At Stryker, we believe that developing the next generation of talent is just as important as developing life-changing medical technologies. As an intern, you won’t just observe — you’ll contribute to meaningful projects, gain exposure to leaders who will mentor you, and experience a culture of innovation and teamwork that is shaping the future of healthcare. As an intern, you will : ​ ​ Apply classroom knowledge and gain experience in a fast-paced and growing industry setting ​ Implement new ideas , be constantly challenged, and develop your skills ​ Network with key/high-level stakeholders and leaders of the business ​ Be a part of an innovative team and culture ​ Experience documenting complex processes and presenting them in a clear format Who we want ​​ Challengers. People who seek out the hard projects and work to find just the right solutions. ​ Teammates. Partners who listen to ideas, share thoughts and work together to move the business forward. ​ Charismatic networkers. Relationship-savvy people who intentionally make connections with both internal partners and external contacts. ​ Strategic thinkers. Interns who propose innovative ideas and consistently exceed their performance objectives . ​ Customer-oriented achievers. Individuals with an unparalleled work ethic and customer-focused attitude who bring value to their partnerships. ​ Game changers. Persistent interns who will stop at nothing to live out Stryker’s mission to make healthcare better. Opportunities Available ​ ​ As a Manufacturing Engineering intern at Stryker, you will : The Manufacturing Engineering Intern will gain hands-on experience applying Lean Six Sigma principles in a manufacturing environment. Working closely with an assigned mentor, the intern will support the identification, analysis, and implementation of improvements to current manufacturing processes. The intern will work with a manufacturing engineering mentor to identify opportunities to reduce defects, rework, or process escapes through mistake-proofing solutions. This project will focus on evaluating current process risks and supporting the design or implementation of simple automation, sensing, or verification methods that prevent incorrect operations from occurring Collaborate with design and operations teams to bring products to market efficiently. Projects may include fixture development, assembly line optimization, lean manufacturing implementation, ergonomics/safety improvements, and process validation . Majors Targeted: Manufacturing Engineering , Industrial & Operations Engineering, Mechanical Engineering or related majors What You Need ​​ Currently pursuing a Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in a related field; must remain enrolled in a degree-seeking program after the internship . ​ Cumulative 3.0 GPA or above ( verified at time of hire ) Must be legally authorized to work in the U.S. and not require employment-based sponsorship now or in the future . ​ Strong written and verbal communication skills, with proven ability to collaborate and build relationships Demonstrated leadership, problem-solving, and organizational skills with the ability to manage multiple priorities Proficiency in Microsoft Office (Excel, Word, PowerPoint) and eagerness to learn in a dynamic environment . $ 20 min hourly wage – $3 5 max hourly wage, sign-on bonus, 11 paid holidays annually, and either paid corporate housing or a living stipend, dependent upon hiring location Travel Percentage: None Stryker Corporation is an equal opportunity employer. jobs.title: Heat Pump Product Engineering Intern, Summer 2027
jobs.location: Fort Worth, TX, United States of America
jobs.body: We’re Watts. Together, we’re reimagining the future of water. We feel proud every day about what we do. We're all part of the same crucial mission, no matter what function we support -- it's to provide safe, clean water for the world, and to protect our planet's most valuable resource. What we do: For 150 years, Watts has built best-in-class products that are trusted by customers in residential and commercial settings across the world. We are at the forefront of innovation, working with cutting-edge technology to provide smart and connected, sustainable water solutions for the future. Watts is a leading brand with a quality reputation — and we have a dynamic future ahead.​ The Watts Internship Program is your chance to bring what you’ve learned in the classroom to life! You’ll dive into real-world projects, gaining hands-on experience while learning how business really works from the inside. During the program, you’ll get to roll up your sleeves and make an impact on day-to-day operations. Plus, you'll have tons of opportunities to network with passionate professionals across manufacturing, industrial engineering, and more—sparking new ideas through cross-department collaboration. It’s all about expanding your skills, challenging yourself, and exploring where your ambitions can take you! Scope of Position This motivated and detail-oriented individual, as part of the Marketing and Product Management team, will be responsible for developing technical training materials and supporting product improvement initiatives that enhance customer understanding of heat pump and water heating systems. The Heat Pump Product Engineering Intern will gain hands-on experience in technical communication, refrigeration design, and applied HVAC technology while collaborating with Product Management, Engineering, and New Product Development teams to create instructional resources, support troubleshooting activities, and evaluate potential product improvements. This position reports to the Product Manager. This role is onsite and is based in Fort Worth, TX. Primary Job Duties and Responsibilities Collaborate with subject matter experts (SMEs) to identify common product startup challenges, troubleshooting procedures, and technical support needs. Develop technical training materials, including instructional manuals, presentations, videos, and online training modules to support field startup and troubleshooting activities. Research existing industry training materials and best practices to ensure instructional resources align with applicable technical standards and customer needs. Assist with the development and organization of training content for online learning platforms to improve accessibility and usability for customers and field personnel. Work with Product Management and Engineering teams to identify commonly failing components and evaluate potential replacement solutions. Support product improvement initiatives by reviewing cost analysis findings, testing results, and technical recommendations. Develop testing plans to evaluate the functionality, reliability, and durability of selected replacement components through functional and stress testing. Collaborate with Engineering and New Product Development teams to gain an understanding of refrigeration design, heat pump systems, and applied HVAC/water heating technologies. Assist with documenting technical findings, testing procedures, and product performance observations to support troubleshooting and continuous improvement initiatives. Utilize Microsoft Office and relevant technical tools to develop training documentation, presentations, and project reports. Participate in internship development activities, networking opportunities, and cross-functional learning experiences. Summarize and present internship project outcomes, technical findings, and recommendations to leadership at the conclusion of the internship. Assume responsibility for other projects and duties as assigned by the Training Manager, Product Manager, or Company management. Demonstrate integrity, accountability, continuous improvement, and transparency by maintaining accurate technical documentation, following established safety and testing procedures, identifying opportunities for product improvements, and effectively communicating project findings. Required Qualifications Current student (junior or senior status). Pursuing a bachelor's degree in Mechanical Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Building Systems, HVAC Technology, Communications, or a related technical or media field. GPA of 3.0 or higher. Strong interest in technical training, renewable energy, and/or HVAC and water heating systems. Proficiency with Microsoft Word, Excel, PowerPoint, and Outlook. Strong organizational and time management skills, with the ability to work independently and manage multiple priorities. Strong verbal and written communication skills. Ability to participate in hands-on demonstrations and technical activities under supervision. Demonstrated initiative, problem-solving skills, and attention to detail. Passionate about your work, with a genuine desire to contribute meaningfully and make an impact. Demonstrated commitment to integrity and respect in interactions with others, fostering a positive and inclusive work environment. Strong sense of accountability, taking ownership of tasks and following through on commitments. Understanding of and adherence to applicable laws, codes, policies, regulations, and safety practices and procedures, as applicable. Must be authorized to work in the United States without requiring sponsorship now or in the future. Must successfully establish employment eligibility and satisfactorily complete background checks and required pre-employment testing as a condition of employment. Preferred Qualifications Completion of junior- or senior-level coursework in a relevant field. Familiarity with computer-aided design (CAD), diagramming, or graphic design tools such as SolidWorks, AutoCAD, Visio, or Adobe Illustrator. Interest in technical documentation, instructional content development, or product training. Interest in refrigeration systems, heat pump technology, or HVAC equipment. General Applicable Company Competencies Commitment to Watts’ values of integrity, accountability, continuous improvement and innovation, and transparency. Punctuality and dependability. Ability to be flexible and adapt to changing work priorities and stressful conditions. Adherence to all personnel policies, procedures, and standards of process as implemented by Watts. Maintain productive and collaborative relationships with other Watts employees. Adherence to Watts’ seven cultural beliefs: Growth Mindset, Customer-Focused Innovation, Constant Communication, Clear Goals, Collaborate Globally, Be Inclusive, and Take Action. Working Conditions While performing the job duties, you will be working on-site at the Fort Worth, TX location in both an office and manufacturing environment. You may, at times, be required to be present on the manufacturing floor and will be required to wear the appropriate personal protective equipment. Your scheduled work hours will be communicated to you by your manager. Physical Requirements: Specific physical abilities required for this position include, but are not limited to: Ability to remain seated at a desk or workstation for extended periods. Ability to physically move around the office, organize or transport files, packages, or other office-related materials. Ability to read documents, use a computer, and perform data entry tasks. Ability to communicate clearly with management and coworkers, particularly in meetings or phone calls. Ability to operate standard office equipment such as computers, printers, phones, and copiers. Ability to stand for long periods of time. Ability to lift and carry up to 25 pounds. Ability to push and pull up to 25 pounds. Ability to physically move around manufacturing floor. Ability to read documents and communicate clearly with management and coworkers. Ability to wear personal protective equipment, which may include, but is not limited to, safety shoes, hearing protection, and safety glasses. Pay Range: $22-26 The expected hourly range for this position is $22–$26 hourly. Actual compensation will be dependent upon individual skills, experience, qualifications, and applicable law. What's In It for You People-First Culture – Enriching and caring for people is at the core of who we are; this includes executing our Diversity, Equity, and Inclusion (DEI) strategy, and providing you with meaningful career growth opportunities, a positive and safe work environment, and affirmation that you are heard, valued, and respected. Flexible PTO Policy – Work-life balance is important at Watts and our interns receive one (1) hour of flexible PTO for every thirty (30) hours worked. Your flexible PTO can be utilized for any type of absence. Paid Holidays – Celebrate the holidays with your loved ones and still get paid! You will receive the following paid holidays off during your time as an Intern with Watts. Where a holiday falls during the weekend, it will be observed on an adjacent weekday. Lunch and Learns – Throughout your internship, there will be opportunities for you to sign up to learn and network with some of the key strategic leaders and thought partners within our core operating model! Sustainability – For five years in a row, Watts has been named one of "America's Most Responsible Companies" by Newsweek. Join our journey as we continue to distinguish Watts as a responsible and committed corporate citizen. Nothing in this job description restricts Watts’ right to assign or reassign duties, responsibilities, and working hours/conditions to this position at any time. This position is “at will,” which means that either the employee or Watts may terminate the employment relationship at any time, with or without notice, and for any lawful reason. #LI (Onsite) Watts in it for you : Please note that the following benefits apply only to permanent roles and do not apply to internship roles. Competitive compensation based on your skills, qualifications and experience Comprehensive medical and dental coverage, retirement benefits Family building benefits, including paid maternity/paternity leave 10 paid holidays and Paid Time Off Continued professional development opportunities and educational reimbursement Additional perks such as fitness reimbursements and employee discount programs Learn more about our benefit offerings here: https://tapintowattsbenefits.com/ How we work: At Watts, our culture is team-oriented and supportive. Employees here genuinely care about the quality of their work, and about each other. Our people are the heart of who we are and contribute to our longevity and continued success. And this is a place where you can have a big career. No matter your role, there are opportunities for learning and development, and your daily contributions make a meaningful impact on the lives of people who use our products and on the future of water. Watts is committed to equal employment opportunity. We follow a policy of administering all employment decisions and personnel actions without regard to race, color, religion, creed, sex, pregnancy, national origin, sexual orientation, age, physical or mental disability, genetic disposition or carrier status, marital status, military or veteran status, minorities, or any other category protected under applicable federal, state, or local law. Consistent with the obligations of state and federal law, Watts will make reasonable accommodations for qualified individuals with disabilities. Any employee who needs a reasonable accommodation should contact Human Resources.

jobs.body: WD is building the infrastructure behind the AI-driven data economy. As AI scales, so does data. Every interaction, every model, every system generates data that must be stored, managed, and made accessible over time. That’s where we come in. We combine deep engineering expertise with global-scale manufacturing to deliver the storage systems that make AI possible, powering hyperscale data centers, cloud platforms, and enterprise infrastructure worldwide. This isn’t theoretical work. It’s real systems, at real scale, people solving some of the hardest challenges in technology today. We’re looking for people who want to build, solve, and operate at that level. Join us and let’s shape the future of data. The Engineering Intern will join Western Digital's Head Backend Business Unit for a structured 3-6 month internship program at the Philippines site (PHO). The internship is designed to provide hands-on exposure to precision manufacturing operations, specifically slider processing and HGA (Head Gimbal Assembly) assembly within the storage technology industry. Interns will be embedded in the Engineering organization and assigned a dedicated buddy/mentor. The internship is structured with clear deliverables, a mid-point check-in, and a final project presentation. High-performing interns will be considered for conversion to the ECT -- under the BEST Program. Key responsibilities include: Supporting day-to-day engineering activities in assigned function area Assisting in data collection, process monitoring, and documentation Contributing to a defined internship project with measurable output Attending structured learning sessions and technical orientations Completing mid-point and end-of-internship assessments Presenting internship project findings to team and mentor at program close REQUIRED: Currently enrolled in a Bachelor’s degree program in Mechanical Engineering, Electronics Engineering, Industrial Engineering, Materials Science, Physics, or a related field. Minimum 3rd-year standing; rising seniors are preferred. In good academic standing. Available for a 3–6-month full-time or part-time internship. The internship is intended for students whose academic program requires or allows an internship for academic credit. PREFERRED: Prior internship, laboratory, or hands-on experience in engineering or manufacturing. Exposure to quality tools, process documentation, or engineering drawings. Basic data analysis skills, including Excel and basic statistics. Strong academic performance in technical subjects. SKILLS Eagerness to learn and develop skills in a manufacturing environment. Strong analytical thinking and attention to detail. Good communication skills and ability to work effectively in a team. Proficiency in Microsoft Office, particularly Excel. Reliable, punctual, and committed to completing the internship duration. Strong written and verbal English communication skills. TARGET ONBOARDING DATES: Candidates should be available to start their internship on one of the following target dates: January 11/12, 2027 April 1, 2027 May 24/25, 2027 WD thrives on the power and potential of diversity. jobs.body: Job Description: Internship - 2027 Undergraduate and Master's Research & Development Intern The role of Undergraduate and Master's Research & Development Intern is intended to start in Summer 2027. Collaborate with Innovative 3Mers Around the World Choosing where to start and grow your career has a major impact on your professional and personal life, so it’s equally important you know that the company that you choose to work at, and its leaders, will support and guide you. With a wide variety of people, global locations, technologies and products, 3M is a place where you can collaborate with other curious, creative 3Mers. An internship is a temporary position within 3M. Interns typically work a full-time schedule throughout a 10-12 week assignment. This position is limited to working 899 hours per service credit year. 3M provides eligible interns with a housing and transportation stipend in accordance with current policy. This position provides an opportunity to transition from other private, public, government or military experience to a 3M career. Applications on this requisition are reviewed and filled on a rolling basis; it is in a candidate’s best interest to apply as soon as possible. Interested candidates should include a resume as part of their application. The Impact You’ll Make in this Role As a Research & Development Intern , you will have the opportunity to tap into your curiosity and collaborate with some of the most innovative people around the world. Here, you will make an impact by: Leveraging expertise to support the development of new technologies, providing growth opportunities, in addition to supporting existing 3M products, businesses, and operations. Building your technical, communication, and leadership skills. Collaborating with other R&D functions across 3M that can help advance projects, including researchers from other groups, analytical chemists, process engineers, etc. Collaborating with senior researchers on an assigned product/technology development or an application/product engineering project. Leading and directing assigned projects towards advanced technical solutions. Documenting detailed experimental records in 3M electronic laboratory notebooks that can be used for invention submissions and potentially patent applications. Analyzing, interpreting, and communicating experimental results. R&D internships are available for both digital science and laboratory-based roles in the following areas: Corporate technology : Researchers working in one of our corporate R&D laboratories are concerned with the materials, processes, and/or analytical tools that go into the development of new technologies/methods and the generation of intellectual property, including patents. Projects in corporate technology may involve formulation science, synthetic chemistry, process design/control, materials characterization, development of new analytical techniques, materials scale-up, etc. Product engineering and development: interns working as product engineers or developers will collaborate with other researchers in our business and corporate research laboratories to address challenges in existing products and/or develop new products. Projects in the product engineering and development space may involve formulation science, process design/control, materials characterization, voice of customers, etc. Digital science and engineering: interns working in this area will use and/or develop digital science tools to address research challenges in the corporate research and business labs. Projects in the digital science and engineering space may involve: optimizing algorithms for computational efficiency, speed, and usability; building capabilities with software tools e.g., Microsoft Azure ML and/or AWS ML, Python; implementing complex data engineering processes to support innovative data science solutions; leveraging key ML or AI solutions toward materials and engineering problems; developing innovative models and simulations of complex chemical and physical processes. Your Skills and Expertise To set you up for success in this role from day one, 3M is looking for candidates who must have the following qualifications: Currently pursuing a bachelor’s or master’s degree in science or engineering from an accredited institution. Additional qualifications that could help you succeed even further in this role include: Currently pursuing a bachelor’s or master’s degree in fields such as Chemical Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Materials Science, Computer Science, Computer Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Data Science, Software Engineering, Chemistry, Polymer Science, Biomolecular Engineering, or related disciplines from an accredited institution. Experience in machine learning, deep learning, data science, computer vision, artificial intelligence, statistics, software engineering, and/or applied mathematics. Strong scientific and technical acumen, with demonstrated interest and ability to make connections between science/technology and real-world concerns. Strong problem-solving skills. Ability to deal with the ambiguity of early-stage scouting and evaluation of new opportunities, and the flexibility to change direction as additional information becomes available. Leadership and networking skills. Self-motivated and self-directed. Excellent communication skills (oral, written, and presentation). Completed a minimum of Freshman Year (2 semesters) by the start of the internship. 6-12 months of practical laboratory experience in the synthesis of polymers and small molecules, chemical/polymer processing, advanced analytical and materials characterization, vapor coating, nanotechnology, development of sensors, and optical materials. Hands-on experience in areas such as additive manufacturing, robotics, mechanical design, and/or hard goods. Experience with Microsoft Azure ML and/or AWS ML. Fluent in one or more programming languages (e.g., Python, MATLAB, C, C++, and/or R). Ability to apply object-oriented design and/or design patterns to software development. Fluent in understanding, manipulating, cleansing, and visualizing complex data. Experience working with complex, distributed Big Data workflows. Previous relevant intern experience or co-op with a company or university. Use of designed experiments and statistical analysis of experimental results. Demonstrated scientific excellence as evidenced by publications and presentations. Work location: This role follows an on-site working model, requiring the employee to work at least four days a week at the 3M Center in Maplewood, MN or Austin, TX. Relocation: 3M provides eligible interns with a housing and transportation stipend in accordance with current policy. Must be legally authorized to work in country of employment without sponsorship for employment visa status (e.g., H1B status). Responsibilities of this position may include direct and/or indirect physical or logical access to information, systems, technologies subjected to the regulations/compliance with U.S. Export Control Laws. U.S. Export Control laws and U.S. Government Department of Defense contracts and sub-contracts impose certain restrictions on companies and their ability to share export-controlled and other technology and services with certain "non-U.S. persons" (persons who are not U.S. citizens or nationals, lawful permanent residents of the U.S., refugees, "Temporary Residents" (granted Amnesty or Special Agricultural Worker provisions), or persons granted asylum. To comply with these laws, 3M must help assess candidates' U.S. person status. The questions asked in this application are intended to assess this and will be used for evaluation purposes only. Failure to provide the necessary information in this regard will result in our inability to consider you further for this particular position. Supporting Your Well-being 3M offers many programs to help you live your best life – both physically and financially. To ensure competitive pay and benefits, 3M regularly benchmarks with other companies that are comparable in size and scope. Chat with Max For assistance with searching through our current job openings or for more information about all things 3M, visit Max, our virtual recruiting assistant on 3M.com/careers. This agreement lays out key terms on using 3M Confidential Information and Trade Secrets. It also has provisions discussing conflicts of interest and how inventions are assigned. Employees that are Job Grade 7 or equivalent and above may also have obligations to not compete against 3M or solicit its employees or customers, both during their employment, and for a period after they leave 3M. Learn more about 3M’s creative solutions to the world’s problems at www.3M.com or on Instagram, Facebook, and LinkedIn @3M. jobs.title: Nuclear Engineering Intern - Summer 2027
jobs.location: Los Angeles
jobs.body: About Us At Antares, our long-term mission is to make clean energy abundant from Earth to the Asteroid Belt. We’re fueled by the belief that advanced nuclear energy can strengthen our military, solve the climate crisis, elevate global living standards, and expand humanity's presence in outer space. To achieve our mission, we’re building mass-producible, inherently safe, deployable microreactors that can be used terrestrially, underwater, and in space. The Antares team hails from SpaceX, the White House, the Pentagon, the Department of Energy, MIT, Rigetti Computing, General Atomics, Relativity Space, Ursa Major, and National Laboratories like Idaho, Oak Ridge, Los Alamos, and Savannah River. Antares has raised over $600M in venture capital from top-tier investors and has hundreds of million-dollars on contract with the military services, NASA, and the Department of Energy. ABOUT THE SUMMER INTERNSHIP PROGRAM Internships at Antares are anything but ordinary. You'll work alongside our team as we design, build, and test fission microreactors built to deliver reliable energy for critical missions on Earth, in space, and underwater. Our interns contribute to real work from day one. Depending on your role, you may touch hardware, write and test software, support manufacturing and operations, or help build the systems that allow Antares to move quickly as we scale. You'll work alongside engineers, operators, and other experts solving challenging problems—and you'll leave your internship with hands-on experience that's difficult to find anywhere else. We work hard, move quickly, and take pride in what we're building. If you're excited to learn by doing and want to contribute to the next generation of nuclear energy, we'd love to have you join us next summer. We will be running two separate cohorts to accommodate students on both semester and quarter schedules: Cohort #1 Monday, May 17 – Friday, August 13 Cohort #2 Monday, June 14 – Friday, September 10 All internship roles are based at our Torrance headquarters and require interns to work onsite five days per week. We will not be considering candidates for remote or hybrid arrangements. Interns will receive a relocation and housing stipend as part of their offer package. About the Team As a Nuclear Engineering Intern, you will work directly on the design and analysis of Antares reactors. You will contribute to reactor design efforts while helping develop and validate the computational physics capabilities used to inform engineering decisions. Interns will be tasked with small starter projects, and then quickly tasked with a long-duration project that will culminate in a technical deliverable and presentation. You will be integrated and evaluated as if you are a first-year junior engineer, not just an “intern”. The bar for success here is high, and the expectation is that you’re able to smartly use your mentor and the resources around you to execute on your project and identify more issues and opportunities for improvement. Roles and Responsibilities: - Drive reactor design work by performing nuclear engineering analyses that inform design decisions. - Develop and validate computational physics capabilities used to analyze and evaluate reactor designs. Basic Qualifications: - Enrolled in at least a bachelor’s degree program, and going into your Junior or Senior year of studies. - 6+ months experience of technical engineering skills outside of the university setting classroom (eg: laboratory, research, extracurricular project teams, volunteering, personal projects or prior internship/work experience) Preferred Skills & Experience: - GPA of 3.5 or above. - Experience in a University club or organization, leadership role preferred. - Strong interpersonal and technical communication skills (examples: leading a student project team, presenting research at conferences, etc.). - Strong analytical and problem-solving skills with attention to detail. - Ability to work cross-departmentally with different groups and teams. - Ability to work effectively in a dynamic environment with changing needs and requirements. - Ability to work independently and in a team, take initiative, and communicate effectively. Location - We are located in Torrance, CA in a 322,000 square foot, brand new facility featuring large open spaces for team collaboration, R&D, and production, as well as easy access to the 405, 105, and 110 freeways. Our facility is in the heart of Los Angeles' vibrant emerging tech ecosystem alongside many other high growth startups and enterprises. Culture At Antares, we like to specifically tie each role to our founding document’s set of values–here are the top five cultural values we think you should believe at your core to be successful: - Think in Systems - Energy and Defense are complex ecosystems with numerous stakeholders with competing priorities, conflicting policies, perverse incentives, and emergent and path-dependent properties. First principles thinking alone is insufficient. Think probabilistically and then take action. “If you want to be certain, then you are apt to be obsolete.” Over-optimizing the components often degrades the system - Obsess over the End User - The customer and end user are often not the same. We will never build globally competitive commercial products if we lose sight of our end users and their entire interaction with the product life cycle - Be Unconstrained by Convention - Our only limits are the laws of physics. Many, even experts, will say what we are working on is impossible. They said the same about SpaceX reusing rockets. Generationally impactful companies, by definition, must accomplish the seemingly impossible. If it were easy, it would have already been done. Never shy away from a solution because it has never been tried before, and never choose to do something because that's “how it's always been done” - Go Where the Work Is - Never miss a chance to meet a customer, user, or stakeholder face to face, even if that means hopping on a plane. If you can’t make it, find a teammate who can channel your intentions and go in your place. Deep work can be done from anywhere, but we believe teams are built in person, and aim to maximize our time together - Operate in the Grey - Embrace nuance in pursuit of truth. Question every fundamental assumption Equal Opportunity Antares is an Equal Opportunity Employer. Employment decisions are based solely on merit, competence, and qualifications, without regard to race, color, religion, gender, national origin/ethnicity, veteran status, disability status, age, sexual orientation, gender identity, marital status, mental or physical disability, or any other legally protected status. ITAR REQUIREMENTS To conform to U.S. Government export regulations, applicant must be a (i) U.S. citizen or national, (ii) U.S. lawful, permanent resident (aka green card holder), (iii) Refugee under 8 U.S.C. § 1157, or (iv) Asylee under 8 U.S.C. § 1158, or be eligible to obtain the required authorizations from the U.S. Department of State. Learn more about the ITAR here https://www.pmddtc.state.gov/?id=ddtc_kb_article_page&sys_id=24d528fddbfc930044f9ff621f961987. Pay range: $34 per hour.

At CesiumAstro, we are developers and pioneers of out-of-the-box communication systems for satellites, UAVs, launch vehicles, and other space and airborne platforms. If you are looking for hands-on, interactive, and autonomous work, CesiumAstro is the place for you. jobs.title: Engineering Intern 1

jobs.body: The group you’ll be a part of The Office of the CTO is where innovation takes center stage. We inspire our global technical community to take on grand challenges, understand emerging trends, identify the critical inflections, and drive our sustainability, Environment, Social, and Governance (ESG) practices that will define the next generation of semiconductors and continued impact. The impact you’ll make We are looking for an internship candidate who wishes to strengthen their skills in Explainability and Interpretability for probabilistic / Bayesian surrogate models and Bayesian Optimization (BO). The internship will focus on Bayesian surrogate model interpretability and explainable Bayesian Optimization techniques over controlled synthetic functions and real semiconductor data. What you’ll do Explore the Explainable AI literature and come up with relevant methods suitable for interpreting Bayesian surrogate models Develop methods to interpret modeled correlations among model outputs and compare learned relationships with known synthetic function / real data properties Create post-hoc explanations for the recommended solution selected via BO, clarifying the model evidence and optimization logic that led to the selected recipe Implement reproducible experiments on synthetic test functions / real data, performing surrogate modeling, BO and explanation pipelines in Python Investigate interpretable representations of correlation, latent structure, and information sharing across outputs Develop local post-hoc explanation methods for BO recommended solutions such as feature/parameter attribution, counterfactual analysis, sensitivity analysis, or decomposition of predictive and acquisition quantities Define fidelity, stability, consistency, and usability criteria; validate explanations using known synthetic function properties or real data Create clear visualizations and concise technical documentation suitable for Data Scientists and process-development stakeholders Who we’re looking for Master or PhD students with strong interest and foundation in statistical machine learning, probabilistic modeling, explainable AI, and Bayesian Optimization Strong knowledge on Gaussian Processes, kernel methods, uncertainty quantification, and Bayesian Optimization Strong Python programming and debugging skills; experience with PyTorch, GPyTorch, BoTorch, NumPy, Pandas, and visualization libraries is preferred Knowledge on correlation analysis, feature attribution / importance, sensitivity analysis, predictive model explanations, and BO decision explanations Experience with synthetic benchmark functions, causal reasoning, spatial data, or structured outputs is advantageous Self-driven, collaborative, and able to communicate technical results clearly. jobs.title: Intern - Compute System Compatibility Engineer
jobs.location: Boise, ID - Main Site, United States of America
jobs.body: Our vision is to transform how the world uses information to enrich life for all . Micron Technology is a world leader in innovating memory and storage solutions that accelerate the transformation of information into intelligence, inspiring the world to learn, communicate and advance faster than ever. We validate Micron memory products on current and next-generation computing platforms. As an Intern System Compatibility Engineer, you will join our System Enablement and Test Development teams and gain hands-on experience with platform bring-up, system configuration, memory validation, test development, automation, data analysis, and AI-enabled engineering workflows under the guidance of experienced engineers. We will provide technical mentorship, structured onboarding, and exposure to DRAM, BIOS and firmware interactions, computer architecture, laboratory workflows, responsible use of approved AI tools, and the memory product lifecycle from initial bring-up through qualification and readiness. Key Responsibilities Set up and support Intel, AMD, and ARM-based systems in Linux, Windows, and UEFI environments; document hardware, BIOS, firmware, operating system, memory, and test configurations for repeatable execution and traceability. Implement memory validation activities that assess compatibility, stability, reliability, performance, and platform readiness. Reproduce and triage failures, collect logs and diagnostic data, use issue-tracking systems, apply structured failure-analysis methods, and support validation of corrective actions. Build or refine automation using Python, PowerShell, C++, or related languages; use approved AI-assisted tools to accelerate code development, test generation, log analysis, data summarization, technical research, documentation, and reporting while applying engineering judgment to verify accuracy and results. Apply responsible AI practices by protecting confidential information, using company-approved tools and data sources, documenting AI-assisted work where appropriate, identifying potential errors or bias, and independently validating generated code, analysis, and technical conclusions before use. Collaborate with System Enablement, Test Engineering, product, quality, and program teams on assigned validation and root-cause investigation activities. Communicate findings, risks, dependencies, corrective actions, and recommended next steps through concise documentation and presentations. Internship Assignment - The intern will complete a bounded technical project or workstream with defined milestones, measurable deliverables, technical documentation, and a final presentation. The assignment will be selected to provide relevant business value while remaining achievable within a three-month summer internship! Required Qualifications Currently pursuing a bachelor’s or graduate degree in Computer Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Computer Science, or a closely related technical field. Must be continuing education in the fall term following the internship; the expected graduation date must not be before September of the same year. Foundational knowledge of computer hardware, operating systems, computer architecture, and structured problem-solving. Programming or scripting experience gained through coursework, projects, laboratories, student organizations, or other technical experience using Python, PowerShell, C++, or a comparable language. Basic proficiency using AI-enabled tools to research technical topics, develop or solve code, analyze data, summarize findings, or improve documentation, with the ability to review outputs critically and confirm accuracy. Ability to follow test procedures, maintain accurate configuration records, analyze data, and summarize technical results. Interest in hands-on laboratory validation, system debug, test development, or engineering automation. Preferred Qualifications Experience working with DRAM, memory systems, BIOS or UEFI, firmware, server or client platforms, or hardware interfaces. Familiarity with x86 or ARM architectures, Intel, AMD, ARM-based, or embedded platforms, and Linux, Windows, or UEFI environments. Experience with oscilloscopes, logic analyzers, protocol analyzers, power measurement equipment, or similar diagnostic tools. Experience applying generative AI, machine learning, automation, or data-analysis tools to an engineering or academic workflow—for example, developing code, generating tests, analyzing logs, identifying patterns, creating dashboards, improving documentation, or automating repetitive tasks. Clear written and verbal communication, attention to detail, adaptability, partnership, and willingness to learn unfamiliar tools and technologies. Our M&S experts are developing new to the world mathematical models which speed the pace and impact of our innovations. Data Science: C ommunicate s complex data or algorithms into simple conclusions that will empower others to drive action based on the insights you derive. jobs.body: Wanna Join the Adventure? Loft Orbital is looking for a Thermal & Manufacturing Engineering Intern to join our team in Golden, Colorado for Summer 2027. You’ll work alongside our Mission Engineering & Analysis and Assembly, Integration & Test (AIT) teams to improve how thermal interface materials are selected, prepared, and used in spacecraft assembly. This internship offers hands-on experience at the intersection of materials, mechanical engineering, and manufacturing. You’ll work directly with AIT technicians and engineers, taking your work from CAD drawings to physical parts used on satellites. You’ll take a process improvement from initial experiments through validation and documentation, then see it used in spacecraft assembly.

jobs.location: San Jose, CA
jobs.body: About the role Muon seeks a Harness Design Intern to join our electrical engineering team. The ideal candidate is someone who has gained familiarity with harnessing through student clubs or internships and has some programming background. The goal is to advance your harness design skills during the internship and then use those skills to build really cool tools. Is there a way we can build an AI agent to review our harness drawings and make sure we don’t make basic errors? Is there a way we can create a harnessing agent to interact with the API of our programs and design harnesses? These are the types of questions we want you to answer during your internship! Responsibilities Work on new tooling and improve the workflows associated with harness design Experiment with AI to update and modify drawings Create harness drawings, BOMs and maintain system diagrams Specify connector and crimp part numbers in accordance with system design Gather feedback from AIT, EE and Mechanical for initial designs and improvements Work with electrical engineering to ensure compliance with signal integrity, grounding, and shielding requirements Release documentation into PLM with ECO/DCO Define electrical test criteria (e.g., continuity, insulation resistance, hipot) for flight and test harnesses. Support or oversee test execution and documentation Qualifications Attention to detail, strong reading comprehension and a desire for ownership Familiarity with creating harness drawings in any software Ability to use the linux terminal, basic git tools, LLMs with MCPs, python programming Ability to build harnesses from scratch - not required daily but helps inform strip lengths, crimper positioners and settings, splicing techniques, heatshrink selection, torque values etc. Excited to work in a fast-paced environment with new challenges each week Nice-to-have Skills Previous internship or co-op experience Previous experience on student teams (i.e. Rocketry club, formula SAE, solar car, etc.) Experience designing harnesses with high reliability requirements Experience with RF cable build and characterization Experience building agents and using AI to complete engineering tasks Pay range Bachelor's $40/hour Master's $45/hour PhD $50/hour About Muon Space Founded in 2021, Muon Space is an end-to-end Space Systems Provider that designs, builds, and operates LEO satellite constellations delivering mission-critical data. Our revolutionary, integrated technology stack enables customers to optimize every dimension of their missions for faster time-to-orbit and superior constellation remote sensing performance. Our state-of-the-art facility in the heart of Silicon Valley is optimized for manufacturing spacecraft and rapid, flexible payload integration at scale. From climate monitoring to national security, Muon Space is dedicated to delivering Earth Intelligence for a safer and more resilient world. jobs.body: ABOUT ROCKET LAB Rocket Lab is the end-to-end space company building rockets, spacecraft, and critical subsystems that keep the world connected, protected, expand humanity’s reach to the Moon, Mars, and beyond. Our comprehensive benefits package includes our industry-leading Employee Stock Purchase Program (with a 15% discount on company stock), top-tier medical plans (HMO, PPO, and a zero cost HDHP option with a significant HSA company contribution), dental and vision coverage, paid vacation and sick time, 11 paid holidays, flexible spending and dependent care accounts, paid parental leave, disability and life insurance, and a 401(k) retirement plan with company match. Additional perks include subsidized EV charging, onsite fitness centers (where available), discounted gym memberships, complimentary snacks and beverages, 50% employee discount on our popular merch store, and a variety of other employee discounts. It takes hard work, determination, relentless innovation, teamwork, grit, and an unwavering commitment to achieving what others often deem impossible. Our people out-think, out-work, and out-pace. We pride ourselves on having each other’s backs, checking our egos at the door, and rolling up our sleeves on all tasks big and small. jobs.location: USA Wilmington, MA - ITC, United States of America
jobs.body: Who we are With its A.I.-powered robotic technology platform, Symbotic is changing the way consumer goods move through the supply chain. Intelligent software orchestrates advanced robots in a high-density, end-to-end system – reinventing warehouse automation for increased efficiency, speed and flexibility. Intern- Manufacturing Engineer Term: Summer (May-Aug) At Symbotic, early career talent plays a meaningful role in helping us reimagine the future of supply chain automation. Through our Internship and Co-op programs, students have the opportunity to contribute to real projects, collaborate with experienced engineers and business leaders, and gain hands-on exposure to the technologies powering our end-to-end robotics and automation solutions. We are looking for curious, motivated students who are excited to solve complex problems, bring new perspectives to cross-functional teams, and see their work make an impact in a fast-moving, innovative environment. Along the way, Interns and Co-ops are supported through mentorship, professional development, networking opportunities, and a robust calendar of events designed to help them build community and grow their careers. Symbotic offers transportation and housing benefits for students who meet our relocation requirements. Continue reading below to learn more about this exciting opportunity! What we need Symbotic is seeking a Manufacturing Engineer Intern to join our External Manufacturing team within our Manufacturing organization. Your job will be to support external manufacturing partners and internal engineering teams by helping improve manufacturing processes, prepare products for production, and support manufacturing readiness for our automated systems. This is a cross-functional internship for a student interested in gaining hands-on experience across mechanical, electrical, manufacturing, and process engineering. What we do The External Manufacturing team sits within the External Manufacturing organization and partners with external manufacturers and internal engineering teams to support the production of Symbotic's automated solutions. Since manufacturing is performed through external partners, the team works closely with suppliers and cross-functional teams to establish manufacturing processes, support production readiness, manage engineering changes, and help ensure products can be manufactured efficiently and reliably. What you'll do Support senior engineers and external manufacturing partners on manufacturing readiness, production support, and continuous improvement activities. Partner with Engineering and Quality teams to prepare manufacturing readiness documentation, support engineering changes, and help maintain standard manufacturing processes and procedures. Work across mechanical and electrical systems, including reviewing drawings, manufacturing requirements, and production-related technical documentation. Support Design for Manufacturability activities and help identify opportunities to improve manufacturability, quality, efficiency, and scalability. Assist with troubleshooting manufacturing and design challenges and collaborate with internal teams and external partners to identify practical solutions. Contribute to process improvement initiatives, including opportunities to use dashboards, data, automation, or AI-enabled tools to improve team efficiency. Travel to external manufacturing partner locations as needed to gain hands-on exposure to manufacturing operations and support production activities. What you'll need Currently pursuing a degree in Industrial Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, or a related engineering discipline. Academic project, lab, internship, co-op, or other hands-on exposure to manufacturing, automation, prototyping, or engineering processes. Ability to interpret and work with mechanical or electrical engineering documentation, with an interest in developing experience across both disciplines. Strong problem-solving and analytical skills with an interest in process improvement and learning how products move from engineering into manufacturing. Interest in using data, dashboards, automation, or emerging tools to improve manufacturing and engineering processes. Our Environment Employees must have a valid driver's license and the ability to drive and/or fly to client locations and company HQ. Employees may be required to use a personal credit card for business travel expenses, which are reimbursed based on the program guidelines. Eligible employees may receive a corporate credit card based on role and travel requirements, but a personal credit card may be needed during onboarding until the corporate card is issued. #LI-KK1 About Symbotic Symbotic is an automation technology leader reimagining the supply chain with its end-to-end, AI-powered robotic and software platform. Symbotic reinvents the warehouse as a strategic asset for the world’s largest retail, wholesale, and food & beverage companies. Applying next-gen technology, high-density storage and machine learning to solve today's complex distribution challenges, Symbotic enables companies to move goods with unmatched speed, agility, accuracy and efficiency. As the backbone of commerce the Symbotic platform transforms the flow of goods and the economics of supply chain for its customers. For more information, visit www.symbotic.com . We are a community of innovators, collaborators and pioneers who embrace our differences, because we know unique perspectives make us stronger and smarter. Every perspective matters. We depend on the collective voices of our employees, customers and community to help guide us as we build a better place to work – for you and the world. That’s why we’re proud to be an equal opportunity employer. We do not discriminate based on race, color, ethnicity, ancestry, religion, sex, national origin, sexual orientation, age, citizenship status, marital status, disability, gender identity, gender expression, veteran status, or genetic information. The base range for this position in the posted location is $29.00 - $37.95 however, base pay offered may vary depending on job-related knowledge, skills, and experience. The compensation package includes medical, dental, vision, disability, 401K, PTO and/or other benefits.

jobs.title: Summer Internship - Plasma Diagnostics
jobs.location: Knoxville, TN
jobs.body: Join us in our mission to commercialize fusion energy ⚡️ About Type One Energy Type One Energy Group is mission-driven to provide sustainable, affordable fusion power to the world. Established in 2019 and venture-backed in 2023, the company is led by a team of globally recognized fusion scientists with a strong track record of building state-of-the-art stellarator fusion machines, together with veteran business leaders experienced in scaling companies and commercializing energy technologies. If you are searching for the best new ideas and share our vision, join us as a Plasma Diagnostics Summer Intern. This is what you need to know: Location: Knoxville, TN Salary: $25-$35/hour, 40 hours per week Contract: 12-week internship, Summer 2027 (May 24th start date) Reporting to: Sr. Diagnostic Scientist Your role in the mission: Type One Energy Group, Inc. is seeking a summer intern in Plasma Diagnostic to apply your education and experience in the design and development of plasma diagnostics for a new fusion energy device. This role requires a self-motivated learner who loves being challenged and gaining new skills. The ideal candidate will have experience in physics, specifically plasma physics and fusion energy, but a broad background including physical laboratory, mathematical/computational, engineering, and software is more important. Key responsibilities could include: Apply physical models and numerical analysis tools to guide the requirements for plasma diagnostics. Collaborate with computational physicists, experimental physicists, and engineers to develop the conceptual design for plasma diagnostics. Develop the data analysis workflow and algorithms to extract physical information from raw instrument data. Build and test physical diagnostic hardware including optical systems and electronic circuits. What you'll need: Senior-level student pursuing a degree in physics, engineering physics, optics, electrical engineering, data science, astrophysics, or a related field. Rising juniors, seniors, graduate, and PhD students are encouraged to apply. Experience with data analysis in python is required. Additional software skills including numerical simulations, optical system design, thermal modeling, electrical schematic/PCB design, SPICE circuit simulation, version control, LINUX, and databases are desirable. Experience with plasma physics, fusion energy, or remote sensing will be a bonus. Hands-on experience working with scientific instruments, microwave/RF systems, optics, lasers, vacuum systems, and/or electronic circuits will be a bonus. Ability to receive guidance, work independently, and contribute to a team. For questions about this position, please reach out to internships@typeoneenergy.com Type One Energy applies proven advanced manufacturing methods, modern computational physics and high-field superconducting magnets to develop its optimized stellarator fusion energy system. Our FusionDirect development program pursues the lowest-risk, shortest-schedule path to a fusion power plant over the coming decade, using a partner-intensive and capital-efficient strategy. Type One Energy is committed to community engagement in the development and deployment of its clean energy technology. For more information, visit www.typeoneenergy.com or follow us on LinkedIn. jobs.body: Who We Are Verkada is transforming how organizations protect their people and places with an integrated, privacy-sensitive AI-powered platform that includes solutions for video security, access control, air quality sensors, alarms, intercoms, and visitor management. We’ve got serious momentum in the market: more than 30,000 customers (including 100+ of the Fortune 500), a $5.8B valuation , more than $1 billion in annualized bookings, and backing from CapitalG, Sequoia Capital, General Catalyst, Felicis Ventures, Next47 and more. Physical AI is one of the most consequential technology shifts of our time, and Verkada is at the center of it. You can look at all kinds of communities to see our platform’s impact in the world. It's the retailer that uses our agentic AI to deter theft before it happens. The warehouse that uses AI-powered alerts to make sure its team is protected on the floor with proper PPE. The school that’s alerted to a threat in real-time and triggers a lockdown in seconds, not minutes. We’re rapidly scaling this impact: today, more than 2 million Verkada devices are deployed across 170+ countries. Our interns are at the forefront of our team, tackling real-world challenges alongside our full-time engineers. Based at our San Mateo HQ, you'll work with cutting-edge, cloud-managed IoT technology, helping our enterprise clients with everything from troubleshooting to system design. This internship is your chance to make a real impact, build valuable technical skills, and jumpstart your career in a dynamic, high-tech environment. And more! From team-building activities to mentorship opportunities, we’re here to support your growth every step of the way Don't just take it from us, hear directly from some of our current and past interns on their experience: “A benefit of being a TSE at Verkada is about being a part of a fast-growing company. Being able to communicate this to them in a reasonable amount of time is paramount to doing well in this role” - Tedrick, TSE Intern, HQ “This internship has given me a lot to think about in terms of career goals. It’s also given me a unique perspective and understanding of enterprise equipment. It serves as a great launching point for your career.” - Thomas, TSE Intern, HQ Additional Information We do sponsor and take over sponsorship of employment visas for this role. If we make you an offer, we will make every reasonable effort to get you a visa. jobs.title: Manufacturing Engineer Intern - Summer 2027

jobs.body: Who We Are Vermeer equips customers doing important work around the world. We are global, driven by innovation and growing. The equipment we make manages natural resources, connects people and feeds and fuels communities. We live out a caring culture, we demonstrate agility, we keep a focus on customers and are stewards of our resources. These beliefs drive our culture, determine how we treat others and steer our business. Work Shift 1 - First Shift Job Summary Are you energized by solving problems and improving how things are made? As a Manufacturing Engineer Intern at Vermeer, you’ll support real-world projects that enhance production processes and drive operational excellence. This internship offers hands-on experience in lean manufacturing, process improvement, and cross-functional collaboration—preparing you for a full-time engineering role upon graduation. What You’ll Do 1. Assist in identifying and implementing process improvements that enhance quality, efficiency, and sustainability across production areas. 2. Support new product introductions and manufacturing improvement initiatives by collaborating with engineering, welding, assembly, and machining teams. 3. Apply lean manufacturing principles—including Just-In-Time (JIT) production and Kaizen events—to reduce waste and improve flow. 4. Document and analyze current and future state processes using tools such as value stream mapping and standard work documentation. 5. Help design and optimize tooling and fixtures, and gain exposure to digital work instruction platforms. 6. Contribute to documentation and change management using Product Lifecycle Management (PLM) and Engineering Change Notification (ECN) systems such as Teamcenter or Windchill. 7. Participate in data-driven decision-making using Enterprise Resource Planning (ERP) systems, Power BI dashboards, and Internet of Things (IoT)-enabled process monitoring tools.
