jobs.body: Job Title: Production Planning Intern Job Description: Production Planning Intern - Summer 2027 Here at Entegris, we use advanced science to enable technologies that transform the world, and we are seeking employees who have the drive to continue the mission. The Role: Our site in Danbury, CT is seeking a Production Planning Intern to join our team for the Summer 2027 season. This assignment is intended to be 12-14 weeks in duration. We are seeking a highly motivated and analytical Production Planning Intern to join our Supply Chain team. This role provides hands-on experience supporting production planning, inventory management, scheduling, and data analysis in a fast-paced manufacturing environment. The intern will work closely with Production Planning, Operations, Procurement, Engineering, Logistics, and Quality to help improve planning visibility and execution. The internship is designed to build practical experience with ERP systems, supply chain analytics, manufacturing operations, and continuous improvement while contributing to a meaningful business project. What You’ll Do: Assist with creating and maintaining production schedules based on demand, capacity, and material availability. Monitor inventory, planned orders, production orders, and work order status to identify potential supply risks. Analyze planning and manufacturing data and prepare reports that support timely business decisions. Support SAP ERP and master data maintenance, including MRP parameters, lead times, lot sizes, and planning settings. Participate in daily and weekly planning meetings, document action items, and track follow-up activities. Collaborate with Operations, Procurement, Engineering, Logistics, and Quality to address material and scheduling issues. Support capacity planning, schedule adherence analysis, and root-cause reviews for performance gaps. Use Microsoft Excel, Power BI, or similar tools to improve dashboards, metrics, and reporting visibility. Identify opportunities to improve planning processes, data accuracy, and manual workflows. Complete and present an internship project with findings and recommendations to Supply Chain and Operations leadership. What We Seek: Strong analytical, critical-thinking, and problem-solving skills. Working knowledge of Microsoft Excel. Effective written and verbal communication skills. Ability to work independently, manage priorities, and collaborate in a team environment. Desired Major(s) & Graduation Year: Expected graduation year: 2027 or later (flexible based on program requirements). Currently pursuing a bachelor’s degree in supply chain management, Industrial Engineering, Operations Management, Business Analytics, Data Analytics, or a related field. Eligibility: Must be a currently enrolled student Available to work 40 hours a week, M-F (8a-5p) beginning in June through August Must be familiar with the university’s requirements to participate in a co-op program Entegris is not currently hiring candidates for co-ops/internships who will need, now or at any time in the future, Entegris sponsorship through the H1-B lottery. WHY WORK AT ENTEGRIS? Lead. Inspire. Innovate. Define Your Future. Not everyone who works for a global company shares the same background, experiences and perspectives. We leverage the differences of our employees to bring new ideas to the table. Every employee throughout the company is encouraged to share input on projects and initiatives. Our decision-making process is truly a collaborative effort as we realize there are leaders at every level of the organization. We put our values at the core of how we operate as an organization — not just when it’s convenient, but in a lasting and meaningful way. We want the time and energy you spend here to have a positive impact on your life inside and outside of the office. WHAT WE OFFER Our total rewards package goes above and beyond just a paycheck. Whether you’re looking to build your career, improve your health, or protect your wealth, we offer generous benefits to help you achieve your goals. Compensation: $20-$30/hour range with actual pay dependent on candidate overall skills for the role Values-driven culture with colleagues that rally around People, Accountability, Creativity and Excellence Entegris does not provide immigration-related sponsorship for this role. Do not apply for this role if you will need Entegris immigration sponsorship (e.g., H1B, TN, STEM OPT, etc.) now or in the future. At Entegris we are committed to providing equal opportunity to all employees and applicants. Our policy is to recruit, hire, train, and reward employees for their individual abilities, achievements, and experience without regard to race, color, religion, sexual orientation, age, national origin, disability, marital or military status.

jobs.title: Micro-Grid Systems Engineering Summer Intern
jobs.location: USA - CO Fort Collins, United States of America
jobs.body: We believe power is a promise - a shared commitment to be there for others when it matters most. For more than 65 years, we've turned big ideas into solutions that help protect homes, strengthen businesses and build a more resilient, efficient, sustainable energy future. Ready to Power a Smarter World with us? At Generac, we are accelerating the transformation of the electric grid through advanced microgrid technologies, distributed energy resources (DERs), and intelligent control systems. We are seeking a highly motivated Microgrid Controls Engineering Intern to join our Industrial Microgrid Controls Team in Fort Collins, Colorado for the summer of 2027. This position offers a unique opportunity to apply advanced data analytics, artificial intelligence, and power systems engineering to improve the performance, reliability, and operation of real-world microgrid deployments. Working alongside experienced controls, software, and power systems engineers, you will analyze operational data from fielded systems, identify performance improvement opportunities, develop predictive insights, validate next-generation control strategies through Hardware-in-the-Loop (HIL) testing, and contribute to the future of intelligent energy systems. Unlike traditional engineering internships, this role provides direct exposure to operational microgrid assets and customer applications, where your work may directly influence future products, system architectures, and customer outcomes. Major Responsibilities Data Analytics & System Intelligence Analyze large data sets from deployed microgrid, energy storage, and distributed energy resource systems to identify trends, anomalies, reliability concerns, and optimization opportunities. Transform this operational data into actionable engineering recommendations. Develop advanced analytics, dashboards, and visualization tools to improve customer value, operational performance, and fleet-wide system insights. Infer from the above analysis what statistical, machine learning, and AI-based approaches may support predictive maintenance, fault detection, and root cause analysis efforts going forward. Next-Generation Controls Validation Design and conduct off-nominal, fault, and edge-case testing scenarios to evaluate system robustness and reliability through model in the loop (MIL) and hardware in the loop (HIL) setups. Support verification and validation efforts for advanced microgrid control architectures. AI & Engineering Productivity Develop AI agents and automation tools to enhance sales applications engineering, technical support, and internal engineering workflows. Investigate emerging AI technologies and their application to power systems, controls engineering, and customer support. Systems Engineering & Innovation Support development of engineering standards, analytics processes, and best practices. Engage with Generac's academic and national laboratory partners to investigate emerging technologies and evolving industry challenges. undefined Minimum Requirements Education Currently pursuing a Bachelor's or Master's degree in: Mechanical, Electrical, or Computer, Energy Systems Engineering, Data Science, Applied Math or related technical discipline. jobs.body: Our vision is to transform how the world uses information to enrich life for all . Micron Technology is a world leader in innovating memory and storage solutions that accelerate the transformation of information into intelligence, inspiring the world to learn, communicate and advance faster than ever. At Micron, the Process Pathfinding organization develops next-generation semiconductor memory technologies and innovative device architectures. The team focuses on advancing process technologies that enable future memory products through fundamental research, process integration, and collaboration across engineering fields. This is an outstanding opportunity to contribute to innovative semiconductor development in a fast-paced, knowledge-focused environment. As a DRAM Dry Etch Process Pathfinding Intern, you will support the development of advanced plasma etch processes for emerging memory technologies. Working alongside experienced engineers and multi-functional partners, you will gain hands-on experience with dry etch equipment, semiconductor process development, materials characterization, and data-driven problem solving. This role provides exposure to advanced manufacturing environments while contributing to process solutions that improve device performance and reliability. Responsibilities Conduct experiments and fundamental research to develop innovative dry etch solutions for next-generation memory technologies. Partner with the Pathfinding team to develop and optimize dry etch processes that meet physical and electrical performance requirements. Apply analytical, statistical, and problem-solving methods to evaluate process performance, hardware capability, and process capability, and aid in resolving problems. Demonstrated ability to analyze technical data and communicate findings through written reports or presentations. Strong interpersonal and collaboration skills demonstrated through academic, laboratory, or project-based work. Ability to work independently, manage priorities, and deliver results in a research or engineering environment. Proficiency with data analysis tools, statistical methods, and digital technologies used to support engineering decisions. Experience using AI-Assisted tools, Artificial Intelligence applications, or data-driven technologies to improve technical analysis, productivity, and learning. jobs.body: RELOCATION ASSISTANCE: Relocation assistance may be available CLEARANCE REQUIRED FOR START: No CLEARANCE TYPE: Secret TRAVEL: Yes, 10% of the Time Description At Northrop Grumman, our employees have incredible opportunities to work on revolutionary systems that impact people's lives around the world today, and for generations to come. Our pioneering and inventive spirit has enabled us to be at the forefront of many technological advancements in our nation's history - from the first flight across the Atlantic Ocean, to stealth bombers, to landing on the moon. We look for people who have bold new ideas, courage and a pioneering spirit to join forces to invent the future, and have fun along the way. Our culture thrives on intellectual curiosity, cognitive diversity and bringing your whole self to work — and we have an insatiable drive to do what others think is impossible. Our mission experience in space runs deep, we know our customers well, and our capabilities are unmatched. jobs.title: Summer Internship - Fusion Engineering
jobs.location: Knoxville, TN
jobs.body: Join us in our mission to commercialize fusion energy ⚡️ About Type One Energy Type One Energy Group is mission-driven to provide sustainable, affordable fusion power to the world. Established in 2019 and venture-backed in 2023, the company is led by a team of globally recognized fusion scientists with a strong track record of building state-of-the-art stellarator fusion machines, together with veteran business leaders experienced in scaling companies and commercializing energy technologies. If you are searching for the best new ideas and share our vision, join us as a Fusion Engineering (Hydrogen-Material Interactions) Summer Intern . This is what you need to know: Location: Knoxville, TN Salary: $25-$35/hour, 40 hours per week Contract: 12-week internship, Summer 2027 (May 24 th start date) Reporting to: Sr. Director Nuclear & Fuel Cycle Engineering Your role in the mission: Type One Energy is looking for a motivated Fusion Engineering Summer Intern to support experimental research and development within our Fuel Cycle and Ceramic Breeder teams. The intern will help investigate how hydrogen and its isotopes interact with materials relevant to fusion energy systems, with particular emphasis on the use of hydrogen and deuterium as non-radioactive surrogates for tritium. This work will contribute to our understanding of hydrogen transport, retention, and release in candidate materials for fusion fuel-cycle and ceramic breeder applications. Working alongside experienced engineers and scientists, the intern will gain practical laboratory experience while contributing to experimental investigations and supporting computational modelling activities. Key responsibility could include: Assist in the planning, preparation, and execution of laboratory experiments investigating hydrogen and deuterium interactions with materials. Support experimental testing of candidate ceramic breeder materials and other materials relevant to fusion fuel-cycle systems. Help develop and test hypotheses relating to hydrogen transport, diffusion, retention, and release under different experimental conditions. Gain hands-on experience with laboratory equipment, experimental instrumentation, gas-handling systems, and materials characterization techniques. Collect, process, and analyse experimental data, identifying trends and comparing results with expected material behaviour. Assist in developing simple computational models and analytical tools to support experimental interpretation and improve understanding of hydrogen–material interactions. Document experimental procedures, results, and findings, and communicate progress to the wider engineering team. Contribute to maintaining a safe, organized, and effective laboratory environment by following established procedures and safe working practices. What you'll need: Pursuing a degree in Materials Science, Mechanical Engineering, Chemical Engineering, Nuclear Engineering, Physics, or a closely related discipline. A fundamental understanding of materials science, thermodynamics, heat and mass transfer, or related engineering principles. An interest in experimental research, laboratory testing, and hands-on engineering activities. Some experience with data analysis, programming, or engineering calculations through coursework, laboratory classes, or personal projects. Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, with attention to detail. Willingness to learn new experimental techniques, computational tools, and laboratory procedures. Ability to communicate technical concepts and experimental findings clearly in written and verbal form. Preferred Qualifications: Previous laboratory experience through university coursework, research projects, or internships. Familiarity with Python, MATLAB, or similar tools for data analysis and basic computational modelling. Coursework or project experience involving materials characterization, diffusion, mass transfer, or hydrogen-related technologies. Familiarity with experimental instrumentation, data acquisition, or gas-handling systems. Interest in fusion energy, hydrogen technologies, advanced materials, or nuclear engineering. For questions about this position, please reach out to internships@typeoneenergy.com Type One Energy applies proven advanced manufacturing methods, modern computational physics and high-field superconducting magnets to develop its optimized stellarator fusion energy system. Our FusionDirect development program pursues the lowest-risk, shortest-schedule path to a fusion power plant over the coming decade, using a partner-intensive and capital-efficient strategy. Type One Energy is committed to community engagement in the development and deployment of its clean energy technology. For more information, visit www.typeoneenergy.com or follow us on LinkedIn. jobs.title: Nuclear Operations & Licensing Engineering Intern - Summer 2027
jobs.location: Idaho Falls
jobs.body: About Us At Antares, our long-term mission is to make clean energy abundant from Earth to the Asteroid Belt. We’re fueled by the belief that advanced nuclear energy can strengthen our military, solve the climate crisis, elevate global living standards, and expand humanity's presence in outer space. To achieve our mission, we’re building mass-producible, inherently safe, deployable microreactors that can be used terrestrially, underwater, and in space. The Antares team hails from SpaceX, the White House, the Pentagon, the Department of Energy, MIT, Rigetti Computing, General Atomics, Relativity Space, Ursa Major, and National Laboratories like Idaho, Oak Ridge, Los Alamos, and Savannah River. Antares has raised over $600M in venture capital from top-tier investors and has hundreds of million-dollars on contract with the military services, NASA, and the Department of Energy. About the Summer Internship Program Internships at Antares are anything but ordinary. You'll work alongside our team as we design, build, and test fission microreactors built to deliver reliable energy for critical missions on Earth, in space, and underwater. Our interns contribute to real work from day one. Depending on your role, you may touch hardware, write and test software, support manufacturing and operations, or help build the systems that allow Antares to move quickly as we scale. You'll work alongside engineers, operators, and other experts solving challenging problems—and you'll leave your internship with hands-on experience that's difficult to find anywhere else. We work hard, move quickly, and take pride in what we're building. If you're excited to learn by doing and want to contribute to the next generation of nuclear energy, we'd love to have you join us next summer. We will be running two separate cohorts to accommodate students on both semester and quarter schedules: Cohort #1 Monday, May 17 – Friday, August 13 Cohort #2 Monday, June 14 – Friday, September 10 All internship roles are based at our Torrance headquarters or Idaho Falls, ID office and require interns to work onsite five days per week. We will not be considering candidates for remote or hybrid arrangements. Interns will receive a relocation and housing stipend as part of their offer package. About the Role As a Nuclear Operations & Licensing Engineering Intern, you will help define how Antares reactor systems are operated, maintained, and deployed. You will work directly with responsible engineers (REs) to translate system designs into practical operating and maintenance requirements and use simulators and other test systems to validate and improve operator training activities. You will also contribute to Antares’ international deployment efforts by evaluating licensing frameworks across different countries, identifying areas of alignment, and assessing approaches for demonstrating compliance across domestic and international deployments. This role provides exposure to the intersection of reactor engineering, operations, training, and nuclear licensing. Roles and Responsibilities: - Interface with responsible engineers (REs) to establish operating requirements for reactor systems - Develop and document maintenance requirements based on system designs and operating needs - Use reactor simulators and other test systems to validate training activities - Identify opportunities to improve training activities based on simulator and test system results - Evaluate international nuclear licensing frameworks relevant to reactor deployment - Identify synergies and differences between domestic and international licensing requirements - Assess approaches for demonstrating compliance across domestic and international deployments Basic Qualifications: - Enrolled in at least a bachelor’s degree program, and going into your Junior or Senior year of studies - Must have prior internship experience, or significant (>1yr) project team, laboratory, or research experience Preferred Skills & Experience: - GPA of 3.5 or above - Experience in a University club or organization, leadership role preferred - Strong interpersonal and technical communication skills (examples: leading a student project team, presenting research at conferences, etc.) - Strong analytical and problem-solving skills with attention to detail - Ability to work cross-departmentally with different groups and teams - Ability to work effectively in a dynamic environment with changing needs and requirements - Ability to work independently and in a team, take initiative, and communicate effectively Location - We are located in Idaho Falls, ID at 545 Shoup Ave in the Rogers Building. The Rogers Building (formerly the Rogers Hotel) has its own nuclear history. In the 1940s, it became base of operations for the Atomic Energy Commission during the Manhattan Project. Today, the Idaho Falls office drives local operations and supports Idaho National Lab collaboration. Culture At Antares, we like to specifically tie each role to our founding document’s set of values–here are the top five cultural values we think you should believe at your core to be successful: - Think in Systems - Energy and Defense are complex ecosystems with numerous stakeholders with competing priorities, conflicting policies, perverse incentives, and emergent and path-dependent properties. First principles thinking alone is insufficient. Think probabilistically and then take action. “If you want to be certain, then you are apt to be obsolete.” Over-optimizing the components often degrades the system - Obsess over the End User - The customer and end user are often not the same. We will never build globally competitive commercial products if we lose sight of our end users and their entire interaction with the product life cycle - Be Unconstrained by Convention - Our only limits are the laws of physics. Many, even experts, will say what we are working on is impossible. They said the same about SpaceX reusing rockets. Generationally impactful companies, by definition, must accomplish the seemingly impossible. If it were easy, it would have already been done. Never shy away from a solution because it has never been tried before, and never choose to do something because that's “how it's always been done” - Go Where the Work Is - Never miss a chance to meet a customer, user, or stakeholder face to face, even if that means hopping on a plane. If you can’t make it, find a teammate who can channel your intentions and go in your place. Deep work can be done from anywhere, but we believe teams are built in person, and aim to maximize our time together - Operate in the Grey - Embrace nuance in pursuit of truth. Question every fundamental assumption Equal Opportunity Antares is an Equal Opportunity Employer. Employment decisions are based solely on merit, competence, and qualifications, without regard to race, color, religion, gender, national origin/ethnicity, veteran status, disability status, age, sexual orientation, gender identity, marital status, mental or physical disability, or any other legally protected status. ITAR REQUIREMENTS To conform to U.S. Government export regulations, applicant must be a (i) U.S. citizen or national, (ii) U.S. lawful, permanent resident (aka green card holder), (iii) Refugee under 8 U.S.C. § 1157, or (iv) Asylee under 8 U.S.C. § 1158, or be eligible to obtain the required authorizations from the U.S. Department of State. Learn more about the ITAR here https://www.pmddtc.state.gov/?id=ddtc_kb_article_page&sys_id=24d528fddbfc930044f9ff621f961987. Pay range: $34 per hour.

jobs.location: Spartanburg, South Carolina, United States of America
jobs.body: The Quality Engineering Co-op will support the Quality team in maintaining and improving product and process quality across manufacturing operations. This role provides hands-on experience in quality assurance, root cause analysis, continuous improvement, and regulatory compliance while working closely with cross-functional teams. The co-op will gain exposure to industry-standard quality tools and methodologies and contribute to initiatives that enhance customer satisfaction and operational excellence. Key Responsibilities: Support quality assurance activities by assisting in the development and execution of quality control plans, inspection procedures, and quality monitoring processes. Participate in audits and inspections of manufacturing processes and finished products to ensure compliance with quality standards and customer requirements. Assist in investigating customer-reported quality concerns and nonconformances, utilizing problem-solving tools such as 5 Whys, Fishbone Diagrams, and Failure Mode and Effects Analysis (FMEA). Support the implementation, tracking, and verification of corrective and preventive actions (CAPA) to address root causes and prevent recurrence. Collect, analyze, and interpret quality data to identify trends, process deviations, and opportunities for improvement. Apply statistical methods to evaluate process capability, product performance, and overall quality effectiveness. Maintain accurate documentation of inspections, nonconformances, corrective actions, and other quality records. Prepare reports, presentations, and quality metrics for internal reviews, management updates, and customer communications. Collaborate with engineering, manufacturing, and other cross-functional teams to improve processes, reduce defects, and enhance product quality. Participate in Lean, Six Sigma, and other continuous improvement initiatives to drive operational excellence. Support compliance with ISO 9001:2015 requirements, customer specifications, and internal quality procedures. Assist with internal audits and help prepare the organization for external audits and regulatory assessments. Attend training sessions on quality systems, industry standards, and company procedures while developing technical and professional skills. Shadow experienced quality professionals to gain practical knowledge of quality engineering principles, manufacturing processes, and problem-solving techniques. Qualifications: Pursuing a degree in Engineering, Quality, Manufacturing, Industrial Engineering, or a related technical field. Strong analytical and problem-solving skills. Proficiency in Microsoft Office applications, particularly Excel. Effective communication and interpersonal skills. Ability to work independently and collaboratively in a team environment. Familiarity with quality tools, statistical analysis, Lean principles, or Six Sigma methodologies is preferred. This position offers an opportunity to gain real-world experience in quality engineering while contributing to continuous improvement and operational excellence initiatives within a manufacturing environment. #CPE This description has been designed to indicate the general nature and level of work being performed by employees within this classification. You'll run test stations, assemble and rework hardware, cable racks, manage inventory, and own the day-to-day operations that turn raw silicon into working systems. You will see how a frontier AI chip goes from a tray of parts to a running rack, and reliable, curious interns take on engineering work over time. This role is for people genuinely excited about what we're building and willing to do real, often repetitive work with precision and care. Evening and weekend availability is a plus. This role is fully in-person in San Jose. You may be a good fit if you: - Have extreme attention to detail - Interested in both software and hardware - Are excited about learning how a hardware company works end to end - Are comfortable with hands-on work - Have evening or weekend availability - Curiosity and bias to action — see what needs doing and figure it out Strong candidates may also have: - Experience with software, mechanical engineering, or thermal systems - Understanding of accelerator hardware, or datacenter environments - Have owned or built hardware testing systems We encourage you to apply even if you do not believe you meet every qualification. Program details - 12-week paid internship - Generous housing support for those relocating - Daily lunch and dinner in our office - Based at our office in San Jose, CA - Direct mentorship from industry leaders and world-class engineers - Opportunity to work on one of the most important problems of our time For any questions, contact internships@etched.com How we're different Etched believes in the Bitter Lesson http://www.incompleteideas.net/IncIdeas/BitterLesson.html. We are the first inference-focused frontier AI system, betting early on transformer and transformer-like architectures and on increasing model sizes. Our addressable market is the entirety of inference. We are a fully in-person team in San Jose and Taipei, and greatly value engineering skills. We do not have boundaries between engineering and research, and we expect all of our technical staff to contribute to both and work across disciplines as needed.

jobs.body: Job Description Summary Job Description Role Overview: We are looking for a motivated Electrical or Computer Engineering intern to join our team, focusing on the evaluation and validation of next-generation Distribution Management System (DMS) applications. In this role, you will play a key part in bridging the gap between innovative software development and real-world grid operations. You will evaluate new applications, ensure they meet industry deployment standards, identify technical defects, and help educate our user base. Key Responsibilities: Application Evaluation: Perform hands-on testing of new Distribution Management applications to assess their functionality, reliability, and integration capabilities within our existing power system environments. Test Development: Design and build comprehensive test cases to validate application performance, edge cases, and user requirements, ensuring all new features meet rigorous quality standards. Deployment Feasibility: Analyze software requirements to determine if new applications can be deployed using standard industry tooling, specifically leveraging GitOps principles and ArgoCD for automated deployments within Linux-based environments . Quality Assurance & Debugging: Actively "stress test" new products by identifying, documenting, and tracking bugs. You will work closely with development teams to verify fixes and ensure a seamless end-user experience. Technical Documentation: Translate complex software features into user-friendly training materials, including technical guides, how-to videos, and internal knowledge-base articles to assist grid operators and engineers. jobs.body: Job Description The Role: This internship exposes qualified candidates to creative careers at General Motors and helps identify talent for direct positions in creative digital sculpting at Design. The individual will gain an understanding of the aesthetic judgments, technology, production methods, program timelines, and materials used in automotive digital sculpting. The role also provides opportunities to collaborate on innovation challenges, interact with industry leaders, attend cross-functional networking events, and participate in community service activities. What You’ll Do: • Work collaboratively with Design, Sculpting, and Engineering to interpret sketches and develop a digital model of a future automotive theme using established and emerging digital-sculpting best practices and techniques. • Present finished models to Design and Sculpting leadership at midterm and final show events. • Support general sculpting assignments within the studio environment. Please note, you must submit a portfolio to be considered for this position – see instructions below. jobs.title: Manufacturing Engineering Co-op (May - December 2027)
jobs.location: Anoka, Minnesota, USA, United States of America
jobs.body: Graco manufactures and markets premium equipment to move, measure, control, dispense and spray a wide variety of fluid and powder materials. What does that mean? Well, we pump peanut butter into your jar, and the oil in your car. We glue the soles of your shoes, the glass in your windows and the screen on your phone. We spray the finish on your vehicle, coatings on your pills, the paint on your house and texture on your walls. Graco is part of your daily life. The Graco Intern Program offers more than just work experience—it’s a chance to make an impact. As an intern, you’ll take on projects that matter to the business, contribute to initiatives that drive progress, and develop skills that prepare you for what’s ahead. Throughout the program, you’ll expand your industry knowledge, collaborate with professionals who are passionate about doing things the right way, and experience a culture that thrives on new ideas and continual growth. You’ll also take part in events designed to support both your learning and personal development. The program concludes with a final presentation where you’ll showcase your achievements and the difference you’ve made. Job Purpose: To support the Strategic Business Unit and the Manufacturing Cell and apply coursework to real-world applications as a Manufacturing Engineer Intern. Position involves providing ideas, inputs and analysis as a project team member. What You Will Do at Graco Provide general production support for machining and/or assembly areas by participating in hands-on troubleshooting issues and providing technical assistance Assist in evaluating the need for machine and/or assembly area upgrades Participate in capital equipment justification as needed Review and analyze standards and operational layouts to suggest improvements Assist in the selection and implementation of tooling and fixtures for machining and/or assembly jobs Participate in cost of quality improvements, root cause analysis and corrective action React to changing priorities in a timely manner Report man-hour estimates What You Will Bring to Graco Currently enrolled and pursing a Bachelor’s Degree in Mechanical or Industrial Engineering or comparable Engineering program Minimum GPA of 3.0 on a 4.0 scale Strong written, verbal, and interpersonal communication skills Ability to work independently and as an effective team member Mechanical aptitude and desire for hands on work Accelerators Experience with CAD software such as AutoCAD Experience with 3D printers Applicants must be legally authorized to work in the United States. This role is not eligible for immigration sponsorship now or in the future (e.g., H-1B, TN, F-1 OPT). At Graco, you truly make a difference. Your unique talents contribute to our organizational growth and future. Not only do you make a difference, but Graco’s culture empowers employees to create their own career path. Whether you choose to advance within your current department or explore new opportunities in different divisions, you have the ability to build your future. Our managers are here to provide support and guidance as you continue to grow within your career. Graco has excellent opportunities available to individuals who want to be part of a fast-moving, growing company that is committed to quality, innovation and solving fluid handling problems for our customers. Graco is proud to be named a Best Place to Work by Fortune Magazine in 2016, 2018, 2019, 2021 & 2022. Graco offers attractive compensation, benefits and career development opportunities. Graco’s comprehensive benefits include medical, dental, stock purchase plan, 401(k), tuition reimbursement and more. Our company uses E-Verify to confirm the employment and eligibility of all newly hired employees. To learn more about E-Verify, including your rights and responsibilities, please visit www.dhs.gov/E-Verify . The base pay range for this position is listed below, exclusive of fringe benefits or other compensation. If you are hired, your final base hourly rate will be determined based on factors such as geographic location, skills, competencies, education, and/or experience. In addition to those factors, we will also consider internal equity of our current employees. Please keep in mind that the range provided is the full base salary range for the role. Hiring at or near the maximum of the range would not be typical to allow for future and continued salary growth. $21.00 - $28.00

Profession (Job Category): Administration & Facilities Job Schedule: Full time Work Arrangement: Hybrid About Us A career at Hitachi Rail will help create a legacy. With operations in every corner of the world, our work goes to the cutting-edge of digital transformation and technology. From the multi-cultural strength of our global organisation to the sustainable and innovative ways we work to bring people together, there’s something for everyone to get stuck into. And that’s where you come in. Job Description: Hitachi Rail is looking for an enthusiastic, self-motivated Intern – Network Engineering for Summer 2027. The position is based in Pittsburgh, PA. At Hitachi Rail , we’re creating a legacy that spans the globe — and we want YOU to be part of it. What’s in it for you? ✅Real-world projects with top industry talent ✅Paid internship ✅Mentorship and intern events ✅A chance to build your career with a global leader driving digital transformation and innovation Hitachi Rail provides signaling systems for metros and light rail systems. Our solutions provide efficient, safe and green transportation solutions for people around the world. This position offers you the opportunity to immerse yourself in the dynamic world of urban transit. You will gain hands-on experience while providing valuable support to your team. By working in this role, you will gain insight into the realm of mobility, significantly enhancing your understanding of Hitachi’s missions and impact. We’re looking for eligible students to join Hitachi Rail! Hiring for May 2027 through August 2027. Accountabilities: Work with engineering, quality, procurement, and manufacturing leadership to establish component engineering processes. Implement risk management strategies to address obsolescence and proactively identify and address future obsolescence. Review design BOMs, conduct part lifecycle analysis and collaborate with engineering & research & development to develop strategies and alternative technical solution to minimize supply chain risk. Monitor / manage component obsolescence per internal processes utilizing IT tools (SAP/Teamcenter/ r BOM REVIEW, IHS, PDM system). jobs.body: This undergraduate internship is a full-time position Summer-Fall 2027 (May or June through December) on site in Rochester, Minnesota. jobs.body: With its five product lines of compact hydraulics Bosch Rexroth Oil Control SpA , with factories in the province of Modena and Reggio Emilia and over 1,300 employees, has been producing and marketing compact hydraulic components for multiple applications for over 40 years, from aerial platforms to cranes, earth-moving machinery, agricultural machinery, industrial applications. What characterizes Bosch Rexroth Oil Control S.p.A. is the ability to study customized solutions in relation to each specific customer requirement. For this reason, the products of Bosch Rexroth Oil Control S.p.A. they are synonymous with quality and represent a guarantee for the global market. In industrial hydraulics, Bosch Rexroth is actively shaping the transition from conventional to intelligent and connected hydraulics. This opens up enormous potential for the easy and economical integration of machines and systems into modern industrial environments. Our R&D department based in Nonantola (MO) is a center of global competence for Compact Hydraulic products. You will gain hands-on experience at the intersection of industrial automation, artificial intelligence, and manufacturing processes . A key focus of your internship will be supporting the implementation of AI-enabled industrial vision systems for the automatic monitoring of assembly and kitting processes, contributing to the development and training of image recognition models in a real manufacturing environment. What you will do & learn Manufacturing Process Analysis: Analyze assembly and kitting processes to identify critical features to be monitored and the main potential sources of errors. Industrial Vision Systems: Support the development and implementation of industrial vision solutions aimed at automatically verifying the correct composition of kits and the execution of assembly operations. AI & Image Recognition: Contribute to the definition, training, and validation of image recognition models for component counting and anomaly detection. Data Analysis & Performance Monitoring: Analyze results and monitor key performance indicators related to quality, efficiency, and scrap reduction, supporting the evaluation of the implemented solutions. Technical Documentation & Standardization: Support the preparation of technical documentation and the definition of operational standards required for the industrialization of the solution. Assigned Project You will contribute to a project focused on the implementation and industrialization of an AI-enabled vision system for assembly and kitting process control . In particular, you will: Analyze current assembly and kitting processes and identify the critical features and potential errors to be detected; Support the development and configuration of an industrial vision system for automated process monitoring; Contribute to the collection and preparation of image data for AI model training and validation; Support the training and validation of image recognition models for component counting and anomaly detection; Evaluate the performance of the developed solution through dedicated quality and process KPIs; Collaborate with Production, Quality, and Manufacturing Engineering to integrate the solution into existing processes; Contribute to the definition of technical documentation and operating standards to support the industrialization of the solution. What distinguishes you? Education: Currently pursuing a Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Automation Engineering, Mechatronics Engineering, Computer Engineering, Electronic Engineering, Industrial Engineering, or a related technical field; Languages: fluent in Italian and English; Others: Basic knowledge of programming and data analysis; familiarity with Python, computer vision, artificial intelligence, or machine learning would be considered a plus; strong interest in artificial intelligence, computer vision, industrial automation, and Industry 4.0 applications; If you feel confident in the position don't hesitate to apply take a look! www.bosch.com www.boschrexroth.com Bosch is proud to be an Equal Opportunity Employer. jobs.title: 2027 Summer Industrial Hygienist & Ergonomist Intern
jobs.location: Berthoud, Colorado
jobs.body: The future of aerospace and defense starts here. Ursa Major was founded to revolutionize how America and its allies access and apply high-performance propulsion, from hypersonics to solid rocket motors, satellite maneuvering and launch. We design and deliver propulsion and defense systems that solve the most urgent and critical national security demands. Position Summary The Industrial Hygienist & Ergonomist intern will work closely with the environmental, health, and safety team by identifying, evaluating, and controlling workplace health and comfort risks, with a focus on chemical, physical, and biological exposures as well as ergonomic risk factors for new processes associated with the Galeton expansion project. This role partners with operations, facilities, HR, and safety teams to develop and implement programs that prevent occupational illness and injury, improve employee well ‑ being, and support regulatory compliance. Key Responsibilities Industrial Hygiene Conduct qualitative and quantitative exposure assessments for chemical, physical (noise, radiation, temperature), and biological hazards in production, laboratory, office, and field environments. Develop and execute industrial hygiene sampling plans using appropriate equipment (e.g., air sampling pumps, dosimeters, direct ‑ reading instruments). Analyze sampling data, interpret results against regulatory and consensus standards (e.g., OSHA PELs, ACGIH TLVs), and recommend control measures. Recommend engineering, administrative, and personal protective equipment (PPE) controls to reduce exposures. Maintain industrial hygiene records, reports, sampling logs, and calibration documentation. Support development and review of Safety Data Sheets (SDS) usage, chemical inventories, and hazard communication programs. Develop and deliver training related to industrial hygiene topics (e.g., respiratory protection, noise/hearing conservation, chemical hygiene). Ergonomics Conduct ergonomic assessments for manufacturing workstations, material handling tasks, laboratory setups, office environments, and remote workstations. Identify ergonomic risk factors (e.g., force, repetition, awkward postures, contact stress, vibration) using recognized assessment tools and methods. Recommend and help implement ergonomic design improvements, equipment, tools, and work practice changes. Collaborate with engineering and operations on the design and review of new processes, workstations, and tools to ensure ergonomic principles are integrated upfront. Support job task analysis and physical demand descriptions. Develop and deliver ergonomic training and awareness programs for employees and supervisors. Program Management & Collaboration Support the development, implementation, and continuous improvement of comprehensive Industrial Hygiene and Ergonomics programs. Work cross ‑ functionally with EHS, Operations, Engineering, Facilities, HR, and Occupational Health to align health and ergonomics initiatives with business objectives. Prepare clear, data ‑ driven reports and presentations for leadership, documenting findings, risk levels, and recommended actions. Qualifications Education Perusing a Bachelor’s degree in Industrial Hygiene, Occupational Health & Safety, Ergonomics, Environmental Health, Safety Engineering, or related field required. Technical Skills Knowledge of OSHA, NIOSH, ACGIH, ANSI and other applicable occupational health and safety standards. Ability to analyze data, interpret exposure results, and communicate risk clearly. Competent with standard office software (Excel, Word, PowerPoint) and EHS management systems. Competencies Strong analytical and problem ‑ solving skills with a practical, solutions ‑ oriented mindset. Ability to influence and collaborate at all levels of the organization. Clear written and verbal communication skills, including training and coaching. Detail ‑ oriented, organized, and able to manage multiple projects and priorities. Demonstrated commitment to health, safety, and continuous improvement. Working Conditions Combination of office and industrial/production environments. Regular presence on shop floors, laboratories, and field locations; use of appropriate PPE as required. May involve occasional lifting, standing, or working in varied postures during assessments. Occasional travel to other sites or facilities. Colorado law requires us to tell you the base compensation range of this role, which is $30.00/hour, determined by your education, experience, knowledge, skills, and abilities. jobs.body: Axiom Space is a human space exploration company, building era-defining space infrastructure and delivering technology-driven solutions that will empower civilization to transcend Earth. Today, guided by the vision of leading humanity's expansion off planet, Axiom Space is the principal provider of commercial human spaceflight services and developer of advanced spacesuits for the Moon and beyond. For more information about Axiom Space, visit www.axiomspace.com . Axiom Space fosters a work environment inclusive of all perspectives. Our mission-driven team is seeking a bold and dynamic Data Analyst Intern who is fueled by high accountability, execution horsepower, and driven to understand our world, science/technology, and life itself, for the benefit of all on Earth and beyond. The Digital Integration team builds and maintains the enterprise analytics environment that gives leadership and program teams visibility into KPIs across Finance, Operations, Supply Chain, and Engineering. This internship offers hands-on experience with a production analytics platform during an active modernization of our data pipelines. Reporting to the Manager of Digital Integration, you will work alongside our Data Analyst and Data Engineer on bounded projects with clear deliverables. jobs.title: Summer 2027 Internship - Architectural Engineering
jobs.location: Los Angeles, CA
jobs.body: About the company General Matter enriches uranium. We are designing, building, and operating the world’s lowest-cost enrichment services, here in the US. In the process, we are restoring America’s ability to produce nuclear fuel to power AI, advanced manufacturing and critical industries our country relies on to remain competitive. Fuel drives the cost of advanced reactor electricity production, and enrichment drives the cost of the fuel that advanced reactors consume. Reliable, low-cost enrichment is the catalyst for the nuclear Renaissance now under way. Our mission is to make nuclear not only the cleanest and safest source of baseload power, but also the most affordable. We believe abundant nuclear energy will lead to a post-scarcity society. We were incubated inside Founders Fund, like Anduril and Palantir before us, and are backed by over a dozen of the world's top venture capital firms. Our lean, world-class team of engineers and operators is applying a first-principles approach to solving the problem of nuclear fuel production. We are a mission-driven company with a culture of urgency, accountability, and transparency. Help us build a high-energy society by making the cleanest, safest form of baseload energy the most affordable. About the Role General Matter is seeking an Architectural Engineering Intern to join our Buildings team in Los Angeles. This role offers a unique opportunity to work alongside experienced engineers and project teams delivering large-scale industrial and nuclear infrastructure projects, including our flagship uranium enrichment facility. You will gain hands-on experience supporting integrated building systems design, multidisciplinary coordination, and construction planning for complex facilities. This role is ideal for a student or graduate who enjoys the intersection of structural, mechanical, and architectural disciplines within the AEC industry. What You’ll Do Support facility structural and mechanical design work for large-scale industrial infrastructure projects. Assist with the preparation of integrated structural and mechanical drawings and technical documentation. Collaborate closely with architectural, civil, electrical, and construction teams to ensure holistic building performance. Help coordinate complex structural and mechanical layouts within the building envelope to optimize space and functionality. Participate in engineering design reviews and project coordination meetings to track progress and resolve technical interface issues. Support high-fidelity BIM modeling using Revit to integrate multidisciplinary designs. Assist engineering teams with constructability reviews and design updates to streamline the transition from theory to field. Help address field design questions and Requests for Information (RFIs) during the construction phase when applicable. What You’ll Bring Current enrollment (Junior or Senior standing) or recent completion of a Bachelor’s degree in Architectural Engineering. Strong interest in industrial infrastructure, energy, or large-scale, high-complexity construction projects. Proficiency in Revit is required; experience with AutoCAD or other BIM/rendering tools is a plus. A multidisciplinary mindset with a foundational understanding of how structural and mechanical systems interact within a facility. Strong problem-solving, collaboration, and communication skills tailored for a fast-paced engineering environment. Interest and/or experience in visual programming (Dynamo, Grasshopper) or coding (Python) to support workflow automation. Bonus Qualifications Internship or academic project experience related to industrial building design or heavy construction. Exposure to facility planning for infrastructure, advanced manufacturing, or power-intensive sites. Interest in nuclear energy, sustainable industrial design, or critical infrastructure resilience. Familiarity with building codes and standards relevant to large-scale facility design. Additional Requirements Ability to work extended hours and weekends as necessary. Equal Opportunity Employer General Matter is an Equal Opportunity Employer; employment with General Matter is governed on the basis of merit, competence and qualifications and will not be influenced in any manner by race, color, religion, gender, national origin/ethnicity, veteran status, disability status, age, sexual orientation, gender identity, marital status, mental or physical disability or any other legally protected status. Compensation and Benefits The hourly pay range for this internship is $28–$40 per hour, depending on the candidate’s current standing in school (i.e. sophomore, senior). Interns will receive a monthly housing stipend and are eligible for overtime pay. Please note that the stated hourly range is an estimate and may be adjusted based on market conditions, business needs, or other factors.

jobs.body: Overview Keysight is at the forefront of technology innovation, delivering breakthroughs and trusted insights in electronic design, simulation, prototyping, test, manufacturing, and optimization. Our ~16,800 employees create world-class solutions in communications, 5G, automotive, energy, quantum, aerospace, defense, and semiconductor markets for customers in over 100 countries. Learn more about what we do. Our award-winning culture embraces a bold vision of where technology can take us and a passion for tackling challenging problems with industry-first solutions. We believe that when people feel a sense of belonging, they can be more creative, innovative, and thrive at all points in their careers. The High Frequency Technology Center (HFTC) in Santa Rosa, CA is seeking an intern to join our Industrial Engineering team. This role offers hands-on experience in a high-frequency semiconductor manufacturing environment and the opportunity to learn the principles behind running an efficient, healthy factory. Working alongside industrial engineers, automation engineers, process engineers, operations personnel, and maintenance/equipment engineering teams, you will help drive major process improvement and capacity expansion efforts. You will take a deep, hands-on dive into specific manufacturing areas — gathering data and observations to own and drive Lean process improvements — and work with the team to develop and improve models and simulations of the factory to increase throughput, reduce turn-around-time, and improve efficiency. This is a full-time, onsite summer internship in Santa Rosa, CA, with a strong possibility of extension for up to a year. We believe internships should be more than a summer job. You will be assigned a defined project with clear objectives, ownership, and measurable outcomes, and work closely with experienced engineers throughout. Our goal is that you finish with a tangible improvement delivered to the organization — a meaningful accomplishment you can put on a resume, discuss in future interviews, and build a career on. We encourage curiosity, welcome questions, and support continuous learning. exposure to Power BI Prior experience in a manufacturing or production environment Exposure to Lean, Six Sigma, or continuous improvement methodology Personal, academic, or internship projects that demonstrate initiative and technical curiosity Engineering Mindset Successful candidates typically demonstrate curiosity and a willingness to learn, attention to detail, strong time management, the ability to collaborate with both technical and non-technical stakeholders, and a desire to understand the people and processes behind a problem — not just its technical requirements. jobs.title: Quality Engineer Intern
jobs.location: Roseville, California
jobs.body: Overview Keysight is a mission-critical design enablement partner for organizations solving the world’s most complex engineering challenges. With deep engineering expertise and leading design, emulation, and test solutions, our ~16,800 employees help customers in over 100 countries accelerate innovation across communications, automotive, energy, quantum, aerospace and defense, semiconductor, and artificial intelligence markets. Learn more about what we do. At Keysight, people come together to explore new ideas, challenge what's possible, and advance the technologies defining the future. Here, you'll find opportunities to do your best work, take your career further, and thrive in an award-winning culture. Learn more about our benefits. Responsibilities The KGSO Quality Engineering Intern will support strategic FY27 initiatives focused on operational planning, capacity analysis, equipment categorization, and test station standardization. This position will play an important role in enabling data-driven decision making for capacity planning while supporting the development of standardized Calibration and Adjust Test Station Bill of Materials (BOMs) to advance KGSO's Global Operations. This part-time position will work closely with engineering, operations, and service teams to analyze shipment data, improve equipment classification accuracy, and establish foundational engineering documentation supporting test station harmonization across KGSO. RTF Data Analysis & Capacity Planning Analyze transshipment data to identify trends, drivers, and operational impacts. Develop data visualizations, dashboards, and reports supporting KGSO capacity and capability planning. Identify opportunities to improve operational efficiency through data-driven recommendations. Support leadership reviews by preparing summarized findings and performance metrics. Product Categorization & Equipment Analysis Perform technical review and categorization of currently uncategorized products. Validate product classifications using engineering documentation, product specifications, and business requirements. Improve equipment master data quality to support forecasting, planning, and operational reporting. Collaborate with cross-functional teams to standardize categorization methodologies. Harmonized Test Station Support Research existing test stations across KGSO sites. Document station configurations, components, and capabilities. Develop and maintain Measurement & Test Equipment (M&TE) BOMs for currently undefined stations. Assist in creating standardized test station definitions supporting global harmonization initiatives. Support engineering teams in identifying common equipment and infrastructure requirements across service centers. Qualifications Education Qualifications Pursuing a Bachelor's in: Electrical Engineering Mechanical Engineering Industrial Engineering Systems Engineering Data Analytics Computer Engineering Related technical discipline Technical Qualifications Strong analytical and problem-solving skills. jobs.body: The Bosch Group has more than 400 000 employees around the world, present in 60 countries, and we are proud to impact people’s lives and to work towards a more sustainable future. In the city of Aveiro, Bosch has one of its biggest production sites for Bosch Home Comfort division, as well as a Research and Development Center for new and improved heating solutions for the residential segment. With more than 1400 employees, focused on innovation, sustainability and collaboration, Bosch Aveiro joins together experts in diverse areas, from mechanical engineering to connectivity and software solutions, as well as industrialization and quality. At Bosch, we shape the future by inventing high-quality technologies and services that spark enthusiasm and enrich people’s lives. What distinguishes you: Academic Degree in Mechanical Engineering, Energy Engineering or similar technical field; Knowledge in turbomachinery and aerodynamics and strong interest in thermal systems, refrigeration or sustainable technologies; Good communication skills in Portuguese and English; Ability to manage multiple priorities and technical topics simultaneously; Innovative mindset with willingness to challenge and improve existing solutions. jobs.title: Manufacturing Engineering Intern Summer 2027
jobs.location: Wallops Island, VA
jobs.body: ABOUT ROCKET LAB Rocket Lab is the end-to-end space company building rockets, spacecraft, and critical subsystems that keep the world connected, protected, expand humanity’s reach to the Moon, Mars, and beyond. We move fast, build real hardware for meaningful missions, and make the impossible routine. Come shape the future with us. As a Manufacturing Engineering Intern based at Rocket Lab’s site in Wallops Island, Virginia, you will have the opportunity to support the developing processes, as well as identifying and design build of necessary equipment for receipt and final integration and launch of the Neutron Launch Vehicle. You’ll work closely the Neutron Vehicle Integration Engineer and other key team members who are responsible for the integration, test and launch of the Neutron launch vehicle. WHAT YOU’LL GET TO DO As an intern, you will work closely with your mentor and other employees within the department to apply your knowledge and grow your skills both technically and professionally Work with a fast-paced group of professionals to apply engineering and industry concepts to solve real challenges Attend frequent 1:1’s with mentors and supervisors to facilitate success and learning while providing progress updates Enjoy tech talks and network with other interns and employees through social and professional events YOU’LL BRING THESE QUALIFICATIONS Ideal candidates will thrive in ambiguity and are excited to work in small, high-performing teams that are focused on continued learning and growth. Success in this position will be measured by the knowledge and experience you bring to the role, your ability to lead development projects without supervision, and your ability to successfully collaborate across teams to deliver results. Must be enrolled in a bachelor’s degree program in an engineering, physics or math discipline and have at least one semester of school remaining post internship GPA of 3.0 or above 3+ months of applied engineering experience (internship, laboratory, and personal/team project experience is applicable) THESE QUALIFICATIONS WOULD BE NICE TO HAVE GPA of 3.5 or above 6+ months of applied engineering experience (internship, laboratory, and personal/team project experience is applicable) Basic coding proficiency (Python, SQL, or automation scripting) Solid Modelling experience Computer-aided design and manufacturing (CAD/CAM) experience Strong interest in identifying and driving process improvement opportunities ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS Able to work full-time, on-site for a minimum of 12 consecutive weeks beginning May or June 2027 COMPENSATION AND OTHER BENEFITS Pay Range MD: $25.00 USD Hourly You may be eligible for a stipend to subsidize relocation costs WHAT TO EXPECT We’re on a mission to unlock the potential of space to improve life on Earth, but that’s not an easy task. It takes hard work, determination, relentless innovation, teamwork, grit, and an unwavering commitment to achieving what others often deem impossible. Our people out-think, out-work, and out-pace. We pride ourselves on having each other’s backs, checking our egos at the door, and rolling up our sleeves on all tasks big and small. We thrive under pressure, work to tight deadlines, and our focus is always on how we can deliver, rather than dwelling on the challenges that stand in the way. Important information: FOR CANDIDATES SEEKING TO WORK IN US OFFICES ONLY: To conform to U.S. Government space technology export regulations, including the International Traffic in Arms Regulations (ITAR), Rocket Lab Employees must be a U.S. citizen, lawful U.S. permanent resident (i.e., current Green Card holder), or lawfully admitted into the U.S. as a refugee or granted asylum, or be eligible to obtain the required authorizations from the U.S. Department of State and/or the U.S. Department of Commerce, as applicable. Learn more about ITAR here . Rocket Lab provides equal employment opportunities to all employees and applicants for employment and prohibits discrimination and harassment of any type without regard to race, color, religion, age, sex, national origin, disability status, genetics, protected veteran status, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, or any other characteristic protected by federal, state, or local laws. This policy applies to all terms and conditions of employment at Rocket Lab, including recruiting, hiring, placement, promotion, termination, layoff, recall, transfer, leaves of absence, compensation, and training. Applicants requiring a reasonable accommodation for the application/interview process for a job in the United States should contact Giulia Johnson at g.biow@rocketlabusa.com. This dedicated resource is intended solely to assist job seekers with disabilities whose disability prevents them from being able to apply/interview. Only messages left for this purpose will be considered. A response to your request may take up to two business days. FOR CANDIDATES SEEKING TO WORK IN NEW ZEALAND OFFICES ONLY: For security reasons, background checks will be undertaken prior to any employment offers being made to an applicant. These checks will include nationality checks as it is a requirement of this position that you be eligible to access equipment and data regulated by the United States' International Traffic in Arms Regulations. Under these Regulations, you may be ineligible for this role if you do not hold citizenship of Australia, Japan, New Zealand, Switzerland, the European Union, or a country that is part of NATO, or if you hold ineligible dual citizenship or nationality. jobs.title: Summer Internship - Health Physics & Radiation Safety
jobs.location: Knoxville, TN
jobs.body: Join us in our mission to commercialize fusion energy ⚡️ About Type One Energy Type One Energy Group is mission-driven to provide sustainable, affordable fusion power to the world. Established in 2019 and venture-backed in 2023, the company is led by a team of globally recognized fusion scientists with a strong track record of building state-of-the-art stellarator fusion machines, together with veteran business leaders experienced in scaling companies and commercializing energy technologies. If you are searching for the best new ideas and share our vision, join us as a Radiation Safety Intern. This is what you need to know: Location: Knoxville, TN Salary: $25-$30/hour, 40 hours per week Contract: 12-week internship, Summer 2027 (May 24th start date) Reporting to: Sr. Radiation Safety Officer Your role in the mission: Type One Energy is seeking a Radiation Safety Intern to support regulatory affairs and radiation safety activities related to fusion facility development, licensing, construction preparation, and radiation protection program implementation. This internship provides hands-on experience across radiation safety, regulatory compliance, environmental requirements, and fusion energy development while contributing to active projects and organizational initiatives. The position is intended to provide practical experience supporting the deployment of commercial fusion energy facilities and the development of future radiation protection and regulatory professionals. Key responsibilities could include: Assist with the development and implementation of radiation safety and radiation protection programs. Support regulatory research, licensing, permitting, radiological inventory management, documentation, and compliance tracking. Support radiation safety and regulatory activities associated with fusion development initiatives. Collaborate with Regulatory Affairs, Radiation Safety, engineering, and project teams on activities supporting facility development, licensing, and construction preparation. Perform other related projects and assignments that provide exposure to health physics, regulatory affairs, and the development of fusion energy facilities. What you'll need : Currently pursuing a degree in Health Physics, Nuclear Engineering, Radiological Sciences, Environmental Science, Environmental Engineering, or a related STEM discipline. Proficiency with Microsoft Office Suite, including Excel, Word, PowerPoint, Teams, Outlook, and SharePoint. Interest in radiation safety, health physics, regulatory affairs, environmental compliance, or fusion energy. Ability to work collaboratively across technical and multidisciplinary teams. Strong organizational, communication, research, and analytical skills. jobs.body: > At BWX Technologies, Inc. (NYSE: BWXT), we are People Strong, Innovation Driven. Ability to communicate technical concepts clearly to non-technical stakeholders. Intellectual curiosity and willingness to learn new technologies and business processes. Ability to work independently while collaborating effectively across business and technical teams. Strong attention to detail when working with financial, commercial, contractual, or supplier information. Strong time-management skills and ability to deliver against defined project milestones. jobs.title: Mechanical Engineering - Summer 2027 Intern (US Person Required)
jobs.location: United States
jobs.body: Honeywell Technologies: Build What Matters At Honeywell Technologies, you can work on technology that helps make the world safer, smarter, and more efficient. We are a global automation company focused on helping customers run critical operations safely, reliably, and efficiently, with about $17B in 2025 sales, 54,000 employees, roughly 600 sites, and headquarters in Charlotte, NC. Work on practical innovation. Honeywell Technologies is moving from automation toward autonomy by combining AI, controls, connected data, and domain expertise to help assets work harder, people work smarter, and processes run more efficiently. Grow with purpose. At Honeywell Technologies, you can grow your career and network by contributing to the company’s success. Join a customer obsessed culture built on respect, collaboration, diverse perspectives, continuous learning, individual well-being, and celebrating achievement. Be part of a culture that values people. Our people are at the heart of what we do, with an emphasis on impact, representing Honeywell with pride, bringing diverse perspectives, and solving problems with curiosity and resilience. Shape the future by making what matters better. ABOUT THE ROLE: As a Mechanical Engineering Intern here at Honeywell Technologies, you will have the opportunity to gain hands-on experience and contribute to cutting-edge projects in the field of mechanical engineering. You will work closely with our team of experienced engineers and professionals, learning from their expertise and applying your knowledge to real-world challenges. This internship will provide you with valuable insights into the industry and help you develop essential skills for your future career in mechanical engineering. In this role, you will have the opportunity to: Assist in the design and development of mechanical systems, components, and assemblies Conduct research and analysis to support engineering projects Collaborate with cross-functional teams to solve technical problems and optimize designs Participate in testing and validation activities Gain exposure to industry-standard tools and software Location: This position is available in multiple locations across the United States. The exact worksite location will be selected based on business requirements and the candidate’s relevant experience and qualifications. The hourly base range for this position is $24.00/hr - $45.00/hr. Please note that this salary information serves as a general guideline. Honeywell considers various factors when extending an offer, including but not limited to the scope and responsibilities of the position, the candidate's work experience, education and training, key skills, as well as market and business considerations. MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS: Currently pursuing a bachelor's degree (or higher) from an accredited college or university in Mechanical Engineering or similar field. Must graduate December 2027 or later Must continue enrollment in degree program upon completion of the internship Validated academic excellence (3.0 GPA and higher) Due to compliance with U.S. export control laws and regulations, candidate must be a U.S. Person, which is defined as, a U.S. citizen, a U.S. permanent resident, or have protected status in the U.S. under asylum or refugee status Honeywell Technologies is currently unable to consider applicants who would require current or future sponsorship for employment authorization for this position. Candidates must be authorized to legally work in the United States without current or future sponsorship requirements. WE VALUE: Previous internship or project experience in mechanical engineering Knowledge of industry standards and best practices Familiarity with product testing and validation processes Understanding of materials and manufacturing processes Interning at Honeywell Technologies provides hands-on experience with cutting-edge technologies, professional development, and mentorship within a global organization. Interns will receive relocation benefits and short-term housing if they are 50 miles or more from their assigned work location (excluding Puerto Rico and Canada). The application period for the intern position is estimated to be through the end of March 2027; however, this may be shortened or extended depending on business needs and the availability of qualified candidates. #HoneywellURNAM

jobs.body: As an EMC Engineering Intern , your core responsibility will be to support electromagnetic compatibility (EMC) Engineering workflows. You will collaborate closely with RF, Avionics, Mechanical, and Software Engineers to test, troubleshoot and report findings of electromagnetic performance on various products. You will have the unique opportunity to contribute on various spacecraft components and system level development. *This internship is 12 weeks long from May/June through August/September 2027 Contribute to optimization of in-house EMC automation. Drive semi-anechoic chamber bringup and inter-chamber repeatability. Conduct analysis and simulation of spacecraft components and systems for phenomen such as radiated emissions, surface charging, and performance in radiation. Conduct component level and system level EMC testing per MIL-STD 461 & MIL-STD-464 Drive test plans, test reports, and troubleshooting efforts with diverse engineering groups across multiple satellite designs. Operate and integrate common EMC lab related equipment including spectrum analyzers, signal generators, RF amplifiers, scopes, etc. Currently enrolled in a bachelor’s or master's program for Electrical Engineering, Physics, or related area. Understanding of circuit theory and EM fundamentals concepts. Familiarity working hands-on in a lab with RF test equipment. Ability to adapt to a dynamic and fast paced environment. Understanding of radiated, conducted, and transient testing. Experience with Python scripting. Understanding of RF fundamentals such as antenna principles, link budgets, desense, S-parameters, transmission line theory, amplifiers, etc. Experience with EMC Design Guidelines and Best Practices. Experience with simulation tools such as EMC Plus, ADS, CST, HFSS, etc. Additional Requirements: Willing and able to work on-site in Redondo Beach, CA for the duration of the internship This role may require overtime hours; interns are eligible for overtime pay. Part sample management, test setups, environmental chamber operation, sample analysis prep, logging, data acquisition and reporting. • Work with electronic module test stands to ensure correct setups and execution of active testing on modules. • Perform diagnostics, repair and maintenance of electronic test stands as well as harness build, debug and repair. • Work with other department associates to ensure full proxy/backup of all key responsibilities. Ability to manage priorities and support multi-tasking activities, self-driven to seek out additional work during slower periods. • Support parts storage practices, labeling and Fixtures organization. PHYSICAL DEMANDS / WORK ENVIRONMENT: • Normal amount of sitting or standing, average mobility to move around an office environment, able to conduct normal amount of work at a computer. • In case necessary deliver parts to external labs and support testing at lab remote locations.
