jobs.title: Project Management Intern
jobs.location: Arlington, VA, United States of America; Washington, DC; Camp Springs, MD
jobs.body: Are you looking to bridge your classroom coursework in computer science, systems administration, or cybersecurity with real-world national defense technology? At Leidos, we don’t just offer internships - we offer career acceleration. Join Leidos’ mission-focused Air Force National Capital Region (AFNCR) IT Services team supporting senior defense leaders and national-level command functions. It's a fast-paced, high-stakes environment where the work directly supports national defense operations where uptime is mission-essential. We’re seeking a motivated Project Management Intern to work directly with experienced Project Managers, technical teams, and functional staff in executing enterprise-level Air Force IT initiatives. Operate at a scale and with mission relevance second to none. As an intern, you will learn how to plan and manage projects across various IT environments and learn how mission-critical servers, client workstations, and secure networks are deployed, patched, monitored, and maintained in an enterprise military environment. Primary Responsibilities: Assist in developing project plans, including timelines, budgets, and resource allocation, to ensure successful project completion. Coordinate meetings, including scheduling, sending reminders, and preparing meeting agendas to facilitate effective communication among project team members. Track project progress by updating project management software and tools, ensuring milestones are met on schedule. Compile and organize project documentation, ensuring all necessary materials are accessible for team members and stakeholders. Conduct risk assessments for projects to identify potential issues and develop mitigation strategies. Support the project manager in liaising with external vendors and stakeholders to maintain communication and project alignment. Analyze project data to prepare reports on project status, performance, and outcomes for internal review and stakeholder updates. Participate in quality assurance processes by reviewing project deliverables and providing feedback to ensure they meet specified standards and requirements. Monitors and tracks project dependencies. Create a work breakdown structure that defines all activities required for the project deliverables. Actively monitor, track, and manage project tasks, timelines, attainment of established milestones and overall quality of project activities and deliverables. Required Qualifications: Currently enrolled in an accredited undergraduate program pursuing or recently completed a degree in Business Administration, Project Management, or IT, or a closely related field. Must be in good academic standing (Rising Sophomores, Juniors, or Seniors considered). U.S. Citizenship is required. Must have the ability to obtain and maintain a Department of Defense (DoD) Secret security clearance (or possess an active clearance). Leidos will guide you through this process. Strong written and verbal communication skills. Proficiency in Microsoft Office applications (PowerPoint, Excel, Word, Outlook/Teams). High organizational ability, attention to detail, and analytical skills. Ability to work independently and collaboratively in a fast-paced environment. Preferred Qualifications: Familiarity with Agile, Scrum, or Waterfall concepts and methodologies. Experience with Microsoft Project, SharePoint, or Planner. Knowledge of risk management, requirements gathering, scheduling, and budgeting. Prior internship or experience in IT, engineering, defense, or customer-support environments. You’ll thrive in this role if you are Curious and adaptive—comfortable learning new domains and asking good questions Organized and self-directed, while still highly collaborative Confident communicating your needs and working as an active team member Work location and schedule National Capital Region (Pentagon / Joint Base Andrews / Joint Base Anacostia-Bolling) FT or PT, core business hours 8am-4pm, 10-12 week internship, target start early June 2027 Limited public transportation options Why Leidos? What This Internship Offers You Real-World Impact: Hands-on exposure to mission-critical systems that support top senior leaders and joint military defense operations. Direct Mentorship: Daily guidance from senior project manager who are invested in your technical growth and professional development. Defense Tech Foundation: Clear pathways toward post-graduation full-time employment, government security clearance attainment, and DoD 8140 compliance. Skill Advancement: Transform academic theory into tangible experience spanning risk and issue management, collaboration, methodology exposure, and administrative tasks. If you're looking for comfort, keep scrolling. At Leidos, we outthink, outbuild, and outpace the status quo — because the mission demands it. We're not hiring followers. We're recruiting the ones who disrupt, provoke, and refuse to fail. Step 10 is ancient history. We're already at step 30 — and moving faster than anyone else dares. Pay Range: Pay Range $48,100.00 - $86,950.00 The Leidos pay range for this job level is a general guideline only and not a guarantee of compensation or salary. Additional factors considered in extending an offer include (but are not limited to) responsibilities of the job, education, experience, knowledge, skills, and abilities, as well as internal equity, alignment with market data, applicable bargaining agreement (if any), or other law.

jobs.body: Who we are With its A.I.-powered robotic technology platform, Symbotic is changing the way consumer goods move through the supply chain. The team helps ensure our robotic material handling systems operate safely and efficiently after go-live, supporting system uptime, operational excellence, and customer success throughout the lifecycle of an installation. Assist with mechanical and service-readiness projects for robotics and automation equipment. Work with Product Lifecycle Management data, including supporting accurate part and engineering information in Siemens Teamcenter. Mechanical aptitude and an interest in robotics, automation, equipment maintenance, or service engineering. Comfort working with technical systems and engineering data, with experience or exposure to PLM tools such as Teamcenter is a plus. Previous internship experience in warehouse or manufacturing settings is a plus Strong project execution and organizational skills with the ability to track details and communicate progress and results. Strong teamwork and communication skills with the ability to collaborate across engineering and service functions. Curiosity, initiative, and a willingness to learn directly from equipment, technical documentation, and experienced engineers. Our Environment Up to 20% of travel may be required. Applying next-gen technology, high-density storage and machine learning to solve today's complex distribution challenges, Symbotic enables companies to move goods with unmatched speed, agility, accuracy and efficiency. We are a global automation company focused on helping customers run critical operations safely, reliably, and efficiently, with about $17B in 2025 sales, 54,000 employees, roughly 600 sites, and headquarters in Charlotte, NC. Work on practical innovation. Honeywell Technologies is moving from automation toward autonomy by combining AI, controls, connected data, and domain expertise to help assets work harder, people work smarter, and processes run more efficiently. Grow with purpose. At Honeywell Technologies, you can grow your career and network by contributing to the company’s success. Join a customer obsessed culture built on respect, collaboration, diverse perspectives, continuous learning, individual well-being, and celebrating achievement. Be part of a culture that values people. Our people are at the heart of what we do, with an emphasis on impact, representing Honeywell with pride, bringing diverse perspectives, and solving problems with curiosity and resilience. Shape the future by making what matters better. ABOUT THE ROLE: As a Manufacturing/Industrial Engineering Intern here at Honeywell Technologies, you will have the opportunity to gain hands-on experience and contribute to various projects within our manufacturing and industrial engineering teams. You will work closely with experienced professionals and learn about optimizing manufacturing operations, improving process efficiency, and driving operational excellence. This internship will give you valuable insights into manufacturing and industrial engineering and help you develop essential skills for your future career. In this role, you will have the opportunity to: Assist in process improvement projects to enhance manufacturing efficiency and reduce waste Support the implementation of lean principles and continuous improvement methodologies Collaborate with cross-functional teams to optimize production processes and ensure product quality Gain exposure to various manufacturing technologies and equipment - Participate in data analysis and problem-solving activities Contribute to the development and maintenance of manufacturing documentation and standard operating procedures Location: This position is available in multiple locations across the United States. The exact worksite location will be selected based on business requirements and the candidate’s relevant experience and qualifications. The hourly base range for this position is $24.00/hr - $45.00/hr . Please note that this salary information serves as a general guideline. Honeywell considers various factors when extending an offer, including but not limited to the scope and responsibilities of the position, the candidate's work experience, education and training, key skills, as well as market and business considerations. MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS: Currently pursuing a bachelor's degree (or higher) from an accredited college or university in Manufacturing, Mechanical, Industrial, or similar field. Must graduate December 2027 or later Must continue enrollment in degree program upon completion of the internship Validated academic excellence (3.0 GPA and higher) Honeywell Technologies is currently unable to consider applicants who would require current or future sponsorship for employment authorization for this position. Candidates must be authorized to legally work in the United States without current or future sponsorship requirements. WE VALUE: Eagerness to learn and contribute to a dynamic team environment Industrial design talent Knowledge of lean principles and continuous improvement methodologies Eagerness to get involved in hands-on work Lean Manufacturing/Six Sigma experience is a plus Ability to easily and effectively balance many priorities and results-oriented demands Good interpersonal skills verbal and written Interning at Honeywell Technologies provides hands-on experience with cutting-edge technologies, professional development, and mentorship within a global organization. Interns will receive relocation benefits and short-term housing if they are 50 miles or more from their assigned work location (excluding Puerto Rico and Canada). The application period for the intern position is estimated to be through the end of March 2027; however, this may be shortened or extended depending on business needs and the availability of qualified candidates. #HoneywellURNAM

jobs.title: Summer Surgical Tech Intern
jobs.location: Rochester, MN, United States
jobs.body: The Summer Surgical Technologist student (Summer ST) provides delegated care to the surgical patient under the direct supervision of the registered nurse and in collaboration with the surgical team. The designated tasks are those which have been taught in the academic programs and/or orientation, and where the individual has demonstrated competence to a designated RN or CST. The functions are those limited by law to unlicensed personnel. The Summer ST performs primarily in the surgical scrub role preparing, selecting and maintaining equipment, instruments, and supplies. Summer ST Experience (June 7, 2027 - August 13, 2027) Rochester, MN site only Objectives Apply the principles of aseptic technique while in the sterile role. Further develop the practical skills required to work as a competent surgical technologist in the perioperative environment. Attain the professional skills of interpersonal communication with all patients and interdisciplinary health care team members. Applications must be received by December 31, 2026. Qualifications: Student must be in good standing in a CAAHEP or ABHES accredited surgical technology program, having completed a minimum of one-semester of surgical technology program curriculum. Student must possess basic knowledge and hands-on skills related to aseptic surgical techniques used in the preparation of instrumentation, supplies, and equipment for various surgical procedures. Basic Life Support (BLS) certification required from American Red Cross or American Heart Association and must not expire during internship. Candidates must be able to work from June 7, 2027, through August 13, 2027. Additional Qualifications : Strong preference for at least 100 clinical hours by internship start date. Adapts to unpredictable situations within the perioperative setting. Proven ability to communicate with a variety of people in a direct, empathetic, and articulate manner. Comprehensive understanding of surgical processes and procedures preferred. Candidates should not graduate prior to September 1, 2027. Applications must be received by December 31, 2026. Application Must Include: BLS/CPR certification RESUME. The resume (can be longer than one page) should highlight the following: educational background (degree and anticipated graduation date), cumulative GPA, paid employment history, awards/honors, and volunteer activities including community involvement, committee involvement, student nurse association, and/or professional organizations. TRANSCRIPTS are required. Transcripts can be unofficial or official scanned and uploaded to documents. Please make sure your name is somewhere on the document. SURGICAL INTEREST AREAS. Create a one-page word document numbered 1-7, using the below list of specialty options and place each area next to your preference number. Number 1 being your highest preference. Include any additional comments that would assist us in determining your preferred areas. TCGS Cardiac Vascular Thoracic Gynecology Ear, Nose, Throat Urology Transplant Please upload each document to your application. License or Certification : Basic Life Support (BLS) for Healthcare Providers certification required from American Red Cross or American Heart Association and must not expire during internship.

jobs.title: Summer III Student Nurse Internship
jobs.location: Rochester, MN, United States
jobs.body: The Mayo Clinic Rochester Summer III (SIII) Nursing Internship is one of the longest-running student nurse internships in the nation. Students from across the U.S. take part in the Summer III Program. The Summer III Student Nurse Internship is a skill based paid 10-week full time program, providing opportunities to gain valuable clinical skills and experience. Rochester, MN campus has over 60 specialties, two hospitals, 10 ICUs, and around 130 operating rooms. Summer III Nurse Interns will perform delegated tasks of direct and indirect patient care under the supervision of a registered nurse (RN) and in accordance with the Minnesota Board of Nursing. The designated tasks are those which have been taught in the academic programs and/or orientation, and where the individual has demonstrated competence. PLEASE READ THE FOLLOWING DETAILS CAREFULLY. INCOMPLETE/INELIGIBLE APPLICATIONS WILL NOT BE CONSIDERED. By June 7th, 2027, applicants must have successfully completed one of the following: 1. The Junior Year of an accredited baccalaureate nursing program, as recognized by the Accreditation Commission for Education in Nursing (ACEN) or Commission on Collegiate Nursing Education (CCNE). 2. Three semesters of an accredited associate degree nursing program. Candidates must NOT be eligible for the NCLEX during the program. Candidates must have an anticipated RN graduation date between August 14th 2027 and June 1st 2028. 2026 SIII PROGRAM DATES: June 7th, 2027 – August 13th 2027. Candidates must be available for the entirety of the 10-week program. SCOPE OF PRACTICE: Please visit the Minnesota Board of Nursing (MN BON) website for current information regarding the scope of practice for a professional nursing program student who is employed and performing patient care: https://mn.gov/boards/assets/FAQ_Stdent_Nurse_Wk_Exp_12-2019_tcm21-354921.pdf In accordance with the MN BON, Summer III interns will be required to enroll in a 1-credit Summer Intern Course at a University or College within Minnesota for the duration of the program. Information will be provided following offer acceptance. HOUSING: For employees who choose to utilize the housing option, there is a nominal cost deducted from payroll. Parking is offered for an additional upfront charge. Additional information will be provided during the offer process. SIII APPLICATION DEADLINE: December 31, 2026 OFFERS WILL BE EXTENDED no sooner than: February 2nd, 2027 APPLICATION REQUIREMENTS – PLEASE READ CAREFULLY. INCOMPLETE APPLICATIONS WILL NOT BE CONSIDERED: 1. RESUME. Resumes can be longer than 1 page. Please include the following information: permanent address, email, phone, academic program (s), anticipated degree and graduation month/year, cumulative GPA, paid employment history, unpaid clinical experiences, volunteer experiences, awards/honors. Other pertinent information. 2. BLS/CPR CERTIFICATION. Please attach proof of completion for one of the following accepted providers: • American Heart Association: Course title ‘BLS for Healthcare Providers’ • Red Cross: Course title CPR/AED for Professional Rescuers and Health Care Providers or BLS for Healthcare Providers • Military Training Network NOTE: If your certification is set to expire between June 7th and August 1st 2026, please renew PRIOR to the first day of employment. 3. DO NOT ATTACH: Cover letters, letters of reference, publications, transcripts, etc. These documents are not required and will not be included in the screening process. QUALIFIED CANDIDATES WILL BE PROMPTED TO COMPLETE PHASE II of the Screening process, which is a pre-recorded interview to be completed at your convenience. You will receive an email with a link to our HireVue OnDemand system. There will be a series of questions for you to respond to, some will require a video recorded response. You will have multiple chances to record your responses. Please consider this a professional interview. THERE WILL BE A DEADLINE TO COMPLETE THIS APPLICATION PHASE.

jobs.body: About JLG, an Oshkosh company JLG began in 1969, when our founder, John L. Grove set out to resolve growing safety concerns in the construction industry. Since then we have been committed to understanding the challenges and delivering innovative solutions to the access market. We partner with customers to provide quality equipment, training opportunities and trusted support within the access industry. We are a global company, and our products—including mobile elevating work platforms, telehandlers, utility vehicles and accessories—can be found all over the world. As an Electrification Intern you will work closely with the engineering team to learn how to utilize your unique skill set to designs functional, reliable and cost-effective heavy-duty vehicle high voltage electrical systems. Performs engineering analysis and electrical design or re-design, and development of electrical systems and subsystems into existing and new vehicles. YOUR IMPACT Under close supervision, perform basic engineering calculations, investigations, data collection, and analysis in accordance with Oshkosh and general industry engineering standards and processes. Support engineers in the preparation of plans, designs, calculations, technical documentation, and reports. Assist with electrical component research, selection, and design activities to meet defined parameters and specifications while considering quality, cost, reliability, and manufacturability. Support the design, development, testing, and troubleshooting of electrical systems and components used in vehicle electrification applications. Assist with the development, testing, and troubleshooting of software used in vehicle electrification systems and engineering applications. Support software development activities, including writing and modifying code, developing scripts or tools, analyzing data, and documenting software changes. Assist engineers with vehicle electrification system design, integration, and validation activities for new and existing vehicles. Support compliance with applicable regulations, engineering standards, and requirements across multiple regions and markets. Collaborate with various engineering groups and disciplines across the organization. Understand, follow, and promote shop safety practices and policies. Maintain effective communication with internal and external customers. Perform job duties in an ethical and professional manner consistent with the Oshkosh Way, the Company’s mission, quality objectives, policies, and procedures. MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS Perusing a Bachelor's in Electrical, Electronic Engineering, Computer Engineering or similar associated discipline. jobs.body: Job Title OMICS Laboratory Intern Location(s) Duluth About Us Revvity is a developer and provider of end-to-end solutions designed to help scientists, researchers, and clinicians solve the world’s greatest health challenges. We pair the enthusiasm of an industry disruptor with the experience of a longtime leader. Our team of 11,000+ colleagues from around the globe are vital to our success and the reason we’re able to push boundaries in pursuit of better human health. Interns will participate in real-world laboratory projects, gain exposure to regulatory and quality frameworks, and experience the technical and analytical skills essential for a career in clinical genetics. Variant Classification: Observe and assist with variant interpretation using ACMG/AMP guidelines; participate in case review discussions Literature Review: Research published literature and databases to support variant classification and clinical correlation Report Generation: Shadow senior staff in preparing clinical laboratory reports and understanding result communication Project Participation & Research Method Validation: Contribute to validation studies for new assays, technologies, or workflows Research Projects: Participate in OMICS research initiatives, including assay optimization and technology evaluation Cross-Functional Collaboration: Work with bioinformaticians, genetic counselors, clinical geneticists, and laboratory scientists on multidisciplinary projects Professional Development Mentorship: Receive guidance from ABMGG-certified laboratory directors and senior geneticists Career Planning: Engage in discussions about ABMGG fellowship pathways, application processes, and career development in clinical genetics Required Qualifications Bachelor's degree in Genetics, Molecular Biology, Biochemistry, or other Life Sciences field Preferred Qualifications Previous laboratory experience (academic research, clinical internship, or industry) Coursework or training in human genetics, genomics, or molecular diagnostics Familiarity with bioinformatics tools (e.g., BLAST, IGV, Galaxy) Knowledge of ACMG/AMP variant interpretation guidelines Experience with LIMS or electronic health record (EHR) systems Technical Skills: Basic laboratory techniques (pipetting, solution preparation, aseptic technique) Familiarity with molecular biology concepts (DNA structure, PCR, sequencing) Proficiency in Microsoft Office and data management tools Attributes: Strong commitment to pursuing a career in clinical genetics and/or the ABMGG Laboratory Genetics & Genomics (LGG) fellowship Exceptional attention to detail and organizational skills Strong written and verbal communication abilities Work independently and collaboratively in a fast-paced environment Competencies for Success Analytical Mindset: Ability to interpret complex data and troubleshoot technical issues Ethical Integrity: Commitment to patient confidentiality, data accuracy, and regulatory compliance Adaptability: Comfortable learning new technologies and adjusting to evolving project needs Collaboration: Works effectively with multidisciplinary teams and seeks mentorship Work Environment & Schedule Location: Duluth, GA, with the possibility for some travel to clinical laboratory in Pittsburgh, PA Physical Requirements: Ability to stand for extended periods, handle laboratory equipment, and work with biological specimens and chemical reagents Safety: Adherence to biosafety protocols, personal protective equipment (PPE) use, and laboratory safety training Compensation The base salary range for this part-time position is $18.00 - 19.00/hour . This range reflects the minimum and maximum target for a new hire in this position. jobs.body: Position EMC Engineering Intern (Year-Round) Location Kokomo, Indiana About Us BorgWarner is a global product leader in delivering innovative and sustainable mobility solutions. We are a company of innovators and independent thinkers that brings together talented employees, meaningful work and amazing technology in a unique environment. At BorgWarner, we constantly work towards our vision of a clean and energy-efficient world. Our Culture BorgWarner promotes and nurtures a diverse and inclusive environment, honors integrity, strives for excellence, commits to responsibility for our communities and the environment, and builds on the power of collaboration. We believe the health and safety of our employees are a top priority. Career Opportunities We manage talent as seriously as we manage our businesses and encourage you to learn about our proud history, strong culture, technologies, and vision for the future. We offer positions locally and globally with over 80 locations in 19 countries. If this position energizes you and you feel you can help us achieve our mission and vision, you are invited to submit an application for consideration. You may see the list of requirements and feel you do not meet all of them. However, remember that BorgWarner thinks differently. If your qualifications align with the majority of those outlined in this job description, we encourage you to apply and share your experience and skills with us. Job Purpose BorgWarner PowerDrive Systems is currently looking for “dynamic, results driven” individual to join as an EMC Engineer Intern. This is a fully onsite internship. The EMC Engineer Intern will support electromagnetic compatibility (EMC) design, simulation, testing, and analysis activities for advanced automotive power electronics products. Working alongside experienced EMC engineers and cross-functional product development teams, the intern will gain hands-on experience applying EMC principles to real-world engineering challenges while contributing to the development and continuous improvement of EMC design methodologies, simulation capabilities, and engineering guidelines. Key Responsibilities Support EMC simulation and analysis activities to identify potential electromagnetic interference risks and evaluate design improvements for automotive power electronics products. Assist with EMC design reviews and investigations, including analysis of grounding, shielding, filtering, PCB design, cabling, and common-mode/differential-mode noise mitigation techniques. Support EMC laboratory testing and development activities, including test setup, measurements, data collection, troubleshooting, and correlation of simulation results with measured results. Analyze EMC test and simulation data, document findings, and provide technical recommendations to engineering teams. Contribute to the development and continuous improvement of EMC design guidelines, simulation methodologies, engineering tools, and best practices. Collaborate with EMC, electrical, mechanical, systems, and other engineering teams to support EMC performance throughout the product development process. Prepare technical documentation and communicate results through engineering reports and presentations. What We Are Looking For Currently enrolled in an accredited college/university GPA of 3.0 on a 4.0 scale, or B average, upon initial hire date Pursuing a Bachelor's, Master's, or PhD degree in Electrical Engineering, Electronics Engineering, Electromagnetic Engineering, or a closely related technical field. Coursework, research, or practical experience related to electromagnetic compatibility (EMC), electromagnetics, power electronics, circuit design, signal integrity, or electrical systems. Familiarity with engineering simulation and analysis tools such as electromagnetic, circuit, or system-level simulation software is preferred. Familiarity with laboratory instrumentation such as oscilloscopes, spectrum analyzers, network analyzers, or other electrical measurement equipment is preferred. Strong analytical and problem-solving skills with an interest in EMC, automotive electronics, electrification, and power electronics. Ability to analyze technical data, document results, and clearly communicate engineering findings. Ability to work effectively both independently and as part of a cross-functional engineering team. jobs.body: Job Description Summary GE Vernova Advanced Research is the central innovation engine for GE Vernova’s portfolio of energy businesses. The research organization is comprised of researchers who are experts in their fields globally - representing virtually every major scientific and engineering discipline. Collectively, they are driving major research programs and initiatives to decarbonize power, accelerate renewables, and promote electrification and the creation of a 21st century grid fit to power a zero-carbon energy future. As a Fellow Intern in the Electrical Power Systems, Electric Machines & High Voltage Team, you will have the opportunity to develop new technologies for any one of the following technical domains: electrical power system or electric machines or high voltage engineering (including dielectrics and insulation). Assignments are typically for 12-14 weeks; working side by side with experts in the field of Electrical, Control Engineering as well as data science and machine learning teams completing challenging technical projects, applying theoretical knowledge to real-life technical problems, and developing skills in a cutting edge global industrial research environment. This program includes seminars on cross-center technology and soft skills development as well as opportunities for networking and showcasing project accomplishments. Are you ready to join our team of technology enthusiasts to help make GE Vernova’s industrial assets safer and more secure to protect our world’s most critical infrastructure? Job Description Roles and Responsibilities: Work with industry leading experts to execute design, analysis, modeling, simulation and testing/validation of innovative power systems or electric machines or high voltage engineering (including dielectrics and insulation). Strong background in any of those above domains Collaborate with Engineers and Scientists from across the GE Vernova Advanced Research Center and business segments, to advance the energy transition. Required Qualifications: Current enrollment in a full-time Ph.D. degree program in Electrical Engineering, or related disciplines at an ABET accredited university. Preferred Qualifications: Strong dedication to a career in technology and passion for supporting and leading the energy transition. Excitement and enthusiasm for growing technical skills in any one or more technical areas listed above. Experience with simulation software such as PSCAD, PSS/E, PSLF, MAPS, OpenDSS, COMSOL, ANSYS etc. Experience with implementation of control algorithms and analytics in control hardware or energy/distribution management systems in a field or lab hardware in the loop environment using RTDS, Opal-RT etc. Effective presentation and technical communication skills; ability to articulate technical problems in clear and simple terms. Ready to Power a Smarter World with us? We are Generac, a leading energy technology company committed to powering a smarter world. jobs.body: INFICON is a leading provider of innovative instrumentation, critical sensor technologies, and Smart Manufacturing/Industry 4.0 software solutions that enhance productivity and quality of tools, processes, and complete factories. These analysis, measurement and control products are essential for gas leak detection in air conditioning/refrigeration and automotive manufacturing. They are vital to equipment manufacturers and end-users in the complex fabrication of semiconductors and thin film coatings for optics, flat panel displays, solar cells and industrial vacuum coating applications. Other users of our vacuum-based processes include the life sciences, research, aerospace, packaging, heat treatment, laser cutting and many other industrial processes. We also leverage our expertise in vacuum technology to provide unique, toxic chemical analysis products for emergency response, security, and environmental health and safety. The co-op/intern will assist the Operations Engineering Team with creating clear and detailed procedure documents for usage by production technicians, helping engineers with identifying the root-cause of an issue while also being able to develop robust solutions to prevent recurrence. Assist engineers with identifying inefficiencies in production processes and be able to propose & implement solutions that will lead to improvements. Available blocks include the spring and/or summer and/or fall 2027 semesters. The position will report into and support the assigned Operations Engineering Team. The intern position will be working collaboratively with Manufacturing Engineering, Test Engineering and Quality Engineering, In this role the main responsibilities will be: Work with Cross Functional Teams to help solve production engineering issues. Assist with troubleshooting and failure isolation. Implement and update manufacturing process documents. Assist with returning failed products to suppliers through our RTV process. Participate in data collection failure analysis studies. Our emphasis on innovation and its source - dedicated employees - keeps us looking for talented individuals who are ready to meet aggressive goals in a high-technology company constantly developing new marketing-leading products. Good people are critical to our success and, in return, we offer opportunities for personal and professional growth, competitive compensation, and excellent benefits for our diverse, global workforce. Required Qualifications: High School Diploma or Equivalent Pursuing a Bachelor's in Mechanical Engineering/Engineering Technology or Manufacturing Engineering/Engineering Technology Preferred Qualifications: Strong Organizational Skills Statistical analysis tools Excellent Communication Skills Passion for Manufacturing Engineering Process Previous Co-Op/Internship Experience or Previous Work Experience is beneficial but not required The expected salary range for this position is between $18 and $26 per hour. The actual compensation will be determined based on experience, location, and other factors permitted by law. jobs.body: As an Information Technology Intern, Service Delivery , you will work directly with the IT Service Delivery team to support day-to-day operations across the company — from user support and hardware deployment to network troubleshooting and infrastructure projects. This role is ideal for someone pursuing a degree in Information Technology, Computer Science, or a related field who wants to gain real-world, practical experience in a fast-paced, high-impact environment. This is a hands-on internship designed for students who are passionate about technology, infrastructure, and operational support. *This internship is 12 weeks from May/June through August/September 2027 Assist in the deployment, configuration, and maintenance of end-user systems including laptops, desktops, peripherals, and mobile devices. Support onboarding and offboarding processes by preparing, imaging, and configuring hardware for new and departing employees. Participate in network troubleshooting, including testing connectivity, validating VLAN assignments, and assisting with switch and access point deployments under supervision. Help document and improve IT operational processes, runbooks, and troubleshooting guides. Assist with low-voltage tasks such as patching cables, labeling ports, and organizing network infrastructure. Support the Service Delivery team in scheduled maintenance, equipment inventory, and asset lifecycle management. Participate in special projects, such as system upgrades, process automation, or hardware refresh initiatives, with mentorship from full-time team members. Currently pursuing a degree in Information Technology, Computer Science, Cybersecurity, or a related technical field. Strong interest in IT operations, service delivery, and infrastructure support. Basic understanding of networking concepts (IP addressing, VLANs, DHCP, DNS) and operating systems (Windows, macOS). Excellent troubleshooting and problem-solving skills with a willingness to learn in a hands-on environment. Strong communication skills and ability to work collaboratively in a team setting. Must be detail-oriented, organized, and able to follow processes and procedures accurately. Experience with ticketing systems or service desk platforms. Familiarity with endpoint management tools (Intune, JAMF, etc.). Exposure to scripting or automation tools is a plus. jobs.location: Beatrice, NE, United States of America
jobs.body: The 2027 Summer Internship Program will run from May 17, 2027, through August 6, 2027. Candidates must be available to start on May 17 and participate through the duration of the program. Applicants must be legally authorized to work in the United States. We are unable to sponsor or take over sponsorship of a school/employment or any other visa, regardless of expiration date, now or in the future. Who Are We? The Toro Company (TTC) has delivered market-leading, innovative products and outstanding customer care for more than 100 years. With over 11,000 employees worldwide, TTC is headquartered in Bloomington, Minnesota, USA. Our company designs and manufactures turf maintenance equipment; turf irrigation systems; landscape and lighting products; snow and ice management solutions; agricultural irrigation systems; rental, specialty and underground construction equipment; and residential turf and snow equipment. We market and sell TTC products worldwide through a network of distributors, dealers, mass retailers, hardware retailers, equipment rental center and home centers—as well as online direct to end users. Exmark, located in Beatrice, Nebraska is a division of The Toro Company. Exmark is the leading manufacturer of commercial mowers and equipment for the landscape professional. Exmark mowers are trusted 2-to-1 over the next best-selling brand of zero-turn mowers by landscape professionals. All Exmark products are designed to help customers increase productivity, while delivering unmatched quality. What Will You Do? In order to grow and build a successful career with The Toro Company, you will be responsible for: Establishes and maintains engineered time standards for direct labor operations. Establishes methods and processes for assembly, welding, paint line and related material handling on new products and equipment. Works with department supervisors and value stream manufacturing engineers with implementation of new methods and processes. Makes recommendations for improving safety, quality, or productivity activities. Implements proper ergonomics in work station setup, processes, tooling and safety equipment. Identify and apply Lean methodologies to ensure processes are scientifically controlled and continuously improved. Creates necessary documentation (standard work, Heijunka cards, etc) for all new product launches. Collaborate across all functions of the business and learn what it takes to be part of a great team What Do You Need? To be considered for this role, an individual should meet the following minimal requirements: Demonstrated mechanical aptitude with an ability to learn and apply new things. Strong analytical and organizational skills. Problem solving acumen. Preferred cumulative GPA of 3.0 or higher. Experience with MS Office (Word, Excel, Outlook), CAD software, Test Instrumentation. Ability to manage multiple projects at once and prioritize based on due dates or importance. What Can We Give You? At The Toro Company, we are always working to make sure our interns know just how valued they are. In addition to a competitive pay- The Toro Company offers interns a variety of perks, including: Dress for your day – We know you're more productive when you're comfortable, which is why TTC employees are encouraged to take advantage of our casual, corporate environment. Volunteerism – The Toro Company is proud to provide interns 8 hours of paid time to volunteer in the community. Competitive Pay – Competitive compensation with an anticipated hourly rate of $22–$28. Actual rates may vary based on factors such as academic standing, business function, and other relevant considerations. The Toro Company is an Equal Opportunity Employer. We consider all qualified applicants based on merit and do not discriminate on the basis of race, color, religion, sex (including pregnancy, gender identity, and sexual orientation), parental status, national origin, age, disability, genetic information, military service, or other non-merit factors. We are committed to creating a welcoming environment for all employees.

jobs.title: Research & Development Engineering Intern, Summer 2027
jobs.location: Blauvelt, NY, United States of America
jobs.body: We’re Watts. Together, we’re reimagining the future of water. We feel proud every day about what we do. We're all part of the same crucial mission, no matter what function we support -- it's to provide safe, clean water for the world, and to protect our planet's most valuable resource. What we do: For 150 years, Watts has built best-in-class products that are trusted by customers in residential and commercial settings across the world. We are at the forefront of innovation, working with cutting-edge technology to provide smart and connected, sustainable water solutions for the future. Watts is a leading brand with a quality reputation — and we have a dynamic future ahead.​ The Watts Internship Program is your chance to bring what you’ve learned in the classroom to life! You’ll dive into real-world projects, gaining hands-on experience while learning how business really works from the inside. During the program, you’ll get to roll up your sleeves and make an impact on day-to-day operations. Plus, you'll have tons of opportunities to network with passionate professionals across manufacturing, industrial engineering, and more—sparking new ideas through cross-department collaboration. It’s all about expanding your skills, challenging yourself, and exploring where your ambitions can take you! Scope of Position This analytical and technically driven individual, as part of the Applied Research team, will provide technical and business support to ongoing product development research. The Research Engineering Intern will support the development of a new commercial electric water heating product by conducting research, evaluating designs, and preparing test plans to validate design specifications, including cost, performance, and size. This position provides hands-on experience in laboratory testing, mechanical and electrical systems, and product development. The intern will work with engineers to evaluate product performance and support certification to applicable safety standards. This position reports to the Director, Applied Research and is based in Blauvelt, NY. Primary Job Duties and Responsibilities Conduct research to support the development and launch of a new commercial electric water heating product. Evaluate designs for compliance with design specifications, conduct comparative evaluations, and create associated documentation. Develop laboratory and field test programs to validate product performance against design specifications and support certification to applicable safety standards. Work with engineers in a laboratory environment to conduct testing using instrumentation and measurement equipment. Document test procedures, analyze data, and summarize results. Work with engineers to gain experience using CAD tools and business software. Demonstrate accountability by maintaining accurate research and testing documentation and following through on assigned project responsibilities. Summarize and present internship learning, project results, and experiences to the leadership team. Assume responsibility for other projects and duties as assigned by the Director, Applied Research or Company management. Required Qualifications Current student (junior or senior status). Pursuing a bachelor’s or master’s degree in Mechanical Engineering. Interest in research and product development, with strong mechanical and electrical knowledge. Data analysis skills. Experience identifying and analyzing problems, making recommendations, and implementing solutions. Ability to understand electrical schematics and mechanical systems. Passionate about your work, with a genuine desire to contribute meaningfully and make an impact. Demonstrated commitment to integrity and respect in interactions with others, fostering a positive and inclusive work environment. Strong sense of accountability, taking ownership of tasks and following through on commitments. Understanding of and adherence to applicable laws, codes, policies, regulations, and safety practices and procedures, as applicable. Must be authorized to work in the United States and not require sponsorship now or in the future. Must successfully establish employment eligibility and satisfactorily complete background checks, including required pre-employment testing as a condition of employment. Preferred Qualifications Familiarity with CAD software, such as SolidWorks and AutoCAD. General Applicable Company Competencies Commitment to Watts’ values of integrity, accountability, continuous improvement and innovation, and transparency. Punctuality and dependability. Ability to be flexible and adapt to changing work priorities and stressful conditions. Adherence to all personnel policies, procedures, and standards of process as implemented by Watts. Maintain productive and collaborative relationships with other Watts employees. Adherence to Watts’ seven cultural beliefs: Growth Mindset, Customer-Focused Innovation, Constant Communication, Clear Goals, Collaborate Globally, Be Inclusive, and Take Action. Working Conditions While performing the job duties, you will be working on-site at a manufacturing facility and will perform the majority of your duties in an office environment. You may, at times, be required to be present on the manufacturing floor and will be required to wear the appropriate personal protective equipment. You will be required to work in the office at the Blauvelt, NY location (Monday – Friday). Your scheduled work hours will be communicated to you by your manager. Physical Requirements Specific physical abilities required for this position include, but are not limited to: Ability to remain seated at a desk or workstation for extended periods. Ability to physically move around the office, organize or transport files, packages, or other office-related materials. Ability to read documents, use a computer, and perform data entry tasks. Ability to communicate clearly with management and coworkers, particularly in meetings or phone calls. Ability to operate standard office equipment such as computers, printers, phones, and copiers. Ability to stand for long periods of time. Ability to occasionally lift and carry up to 25 pounds. Ability to push and pull up to 20 pounds. Ability to physically move around the manufacturing floor and laboratory. Ability to read documents and communicate clearly with management and coworkers. Ability to wear personal protective equipment, which may include, but is not limited to, safety shoes, hearing protection, and safety glasses. Ability to frequently walk, talk, and/or hear while performing job responsibilities. Ability to use hands to finger, handle, or feel while working with laboratory instruments, measurement equipment, and product components. Specific vision abilities include close vision, color vision, peripheral vision, depth perception, and the ability to adjust focus. Pay Range The expected hourly range for this position is $22–$24 hourly. Actual compensation will be dependent upon individual skills, experience, qualifications, and applicable law. What’s In It for You People-First Culture – Enriching and caring for people is at the core of who we are; this includes executing our Diversity, Equity, and Inclusion (DEI) strategy, and providing you with meaningful career growth opportunities, a positive and safe work environment, and affirmation that you are heard, valued, and respected. Flexible PTO Policy – Work-life balance is important at Watts and our interns receive one (1) hour of flexible PTO for every thirty (30) hours worked. Your flexible PTO can be utilized for any type of absence. Paid Holidays – Celebrate the holidays with your loved ones and still get paid! You will receive the following paid holidays off during your time as an Intern with Watts. Where a holiday falls during the weekend, it will be observed on an adjacent weekday. Lunch and Learns – Throughout your internship, there will be opportunities for you to sign up to learn and network with some of the key strategic leaders and thought partners within our core operating model! Sustainability – For five years in a row, Watts has been named one of “America’s Most Responsible Companies” by Newsweek. Join our journey as we continue to distinguish Watts as a responsible and committed corporate citizen. Nothing in this job description restricts Watts’ right to assign or reassign duties, responsibilities, and working hours/conditions to this position at any time. This position is “at will,” which means that either the employee or Watts may terminate the employment relationship at any time, with or without notice, and for any lawful reason. #LI ( Onsite) Watts in it for you : Please note that the following benefits apply only to permanent roles and do not apply to internship roles. Competitive compensation based on your skills, qualifications and experience Comprehensive medical and dental coverage, retirement benefits Family building benefits, including paid maternity/paternity leave 10 paid holidays and Paid Time Off Continued professional development opportunities and educational reimbursement Additional perks such as fitness reimbursements and employee discount programs Learn more about our benefit offerings here: https://tapintowattsbenefits.com/ How we work: At Watts, our culture is team-oriented and supportive. Employees here genuinely care about the quality of their work, and about each other. Our people are the heart of who we are and contribute to our longevity and continued success. And this is a place where you can have a big career. No matter your role, there are opportunities for learning and development, and your daily contributions make a meaningful impact on the lives of people who use our products and on the future of water. Watts is committed to equal employment opportunity. We follow a policy of administering all employment decisions and personnel actions without regard to race, color, religion, creed, sex, pregnancy, national origin, sexual orientation, age, physical or mental disability, genetic disposition or carrier status, marital status, military or veteran status, minorities, or any other category protected under applicable federal, state, or local law. Consistent with the obligations of state and federal law, Watts will make reasonable accommodations for qualified individuals with disabilities. Any employee who needs a reasonable accommodation should contact Human Resources.

jobs.body: Job Title: Manufacturing Engineering Co-Op Job Description: Here at Entegris, we use advanced science to enable technologies that transform the world, and we are seeking employees who have the drive to continue the mission. The Role: Our site in Aurora, IL is seeking a Manufacturing Engineering Co-Op to join our team for the Spring 2027 season. This assignment is intended to be 6 months in duration. In this role, you will support the quality and documentation priorities of the Slurries business unit, working alongside our manufacturing engineers across the mixing, blending, and filling room processes. You will lead a systematic refresh of critical process documentation — SOPs, batch cards, response flow checklists, and work instructions — and support quality investigations using process and quality data. You will finish the assignment with hands-on manufacturing experience, a broad network across engineering, operations, and quality, and documentation and quality improvements that outlast your term. What You’ll Do: Create and update critical process documentation for the Slurries lines — Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs), batch cards, response flow checklists, and operator work instructions — and drive them through the review and approval process. Audit existing documentation against current practice on the floor, identify gaps and outdated content, and maintain a prioritized plan to close them. Support quality investigations and root-cause analysis on nonconformances, customer complaints, and scrap/rework drivers, including data collection, analysis, and verification of corrective actions. Analyze quality and process data to identify variation and improvement opportunities, and help build dashboards or reports that make quality performance visible to the team. Support audit and compliance readiness, including document control practices, training records, and change documentation. Partner with Manufacturing Engineering, Operations, and Quality teams, and present project status and results to the Slurries leadership team, including a final summary of outcomes and recommendations. What We Seek: Currently pursuing a Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Chemical, Mechanical, Industrial, or Manufacturing Engineering, with an interest in manufacturing quality and process documentation. Strong technical writing skills — able to turn floor observations and engineering input into clear, accurate, usable procedures. Detail-oriented and organized, with the discipline to carry documentation through review and approval to completion. Comfortable with data analysis tools (Excel, Minitab, JMP, Power BI or similar); exposure to Six Sigma, statistical process control, or quality systems is a plus. Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including comfort interviewing operators and presenting leadership. Adaptable, proactive, and technologically savvy, with a passion for problem-solving and a willingness to learn from experienced engineers. Desired Major(s) & Graduation Year: Chemical Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Industrial Engineering, Manufacturing Engineering; coursework or project experience in quality engineering, statistics, data analytics, or machine learning is a plus. jobs.body: Job Description Summary Addressing the climate crisis is an urgent global priority, and at GE Vernova, we take our responsibility seriously. jobs.body: Bosch first started its operations in Vietnam in 1994 and registered a wholly-owned subsidiary in 2008. According to the business strategy of Bosch in Vietnam, from 1st July 2014 on all business entities were merged into Bosch Vietnam Co. Ltd. with its head office at Ho Chi Minh City plant (HcP) in Dong Nai Province. HcP has started its belt assembly in a rented building on 1st August 2008 as the assembly plant of Tilburg Plant (TbP). On 14th April 2011, HcP celebrated the inauguration of the new plant (Lth101 with 17,000 sqm), which did not only allow to increase the production depth, but also to facilitate the push belt assembly of this high-tech product. jobs.body: WD is building the infrastructure behind the AI-driven data economy. As AI scales, so does data. Every interaction, every model, every system generates data that must be stored, managed, and made accessible over time. That’s where we come in. We combine deep engineering expertise with global-scale manufacturing to deliver the storage systems that make AI possible, powering hyperscale data centers, cloud platforms, and enterprise infrastructure worldwide. This isn’t theoretical work. It’s real systems, at real scale, people solving some of the hardest challenges in technology today. We’re looking for people who want to build, solve, and operate at that level. Join us and let’s shape the future of data. Job Summary This internship provides an opportunity to gain hands-on experience in plating process engineering within a manufacturing environment. The intern will support the engineering team in monitoring plating processes, collecting and analyzing process data, assisting with process improvement activities, and maintaining manufacturing documentation. The role will provide exposure to plating chemistry, process control, contamination control, manufacturing quality, and operational efficiency. The intern will work closely with experienced engineers and cross-functional teams to learn practical problem-solving and continuous improvement methodologies in a manufacturing environment. ESSENTIAL DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES: Support engineers in monitoring plating process parameters and identifying process trends. Assist with plating DI water, LPC, contamination, and other process-related data monitoring. Support plating chemical inventory tracking and basic planning activities. Assist with monitoring plating pretreatment, strip line, filter change, and related process conditions. Collect, organize, and analyze process and production data to support quality and yield improvement. Assist engineers in investigating process deviations and line-to-line variations. Participate in process improvement and optimization projects under the guidance of experienced engineers. Support contamination control activities and follow cleanroom and safety procedures. Assist with OEE data tracking and analysis to identify potential improvement opportunities. Participate in FMEA, risk assessment, and other engineering review activities as required. Support process parameter evaluation, documentation updates, and change implementation activities. Prepare basic reports, charts, presentations, and technical documentation to communicate findings and project progress. Collaborate with manufacturing, quality, equipment, and other engineering teams on assigned projects. Perform other engineering-related tasks and projects as assigned. REQUIRED: Currently pursuing a Bachelor's Degree or above in Chemical Engineering, Materials Engineering, Manufacturing Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, or other relevant engineering disciplines. PREFERRED: Basic understanding of manufacturing processes, chemistry, electroplating, or process control is an advantage. Basic knowledge of data analysis and statistical methods is preferred. Comfortable working in a manufacturing and cleanroom environment. Proficient in Microsoft Office applications, particularly Excel and PowerPoint. Able to communicate effectively in English. Previous internship, academic project, laboratory, or manufacturing-related experience is an advantage but not required. SKILLS Strong willingness to learn and develop practical engineering knowledge. Good analytical and problem-solving skills. Detail-oriented with the ability to organize and interpret data. Good communication and teamwork skills. Self-motivated, responsible, and able to complete assigned tasks with appropriate guidance. Basic knowledge of problem-solving or quality tools such as 6 Sigma, DOE, FMEA, or 8D is an advantage. FOR JOBS IN THE US, PLEASE USE ALL 3 PARAGRAPHS. Job Description This role is responsible for supporting professional employees working in an organizational function related to the Intern's area of study. Depending on the internship assignment, the intern may work alongside engineers, scientists, or industry professionals to contribute to various projects related to their area of study. Under guided supervision, interns will assist with various projects and tasks, contributing to the organization's goals while learning from experienced professionals in the field. We accept and review applications on a rolling basis, and we extend offers as individual positions are finalized and specific team hiring needs are confirmed. Submitting an application places you in consideration for upcoming opportunities as they open. What You'll Do Define the fire and life safety basis for manufacturing and support operations by evaluating and analyzing buildings, equipment, processes, and procedures; implement and facilitate Fire Protection programs and procedures; and monitor the effectiveness of Fire Protection items relied on for safety (IROFS), limits, controls, systems, and equipment. Develop/review/revise Fire Hazard Analysis documents to identify and evaluate potential fire hazards and exposure scenarios for normal operations and process upsets of TRISO-X fuel fabrication processes and TRISO-X Facility operations, including processes involved in storage of flammable/combustible chemicals/gases, producing TRISO fuel forms, quality control activities, recycling/recovery of process materials, managing effluents and waste materials, and conducting maintenance activities. Develop/review/revise compliance plans that demonstrate Life Safety code requirements are being met. Develop/review/revise calculations by executing computer codes and models to support Fire Protection evaluations. Develop/review/revise/implement safety and compliance programs and procedures. Participate in Process Hazards Analysis activities with multidiscipline teams to identify potential criticality, radiological, chemical, and fire/explosion hazards to support the Integrated Safety Analysis (ISA) process. Consult with and advise operations, maintenance, and engineering personnel on the Fire Protection impacts of new or proposed changes to processes, procedures, and facility designs/modifications. Participate in design reviews. Conduct surveillances, inspections, walk-downs, investigations, and audits/assessments of manufacturing and support operations, and unusual incidents to ensure compliance with approved procedures and safety bases. Develop/revise/deliver Fire Protection training to operations, maintenance, and other personnel. Develop/revise Fire Protection postings and operator aids to implement administrative controls to ensure they are unambiguous, easily understood, and readily achievable. Provide support to the emergency response team. Maintain professional demeanor and behavior at all times in all forms of communication. Perform other duties as assigned by manager. Proficiency with the Microsoft Office Suite (Outlook, Word, Excel, PowerPoint). Curiosity, initiative, and a collaborative mindset — you're eager to learn and ready to contribute. Letters should come from a professor, academic advisor, employer, or professional mentor who can speak directly to your qualifications, work ethic, and potential. jobs.body: Stanley Black & Decker Intern – Embedded Software Engineering Intern Location: Onsite Towson, MD Come build your career. It takes great people to achieve greatness. People with a sense of purpose and integrity. People with a relentless pursuit of excellence. People who care about making things better For Those Who Make The World™. Sound like you? Join our top-notch team of more than 50,000 diverse and high-performing professionals globally who are making their mark on some of the world’s most beloved brands, including DEWALT®, BLACK+DECKER®, CRAFTSMAN®, STANLEY®, CUB CADET®, and HUSTLER®. Opportunity for career advancement upon graduation. Competitive compensation and career development opportunities. The base pay range for this position in Maryland is $22.00- $27.00 per hour. jobs.body: Work Schedule Standard (Mon-Fri) Environmental Conditions Office Job Description Why Join Us? At Thermo Fisher Scientific, our internship program is designed to be a strategic pipeline for future leadership talent. Interns who demonstrate exceptional performance, leadership potential, and alignment with our values will be considered for full-time opportunities during their internship with us to begin post-graduation. These opportunities include potential placement into one of our Leadership Development Programs (LDPs) or other early career roles across the organization. As a global company with opportunities spanning multiple businesses, functions, and locations, applicants are required to be geographically flexible and mobile for both their internship assignment and potential future employment opportunities. Potential placement into internship, LDP, or full-time roles is based on business needs and organizational priorities at the time of selection. Onsite and in-office work is an essential function of this role and a requirement of the position. Strategic Business Impact Our internships are 10-week positions and students have the option to join us on either May 24, 2027 or June 14, 2027. All projects will have significant strategic and/or operating importance to the business to which they are assigned. The Supplier Relations Specialist will provide support to the Third-Party supplier category team to drive our program’s value across the supplier community, and to achieve revenue and margin targets while improving the supplier and customer experience. The position will require daily interaction with external Third-Party suppliers to establish, maintain, improve supplier relationships, negotiate favorable pricing, drive profitability, and support operational projects, including but not limited to enhanced electronic transactions, backlog reduction, order fulfilment improvements, etc. Key Responsibilities: • Demonstrate relationship management and negotiation skills • Assist Category Manager in prospecting and researching suppliers and their competitors’ products to understand the market, their market share and evaluate the opportunity to make the best decision for our customers and our company • Assist in preparing, organizing, and analyzing supplier information to aid in supplier discussions, negotiations, and business reviews • Present our value proposition to suppliers • Negotiate new or improved discounted pricing or rebates with the category suppliers to achieve margin and sales improvement targets • Support the category with compiling and sending 3P centric Supplier Scorecards on a quarterly basis. Assist with analyzing the data for areas of improvement • Assist with collaborating with suppliers on use of the Supplier Portal utilizing new product additions, lead time updates and promise date uploads • Submit substitutions and cross references on items to more profitable Encompass suppliers or from items that have been discontinued • Assist suppliers in resolving issues or concerns • Act as a liaison between the Category Manager and 3P Purchasing and Open Order Specialists with daily Supplier related issues • Collaborate with internal groups such as Portfolio Management, Supply Chain, Transportation, Cross Referencing, Regulatory, Product Administration, Finance, IT, etc. as needed • Assist the Encompass Customer Team on customer specific requests/needs • Perform other duties as assigned Compensation & Relocation Our Undergraduate internships offer an hourly rate between $18.50 - $28.75 dependent upon the role type and location you are supporting (aligned to respective cost-of-living guidelines). If eligible, a relocation stipend is offered in the amount of $5,000 . Students must be located 50+ miles away from the physical location of the internship to be eligible for the relocation stipend. Please note that interns are required to have a reliable mode of transportation to and from their assigned work location for the duration of their internship. What We Look For Academic Background & Work Experience: Undergraduate student completing a Bachelor’s degree in Business, Business Management, Finance or related field between December 2027 – June 2028 . A background in Chemistry, Biology or related field is a plus, however, not required Previous related internships and / or work experience totaling 1+ years experience required. Leadership Profile: Proven leadership experience through student organizations, athletics, Greek life, community service, volunteer organizations, campus programs, military service, or other leadership roles. A track record of influencing others, leading initiatives, driving results, and creating positive impact within teams and organizations. Demonstrated ability to navigate ambiguity, adapt to changing priorities, and solve complex problems. Evidence of grit, resilience, and perseverance when facing challenges, setbacks, or competing priorities. Strong learning agility, intellectual curiosity, and an innovative mindset. Excellent interpersonal communication skills and emotional intelligence, with the ability to build relationships across diverse teams. Geographic mobility and flexibility required to pursue internship and future career opportunities in locations aligned with business needs. Onsite and in-office work is an essential function of this role and is required throughout the program and in future placements to support collaboration across businesses, functions, and locations. If this sounds like you, we'd love to hear from you! To qualify, applicants must be legally authorized to work in the United States and should not require sponsorship (current or future) for employment visa status. Thermo Fisher does not offer employment in this position to holders of F-1, J-1, H-1, OPT, and CPT Visas for the purpose of obtaining practical experience.

jobs.title: NPD Engineer Intern, Summer 2027
jobs.location: Fort Worth, TX, United States of America
jobs.body: We’re Watts. Together, we’re reimagining the future of water. We feel proud every day about what we do. We're all part of the same crucial mission, no matter what function we support -- it's to provide safe, clean water for the world, and to protect our planet's most valuable resource. What we do: For 150 years, Watts has built best-in-class products that are trusted by customers in residential and commercial settings across the world. We are at the forefront of innovation, working with cutting-edge technology to provide smart and connected, sustainable water solutions for the future. Watts is a leading brand with a quality reputation — and we have a dynamic future ahead.​ The Watts Internship Program is your chance to bring what you’ve learned in the classroom to life! You’ll dive into real-world projects, gaining hands-on experience while learning how business really works from the inside. During the program, you’ll get to roll up your sleeves and make an impact on day-to-day operations. Plus, you'll have tons of opportunities to network with passionate professionals across manufacturing, industrial engineering, and more—sparking new ideas through cross-department collaboration. It’s all about expanding your skills, challenging yourself, and exploring where your ambitions can take you! Scope of Position The New Product Development (NPD) Intern, as part of the New Product Development department within the Conditioning and Filtration platform, will support the development and evaluation of product-validation methods for water-conditioning and filtration products. This motivated individual will gain hands-on technical experience designing experiments, conducting laboratory-scale testing, analyzing technical data, and documenting results to support new product development initiatives. This position reports to the New Product Development Manager. This role is onsite and is based in Fort Worth, Texas. Primary Job Duties and Responsibilities Support water-treatment projects through the development and evaluation of engineering tools and test methods. Design and conduct laboratory-scale experiments to evaluate product performance and validation methods. Contribute to instrumentation-focused projects supporting water-treatment new product development. Assist with regulatory and product qualification projects, as needed. Analyze and process project data to support technical evaluation and reporting. Document testing procedures, experimental results, and technical findings to support product development activities. Maintain accurate testing records, communicate findings transparently, and identify opportunities for continuous improvement. Assume responsibility for other projects and duties as assigned by the New Product Development Manager or Company management. Responsibility directly tied to Watts Value (Integrity, Accountability, Continuous Improvement, Transparency) Required Qualifications Current student (sophomore, junior or senior status). Pursuing a Bachelor's degree in Engineering or a related scientific field. Interest in product development, water-treatment technologies, and related applications. Passionate about your work, with a genuine desire to contribute meaningfully and make an impact. Demonstrated commitment to integrity and respect in interactions with others, fostering a positive and inclusive work environment. Strong sense of accountability, taking ownership of tasks and following through on commitments. Understanding of and adherence to applicable laws, codes, policies, regulations, and safety practices and procedures, as applicable. Preferred Qualifications Coursework, projects, or prior experience in Chemical or Industrial Engineering. Previous laboratory experience. Experience with experimental design or test-method development. Experience with basic statistical analysis and technical data analysis. Coursework or prior experience related to regulatory requirements. Familiarity with laboratory instrumentation and testing equipment. Experience with technical data analysis, processing, and documentation. General Applicable Company Competencies Commitment to Watts’ values of integrity, accountability, continuous improvement and innovation, and transparency. Punctuality and dependability. Ability to be flexible and adapt to changing work priorities and stressful conditions. Adherence to all personnel policies, procedures, and standards of process as implemented by Watts. Maintain productive and collaborative relationships with other Watts employees. Adherence to Watts’ seven cultural beliefs: Growth Mindset, Customer-Focused Innovation, Constant Communication, Clear Goals, Collaborate Globally, Be Inclusive, and Take Action. Working Conditions While performing the job duties, you will be working on-site at a manufacturing facility and will perform the majority of your duties in an office environment. You may, at times, be required to be present on the manufacturing floor and will be required to wear the appropriate personal protective equipment. You will be required to work in the office at the Fort Worth, TX location (Monday – Friday). Your scheduled work hours will be communicated to you by your manager. Physical Requirements: Specific physical abilities required for this position include, but are not limited to: Ability to remain seated at a desk or workstation for extended periods. Ability to perform repetitive tasks such as typing on a keyboard or using a mouse for extended periods. Ability to physically move around the office, organize or transport files, packages, or other office-related materials. Ability to read documents, use a computer, and perform data entry tasks. Ability to communicate clearly with management and coworkers, particularly in meetings or phone calls. Ability to operate standard office equipment such as computers, printers, phones, and copiers. Ability to stand for long periods of time. Ability to lift and carry up to 20 pounds. Ability to push and pull up to 20 pounds. Ability to physically move around the manufacturing floor. Ability to wear personal protective equipment, which may include, but is not limited to, safety shoes, hearing protection, and safety glasses. Pay Range: $22-26 The expected hourly range for this position is $22–$26 hourly . Actual compensation will be dependent upon individual skills, experience, qualifications, and applicable law. What's In It for You People-First Culture – Enriching and caring for people is at the core of who we are; this includes executing our Diversity, Equity, and Inclusion (DEI) strategy, and providing you with meaningful career growth opportunities, a positive and safe work environment, and affirmation that you are heard, valued, and respected. Flexible PTO Policy – Work-life balance is important at Watts and our interns receive one (1) hour of flexible PTO for every thirty (30) hours worked. Your flexible PTO can be utilized for any type of absence. Paid Holidays – Celebrate the holidays with your loved ones and still get paid! You will receive the following paid holidays off during your time as an Intern with Watts. Where a holiday falls during the weekend, it will be observed on an adjacent weekday. Lunch and Learns – Throughout your internship, there will be opportunities for you to sign up to learn and network with some of the key strategic leaders and thought partners within our core operating model!
