jobs.body: With its five product lines of compact hydraulics Bosch Rexroth Oil Control SpA , with factories in the province of Modena and Reggio Emilia and over 1,300 employees, has been producing and marketing compact hydraulic components for multiple applications for over 40 years, from aerial platforms to cranes, earth-moving machinery, agricultural machinery, industrial applications. What characterizes Bosch Rexroth Oil Control S.p.A. is the ability to study customized solutions in relation to each specific customer requirement. For this reason, the products of Bosch Rexroth Oil Control S.p.A. they are synonymous with quality and represent a guarantee for the global market. In industrial hydraulics, Bosch Rexroth is actively shaping the transition from conventional to intelligent and connected hydraulics. This opens up enormous potential for the easy and economical integration of machines and systems into modern industrial environments. Our R&D department based in Nonantola (MO) is a center of global competence for Compact Hydraulic products. Between Process Optimization, HSE management and data analytics , you will play a key role in bridging corporate standards with global safety regulations . By mapping Bosch internal requirements beside Italian and International Technical Standards, you will leverage data and technology to drive operational efficiency, structure a robust management system and foster a safer workplace . This is a hands-on opportunity to apply digital solutions to real-world industrial safety and technical challenges. What you will do & learn Harmonize Standards: support the integration of internal Bosch Requirements with Italian and International Technical Standards to build a robust Electrical Safety Management System. Leverage Data & Tech: use data analytics and process optimization tools to modernize traditional safety workflows. Drive Safety & Efficiency: active collaboration to foster a workplace culture that is both safe and highly efficient. Assigned Project Collect and analyze existing technical documentation related to electrical systems and equipment Collaborate in defining and standardizing an electrical safety management system Interface with internal technical departments (Maintenance, Engineering, Production) Be involved in new projects’ management at different sites Support the execution of risk assessments on electrical systems across different company sites Define a robust but flexible management system on electrical safety transversally and across various departments Education: currently pursuing a bachelor’s or master’s degree in Engineering preferably with a focus on Electrotechnical, Health, Safety & Environment, data analysis, or industrial processes or related scientific/technical fields (e.g., Environmental Sciences, Occupational Health and Safety) with a genuine interest in HSE topics. Others: Interest in technical topics and in health, safety, and environmental themes; good knowledge of the Microsoft Office package (especially Excel); strong organizational skills and attention to details. What do we offer: Structured Mentorship: You will be paired with a dedicated HSE tutor who will support your professional growth and guide you step-by-step through your project; International Environment: The opportunity to experience the dynamics, standards, and best practices of a global manufacturing leader; Flexible Learning: A supportive team culture that respects your university deadlines, exam sessions, and academic commitments; HSE and Technical Field Exposure: A highly practical internship where you won't just do office work, but actively participate in plant operations; If you feel confident in the position don't hesitate to apply take a look! www.bosch.com www.boschrexroth.com Bosch is proud to be an Equal Opportunity Employer. jobs.title: [Bosch HcP - Internship] Lean Manufacturing & Industrial Engineering Intern
jobs.location: An Phuoc Commune, Dong Nai, vn
jobs.body: Bosch first started its operations in Vietnam in 1994 and registered a wholly-owned subsidiary in 2008. According to the business strategy of Bosch in Vietnam, from 1st July 2014 on all business entities were merged into Bosch Vietnam Co. Ltd. with its head office at Ho Chi Minh City plant (HcP) in Dong Nai Province. HcP has started its belt assembly in a rented building on 1st August 2008 as the assembly plant of Tilburg Plant (TbP). On 14th April 2011, HcP celebrated the inauguration of the new plant (Lth101 with 17,000 sqm), which did not only allow to increase the production depth, but also to facilitate the push belt assembly of this high-tech product. On 3rd July 2012 HcP marked a big milestone by starting to produce the second component (loop-set) for its push belt. Since November 2012, HcP doubled the production floor space and increase the net total floor space up to 56.000 m², and have successfully increased its production capacity and realized a lot of new line SOP’s. For further information, please visit our website: www.bosch.com.vn 1. BPS (Bosch Production System) Methodology: Support Lean Manufacturing (BPS) activity including training preparation, documentation, workshops, and improvement projects. Support 5S, Suggestion Scheme activities through coordination, system administration, data tracking, and communication. Collect and analyze data to support continuous-improvement initiatives. Assist with the preparation of presentations, reports, and project updates. 2. Industrial Engineering: Support time studies, cycle-time measurement, and production time-data analysis. Assist with standardized work, line balancing, and operator workload analysis. Other tasks assigned by Managers. Undergraduate student majoring in Engineering, Industrial Engineering, Business Administration, or a related technical field. Good command of English, with effective verbal and written communication skills. Reliable, proactive, highly disciplined, patient, detail-oriented, and comfortable working with data and figures. Proficient in Microsoft Office applications, particularly Excel, Word, and PowerPoint. Basic knowledge of Power BI and Power Automate is preferred. Able to work independently as well as collaboratively in a team environment. Eagerness to learn and adapt in a dynamic manufacturing environment. A learning-driven, professional, inclusive multinational work environment fosters personal growth and expands professional networks. An attractive monthly allowance. Bus transportation and lunch are provided daily. Full-paid leaves for Vietnam public holidays, birthday, sickness and 01 day per working month. Opportunities to become a Bosch associate after graduation.

jobs.title: Spatial Data R&D Intern - The Toro Company
jobs.location: Bloomington, MN, United States of America
jobs.body: The 2027 Summer Internship Program will run from May 17, 2027, through August 6, 2027. Candidates must be available to start on May 17 and participate through the duration of the program. Applicants must be legally authorized to work in the United States. We are unable to sponsor or take over sponsorship of a school/employment or any other visa, regardless of expiration date, now or in the future. Who Are We? The Toro Company (TTC) has delivered market-leading, innovative products and outstanding customer care for more than 100 years. With over 11,000 employees worldwide, TTC is headquartered in Bloomington, Minnesota, USA. Our company designs and manufactures turf maintenance equipment; turf irrigation systems; landscape and lighting products; snow and ice management solutions; agricultural irrigation systems; rental, specialty and underground construction equipment; and residential turf and snow equipment. We market and sell TTC products worldwide through a network of distributors, dealers, mass retailers, hardware retailers, equipment rental center and home centers—as well as online direct to end users. What Will You Do? In order to grow and build a successful career with The Toro Company, you will be responsible for: Develop tools to ingest, curate, model, and visualize spatial data collections. Conduct customer site assessments using spatial data in support of improved machine performance and sustainability. Perform literature reviews and identify potential applications for relevant models, algorithms, and methods. Collaborate with other team members and external partners to develop and manage experiments which simulate the requirements of the customer. Assist in development, testing, maintenance, and operation of sensing systems for landscape applications. What Do You Need? To be considered for this role, an individual should meet the following minimal requirements: Undergraduate Junior or Senior or Masters candidate in GIS, Computer or Data Science, or relevant Science and Engineering discipline Proficiency with ArcGIS, QGIS, or programmatic spatial data analysis tools (e.g. GDAL, GeoPandas, Shapely, Leaflet, etc.) required Experience with MySQL, PHP, HTML, and JavaScript preferred Must be motivated, self-directed, and able to communicate efficiently with team members What Can We Give You? At The Toro Company, we are always working to make sure our interns know just how valued they are. In addition to a competitive pay- The Toro Company offers interns a variety of perks, including: Dress for your day – We know you're more productive when you're comfortable, which is why TTC employees are encouraged to take advantage of our casual, corporate environment. Volunteerism – The Toro Company is proud to provide interns 8 hours of paid time to volunteer in the community. Summer Hours *Based on Location* – Enjoy a flexible schedule during the summer! By working a little more during the first few days of the week, TTC employees at certain locations are able to start their weekends early and leave by noon on Friday. Competitive Pay – Competitive compensation with an anticipated hourly rate of $22–$28. Actual rates may vary based on factors such as academic standing, business function, and other relevant considerations. The Toro Company is an Equal Opportunity Employer. We consider all qualified applicants based on merit and do not discriminate on the basis of race, color, religion, sex (including pregnancy, gender identity, and sexual orientation), parental status, national origin, age, disability, genetic information, military service, or other non-merit factors. We are committed to creating a welcoming environment for all employees.

jobs.title: Manufacturing Quality Intern, Summer 2027
jobs.location: Fort Myers, FL, United States of America
jobs.body: We’re Watts. Together, we’re reimagining the future of water. We feel proud every day about what we do. We're all part of the same crucial mission, no matter what function we support -- it's to provide safe, clean water for the world, and to protect our planet's most valuable resource. What we do: For 150 years, Watts has built best-in-class products that are trusted by customers in residential and commercial settings across the world. We are at the forefront of innovation, working with cutting-edge technology to provide smart and connected, sustainable water solutions for the future. Watts is a leading brand with a quality reputation — and we have a dynamic future ahead.​ The Watts Internship Program is your chance to bring what you’ve learned in the classroom to life! You’ll dive into real-world projects, gaining hands-on experience while learning how business really works from the inside. During the program, you’ll get to roll up your sleeves and make an impact on day-to-day operations. Plus, you'll have tons of opportunities to network with passionate professionals across manufacturing, industrial engineering, and more—sparking new ideas through cross-department collaboration. It’s all about expanding your skills, challenging yourself, and exploring where your ambitions can take you! Scope of Position As a valued member of the Manufacturing Engineering team, the Manufacturing Quality Intern will contribute to impactful projects that support factory transformation, product line optimization, and production floor redesign. This internship offers hands-on experience in a dynamic manufacturing environment, providing exposure to real-world engineering challenges and opportunities to collaborate across teams. This position reports to the Quality and Sustaining Engineer Supervisor and is onsite in Fort Myers, FL. Primary Job Duties and Responsibilities Collaborate with the Manufacturing Engineering team on the factory transformation initiative, focusing on modernizing workflows, integrating new technologies, and driving process improvements. Support efforts to optimize the MCX/MCX2 product line, a key component of our business, through data analysis, process mapping, and continuous improvement strategies. Assist in the redesign of the production floor layout to enhance operational efficiency, reduce waste, and improve safety and ergonomics. Provide ongoing support for cross-functional engineering projects, including documentation, testing, and implementation activities. Participate in team meetings, brainstorming sessions, and project reviews, gaining exposure to engineering decision-making and project management. Deliver a final presentation summarizing internship learnings, contributions, and outcomes to the leadership team. Required Qualifications Current student (junior or senior status). Pursuing a bachelor’s degree in Engineering. Strong analytical and problem-solving skills with a hands-on approach to learning. Effective communication and collaboration skills. Passionate about your work, with a genuine desire to contribute meaningfully and make an impact. Demonstrated commitment to integrity and respect in interactions with others, fostering a positive and inclusive work environment. Strong sense of accountability, taking ownership of tasks and following through on commitments. Understanding of and adherence to applicable laws, codes, policies, regulations, and safety practices and procedures, as applicable. Must be authorized to work in the United States without requiring sponsorship now or in the future. Must successfully establish employment eligibility and satisfactorily complete background checks and required pre-employment testing as a condition of employment. Preferred Qualifications Preferably pursuing a degree in Industrial, Mechanical, Process, or Manufacturing Engineering. Exposure to Lean Manufacturing principles and Continuous Improvement methodologies. Familiarity with Lean Six Sigma tools and techniques. General Applicable Company Competencies Commitment to Watts’ values of integrity, accountability, continuous improvement and innovation, and transparency. Punctuality and dependability. Ability to be flexible and adapt to changing work priorities and stressful conditions. Adherence to all personnel policies, procedures, and standards of process as implemented by Watts. Maintain productive and collaborative relationships with other Watts employees. Adherence to Watts’ seven cultural beliefs: Growth Mindset, Customer-Focused Innovation, Constant Communication, Clear Goals, Collaborate Globally, Be Inclusive, and Take Action. Working Conditions: While performing the job duties, you will be working on-site at a manufacturing facility and will perform the majority of your duties in an office environment. You may, at times, be required to be present on the manufacturing floor and will be required to wear the appropriate personal protective equipment. You will be required to work in the office at the Fort Myers, FL location (Monday – Friday). Your scheduled work hours will be communicated to you by your manager. Physical Requirements : Specific physical abilities required for this position include, but are not limited to: Ability to remain seated at a desk or workstation for extended periods. Ability to perform repetitive tasks like typing on a keyboard or using a mouse for extended periods. Ability to physically move around the office, organize or transport files, packages, or other office-related materials. Ability to read documents, use a computer, and perform data entry tasks. Ability to communicate clearly with management and coworkers, particularly in meetings or phone calls. Ability to operate standard office equipment such as computers, printers, phones, and copiers. Ability to occasionally lift and carry light objects, such as office supplies, documents, or small equipment. Ability to stand for long periods of time. Ability to lift and carry up to 30 pounds. Ability to push and pull up to 30 pounds. Ability to physically move around manufacturing floor. Ability to read documents and communicate clearly with management and coworkers. Ability to wear personal protective equipment, which may include, but is not limited to, safety shoes, hearing protection, and safety glasses. Pay Range: The expected hourly range for this position is $22- $26 hourly. Actual compensation will be dependent upon individual skills, experience, qualifications, and applicable law. What's In It for You People-First Culture – Enriching and caring for people is at the core of who we are; this includes executing our Diversity, Equity, and Inclusion (DEI) strategy, and providing you with meaningful career growth opportunities, a positive and safe work environment, and affirmation that you are heard, valued, and respected. Flexible PTO Policy – Work-life balance is important at Watts and our interns receive one (1) hour of flexible PTO for every thirty (30) hours worked. Your flexible PTO can be utilized for any type of absence. Paid Holidays – Celebrate the holidays with your loved ones and still get paid! You will receive the following paid holidays off during your time as an Intern with Watts. Where a holiday falls during the weekend, it will be observed on an adjacent weekday. Lunch and Learns – Throughout your internship, there will be opportunities for you to sign up to learn and network with some of the key strategic leaders and thought partners within our core operating model! Sustainability – For five years in a row, Watts has been named one of "America's Most Responsible Companies" by Newsweek. Join our journey as we continue to distinguish Watts as a responsible and committed corporate citizen. Nothing in this job description restricts Watts’ right to assign or reassign duties, responsibilities, and working hours/conditions to this position at any time. This position is “at will,” which means that either the employee or Watts may terminate the employment relationship at any time, with or without notice, and for any lawful reason. #LI (Onsite) Watts in it for you : Please note that the following benefits apply only to permanent roles and do not apply to internship roles. Competitive compensation based on your skills, qualifications and experience Comprehensive medical and dental coverage, retirement benefits Family building benefits, including paid maternity/paternity leave 10 paid holidays and Paid Time Off Continued professional development opportunities and educational reimbursement Additional perks such as fitness reimbursements and employee discount programs Learn more about our benefit offerings here: https://tapintowattsbenefits.com/ How we work: At Watts, our culture is team-oriented and supportive. Employees here genuinely care about the quality of their work, and about each other. Our people are the heart of who we are and contribute to our longevity and continued success. And this is a place where you can have a big career. No matter your role, there are opportunities for learning and development, and your daily contributions make a meaningful impact on the lives of people who use our products and on the future of water. Watts is committed to equal employment opportunity. We follow a policy of administering all employment decisions and personnel actions without regard to race, color, religion, creed, sex, pregnancy, national origin, sexual orientation, age, physical or mental disability, genetic disposition or carrier status, marital status, military or veteran status, minorities, or any other category protected under applicable federal, state, or local law. We design and develop labeling and functional materials, radio-frequency identification (RFID) inlays and tags, software applications that connect the physical and digital and offerings that enhance branded packaging and carry or display information that improves the customer experience. Serving industries worldwide — including home and personal care, apparel, general retail, e-commerce, logistics, food and grocery, pharmaceuticals and automotive — we employ approximately 35,000 employees in nearly 60 countries. We’re seeking an RFID Applications Engineer Co-Op to join our business in North America during the summer. jobs.body: If you are an engineering student looking for an opportunity to grow, Emerson has an exciting opportunity for you! Maintain accurate technical documentation and support communication among engineering, manufacturing, and project teams. Contribute to cross-functional problem solving and process improvement efforts throughout the project lifecycle. You communicate clearly and effectively in a variety of settings, tailoring your message to different audiences. You build partnerships and work collaboratively with others to meet shared objectives. You seek out information, learn from new experiences, and adapt your approach to support successful outcomes. For This Role, You Will Need: Currently enrolled in an accredited college/university and pursing a Bachelor of Science or Master of Science degree in an engineering, technical, business discipline Commitment to full-time (40 hour) Summer/Fall (June 2027-December 2027) Co-op experience in St. Louis, MO Legal authorization to work in the United States. Sponsorship will not be provided for this position. Preferred Qualifications That Set You Apart: Previous co-op or intern experience a plus Demonstrated leadership skills (served in leadership role in student organization) Previous coursework involving automation, PLC, process controls, or simulation Technical curiosity and an eagerness to understand how products, systems, and processes work. Our Culture & Commitment to You: At Emerson, we prioritize a workplace where every employee is valued, respected, and empowered to grow. We foster an environment that encourages innovation, collaboration, and diverse perspectives—because we know that great ideas come from great teams. Our commitment to ongoing career development and growing an inclusive culture ensures you have the support to thrive. Whether through mentorship, training, or leadership opportunities, we invest in your success so you can make a lasting impact. We believe diverse teams, working together are key to driving growth and delivering business results. We recognize the importance of employee wellbeing and know that to do your best you must have flexible, competitive benefits plans to meet you and your family’s physical, mental, financial, and social needs. We provide, a variety of medical insurance plans, with dental and vision coverage, Employee Assistance Program, profit sharing retirement, tuition reimbursement, employee resource groups, recognition, and much more. Our culture prioritizes work-life balance and offers flexible time off plans, including paid parental leave (maternal and paternal), vacation and holiday leave. Our training programs and initiatives focus on end-to-end development, from onboarding through senior leadership. We provide a wide range of development opportunities, including face-to-face and virtual training, mentorship and coaching, project management, and on-the-job training. Our compensation philosophy is simple: we pay a competitive base salary, within the local market in which we operate, and reward performance during our annual merit review process. jobs.body: About Pierce, an Oshkosh company At Pierce Manufacturing, we build trucks that protect people and communities around the world. To our team, there is no room for anything less than providing the absolute best. Since 1913, building truck bodies on Model T Ford chassis in an old converted church has evolved to creating highly customized, carefully designed and engineering pumpers, aerials, tankers and rescue units that have no equal. Today, you'll find more than 30,000 Pierce apparatuses on the road that are making a difference in people's lives, every day. To us, every step in the process of building our trucks is personal. From innovation and expertise, to the customization and service. Our trucks are designed to perform under the toughest conditions. SUMMARY Assist and support the Materials department within Pierce Manufacturing. This role will utilize analytical skills to identify opportunities and develop solutions that result in optimal material flow at the lowest total landed cost. Develop process improvements within the Materials department. Support standardization, advancement and implementation of a lean enterprise material flow strategy. Run and compile various reports as well as run various data analytics to understand the data Assist in the continuous improvement techniques including Continuous Improvement events and 5S. jobs.location: Burlingame, CA
jobs.body: Job Title: Automation Engineering Intern Location: Burlingame, CA Department: Manufacturing Engineering Reports to: Luke Anderson Position Type: Internship (3, 6, or 9 months available) Start Date: Fall/Winter 2026 Compensation: $30–$35/hour About the Company Peak Energy is the first American venture to advance globally proven Sodium-Ion battery systems as the storage standard for the new era of renewable energy on a resilient grid. Sodium-Ion is cheap, readily available and safe, making it the leading contender in a rapidly evolving market. Our leadership team is powered by decades of expertise in scaling gigawatt-level innovation at world-class companies such as Tesla, Northvolt, SunPower, Fluence, and Enovix. We are backed by strategic investment and product partners such as TDK Ventures and Eclipse Ventures. We are a team of engineers, technicians, entrepreneurs, and partners driven by a shared ambition to set the new performance standard for renewable energy and grid resilience. About the Job Peak Energy is seeking a motivated Automation Engineering Intern to join our Manufacturing Engineering team supporting Battery Energy Storage System (BESS) manufacturing automation. This is a hands-on internship focused on gaining direct exposure to the PLC, SCADA, and HMI systems that keep our production lines running safely and efficiently. You will work closely with senior Controls Engineers, Equipment Engineers, and Process Engineers, contributing to real automation projects that support Peak Energy's work scaling ESS production toward 1 GWh/year capacity by 2027. One day you might be helping commission a PLC program on the pilot line; another, you could be out on the production floor troubleshooting a control system fault alongside a senior engineer, or documenting a new HMI screen for operators. You'll have the opportunity to contribute to meaningful projects and build real, hands-on experience with the tools and systems used in industrial automation. If you want to actually contribute as part of the team, not just observe from the sidelines, we'd love for you to apply. Responsibilities: Support the programming, testing, and commissioning of PLC, SCADA, and HMI systems for BESS manufacturing equipment, under the guidance of senior Controls Engineers. Partner with Equipment Engineers to help integrate automation solutions into new and existing manufacturing equipment. Help analyze production processes and identify opportunities for automation and control improvements. Support the implementation and upkeep of data acquisition systems, helping collect and organize production data for Process and Automation Engineers to analyze. Assist in maintaining safety systems, such as emergency shutdown procedures and safety interlocks. Help troubleshoot control system issues on the manufacturing floor alongside senior engineers, and support routine maintenance of automation systems. Collaborate with Process Engineers, Equipment Engineers, and Maintenance to ensure control systems support production needs. Contribute to documentation of control system designs, revisions, and updates, and support operator and maintenance training materials. Participate in hands-on testing and validation of automation equipment and control system changes. Minimum Qualifications: Pursuing or recently completed a degree in Electrical Engineering, Controls/Automation Engineering, or a related engineering field. Foundational knowledge of PLC programming, SCADA systems, and HMI design principles, gained through coursework, capstone projects, or hands-on experience. Hands-on experience building, testing, troubleshooting, or modifying automation or control systems through coursework, student projects, internships, research, or personal projects. Strong problem-solving and analytical skills, with a willingness to learn and take direction from senior engineers. Clear communicator who works well in cross-functional teams. Available to work onsite in Burlingame, CA for a 3-, 6-, or 9-month internship term. Eligible to work in the U.S. Preferred Qualifications: Exposure to industrial automation platforms (e.g., Beckhoff TwinCAT, Allen-Bradley, or Siemens) through coursework or hands-on projects. Familiarity with data acquisition or historian platforms, such as Ignition by Inductive Automation. Previous automation, controls, or manufacturing engineering internship or project experience. Basic understanding of environmental and safety regulations relevant to controls and automation in manufacturing. Eagerness to adapt to new technologies and grow technical skills in a fast-paced manufacturing environment. Peak Energy Core Values Speed Through Focus: Prioritize what matters most and execute quickly without distractions. Mission Over Self: Put the company's mission and team success ahead of individual interests. Face the Brutal Truth: Embrace honesty, even when it's uncomfortable, to make informed decisions. Be a Good Person: Treat everyone with respect and integrity, fostering a positive and ethical work environment. Compensation and Benefits The pay for this role is $30–$35/hour. You'll gain hands-on experience with cutting-edge energy storage technology and mentorship from experienced controls and automation engineers while contributing directly to Peak Energy's mission to scale sustainable battery manufacturing. At Peak Energy Technologies Inc., we believe that a diverse and inclusive workplace makes us a more capable, innovative, and competitive company. We welcome people who represent diversity in their backgrounds, ethnicities, cultures, and experiences. Peak Energy Technologies Inc. is an equal opportunity employer, aiming to reach our company's full potential by cultivating an inclusive workforce. We do not discriminate on the basis of race, color, ancestry, religion, national origin, sexual orientation, citizenship, marital or family status, disability, gender identity or expression, veteran status, or any other legally protected status.

jobs.body: Stanley Black & Decker Co-Op Engineering 2027 Onsite: Valley City, OH Make Your Mark. Shape Your Future. It takes great people to achieve greatness. People with a sense of purpose and integrity. People with a relentless pursuit of excellence. People who care about making things better For Those Who Make The World™. Sound like you? Join our top-notch team of more than 50,000 diverse and high-performing professionals globally who are making their mark on some of the world’s most beloved brands, including DEWALT®, BLACK+DECKER®, CRAFTSMAN®, STANLEY®and CUB CADET® The exciting, full-time, paid Co-op internship program aligns with the standard Fall, Spring and Summer semester schedule. jobs.title: Social Community Intern - The Toro Company
jobs.location: Bloomington, MN, United States of America
jobs.body: The 2027 Summer Internship Program will run from May 17, 2027, through August 6, 2027. Candidates must be available to start on May 17 and participate through the duration of the program. Applicants must be legally authorized to work in the United States. We are unable to sponsor or take over sponsorship of a school/employment or any other visa, regardless of expiration date, now or in the future. Who Are We? The Toro Company (TTC) has delivered market-leading, innovative products and outstanding customer care for more than 100 years. With over 11,000 employees worldwide, TTC is headquartered in Bloomington, Minnesota, USA. Our company designs and manufactures turf maintenance equipment; turf irrigation systems; landscape and lighting products; snow and ice management solutions; agricultural irrigation systems; rental, specialty and underground construction equipment; and residential turf and snow equipment. We market and sell TTC products worldwide through a network of distributors, dealers, mass retailers, hardware retailers, equipment rental center and home centers—as well as online direct to end users. As a Social Community Intern, you’ll help bring Toro’s brand to life across social media by supporting content creation, engaging with online communities, and monitoring social media activity. You’ll use research, customer feedback, and performance metrics to identify trends, share insights, and help strengthen Toro’s social presence while ensuring content aligns with Toro and RLC brand guidelines. What Will You Do? In order to grow and build a successful career with The Toro Company, you will be responsible for: Coordinate social media calendar, programming and (platform) content publishing. Follow the content and messaging hierarchy, content types, tone, voice and creative interpretation of content to ensure alignment with brand marketing and business objectives. Create and monitor social listening and reporting dashboards. Respond to comments and customer queries in a timely manner. Collaborate with marketing, sales, and customer service teams to craft. Engage in online conversations with prospective and existing customers about our topics in our industry, products, and brand. Monitor social media campaigns, analyze web traffic from the online community using key performance indicators (KPIs) and provide insights and recommendations based on sentiments, traffic data, follower trends, and more. Provide community feedback to the management and stakeholders. Provide insights to our marketing team about industry, competitors, and relevant topics found online. Stay up to date with digital technology/social media trends. Align with content matrices and (editorial) calendars to track and manage content updates. Support efforts to ensure Toro RLC content is usable, findable, targeted by audience, aligned with best practices and business goals, and is developed with consideration of competitive analysis and research. What Do You Need? To be considered for this role, an individual should meet the following minimal requirements: Enrollment in a degree program in Communications, Marketing or similar field preferred. Familiarity with customer engagement software, including Sprinklr and Bazaarvoice preferred. Working knowledge of Adobe Creative Suite programs including Photoshop, Premiere Pro, and XD preferred. Mastery of the major social media platforms including Facebook, YouTube, Instagram, TikTok and Twitter. Clear, concise communicator with the ability to flex communication to audience. Ability to discern, communicate, and uphold online community guidelines. Must be extremely well-organized, capable of handling multiple details simultaneously, and able to easily move between strategic and tactical work. Excellent verbal, written and presentation skills. Proficient with Microsoft Office suite. What Can We Give You? At The Toro Company, we are always working to make sure our interns know just how valued they are. In addition to a competitive pay- The Toro Company offers interns a variety of perks, including: Dress for your day – We know you're more productive when you're comfortable, which is why TTC employees are encouraged to take advantage of our casual, corporate environment. Volunteerism – The Toro Company is proud to provide interns 8 hours of paid time to volunteer in the community. Summer Hours *Based on Location* – Enjoy a flexible schedule during the summer! By working a little more during the first few days of the week, TTC employees at certain locations are able to start their weekends early and leave by noon on Friday. Competitive Pay – Competitive compensation with an anticipated hourly rate of $20–$24. Actual rates may vary based on factors such as academic standing, business function, and other relevant considerations. The Toro Company is an Equal Opportunity Employer. We consider all qualified applicants based on merit and do not discriminate on the basis of race, color, religion, sex (including pregnancy, gender identity, and sexual orientation), parental status, national origin, age, disability, genetic information, military service, or other non-merit factors. We are committed to creating a welcoming environment for all employees.

We are at the forefront of innovation, working with cutting-edge technology to provide smart and connected, sustainable water solutions for the future. Watts is a leading brand with a quality reputation — and we have a dynamic future ahead.​ The Watts Internship Program is your chance to bring what you’ve learned in the classroom to life! You’ll dive into real-world projects, gaining hands-on experience while learning how business really works from the inside. During the program, you’ll get to roll up your sleeves and make an impact on day-to-day operations. Plus, you'll have tons of opportunities to network with passionate professionals across manufacturing, industrial engineering, and more—sparking new ideas through cross-department collaboration. It’s all about expanding your skills, challenging yourself, and exploring where your ambitions can take you! Scope of Position This motivated and detail-oriented individual, as part of the Systems Engineering team, will support training initiatives by updating internal and external training materials. The Applications Engineering Intern will develop presentation templates and refresh existing documents to improve consistency, align with branding guidelines, and support effective training. This position reports to the Senior Manager of Systems Engineering. This role is onsite and is based in Blauvelt, NY. Primary Job Duties and Responsibilities Learn and apply the branding guidelines for four Watts entities. Create presentation templates for branded and generic training materials. Update outdated presentations and other training documents to align with current branding guidelines. Support Watts’ goals for quality and customer focus by developing clear, consistent training materials and contributing as a functional team member. Demonstrate respect for coworkers through daily interactions and collaboration. Assume responsibility for other projects and duties as assigned by the Senior Manager of Systems Engineering or Company management. Proficient in Microsoft Office Suite, including Word, Excel, and PowerPoint. Passionate about your work, with a genuine desire to contribute meaningfully and make an impact. Demonstrated commitment to integrity and respect in interactions with others, fostering a positive and inclusive work environment. Strong sense of accountability, taking ownership of tasks and following through on commitments. Understanding of and adherence to applicable laws, codes, policies, regulations, and safety practices and procedures, as applicable. Must successfully establish employment eligibility and satisfactorily complete background checks, including required pre-employment testing as a condition of employment. Preferred Qualifications Experience creating presentation templates or training materials through coursework, projects, or previous internships. Familiarity with branding guidelines, visual consistency, and document formatting. Experience organizing technical information into clear, accessible content for different audiences. General Applicable Company Competencies Commitment to Watts’ values of integrity, accountability, continuous improvement and innovation, and transparency. Punctuality and dependability. Ability to be flexible and adapt to changing work priorities and stressful conditions. Adherence to all personnel policies, procedures, and standards of process as implemented by Watts. Maintain productive and collaborative relationships with other Watts employees. Adherence to Watts’ seven cultural beliefs: Growth Mindset, Customer-Focused Innovation, Constant Communication, Clear Goals, Collaborate Globally, Be Inclusive, and Take Action. You will work at the Blauvelt, NY location Monday–Friday. Your scheduled work hours will be communicated to you by your manager. Physical Requirements : Specific physical abilities required for this position include, but are not limited to: Ability to sit, stand, and walk while performing assigned duties. Ability to physically move around the office, manufacturing floor, and Engineering Test Facility. Ability to use hands to handle objects, tools, and other materials. Ability to read documents, use a computer, and perform data entry tasks. Ability to communicate clearly and effectively with management and coworkers. Ability to operate standard office equipment such as computers, printers, phones, and copiers. Ability to occasionally lift, push, and pull up to 25 pounds. Visual abilities necessary to perform assigned duties, including close vision, distance vision, color vision, peripheral vision, depth perception, and the ability to adjust focus. Ability to wear appropriate personal protective equipment, which may include safety shoes, hearing protection, and safety glasses. Pay Range : $22–$26 The expected hourly range for this position is $22–$26 hourly. Actual compensation will be dependent upon individual skills, experience, qualifications, and applicable law. Your flexible PTO can be utilized for any type of absence. Paid Holidays – Celebrate the holidays with your loved ones and still get paid! You will receive paid holidays off during your time as an Intern with Watts. Where a holiday falls during the weekend, it will be observed on an adjacent weekday. jobs.body: We’re Watts. Together, we’re reimagining the future of water. We feel proud every day about what we do. We're all part of the same crucial mission, no matter what function we support -- it's to provide safe, clean water for the world, and to protect our planet's most valuable resource. What we do: For 150 years, Watts has built best-in-class products that are trusted by customers in residential and commercial settings across the world. We are at the forefront of innovation, working with cutting-edge technology to provide smart and connected, sustainable water solutions for the future. Watts is a leading brand with a quality reputation — and we have a dynamic future ahead.​ The Watts Internship Program is your chance to bring what you’ve learned in the classroom to life! You’ll dive into real-world projects, gaining hands-on experience while learning how business really works from the inside. During the program, you’ll get to roll up your sleeves and make an impact on day-to-day operations. Plus, you'll have tons of opportunities to network with passionate professionals across manufacturing, industrial engineering, and more—sparking new ideas through cross-department collaboration. It’s all about expanding your skills, challenging yourself, and exploring where your ambitions can take you! Scope of Position This innovative and detail-oriented individual, as part of the Operations team, will support the identification and implementation of shop floor process improvements aimed at increasing efficiency, reducing costs, and enhancing production output. The Manufacturing Engineering Intern will work with cross-functional teams to support continuous improvement initiatives and gain hands-on experience with manufacturing processes. This position reports to the Senior Manager of Advanced Manufacturing & Continuous Improvement. This role is onsite and is based in St. Pauls, NC. Primary Job Duties and Responsibilities Help create and maintain shop floor work instructions, including specifications, engineering changes, process controls, and tooling requirements. Participate in lean manufacturing initiatives that support continuous process improvement. Collaborate with hourly employees and teams across Quality, Safety, Sourcing, and other functions on manufacturing projects. Support the scoping, planning, and execution of manufacturing engineering requests under the guidance of the Manufacturing Engineering team, including improving manufacturing efficiency, implementing engineering changes, improving product quality, and addressing production line technical issues. Analyze and document existing manufacturing processes to identify improvement opportunities. Support Watts’ commitment to continuous improvement by identifying process inefficiencies, communicating findings transparently, and taking accountability for assigned project deliverables. Assume responsibility for other projects and duties as assigned by the Manufacturing Engineer Manager or Company management. Required Qualifications Current student (sophomore, junior or senior status). Pursuing a degree in Manufacturing, Mechanical, or Industrial Engineering. Ability to present complex data effectively through charts, tables, graphs, and pivot tables. Ability to work independently and manage assigned tasks with appropriate guidance. Ability to communicate professionally and effectively with colleagues across departments and levels of the organization. Passionate about your work, with a genuine desire to contribute meaningfully and make an impact. Demonstrated commitment to integrity and respect in interactions with others, fostering a positive and inclusive work environment. Strong sense of accountability, taking ownership of tasks and following through on commitments. Understanding of and adherence to applicable laws, codes, policies, regulations, and safety practices and procedures, as applicable. Must be authorized to work in the United States without requiring sponsorship now or in the future. Must successfully establish employment eligibility and satisfactorily complete background checks, including required pre-employment testing as a condition of employment. Preferred Qualifications Knowledge of Lean manufacturing principles. Familiarity with quality standards and process improvement methodologies, such as Six Sigma. General Applicable Company Competencies Commitment to Watts’ values of integrity, accountability, continuous improvement and innovation, and transparency. Punctuality and dependability. Ability to be flexible and adapt to changing work priorities and stressful conditions. Adherence to all personnel policies, procedures, and standards of process as implemented by Watts. Maintain productive and collaborative relationships with other Watts employees. Adherence to Watts’ seven cultural beliefs: Growth Mindset, Customer-Focused Innovation, Constant Communication, Clear Goals, Collaborate Globally, Be Inclusive, and Take Action. Working Conditions While performing the job duties, you will be working on-site at a manufacturing facility and will perform the majority of your duties in an office environment. You may, at times, be required to be present on the manufacturing floor and will be required to wear the appropriate personal protective equipment. You will be required to work in the office at the St. Pauls, NC location (Monday–Friday). Your scheduled work hours will be communicated to you by your manager. Physical Requirements Specific physical abilities required for this position include, but are not limited to: Ability to remain seated at a desk or workstation for extended periods. Ability to physically move around the office, organize or transport files, packages, or other office-related materials. Ability to read documents, use a computer, and perform data entry tasks. Ability to communicate clearly with management and coworkers, particularly in meetings or phone calls. Ability to operate standard office equipment such as computers, printers, phones, and copiers. Ability to stand for long periods of time. Ability to lift and carry up to 20 pounds. Ability to push and pull up to 20 pounds. Ability to physically move around the manufacturing floor. Ability to read documents and communicate clearly with management and coworkers. Ability to wear personal protective equipment, which may include, but is not limited to, safety shoes, hearing protection, and safety glasses. Pay Range: $21-27 The expected hourly range for this position is $21–27 hourly. Actual compensation will be dependent upon individual skills, experience, qualifications, and applicable law. What’s In It for You People-First Culture – Enriching and caring for people is at the core of who we are; this includes executing our Diversity, Equity, and Inclusion (DEI) strategy, and providing you with meaningful career growth opportunities, a positive and safe work environment, and affirmation that you are heard, valued, and respected. Flexible PTO Policy – Work-life balance is important at Watts and our interns receive one (1) hour of flexible PTO for every thirty (30) hours worked. Your flexible PTO can be utilized for any type of absence. Paid Holidays – Celebrate the holidays with your loved ones and still get paid! You will receive the following paid holidays off during your time as an Intern with Watts. Where a holiday falls during the weekend, it will be observed on an adjacent weekday. Lunch and Learns – Throughout your internship, there will be opportunities for you to sign up to learn and network with some of the key strategic leaders and thought partners within our core operating model! Sustainability – For five years in a row, Watts has been named one of "America's Most Responsible Companies" by Newsweek. Join our journey as we continue to distinguish Watts as a responsible and committed corporate citizen. Nothing in this job description restricts Watts’ right to assign or reassign duties, responsibilities, and working hours/conditions to this position at any time. This position is “at will,” which means that either the employee or Watts may terminate the employment relationship at any time, with or without notice, and for any lawful reason. #LI-Onsite Watts in it for you : Please note that the following benefits apply only to permanent roles and do not apply to internship roles. Employees here genuinely care about the quality of their work, and about each other. Our people are the heart of who we are and contribute to our longevity and continued success. And this is a place where you can have a big career. No matter your role, there are opportunities for learning and development, and your daily contributions make a meaningful impact on the lives of people who use our products and on the future of water. jobs.body: We’re Watts. Together, we’re reimagining the future of water. We feel proud every day about what we do. What we do: For 150 years, Watts has built best-in-class products that are trusted by customers in residential and commercial settings across the world. We are at the forefront of innovation, working with cutting-edge technology to provide smart and connected, sustainable water solutions for the future. Watts is a leading brand with a quality reputation — and we have a dynamic future ahead.​ The Watts Internship Program is your chance to bring what you’ve learned in the classroom to life! You’ll dive into real-world projects, gaining hands-on experience while learning how business really works from the inside. During the program, you’ll get to roll up your sleeves and make an impact on day-to-day operations. Plus, you'll have tons of opportunities to network with passionate professionals across manufacturing, industrial engineering, and more—sparking new ideas through cross-department collaboration. It’s all about expanding your skills, challenging yourself, and exploring where your ambitions can take you! Scope of Position This innovative individual, as part of the Product Management team, will be responsible for providing daily and ongoing product and project support, including new product development coordination, product documentation, and collateral and label development. The Product Specialist Intern will collaborate with cross-functional teams to support product launches, organize product information, and assist with product-related issues. This position reports to the Senior Product Manager. This role is onsite and is based in Fort Myers, Florida. Primary Job Duties and Responsibilities Assist the Product Management team with product documentation, label creation, and marketing collateral updates. Support cross-functional teams during new product development by tracking tasks and maintaining project timelines. Collaborate with Engineering and Product Development to support new product launches and help keep projects on schedule and within budget. Gather and organize product data, including specifications, product requirements, and feedback from internal teams. Update databases and collect information to support the development of business cases. Help identify and report product-related issues, working closely with Engineering and Customer Support. Create product documentation and sales collateral for sales and technical presentations. Support dashboard development and data analysis to help the team monitor product performance. Learn and apply foundational product management principles under the guidance of the Senior Product Manager. Assume responsibility for other projects and duties as assigned by the Senior Product Manager or Company management. Demonstrate integrity, accountability, continuous improvement, and transparency by maintaining accurate product information, taking ownership of assigned tasks, identifying process improvements, and clearly communicating project updates. Required Qualifications Current student (sophomore, junior or senior status). Pursuing a degree in Engineering, Marketing, Business Administration, or a related field. Technical competency in understanding and preparing documentation for technical systems. Proficiency in Microsoft Office applications. Passionate about your work, with a genuine desire to contribute meaningfully and make an impact. Demonstrated commitment to integrity and respect in interactions with others, fostering a positive and inclusive work environment. Strong sense of accountability, taking ownership of tasks and following through on commitments. Understanding of and adherence to applicable laws, codes, policies, regulations, and safety practices and procedures, as applicable. Must be authorized to work in the United States without requiring sponsorship now or in the future. Must successfully establish employment eligibility and satisfactorily complete background checks and required pre-employment testing as a condition of employment. Preferred Qualifications Engineering focus with a minor in Marketing or Business. Interest in gaining experience in Product Management. Familiarity with Microsoft Teams and SharePoint. Experience with or exposure to Power BI, dashboard development, and data analysis through coursework, academic projects, or previous internships. General Applicable Company Competencies Commitment to Watts’ values of integrity, accountability, continuous improvement and innovation, and transparency. Punctuality and dependability. Ability to be flexible and adapt to changing work priorities and stressful conditions. Adherence to all personnel policies, procedures, and standards of process as implemented by Watts. Maintain productive and collaborative relationships with other Watts employees. Adherence to Watts’ seven cultural beliefs: Growth Mindset, Customer-Focused Innovation, Constant Communication, Clear Goals, Collaborate Globally, Be Inclusive, and Take Action. Working Conditions: While performing the job duties, you will be working on-site at a manufacturing facility and will perform the majority of your duties in an office environment. You may, at times, be required to be present on the manufacturing floor and will be required to wear the appropriate personal protective equipment. You will be required to work in the office at the Fort Myers location (Monday – Friday). Your scheduled work hours will be communicated to you by your manager. Physical Requirements : Specific physical abilities required for this position include, but are not limited to: Ability to remain seated at a desk or workstation for extended periods. Ability to physically move around the office, organize or transport files, packages, or other office-related materials. Ability to read documents, use a computer, and perform data entry tasks. Ability to communicate clearly with management and coworkers, particularly in meetings or phone calls. Ability to operate standard office equipment such as computers, printers, phones, and copiers. Ability to stand for long periods of time. Ability to lift and carry up to 20 pounds. Ability to push and pull up to 20 pounds. Ability to physically move around manufacturing floor. Ability to read documents and communicate clearly with management and coworkers. Ability to wear personal protective equipment, which may include, but is not limited to, safety shoes, hearing protection, and safety glasses. Pay Range : $21-27 The expected hourly range for this position is $21-27. Actual compensation will be dependent upon individual skills, experience, qualifications, and applicable law. What's In It for You People-First Culture – Enriching and caring for people is at the core of who we are; this includes executing our Diversity, Equity, and Inclusion (DEI) strategy, and providing you with meaningful career growth opportunities, a positive and safe work environment, and affirmation that you are heard, valued, and respected. Your flexible PTO can be utilized for any type of absence. Paid Holidays – Celebrate the holidays with your loved ones and still get paid! Sustainability – For five years in a row, Watts has been named one of "America's Most Responsible Companies" by Newsweek. Join our journey as we continue to distinguish Watts as a responsible and committed corporate citizen. jobs.body: The Bosch Group is a leading global supplier of technology and services. BGSV nowadays have over 4,000 associates, with a global footprint and presence in the US, Europe, and the Asia Pacific region. With our unique ability to offer end-to-end solutions that connect sensors, software, and services, we enable businesses to move from the traditional to digital or improve businesses by introducing a digital element in their products and processes. Model Development: Assist in developing and implementing AI/ML models, focusing on Generative AI. Research and Analysis: Stay updated on AI trends; analyze data for model improvements. jobs.body: Bosch first started its operations in Vietnam in 1994 and registered a wholly-owned subsidiary in 2008. jobs.title: Project Coordinator Intern (Summer 2027)
jobs.location: Hagerstown, MD, United States of America
jobs.body: Come start your career with some of the brightest and most innovative minds in the country! As a Project Coordinator Intern, you will participate in a comprehensive summer internship program designed to provide hands-on experience in a dynamic aerospace and defense environment. You will work alongside industry experts, contribute to real-world projects, and develop valuable technical and professional skills. This internship offers a unique opportunity for growth through mentoring, cross-functional workshops, and direct involvement in company projects. The ISR (Intelligence, Surveillance & Reconnaissance), Aviation, and Security (IAS) business area is a leader in ISR and aviation, it is a leading prime manned and unmanned aircraft systems integrator for innovative, high-performance ISR and aviation systems. Its end-to-end Command, Control, Computers, Communications and Intelligence, Surveillance & Reconnaissance (C4ISR) capabilities encompass design, integration, test, certification, ground/flight training and complete logistics support. IAS tailors solutions to customer cost, performance, and schedule requirements and designs to consistently exceed expectations – with an unrivaled record of on time and on (or under) budget deliveries. Responsibilities: Participate in actual technical projects and contribute to team objectives by completing assigned tasks. Receive guidance and mentorship from experienced industry professionals in your field. Prepare and maintain technical documentation, reports, and records as required. Assist in collecting, analyzing, and interpreting technical data to support engineering decisions. Attend planning meetings to understand project requirements, timelines, and team goals. Perform hands-on technical work assignments to gain practical experience and build technical skills. Work closely with team members, absorb and learn from their expertise, and apply that learning to ongoing projects. Identify opportunities for process improvements and support the implementation of best practices. Participate in workshops designed to provide a deeper understanding of the business and company culture. Qualifications You Must Have: Must be a Sophomore, Junior, or Senior in college or technical school, with at least 6 months until graduation after end of internship. Currently enrolled in a university or college program pursuing a degree in Engineering, Computer Science, or a related technical field. Strong analytical and problem-solving skills. Strong skills in Word, Excel, PowerPoint and Visio. Ability to work in a highly collaborative team environment. Strong organization skills and work ethic; detail oriented. The ability to obtain and maintain a Secret U.S. Security Clearance is required Qualifications We Prefer: Prior internship or work experience in a technical or engineering role. Familiarity with the Aerospace and Defense industry. Basic knowledge of engineering software tools (e.g., CAD, MATLAB). Microsoft Access skills. Pursuing a degree in engineering or a related discipline. Essential Functions: Ability to sit at a computer for extended periods. Proficiency with computers and office equipment. Manual dexterity for handling tools and technical equipment. Ability to lift up to 25 lbs occasionally. Ability to work in a laboratory or workshop environment, which may involve exposure to loud noise levels or hazardous conditions. Ability to travel may be required. This posting will be open for application for a minimum of 5 days and may be extended based on business needs. Estimated Starting Salary Range: $16.48 - $28.84. Compensation varies depending on a wide array of factors, such as candidates' key skills, relevant work experience, and education/training/certifications. The disclosed range estimate may be adjusted for any applicable geographic differential associated with the location at which the position may be filled. SNC offers a generous benefit package, including medical, dental, and vision plans, 401(k) with 150% match up to 6%, life insurance, 3 weeks paid time off, tuition reimbursement, and more . IMPORTANT NOTICE: This position requires the ability to obtain and maintain a Secret U.S. Security Clearance. U.S. Citizenship status is required as this position needs an active U.S. Security Clearance for employment. Non-U.S. citizens may not be eligible to obtain a security clearance. The Department of Defense Consolidated Adjudications Facility (DoD CAF), a federal government agency, handles the adjudicative aspects of the security clearance eligibility process for industry applicants. Adjudicative factors which affect the outcome of the eligibility determination include, but are not limited to, allegiance to the U.S., foreign influence, foreign preference, criminal conduct, security violations and illegal drug use. Learn more about the background check process for Security Clearances. SNC is a global leader in aerospace and national security committed to moving the American Dream forward. We’re known and respected for our mission and execution focus, agility, and disruptive and rapid innovation. We provide leading edge technologies and transformative solutions that support our nation’s most critical security needs. If you are mission-focused, thrive in collaborative environments, and want to make our country stronger with state-of-the-art technologies that safeguard freedom, join our team! SNC is an Equal Opportunity Employer committed to an environment free of discrimination. Employment decisions are made based on merit without regard to race, color, age, religion, sex, national origin, disability, status as a protected veteran or other characteristics protected by law.

jobs.body: We’re Watts. Together, we’re reimagining the future of water. We feel proud every day about what we do. We're all part of the same crucial mission, no matter what function we support -- it's to provide safe, clean water for the world, and to protect our planet's most valuable resource. What we do: For 150 years, Watts has built best-in-class products that are trusted by customers in residential and commercial settings across the world. We are at the forefront of innovation, working with cutting-edge technology to provide smart and connected, sustainable water solutions for the future. Watts is a leading brand with a quality reputation — and we have a dynamic future ahead.​ The Watts Internship Program is your chance to bring what you’ve learned in the classroom to life! You’ll dive into real-world projects, gaining hands-on experience while learning how business really works from the inside. During the program, you’ll get to roll up your sleeves and make an impact on day-to-day operations. Plus, you'll have tons of opportunities to network with passionate professionals across manufacturing, industrial engineering, and more—sparking new ideas through cross-department collaboration. It’s all about expanding your skills, challenging yourself, and exploring where your ambitions can take you! What You’ll Do We are seeking a motivated and detail-oriented intern to join our Quality and Production Engineering Team. This role offers a unique opportunity to gain hands-on experience in a fast-paced manufacturing environment while contributing to meaningful projects that support operational excellence. Key responsibilities include: Support Production Engineers by contributing to project execution and daily operational tasks. Collaborate with cross-functional teams including Purchasing, Sustaining Engineering, and Production Supervisors to advance project goals. Design and develop fixturing and tooling solutions to enhance production cell efficiency. Create and revise factory floor layouts to optimize space utilization and workflow. Engage directly with production cells and operators on the factory floor to observe, learn, and support operations. Proficient in Microsoft Office Suite, including Word, Excel, and PowerPoint. Demonstrates a strong passion for engineering and a genuine desire to contribute meaningfully to team objectives. Committed to integrity, respect, and fostering a positive, inclusive work environment. Exhibits a strong sense of accountability, with the ability to take ownership of tasks and follow through on commitments. Must be authorized to work in the United States without current or future sponsorship requirements. The expected salary range for this position is $22 - $26 an hour. Actual compensation will be dependent upon individual skills, experience, qualifications, and applicable laws. What’s In It for You People-First Culture – Enriching and caring for people is at the core of who we are; this includes executing our Diversity, Equity, and Inclusion (DEI) strategy, and providing you with meaningful career growth opportunities, a positive and safe work environment, and affirmation that you are heard, valued, and respected. Flexible PTO Policy – Work-life balance is important at Watts and our interns receive one (1) hour of flexible PTO for every thirty (30) hours worked. Your flexible PTO can be utilized for any type of absence. Paid Holidays – Celebrate the holidays with your loved ones and still get paid! You will receive paid holidays off during your time as an Intern with Watts. Where a holiday falls during the weekend, it will be observed on an adjacent weekday. Lunch and Learns – Throughout your internship, there will be opportunities for you to sign up to learn and network with some of the key strategic leaders and thought partners within our core operating model! Sustainability – For five years in a row, Watts has been named one of "America's Most Responsible Companies" by Newsweek. Join our journey as we continue to distinguish Watts as a responsible and committed corporate citizen. Working Conditions Work in both office and manufacturing environment. May occasionally be required to perform job responsibilities outside the typical office setting. While performing the responsibilities of this job, the employee is frequently required to walk, talk, and/or hear. The employee is occasionally required to stand, sit, and use hands to finger, handle, or feel. You must occasionally lift and/or move up to 25 pounds. Specific vision abilities required by this job include: close vision, color vision, peripheral vision, depth perception and ability to adjust focus. Watts in it for you : Please note that the following benefits apply only to permanent roles and do not apply to internship roles. Competitive compensation based on your skills, qualifications and experience Comprehensive medical and dental coverage, retirement benefits Family building benefits, including paid maternity/paternity leave 10 paid holidays and Paid Time Off Continued professional development opportunities and educational reimbursement Additional perks such as fitness reimbursements and employee discount programs Learn more about our benefit offerings here: https://tapintowattsbenefits.com/ How we work: At Watts, our culture is team-oriented and supportive. Employees here genuinely care about the quality of their work, and about each other. Our people are the heart of who we are and contribute to our longevity and continued success. And this is a place where you can have a big career. No matter your role, there are opportunities for learning and development, and your daily contributions make a meaningful impact on the lives of people who use our products and on the future of water.
